E daŋ kaŋɛ ewurkpa be nyɛrbi na nna fanɛ b sa ekama nsa kanaŋkamaso nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n nuu. 9Jemanɛ nɛ benyɛn na nɛ ewura na bee ji na nɛ ewurche Vashti gba wora kejigboŋ n sa kade na to be beche kikɛ ashi ewura Sɛgsis be laŋ to. 10Kachɛ shunusopo na nɛ ewura na be kagbene fuli mo ga ŋkpal nsa nɛ e nuu na so, nɛ e tre mbe nyɛrbi ashunu nɛ b fɛl bumo nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ saŋkikɛ a shuŋ mo na. Bumo e la Mehuman nɛ Bizta nɛ Harbona nɛ Bigta nɛ Abagta nɛ Zeta nɛ Kakas. 11E daŋ shuŋi bumo fanɛ b ya shin nɛ ewurche Vashti e buu mbe kuwurwuro m ba mo kutɔ. Ewura na daa sha keta ewurche na nna n ji njɔŋ n ŋini ekrachiana na nɛ mbe befɔ nɛ b ba ndoŋ na kikɛ ŋkpal mbe kebita so. 12Ewura na be nyɛrbi na ka ya kaŋɛ ewurche Vashti kusɔ nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ na, nɛ e kini keba. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ewura na nya agbo ga nseŋ tinto. 13Saŋkama malɛ, pɔɛŋ nɛ ewura na e wora kusɔ ko a laŋɛ bumo be daŋkare nɛ mbra be ekpa so, e bee tre mbe benyiashempo nna m bishi bumo kusɔ nɛ k daga kewora. Amoso e daŋ tre mbe basa nɛ baa ji mo asoeto nna m bishi bumo kusɔ nɛ k daga fanɛ e wora. 14Bumo e la Kashena nɛ Sheta nɛ Admata nɛ Tarshish nɛ Mɛrɛs nɛ Masena nɛ Memukan nɛ b la Pɛshiya nɛ Midia be efuli so be benimugboŋ ashunu nɛ e bee to jina saŋkikɛ na. 15Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Ma ewura Sɛgsis e shuŋi n tre ewurche Vashti nɛ e kini keba! Naniere nuso nɛ anyi be mbra bee ŋini fanɛ an wora mo?” 16Ndoŋ nna nɛ Memukan kaŋɛ ewura na nɛ mbe benimuana na le: “Mannɛ ewura ere nawule nɛ ewurche Vashti keni jiga na, ama mbe benimuana nɛ mbe efuli so ebi kikɛ nɛ e keni jiga na. 17Efuli ere so be beche baŋ nu kusɔ nɛ ewurche Vashti wora ere baaŋ fara a keni bumo kulana jiga. Baaŋ baa kaŋɛ le: ‘Ewura Sɛgsis tre ewurche Vashti nɛ e kini.’ 18Pɛshiya nɛ Midia be benimuana be beche baŋ nu kusɔ nɛ ewurche ere wora, bumo alɛ gba beeŋ fara a wora bumo kulana loŋ kabre kikɛ. Kaplɛkama malɛ be beche beeŋ fara a fɛl bumo kulana, nɛ bumo kulana malɛ e baa nya agbo n wɔtɔ bumo. 19Yiramu, nɛ k par fo bre, fo nase mbra nɛ baaŋ sibɛ n wɔtɔ Pɛshiya nɛ Midia be efuli so be mbra be nwɔl to nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n chɛrga kumo, fanɛ Vashti e sa maŋ naŋ ta keya n cha ewura pe kikɛ. Kumo be kaman nɛ fo ta mbe kuwurche na n sa eche nɛ e bɔ mo. 20Fo baŋ nase le be mbra ere n sa fo efuli gboŋgboŋi ere kikɛ so ebi bre, beche nɛ b wɔ efuli ere so kikɛ beeŋ baa sa bumo kulana bunyaŋ hale nɛ b la damawuraana ŋko betirpo gba.” 21Le be nfɛra nɛ Memukan bar ere daŋ par ewura na nɛ mbe benimuana ga, nɛ ewura na wora kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo na kikɛ. 22Ewura na daŋ sibɛ nwɔl yiri kikɛ be ŋgbarto nna n sa mbe efuli so ebi kikɛ fanɛ, k daga kowurnyɛn kikɛ be kamalga ka kɔ eleŋ mbe laŋ to.

english_text:
Esther Becomes Queen
1After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her. 2Then the king's personal servants said:
Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women. 3You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments. 4Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen.
King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
5At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 6 Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
7Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died. 8When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them.
Hegai was put in charge of all the women, 9and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
10Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him. 11He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
12The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes. 13When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters. 14In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
15-16Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
17Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti. 18In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts.
Mordecai Saves the King's Life
19When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official. 20He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
21Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him. 22Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out. 23King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_text:
B ka ta Ɛsta ŋ ki ewurche be asheŋ
1Ewura Sɛgsis be agbo ka wushi na kikɛ, nɛ e kraa fɛ kusɔ nɛ Vashti wora na nɛ mbra nɛ mo alɛ nase a yɔ mbe kaplɛa so na be asheŋ. 2Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na be besoetojipo nɛ e yirda ga na be beko kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ b luri to n fin besuŋgurbi nɛ b walɛ abita nsaa maŋ nyi benyɛn m ba sa ewura. 3Lara fo efuli ere be kaba kama so be ekrachi n shin nɛ b fin besuŋgurbi nɛ b walɛ abita m ba Susa m baa wɔtɔ ewura be laŋ to be kaboŋ nɛ baa wɔtɔ beche nawule na. Nseŋ ta bumo m bɔɔ Heegai nɛ b fɛl nɛ e bee keni beche so na enɔ, nɛ e ŋini bumo kananɛ baŋ baa lɔŋɛ bumo be amu nɛnɛ n lar kebita n ti so. 4Saŋɛ na so feeŋ lara bumo to be emo nɛ fee sha nɛ e ki ewurche n tal Vashti to.” Ewura na ka nu le be kasotoji ere nɛ e wu fanɛ k walɛ nseŋ bɛ kumo so. 5Jemanɛ ere so nɛ Juw be kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Mɔdikaya na wɔ Susa. Mo tuto e daa la Jaɛr nɛ mo nananyɛn Shimei malɛ la Kish nɛ e shi Bɛnjamin be kanaŋ to na pibinyɛn. 6Mɔdikaya daŋ ti basa nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza nɛ e la Babilɔn be ewura na daŋ pɛ fanɛ anya ashi Jerusalɛm nseŋ tintiŋ bumo n yɔ mbe efuli so, saŋɛ nɛ e daŋ pɛ Juda be ewura Jehowachin na so nna. 7Mɔdikaya mo wɔpa pibiche ko nɛ e daa walɛ kebita ga nsaa la kumunibi nɛ mbe Juw be ketre la Hadasa nɛ mbe ketre ko malɛ la Ɛsta na, daa wɔ Mɔdikaya kutɔ nna. Mɔdikaya daŋ ta mo nna fanɛ mo gbagba pibi ŋkpal mo nio nɛ mo tuto kikɛ ka wu ŋ ka mo so. 8Ewura na ka sa ebɔl nɛ b bar besuŋgurbi damta ewura be laŋ to be kakpa nɛ baa wɔtɔ beche nawule ashi Susa na, Ɛsta gba daŋ ti bumo so. B daŋ yɛr mo alɛ gba Heegai nɛ e bee keni ewurkpa be beche so na kutɔ nna. 9Ɛsta be asheŋ daŋ par Heegai ga. Ŋkpal loŋ so, e daa sa mo abitasɔ nɛ ajibi lela nna. Kaboŋ nɛ b wɔtɔ beche na be kakpa lela nɛ e daŋ shin nɛ b ta mo n wɔtɔ nseŋ lara ewurkpa be mbita ashunu nɛ baa shuŋ mo. 10Ŋkpal Mɔdikaya ka ji Ɛsta asoeto so e daa maŋ lara mbe kumu efuli ŋ ŋini bumo fanɛ e la Juw be esa nna. 11Karechɛ kama malɛ Mɔdikaya daa nite nna a kulti ewurkpa be kakpa nɛ beche na kikɛ wɔ na be anishito a fin kepin kananɛ Ɛsta du nɛ kusɔ nɛ k bee wora mo. 12Kafɛ koŋwule nɛ b sa beche na fanɛ b ta n lɔŋɛ bumo be amu n nyalɛ kebita n ti so. Baaŋ ta ŋku nɛ baa tre mir na n lɔŋɛ bumo be eyur so afɔl ashe nseŋ ta etulale malɛ be ŋku n lɔŋɛ bumo be eyur afɔl ashe nɛ a ka na. Kumo be kaman nɛ b yɛr beche na be ekama ewura Sɛgsis be anishito kukoko to. 13Saŋkama nɛ beche na be ekama bee sha nɛ e yɔ ewura na be anishito, kusɔ kama nɛ k par eche na nɛ e bee buu a lar kakpa nɛ b wɔtɔ beche na a yɔ ewura na be anishito. 14Eche na beeŋ yɔ ewura na kutɔ kaaseso nseŋ ya bɛta m ba Shaashgaz nɛ b fɛl nɛ e bee keni ewura be beche so ashi kakpa nɛ beche nawule wɔ na kutɔ kachipurso. Mo alɛ maaŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ ewura na kutɔ kikɛ ama mbe asheŋ baaŋ par Ewura na nna nɛ e ti mbe ketre n shuŋi n tre mo. 15Jemanɛ ka fo nɛ Mɔdikaya mo wɔpa nɛ baa tre Abihail na, pibiche Ɛsta nɛ e ta ŋ ki fanɛ mo gbagba pibiche na e yɔ ewura na kutɔ nɛ e buu nle nɛ Heegai nɛ e bee keni kakpa nɛ beche na wɔ so na kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e buu na. Ɛsta malɛ be asheŋ daa par ekama nna. 16Ewura Sɛgsis ka ji kuwura be kafɛ shunusopo be kufɔl kudusopo nɛ baa tre Tibez na nɛ b bar Ɛsta ewura na pe. 17Ɛsta be asheŋ daŋ par ewura na ga nseŋ bɔlɔ mo kenishi nɛ e sha mo a chɔ beche na be ekama. Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ e ta kuwurche be kuwurwuro n buu mo nɛ e ki ewurche n tal ewurche Vashti to. 18Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na shin nɛ b wora kejigboŋ n sa benimuana na nɛ ekrachiana na ŋkpal Ɛsta so. Nseŋ sa ebɔl fanɛ kumo be kachɛ e baa la kewushiachɛ n sa mbe efuli so be basa kikɛ. Ewura na daŋ sa basa ŋkɛ damta gba n ti so.
Mɔdikaya ka mɔlga ewura na be ŋkpa be asheŋ
19Besuŋgurbi na ka naŋ ba gama abar so kela nyɔsopo na, nɛ ewura na teŋ ta Mɔdikaya ŋ ki ewurkpa be krachi. 20Ŋkpal Mɔdikaya ka kaŋɛ Ɛsta fanɛ e sa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kama yiri nɛ k la mo so, Ɛsta daa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kikɛ yiri nɛ k la mo. Ɛsta daŋ wora loŋ nna ŋkpal e ka bee wora Mɔdikaya kasonu mbe kebia to kikɛ so.
21Jemanɛ nɛ Mɔdikaya daa la ewurkpa be krachi na, nɛ Bigtana nɛ Terɛsh nɛ b fɛl bumo nɛ baa keni ewura be ebu dese to so be kabuna so na, nya agbo n wɔtɔ ewura Sɛgsis nsaa kre mbe kemɔ ŋgbalanto. 22Mɔdikaya ka pin kumo be loŋ, nɛ e nya manaŋ n ya kaŋɛ ewurche Ɛsta nɛ mo alɛ kaŋɛ ewura na kusɔ nɛ Mɔdikaya kaŋɛ mo. 23B ka lara basa nɛ b lege kesheŋ na to n ya wu fanɛ k la kashenteŋ nna nɛ b chɛ basa anyɔ na efɔl n shiga ndibi so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na shin nɛ b yili mbe anishi to n sibɛ loŋ be kesheŋ na n wɔtɔ bumo be adrasheŋ be nwɔl to nɛ k baa la kanyiŋi.

english_text:
Haman Plans To Destroy the Jews
1Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag, 2and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai. 3When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command, 4he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
5Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him. 6And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
7It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
8 Then Haman went to the king and said:
Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them! 9Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
10The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him, 11“Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
12On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
13The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
14-15King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_text:
Heman ka kre Juwebi be kemɔ be asheŋ
1Asheŋ ere be kaman nɛ ewura Sɛgsis ta kenimu nɛ k bɛ ewura na so na n sa kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre mo Heman nɛ e la Hammedaata pibinyɛn nseŋ shi Agag be kanaŋ to na. 2Ewura na daŋ tre mbe benimu nɛ baa shuŋ ewurkpa na kikɛ nna, ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b baa bunyaŋ Heman nseŋ naa jɔŋɛ mo ase. Nɛ bumo kikɛ bɛ kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ na so ama Mɔdikaya nawule. 3Ndoŋ nna nɛ benimu nɛ baa shuŋ ewurkpa na bishi Mɔdikaya le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo ere maa bɛ kusɔ nɛ ewura nase n sa anyi na so?” 4Saŋkama nɛ b baŋ kaŋɛ Mɔdikaya fanɛ e jɔŋɛ Heman ase, e bee kini nna nseŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ mo ere la Juw be esa nna, amoso e maaŋ jɔŋɛ Heman ase. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ Heman kumo be asheŋ nsaa keni ŋko e beeŋ yige Mɔdikaya ŋkpal e ka la Juw so.
5Heman ka pin fanɛ Mɔdikaya kini kejɔŋɛ mo ase ŋko m bunyaŋ mo, nɛ e nya agbo ga. 6E ka pin fanɛ Mɔdikaya la Juw be esa nna nɛ e yili kumo fanɛ e maaŋ tɔrɔ Mɔdikaya nawule, nsaa kre nia fanɛ e beeŋ mɔ Juw kama nɛ e wɔ Ewura Sɛgsis be efuli so. 7Ewura Sɛgsis ka ji kuwura be kafɛ kuduanyɔsopo be kufɔl sososo nɛ baa tre Nisan na to, nɛ Heman shin nɛ b to beri a fin kachɛ nɛ k daga fanɛ e wora kusɔ nɛ e bee kre na. Nɛ beri na ya tɔr kufɔl kuduanyɔsopo nɛ baa tre Ada na be nchɛ kuduasa. 8Ndoŋ nna nɛ Heman kaŋɛ ewura Sɛgsis le: “Yiri ko ebi salga to m bɔlɔ fo efuli ere kikɛ so. Bumo alɛ be daŋkare kɔr basa kama peya to. B maa bɛ efuli ere be mbra gba so, amoso m baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ nɛ fo yige bumo, k maaŋ chɛ fo to. 9Nɛ k par fo, kumo ere, Yiramu, fo nase mbra fanɛ bumo kikɛ daga kemɔ. Nɛ fo shuli so n wora loŋ, ma alɛ beeŋ wora ania n fin amansherbi damta n wɔtɔ ewurkpa be amansherbi be kɔlgu na to nɛ ekrachi nɛ b wɔ ewurkpa na e ta amo n shuŋ.” 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na lara mbe kepinibi nɛ e kɔ a dulgi mbe nwɔl sibɛ so na n sa Hammedaata pibinyɛn Heman nɛ e la Juwebi bumo doŋ na 11nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Basa na nɛ bumo be amansherbi kikɛ la fo peya nna; amoso wora bumo kusɔ kama nɛ k par fo.” 12Amoso kufɔl sososo na to be kachɛ kuduasasopo na nɛ Heman tre ewura na be nwɔlsibɛpoana na ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b kilgi mbe mbra nɛ e nase na n wɔtɔ bumo be efuli na so be ŋgbarana nɛ nsibɛ be yiriana to n chige to n sa bewurbi nɛ benimu nɛ ekrachiana nɛ b wɔ efuli na so na kikɛ. Ewura Sɛgsis be ketre so nɛ b daŋ bɔla n sibɛ nwɔl na nseŋ ta mbe kepinibi n dulgi amo. 13Mbɔ nɛ b kɔ eleŋ a shile ga na, nɛ b ta nwɔl na n shuŋi fanɛ b chige efuli na so kikɛ. Kusɔ nɛ kawɔl na bee kaŋɛ e la fanɛ b mɔ Juwebi na kikɛ kufɔl kuduanyɔsopo nɛ baa tre Ada na be kachɛ kuduasasopo na to. Kawɔl na bee ŋini fanɛ b mɔ mbia nɛ benimu nɛ beche nɛ mbiwurbi kikɛ kumo be kamɔnchɛ na nseŋ muu bumo be asɔ nɛ b kɔ kikɛ. 14A daga fanɛ b yili jimaŋ to ŋ kraŋ kusɔ nɛ k wɔ kawɔl na to n sa efuli na so be kaba kama so ebi kikɛ. Saŋɛ na so ekama beeŋ bela ase a jo kumo be kachɛ. 15Ewura Sɛgsis e daŋ shin nɛ b yili jimaŋ to n wora mbra na manaŋ manaŋ ashi Susa be kade to. Ewura na nɛ Heman daŋ chena nna a nuu nsa, nɛ Susa be kade to ebi malɛ be nfɛra bee baga bumo to ŋkpal mbra na so.

english_text:
Mordecai Asks for Esther's Help
1When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping. 2But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace. 3 In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
4When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
5Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
6Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate, 7and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
8Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
9Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said. 10She answered, “Tell Mordecai 11there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
12When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, 13he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace. 14If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
15Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying, 16“Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
17Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_text:
Mɔdikaya ka bee fin kechɛto ashi Ɛsta kutɔ be asheŋ
1Mɔdikaya ka nu kusɔ nɛ ewura na wora na, nɛ e kpɛa mbe asɔbuuso to kagbenejijaso, nseŋ ta kagbenejijaso be kusɔbuuso m buu n wora nsunɔ n wurge mbe kumu so nsaa shu awɔrso ebesa so a na a kulti kade na to, 2hale m ba fo ewura na be lambu be kabuna ase. Mo alɛ daa maŋ nya ekpa n luri lambu na to ŋkpal manɛ so esa kama nɛ e buu kagbenejijaso be kusɔbuuso maŋ kɔ ekpa nɛ e luri ndoŋ. 3Efuli na so be kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ b kraŋ kawɔl na jimaŋ to, Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ bee teŋi keeli nna a boŋto a shu. B daŋ kishi nna nseŋ shu ga nɛ bumo be bedamta ta kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso m buu nseŋ dese nsunɔ to. 4Ɛsta be mbita nɛ benyɛn nɛ b fɛl nɛ baa shuŋ mo na ka kaŋɛ mo Mɔdikaya be asheŋ, nɛ mbe kagbenejija mo ga, nɛ e ta asɔbuuso lela n sa fanɛ b ya sa Mɔdikaya, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ lara kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso na, nɛ Mɔdikaya kini. 5Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛsta shin nɛ ewura na be benyɛn nɛ b fɛl e la Ɛsta be kayɛrbi, nɛ baa tre mo Hataak na, ya bishi Mɔdikaya kusɔ nɛ k kɔ mo. 6Nɛ Hataak yɔ Mɔdikaya kutɔ ashi ewurkpa be kelɔnɛ so. 7Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mɔdikaya kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ k wora kikɛ nɛ kananɛ Heman nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e beeŋ ta amansherbi damta n wɔtɔ ewurkpa be kɔlgu to, nɛ b mɔ Juwebi kikɛ. 8Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta kawɔl nɛ b sibɛ ashi Susa nɛ k bee kaŋɛ fanɛ a daga b ka mɔ Juwebi kikɛ na be kuko n sa Hataak fanɛ e ta n ya ŋini Ɛsta nseŋ bugi to ŋ kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ k wɔtɔ, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ kule ewura na nɛ e wu mbe basa kuwɔr. 9Nɛ Hataak wora loŋ. 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛsta sa ebɔl fanɛ e bɛta n ya kaŋɛ Mɔdikaya le: 11“Ewurkpa be mbra bee ŋini fanɛ esa kama nɛ e luri ewura kutɔ nɛ e maŋ tre mo, daga luwu. Ewura na be asoetojipoana nɛ mbe kasawule so be kaba kikɛ so ebi gba nyi kumo be loŋ. Ama ewura na baaŋ teŋi mbe shuwa be kuwurkpabi na nna ŋ shoŋi esa na. Loŋ bre, b maaŋ mɔ mo. Amoso k beeŋ baa du kpakpa n sa ma nɛ n wu ewura na ŋkpal manɛ so kufɔl lelemu nna na e ka maŋ shuŋi n tre ma.” 12Mɔdikaya ka nu Ɛsta be kubɔya na 13nɛ mo alɛ ta le be kubɔya ere n shoŋi mo: “Sa maŋ kaa fɛ fanɛ nɛ baa mɔ Juwebi kikɛ, fo ere beeŋ nya fo kumu ŋkpal fo ka wɔ ewura pe so. 14Nɛ fo baŋ maŋ wora shɛŋ le be jemanɛ ere, ashere, echɛtopo ko beeŋ shi kakpa ko m ba mɔlga anyi. Ama fo ere nɛ fo tuto be kanaŋ to ebi kikɛ beeŋ mur. Wanɛ e nyi fanɛ le bre so nɛ fo ki ewurche le be jemanɛ ere?” 15Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛsta shuŋi ŋ kaŋɛ Mɔdikaya le: 16“Shin nɛ Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Susa na kikɛ e ba abar so m ba kishi nchɛ asa nɛ nnyɛ asa ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n sa ma. Ma alɛ gba nɛ ma mbita beeŋ luri loŋ be ekishi na to. Kumo be kaman, nɛ n yɔ ewura na kutɔ. Hale nɛ mbra maŋ sa ma ekpa gba, meeŋ wora loŋ. Nɛ k la luwu nɛ n wu.” 17Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mɔdikaya ya wora kusɔ kama nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ mo na kikɛ.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Ɛsta ka tre ewura na nɛ Heman kejigboŋ to be asheŋ
1Ekishi na be kachɛ sasopo nɛ Ɛsta ta mbe kuwurche be kale m buu nseŋ ya yili ewura na be lambubi na be kabuna to. Ewura na malɛ daa tase mbe kuwurputi so nna lambu na to a keni kabuna to. 2Ewura na ka wu ewurche Ɛsta ka yil kabuna to na, nɛ mbe asheŋ par mo ga, nɛ e teŋi mbe shuwa be kuwurkpabi na ŋ shoŋi mo. Nɛ Ɛsta ya pɛ kuwurkpabi na be kɔnɔso. 3Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na bishi le: “Ewurche Ɛsta, manɛ e kɔ fo? Manɛ nɛ fee sha? Kaŋɛ ma kusɔ kama nɛ k tir fo. Hale ma efuli ere be bargato gba nɛ fee sha, meeŋ ta n sa fo.” 4Nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu! Nɛ k par fo, kumo ere fo nɛ Heman e ba tu ma n ji kejigboŋ kabre kaaseso.” 5Nɛ ewura na shuŋi fanɛ b ya tre Heman manaŋ m ba nɛ b yɔ Ɛsta kutɔ. Nɛ Heman ba, nɛ mo nɛ ewura na yɔ Ɛsta be kejigboŋ na to. 6B ka bee nuu nsa nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Ɛsta le: “Kaŋɛ kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha nɛ n sa fo kumo. Manɛ bre e tir fo? Hale ma efuli ere be bargato gba nɛ fee sha, meeŋ sa fo kumo.” 7Nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ: 8“Nɛ k par fo Yiramu, fo nɛ Heman e naŋ ba tu ma n ji kejigboŋ nfe echefo, saŋɛ na so, meeŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ mee sha.”
Heman ka kre kemɔ Mɔdikaya be asheŋ
9Nɛ Heman ta kagbenefuli nɛ kagbenewushi n lar Ɛsta kutɔ. E ka bee yɔ na nɛ e wu Mɔdikaya ewurkpa be kabuna na ase. Ama e ka wu fanɛ Mɔdikaya maŋ koso n yili n sa mo bunyaŋ nɛ e nya agbo ga. 10Ama e daŋ ji kanyiti nna n yɔ epe n ya tre mo teriana nɛ mbe eche Zɛrɛsh n shɛr, 11n ji njɔŋ ŋ ŋini bumo kananɛ e dii kedama nɛ kananɛ e kɔ mbinyɛnsobi damta nɛ kananɛ ewura maŋ mo so nseŋ sa mo kenimu a chɔ ekrachiana nɛ benimuana na be ekama. 12Kede be kaman nɛ Heman naŋ kaŋɛ: “Asɔ damta gba kraŋ ti so, ma nɛ ewura nawule nɛ ewurche Ɛsta tre mbe kejigboŋ to, e maŋ tre esa kikɛ n ti anyi so. E yɛ echefo gba an naaŋ ba tu mo n ji. 13Ama ade kikɛ kraa maa bɔlɔ ma kenishi ŋkpal Juwnyɛn na, Mɔdikaya, ka kraa chena ewurkpa be kabuna to na so.” 14Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo teriana nɛ mbe eche Zɛrɛsh kaŋɛ mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo maaŋ ku kadebi nɛ kumo be nteŋ sa fanɛ ayadra adushunu nɛ anu n yuu nseŋ kule ewura ekpa echefo kachipurso n ya chɛ Mɔdikaya efɔl n shiga kumo so. Kumo be kaman nɛ fo ta kagbenefuli n tu ewura na n yɔ kejigboŋ na to.” Heman be kagbene daŋ fuli mo ga ŋkpal le be nfɛra nɛ b sa mo ere so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shin nɛ b yuu kedibi na.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Ewura na ka sa Mɔdikaya bunyaŋ be asheŋ
1Kanyɛ ka biri nɛ ewura na di ŋ gben, nseŋ shin nɛ b bar mbe efuli na so be asheŋ nɛ a wora mbe kuwurji be jemanɛ so nɛ b sibɛ amo n wɔtɔ nwɔl to na kikɛ, m baa kaa kraŋ a ŋini mo. 2B ka bee kraŋ na, nɛ b ya lar kananɛ Mɔdikaya daŋ pin Bigtana nɛ Tɛrɛsh nɛ b daŋ fɛl nɛ baa yili a kuŋ ewura be ebu be kabuna to na, ka daa kre ewura be kemɔ ŋgblaŋto be asheŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ ewura na. 3Nɛ ewura na bishi bumo le: “Mɔdikaya ka wora le ere bre, manɛ be kakɔka nɛ kemaŋkura bre nɛ an sa mo n tal to?” Nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na yɛ: “B maŋ wora shɛŋ n sa mo.” 4Loŋ be jemanɛ so nɛ Heman baŋ ba luri ewurkpa nɛ e ba kule ewura ekpa n ya shin nɛ b chɛ Mɔdikaya efɔl n shiga kedibi nɛ e yuu na so. Nɛ ewura bishi le: “Wanɛ e wɔ lambu to ere?” 5Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na kaŋɛ: “Heman nna.” Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ: “Men shin nɛ e baa luri.” 6Heman ka luri nɛ ewura na bishi mo le: “Manɛ e daga ŋ ka wora n sa esa nɛ mee sha keta n yili bunyaŋ be eyilikpa?” Nɛ Heman fɛ le: “M baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ ma nɛ ewura bee sha kewora le be kusɔ ere n sa na.” 7Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ ewura na le: 8“Shin nɛ b ta fo piŋi tenteŋ nɛ fo buu ere be kuko m buu esa kama nɛ e daga le be bunyaŋ ere nseŋ shin nɛ b mɛa fo gbagba be egbaŋɛ ere be eko to, 9nseŋ shin nɛ fo benimuana na be eko e ta esa na n chena gbaŋɛ na so ŋ keta mo ŋ kulti kade ere be abɔrbi kikɛ so a kaŋɛ awɔrso le: ‘Men keni, kananɛ ewura bee ta esa a yili bunyaŋ be eyilikpa nna!.’ ” 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Heman le: “Kumo ere wora manaŋ n ya fin piŋi na nɛ gbaŋɛ na m ba wora kusɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ ere gbagba n sa Mɔdikaya nɛ e la Juw na. Mo e naa chena ewurkpa be kabunagboŋ na ase na. Nyiŋi n wora kusɔ kama nɛ fo kaŋɛ ere n sa mo nsaa maaŋ teŋ shɛŋ so.” 11Ndoŋ nna nɛ Heman ta ewura be piŋi m buu Mɔdikaya nseŋ shin nɛ e chena gbaŋɛ nɛ b mɛa to fanɛ ewura peya na so nɛ e juŋkpar a nite a gberge Mɔdikaya nɛ gbaŋɛ na a kulti kade na to a kaŋɛ awɔrso le: “Men keni kananɛ ewura bee ta esa a yili bunyaŋ be eyilikpa!” 12B ka kilgi to n loge, nɛ Mɔdikaya bɛta n ya chena ewurkpa be kabunagboŋ na ase, nɛ Heman malɛ ta anishinyɔr gboŋgboŋi n jɔto n yɔ epe, 13n ya kaŋɛ mbe eche nɛ mo teriana kusɔ nɛ k nya mo kikɛ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe eche nɛ mo teriana na kaŋɛ mo le: “Mɔdikaya ka la Juw be esa ere bre fo maaŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ mo so kikɛ. Baa nyi fanɛ fo eleŋ baa fo ekar nna na. Feeŋ ki esa fuloŋ.” 14B kraa malga nna nɛ ewura be nyɛrbi ba shin nɛ Heman wora manaŋ nɛ b yɔ Ɛsta be kejigboŋ nɛ e wora n yili na to.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
B ka Mɔ Heman be asheŋ
1Kede be kaman nɛ ewura na nɛ Heman yɔ Ɛsta kutɔ nɛ b ya ji. 2B kaa tase a nuu nsa kejigboŋ nyɔsopo na to na, nɛ ewura na naŋ bishi Ɛsta le: “Manɛ bre e tir fo? Kusɔ kama nɛ k tir fo, fo kaŋɛ ma nɛ n sa fo kumo. Hale ma efuli ere be bargato gba nɛ fee sha, feeŋ nya kumo.” 3Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewurche Ɛsta kaŋɛ: “Yiramu, nɛ k par fo bre, kumo ere fo wora le be kusɔ ere n sa ma. Mɔlga ma ŋkpa nseŋ sɔ ma basa n yige n sa ma. 4B fa ma nɛ ma basa kikɛ fanɛ b mɔ anyi nna. K daa la fanɛ baa fa anyi nna fanɛ anya gba, ndafanɛ maaŋ bugi kɔnɔ ŋ kaŋɛ fo shɛŋ, ama baa kre kemɔ anyi kikɛ nna!” 5Nɛ ewura Sɛgsis bishi Ewurche Ɛsta le: “Wanɛ malɛ e nya kagbene a sha kewora le be kesheŋ ere? Nnɛ nɛ loŋ be esa na wɔ?” 6Nɛ Ɛsta yɛ: “Mo e la Heman ere. E la esa lubi nɛ edoŋ nɛ emɔpo nna.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kufu pɛ Heman ga ashi ewura na nɛ ewurche na be anishito.
7Nɛ ewura na nya agbo ga ŋ koso n yige nsa na nseŋ yɔ ewurkpa be kelɔnɛ na so. Heman ka pin fanɛ ewura na beeŋ gberge mo kusoe nɛ e shir kaman a kule ewurche Ɛsta fanɛ e mɔlga mbe ŋkpa. 8Ewura na ka shi kelɔnɛ na so m bɛta a ba ebu na to nɛ e wu Heman ka jɔŋɛ ŋ gbasa Ɛsta be kuwurputi a kule mo kenishipereso fanɛ e chɛ mo to. Ewura na ka wu loŋ nɛ e ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kanyɛn ere bee sha kepur ma eche ere ma anishito nna ashi ewurkpa nfe a?” Ewura na maŋ naŋ malga n loge gba nɛ mbe nyɛrbi ba nyaŋ Heman ŋ gberge mo ashi ewurche na kutɔ. 9Nɛ nyɛrbi na be emo nɛ baa tre Harbona na kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, Heman koŋwule ere yuu kedibi nna mbe laŋ to fanɛ b chɛ Mɔdikaya nɛ e mɔlga fo ŋkpa na efɔl n shiga so. Kedibi na be nteŋ la ayadra adushunu nɛ anu nna!” Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ: “Men chɛ Heman efɔl n shiga loŋ be kedibi na so!” 10Nɛ b ya chɛ Heman efɔl n shiga kedibi nɛ e yuu fanɛ b chɛ Mɔdikaya n shiga so na so. Nɛ ewura na be kagbene wushi mo.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
Juwebi ka kɔ n sɔ bumo be amu be asheŋ
1Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura Sɛgsis ta Heman nɛ e la Juwebi bumo doŋ na be kapetɛ kikɛ n sa ewurche Ɛsta kumo kamɔnchɛ kikɛ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ ewura na kananɛ mo nɛ Mɔdikaya be kekurgeto lar kikɛ. Kumo be kamɔnchɛ nɛ ewura ta Mɔdikaya ŋ ki mbe ekrachi nimuso na be eko. 2Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na ta mbe kepinibi nɛ k daa wɔ Heman kutɔ nɛ b kɔ a dulgi ewura be nwɔl sibɛso na n sa Mɔdikaya. Nɛ Ɛsta malɛ shin nɛ Mɔdikaya bee keni Heman be asɔ na so. 3Nɛ Ɛsta naŋ laŋɛ n yɔ Ewura na kutɔ n ya gbir mbe anishito n shu ŋ kule mo fanɛ e wora ania n laŋɛ Heman nɛ e la Agag be kaman to ebi be ŋkre lubi nɛ e daŋ kre Juwebi na. 4Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na teŋi mbe shuwa be kuwurkpabi na ŋ shoŋi Ɛsta nɛ e niŋi to n yili nseŋ kaŋɛ le: 5“Yiramu, nɛ k par fo nsaa walɛ n sa fo, nɛ fee fɛ ma asheŋ bre, kumo ere fo sibɛ nwɔl ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ kananɛ Heman kre fanɛ b mɔ anyi Juwebi kikɛ ashi fo kasawule so na e sa maŋ naŋ wora. 6M maaŋ tiŋ n chena a keni nɛ ma basa e mur.” 7Nɛ ewura Sɛgsis kaŋɛ ewurche Ɛsta nɛ Mɔdikaya nɛ e la Juw be esa na le: “Ŋkpal Heman ka bee fin kewora Juwebi na kulubi so nɛ n shin nɛ b chɛ mo n shiga kedibi so, nseŋ ta mbe kapetɛ gba n sa Ɛsta na. 8Ŋkpal esa ka maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n chɛrga kawɔl kikɛ nɛ b sibɛ ashi ewura be ketre to nseŋ ta mbe kepinibi n dulgi so, n sa fo ekpa fanɛ fo ere gba e sibɛ kawɔl kananɛ k par fo nsaa beeŋ tiŋ m mɔlga Juwebi na nseŋ ta ewura be kepinibi nɛ b kɔ a dulgi mbe nwɔl sibɛso na n dulgi kumo.” 9Kufɔl sasopo nɛ baa tre Sivan na be nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ asa nɛ b shɛr ewurkpa be nwɔlsibɛpoana na epul to, nɛ Mɔdikaya malga nɛ b sibɛ nwɔl n sa Juwebi na nɛ bejuŋkparpo nɛ ekrachiana nɛ benimuana nɛ b wɔ efuli na be abonfu kalfa nɛ adunyɔ nɛ ashunu nɛ a yili Indiya be efuli so ashi epeŋilarkpa n ya fo Etopiya be efuli so ashi epeŋitɔrkpa na. Efuli kama so ebi be ŋgbar to nɛ Juwebi be ŋgbar to nɛ b daŋ sibɛ nwɔl na n sa bumo. 10Ewura Sɛgsis be ketre to nɛ Mɔdikaya daŋ shin nɛ b sibɛ nwɔl na kikɛ nseŋ ta ewura na be kepinibi nɛ b kɔ a dulgi nwɔl na n dulgi amo kikɛ. Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta amo n sa ewura be egbaŋɛ nɛ baa shile ga na be bediipo fanɛ b chige. 11Kusɔ nɛ nwɔl na kaŋɛ e la fanɛ ewura sa Juwebi ekpa fanɛ b kreto nɛnɛ ŋ kɔ m mɔlga bumo amu. E yɛ nɛ benapo ko koso nɛ b ba kɔ Juwebi be benyɛn ŋko beche ŋko mbia, Juwebi na kɔ ekpa nɛ b tu loŋ be bedoŋ na ŋ kɔ m mɔ bumo be kikɛ nseŋ ta bumo asɔ kikɛ ŋ ki bumo peya. 12Kufɔl kuduanyɔsopo nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduasa, nɛ b daŋ yili fanɛ baaŋ mɔ Juwebi kikɛ ashi ewura Sɛgsis be efuli so na nɛ mbra nɛ Mɔdikaya sa na gba daga fanɛ k shuŋ. 13A daga fanɛ efuli na so ebi kikɛ ka nu mbra na, saŋɛ na so Juwebi na beeŋ wora shiriya ŋ kɔ bumo doŋana na loŋ be kamɔnchɛ. 14Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura sa ekpa nɛ egbaŋɛdiipoana na ta ewurkpa be egbaŋɛ na n lar n shile eleŋso n ya chige nwɔl na efuli na kikɛ so. Nɛ mbra na sɔ Susa gba be kade to kikɛ. 15Kumo be kaman nɛ Mɔdikaya ta kuwurpiŋi lela ko nɛ k la buru nɛ kefuful be weato m buu nseŋ ta ago be piŋi peper kunɔkunɔ m buu n deŋi kumo so, n ta shuwa be kuwurwuro nyɛkpɛso m buu nseŋ lar ewurkpa n yɔ. Nɛ Susa be kade to ebi be ŋgbene fuli bumo nɛ baa cha awɔr nsaa ponte to kagbenefuliso 16K daa la kagbenefuli nɛ kumu saŋɛ nna n sa Juwebi na kikɛ nɛ b nya tama fanɛ baaŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so. 17Efuli kama nɛ kade kama to nɛ ewura na be mbra na yɔ, Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ be ŋgbene bee fuli bumo nna ga nɛ baa ji eyur nsaa wora kejigboŋ. Ŋkpal loŋ so basa damta daŋ ta bumo be amu nna ŋ ki Juwebi ŋkpal b ka bee ŋana Juwebi na so so.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Juwebi na ka kɔ m pɔɔ bumo doŋana so be asheŋ
1Kufɔl kuduanyɔsopo nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduasa nɛ sososo be mbra na daŋ daga fanɛ k shuŋ. Loŋ be kachɛ na nɛ Juwebi bumo doŋana na daŋ fɛ fanɛ baaŋ pɔɔ bumo so nseŋ wora bumo, bumo be kepar ama Juwebi na e daŋ kilgi m pɔɔ bedoŋana na so. 2Juwebi na daŋ chala abar so nna kade kama to nɛ b wɔ ashi efuli na so kikɛ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ kɔ basa kama nɛ baa sha ketɔrɔ bumo na. Basa nɛ b wɔ efuli na so na malɛ be bekama daŋ maŋ tiŋ n tu Juwebi na ŋ kɔ ŋkpal manɛ so b daa ŋana bumo nna. 3Abane b ekrachiana nɛ efuli na so be benimuana nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na kikɛ daa yil Juwebi na be kaman nna ŋkpal bumo kikɛ ka daa ŋana Mɔdikaya so. 4Mɔdikaya daŋ ki esagboŋ nna ashi ewurkpa na nɛ mbe ketre dii ashi efuli na so kikɛ nɛ mbe eleŋ malɛ bee ti so saŋkama. 5Ŋkpal loŋ so Juwebi na daŋ wora bumo doŋana na kusɔ k par bumo nna nseŋ ta etokobi m mɔ bumo kikɛ. 6Juwebi na daŋ mɔ basa alfa anu nna ashi Susa be kade to gbagba, ama b daa maŋ ta bumo be asɔ bre. 7-10Heman nɛ e daa la Juwebi bumo doŋ na daa kɔ mbia kudu nna. Bumo alɛ gba daŋ ti basa nɛ b mɔ na so. Mbe mbia na e daa la Pashandaata nɛ Dalfɔn nɛ Aspaata nɛ Poraata nɛ Adalia nɛ Aridaata nɛ Pamashta nɛ Arisai nɛ Aridai nɛ Vaizaata. 11Kumo be kamɔnchɛ gbagba nɛ b kaŋɛ ewura basa nɛ b mɔ ashi Susa be kade to. 12Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ ewurche Ɛsta le: “Basa alfa anu nɛ Juwebi na mɔ ashi Susa be kade to gbagba. Heman be mbinyɛnbi kudu kikɛ daŋ ti bumo so. Kusɔ nɛ b naŋ wora ma efuli na be mba nɛ a ka na bre m maŋ nyi. Manɛ nɛ fo naa sha ŋ ka naŋ wora n sa fo? Kaŋɛ ma! Meeŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha n sa fo.” 13Nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu, nɛ k par fo bre, fo naŋ shin nɛ Juwebi na e wora kusɔ nɛ b wora kabre ashi Susa ere echefo gba, nseŋ shin nɛ b chɛ Heman be mbinyɛnsobi kudu na be kebuni efɔl n shiga ndibi nɛ b yuu na so.” 14Nɛ Ewura na sa ekpa ashi Susa be kade to fanɛ b chɛ Heman be mbia na be kebuni efɔl n shiga nɛ esa kama e wu bumo. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b chɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi kudu na kikɛ be kebuni efɔl n shiga. 15Kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduana nɛ Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Susa be kade to na naŋ chala abar m mɔ basa alfa asa kade na to, ama b maŋ ta bumo be kusɔ kama bre. 16Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ewura na be efuli na so be abonfu nɛ a ka na gba daŋ chala abar nna ŋ kɔ n sɔ bumo be amu ashi bumo doŋana kutɔ. Bumo alɛ daŋ mɔ basa ŋgboŋ adushunu nɛ anu ama, b daa maŋ ta bumo be kusɔ kama. 17Kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduasa na nɛ loŋ daŋ wora. Kachɛ kuduanasopo na bre, b daa maŋ mɔ basa. B daŋ ta loŋ be kachɛ na nna ŋ ki kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ be kachɛ. 18Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Susa na bre daŋ ta kufɔl na be nchɛ kuduanu na nna ŋ ki kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ nɛ kewushiachɛ ŋkpal manɛ so bumo ere daŋ mɔ bumo doŋana nchɛ kuduasa nɛ kuduana na nna. 19Amoso nɛ Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ndekarso na yili kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduana na fanɛ kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ be kewushiachɛ nɛ kachɛ nɛ baa chige abar ajibi na. 20Mɔdikaya daŋ sibɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k wora na kikɛ n wɔtɔ kawɔl to, nseŋ sa Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ewura Sɛgsis be efuli so na kikɛ nwɔl na, 21fanɛ kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduana nɛ kuduanu na e baa la nchɛgboŋ kafɛ kikɛ to n sa bumo. 22Le be nchɛ ere nɛ Juwebi na daŋ pɔɔ bumo doŋana so nɛ bumo kagbenejija ki kagbenefuli na. E daŋ kaŋɛ bumo nna fanɛ b ta loŋ be nchɛ na nna ŋ ki kejigboŋ nɛ ajibi be kedaŋɛ n chige abar nɛ betirpo. 23Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juwebi na shuli n sɔ kusɔ kama nɛ Mɔdikaya sibɛ n sa bumo na, nseŋ ta loŋ be nchɛ na ŋ ki nchɛgboŋ kafɛ kikɛ to.
24Hammedaata nɛ e shi Agag be kanaŋ to na pibinyɛn Heman nɛ e la Juwebi bumo doŋ na e daŋ to beri m fin kachɛ nɛ k daga b ka mɔ Juwebi na kikɛ. 25Nɛ Ɛsta yɔ ewura kutɔ nɛ ewura na shin nɛ b sibɛ mbra nɛ k shin nɛ kusɔ nɛ Heman kre fanɛ e beeŋ wora Juwebi na laŋɛ n ji mo. Nɛ b chɛ mo nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi kikɛ efɔl n shiga ndibi nɛ b yuu na so. 26Ŋkpal kawɔl nɛ Mɔdikaya sibɛ na so, nɛ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ k wora Juwebi na so, b daa tre nchɛgboŋ na Purim nna. Kumo be kifito e la keto beri. 27Juwebi na yili kumo nna fanɛ bumo nɛ bumo nanabiana kikɛ nɛ esa kama nɛ e beeŋ ba ki Juw be esa kachako so, beeŋ baa ji loŋ be nchɛgboŋ anyɔ na fanɛ kananɛ Mɔdikaya kaŋɛ bumo na gbagba. 28Amoso, baŋ yili loŋ be saŋɛ na a yɔ k ki mbra nna fanɛ Juwebi na nɛ bumo be kanaŋ kikɛ, nɛ bumo nɛ baaŋ koso kachako so kikɛ daga b ka bee nyiŋi nchɛgboŋ anyɔ nɛ baa tre Purim na nsaa ji amo kafɛ kikɛ. 29Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewurche Ɛsta nɛ e la Abihail pibiche na nɛ Mɔdikaya cha abar n sibɛ kawɔl kpakpaso ko nɛ k kɔ ewurche na be eleŋ na ti kawɔl nɛ Mɔdikaya teŋ sibɛ a laŋɛ nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na so. 30Kumo be kaman nɛ Mɔdikaya chige nwɔl na to n sa Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ewura Sɛgsis be efuli kalfa nɛ adunyɔ nɛ ashunu na so kikɛ. Kagbenewushi nɛ keleŋto gba be asheŋ daa wɔ kawɔl na to, 31nsaa nyiŋi Juwebi na nɛ bumo nanabiana fanɛ b baa nyiŋi a ji nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na fanɛ kananɛ baa ji ekishi nɛ nli be nchɛgboŋ na. Mɔdikaya nɛ ewurche Ɛsta e daŋ yili le be kesheŋ ere n sa bumo. 32Ewurche Ɛsta be eleŋ so nɛ b wora nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na be mbra n nase kanyiŋi be nwɔl to.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Mɔdikaya ka ki esagboŋ be asheŋ
1Ewura Sɛgsis yili lampo nna n sa basa nɛ b tase teku ase nɛ bumo nɛ b maŋ tase teku ase ashi mbe efuli so kikɛ. 2B sibɛ kananɛ e ji eleŋ mbe kuwura to nɛ kananɛ e maŋ Mɔdikaya so n yili eyilikpagboŋ kikɛ n wɔtɔ Pɛshiya nɛ Midia be efuliana so be bewura be adrasheŋ be nwɔl kikɛ to nna. 3Mɔdikaya e daa la enimu m bɛ ewura Sɛgsis so. E daa la esagboŋ nna Juwebi na kutɔ nɛ b daa sha mbe asheŋ ga ŋkpal e ka daŋ chɛ bumo to nsaa malga a sɔ bumo a yige so.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Job nɛ mbe kanaŋ be asheŋ
1Kanyɛn ko e daa wɔ Uz be kasawule so nɛ baa tre mo Job. Job daa la esa nɛ esa kikɛ maŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna. E daa la esa nɛ e bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora nna. 2E daa kɔ bibinyɛn ashunu nɛ bibiche asa nna, 3nseŋ daa kɔ mbolpɔ ŋgboŋ ashunu nɛ enyɔma ŋgboŋ asa nɛ ana kagboŋ nɛ ekurma alfa anu nna. Mo alɛ daa naa kɔ beshumpo damta ga nseŋ daa la esa nɛ e dii dama a chɔ ekama ashi efuliana nɛ a wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na.
4Job be bibinyɛn ashunu na daa wora kejigboŋ bumo be elaŋana to kebɛso kebɛso nna nsaa tre bumo sipocheana besa na nɛ baa ba m ba kaa tu bumo a ji nsaa nuu. 5Mbia na baŋ ji kejigboŋ ŋklade kachipurso kikɛ, Job beeŋ shuŋi n tre bumo m ba lara esarga chɔɔso n sa Ebɔrɛ ŋ kule alubi be ketampaŋ n sa mbia na, a fɛ fanɛ ashere b kaa bee ji nsaa nuu na b wora kulubi ko n da Ebɔrɛ so nɛ b maŋ nyi.
Sososo be kewora ŋ keni nɛ k ba Job so be asheŋ
6Kachako nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ba shɛr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ ashi ebɔrɛso nɛ Setani gba ba ti bumo so ndoŋ. 7Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi Setani le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo shi! Manɛ nɛ fo daa wora?”
Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ: “N na a kulti durnya kikɛ to nna.”
8Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ bishi Setani le: “Manɛ nɛ fee fɛ a laŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Job be kaplɛa so? Durnya kikɛ to, esa kikɛ maŋ du fanɛ mo. Ŋkpal manɛ so, e la esa nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna. Mo alɛ bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora nna.”
9Ndoŋ nna nɛ Setani malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nna nɛ Job maaŋ baa ŋana Ebɔrɛ? 10Jemanɛ kikɛ fee kuŋ mo nɛ mbe kanaŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ nna nseŋ naa shin nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e bee wora bee nyalɛ a sa mo, hale nɛ mbe mbolpɔ nɛ ana salga to n sɔ kaplɛkama. 11To, fo ere e mur mbe kusɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ ŋ keni a, e maaŋ yili fo gbagba be anishito n shoduu fo?”
12Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Setani le: “Yoo, n ta kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ m bɔɔ fo enɔ, ama sa maŋ kaŋ doro Job gbagba bre.”
Nɛ Setani lar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kutɔ n choŋ.
Job be kusɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ ka mur be asheŋ
13Kachako nɛ Job be bibinyɛn ashunu nɛ bumo sipocheana besa na yaŋ wora kejigboŋ a ji nsaa nuu ashi Job be wurkoŋ be laŋ to. 14Ndoŋ nɛ nna kabɔ ko ber to m ba Job kutɔ m ba kaŋɛ mo le: “An daa kɔ ana na nna a dɔ nɛ ekurma na malɛ wɔ kupuŋ to m mata anyi a ji. 15Epul na to nɛ Sabiaebi ko ba lar anyi so m mɔ beshumpo na nseŋ kpa ana nɛ ekurma na kikɛ n choŋ. N nawule e tiŋ n nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”
16Kabɔ na kraa malga nna nɛ enyɔsopo shile m ba kaŋɛ le: “Bɔrɛ nyɛkpɛ nna m ponte mbolpɔ na nɛ mbolpɔkpapoana na m mɔ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”
17Mo alɛ gba kraa malga nna nɛ kabɔ sasopo ba kaŋɛ Job le: “Beyu nɛ b kɔ akɔsɔ be ntuŋ asa shi Babilɔn be efuli so nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso be epeŋilarkpa na nna m ba kɔ n suge fo enyɔma na nseŋ kpa amo kikɛ n choŋ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”
18Loŋ be kabɔ na gba kraa malga nna nɛ enasopo shile m ba kaŋɛ le: “Fo mbia daŋ wora kejigboŋ nna a ji nsaa nuu ashi fo wurkoŋ be laŋ to 19nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ ko ber n shi keshishɛrsawule so epul to m ba da kowu na n lɛ fo mbia na kikɛ so m mɔ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”
20Job ka nu le be asheŋ ere kikɛ, nɛ e pɛ mbe asɔbuuso ŋ kpɛa to nseŋ she mbe kumu so be emin kikɛ ŋkpal kagbenejija damta nɛ k tɔr mo so na so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e gbir m bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ 21nseŋ kaŋɛ le:
“B ka kurge ma m ba durnya to,
m maaŋ bar shɛŋ.
Ŋ ka naŋ wu a lar durnya to, m maaŋ ta shɛŋ n lar.
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e sa, mo alɛ e sɔ;
Kemaŋkura e baa la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ peya!”
22Asheŋ nɛ e wora ere kikɛ to, Job daa maŋ wora kulubi m malga ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Job be kewora ŋ keni nyɔsopo be asheŋ
1Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ka naŋ ba shɛr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito ashi ebɔrɛso, nɛ Setani gba naŋ ba tu bumo n shɛr ndoŋ. 2Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi Setani le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo shi! Manɛ nɛ fo daa wora?”
Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ: “N na a kulti durnya kikɛ to nna.”
3Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fee fɛ a laŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Job be kaplɛa so? Durnya kikɛ to esa kama maŋ du fanɛ mo. E la esa nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna nɛ mo alɛ bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora. Fo ka kule ma ekpa n ya mur mbe asɔ kikɛ, nɛ e maŋ wora shɛŋ gba na, e kraa maŋ chɛrga mbe kebaawɔtɔ to.”
4Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ le: “Esa shuli e ka paŋ asɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ nsaa kɔ mbe ŋkpa a wɔtɔ. 5Fo ere e ta kayurnyaŋ n lɛ Job so ŋ keni, e beeŋ yili fo gbagba be anishito n shoduu fo.”
6Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ naŋ kaŋɛ le: “To, n nu! Feeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ kayurnyaŋ e tɔr Job so nɛ e ji awurfoŋ kananɛ fee sha, ama sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ mo bre!” 7Nɛ Setani lar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito nseŋ ya ta achuu besa so n lɛ Job so. Yili mbe kumu so m ba fo mbe ayadra so kikɛ daŋ wora achuu nna.
8Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job lar n ya chena kumuni so nseŋ ta kapɛlanfu a kuti mbe achuu na to. 9Nɛ mbe eche ba kaŋɛ mo: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo kraŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ ashi awurfoŋ nɛ fee ji ere kikɛ to? Shoduu mo nseŋ wu nɛ k loge!”
10Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ mbe eche le: “Sa maa malga fanɛ ewulpo! Nɛ anyeeŋ sɔ Ebɔrɛ be nɛfa nɛ enɔgboŋ anyɔ, manɛ nna nɛ anyi maaŋ sɔ etɔrɔ bre mo kutɔ?” Asheŋ ere kikɛ to, Job maŋ malga ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e maŋ wora n nyalɛ.
Job mo teriana besa na be asheŋ
11Job daa kɔ benekpana kpakpaso asa ko nna. Bumo e daa la Ɛlifaz nɛ e shi kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Tɛman na nɛ Bildad nɛ e shi Shuuwa be kasawule so nɛ Zofa nɛ mo alɛ shi Naama be kasawule so na. B ka nu awurfoŋ nɛ Job bee ji na be asheŋ nɛ b kre keyɔ n ya leŋ mo to nseŋ wushi mo kagbene. 12B kraa wɔ kufɔ kufɔ nna nseŋ wu Job, ama b daa maŋ pin mo. B ka ba pin fanɛ Job nna nɛ b fara a shu a boŋ to awɔrso nseŋ kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to nsaa wora eshishɛr a wurge bumo be amu so a ŋini fanɛ bumo be ŋgbene jija bumo. 13Kumo be kaman nɛ b ya tu Job n chena kasawule nchɛ ashunu nɛ nnyɛ ashunu nɛ ekama maa bugi kɔnɔ a kaŋɛ shɛŋ, ŋkpal awurfoŋ gboŋgboŋi nɛ b wu e ka bee ji so.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Job ka fubel n sa Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ
1Kumo be lalaloge nɛ Job fara
m malga n shoduu mbe kakurgeachɛ ŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ le:
2-3O Ebɔrɛ, sho kachɛ nɛ b kurge ma na kɔnɔ,
nseŋ shoduu kanyɛ nɛ n nio sɔ ma kedampo na gba!
4Ebɔrɛ, shin nɛ loŋ be kachɛ na e ki tentembiri plɔ.
Sa maŋ naa nyiŋi kumo be asheŋ kikɛ kuraa,
fo alɛ e sa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ k fulto kikɛ.
5Shin nɛ k baa la kachɛ nɛ k biri to a la tentembiri plɔ;
nseŋ shin awɔlpa e buu kumo so nɛ epeŋi e sa maŋ nyaŋɛ.
6Lara loŋ be kanyɛ na ashi kafɛ be nchɛ to,
nsaa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ b karga kumo n ti nchɛ so.
7Sa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ b kurge ebi le be kachɛ fanɛ kede ere,
ŋko n naŋ shin nɛ kusɔ ko e wora nɛ basa e baa wora awɔr
kagbenefuli so loŋ be kanyɛ kikɛ mbaanaayɔ.
8Sa belejipo ekpa nɛ b shoduu loŋ be kachɛ na.
Bumo e naa tiŋ a shin nɛ teku to
be kusɔbɔya gbeyeso gboŋgboŋi na bee nyaŋɛ to.
9Shin nɛ kachɛ na be kachipurso be kechɛkpabi e biri to,
nsaa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ k baa tama karechɛ kikɛ.
10Sho kanyɛ nɛ b kurge ma na kɔnɔ
ŋkpal k ka shin nɛ b kurge n wɔtɔ durnya
nɛ etɔrɔ bɔlɔ kumo to ere so.
11Manɛ nna nɛ n daa maŋ laŋɛ
kachɛ nɛ b kurge ma na bre?
12Manɛ nna nɛ n nio ta ma n deŋi mbe aya so,
nseŋ sa ma mbe kenyipo nɛ n nyipo?
13N daŋ wu n laŋɛ nna,
ndafanɛ n daa beeŋ ya tu
14bewura nɛ benimuana nɛ b wu
nseŋ ka bumo be ewurkpaana nɛ nwugboŋ
nɛ a bure a dese na.
15Ndoŋ nɛ meeŋ ya dese a di fanɛ bewura
nɛ b daŋ gbare eshuwa nɛ egbiti m bɔlɔ nwu,
16ŋko n ya dese nchaŋ to fanɛ kebia
nɛ b kurge nɛ e laŋɛ nsaa
maŋ wu kananɛ karechɛ du na.
17Basa lubi maŋ naa tiŋ a wora asheŋ lubi nchaŋ to,
basa nɛ b shuŋ ŋ gben malɛ bee nya a wushi ndoŋ nna.
18Basa nɛ b daŋ ti ebu gba bee nya kayurwushi nna,
b maŋ naa nu basa nɛ baa keni bumo so na be kaponte
ŋko a wu bumo be kamɛaŋ.
19Basa nɛ b kɔ atre nɛ bebɔlpo kikɛ wɔ ndoŋ nna.
Anya gba nya bumo be amu ndoŋ.
20Manɛ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ n wɔ ŋkpa to,
saŋɛ nɛ kebaawɔtɔ du kekekra le ere?
21Ma ere bee sha luwu ga
a chɔ keta kenishipere n fin
yawu kpakpaso be asɔ,
ama luwu malɛ maa ba.
22Shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n fuli ma kagbene
a chɔ kewu n yɔ nchaŋ to.
23Manɛ nna nɛ ŋ kraa wɔ ŋkpa to,
jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ nawule nyi kananɛ
ma kebaawɔtɔ beeŋ baa du echefoso?
24Ma keji nɛ kenuu e ki
ebɔl to nɛ kagbene to be kushu na.
25Asheŋ nɛ mee ŋana ga na
kikɛ e ki kashenteŋ na.
26M maŋ kɔ kagbenewushi
ŋko ewushi kikɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ to,
she etɔrɔ nɛ kagbenekuu damta nawule.

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Ɛlifaz ka juŋkpar m malga be asheŋ
(4:1—14:22)
Ɛlifaz
1Job mo nekpa Ɛlifaz, nɛ e shi
Tɛman be kadegboŋ to na e juŋkpar ŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Job, jande nya kanyiti n sa ma
nseŋ nu kusɔ nɛ mee sha kekaŋɛ ere.
3-4Nyiŋi kananɛ fo mmalga daŋ leŋ basa damta
nɛ asheŋ daŋ tir bumo na to,
a ŋini bumo kananɛ baaŋ baa wora asheŋ na.
5Ama naniere kufugboŋ tɔr fo so
nɛ fo gbagba bee kule a fin luwu
ŋkpal etɔrɔ ka ba fo so na so.
6Fo la esa nɛ e bee shuŋ Ebɔrɛ
a wɔ kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso to nna,
amoso nya kagbene nsaa maŋ paŋ tama!
7Fo daŋ nu fanɛ esa nɛ e niŋi kebaawɔtɔ to
daŋ ji awurfoŋ pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu a?
8Kusɔ nɛ ma ere nyi e la fanɛ
basa nɛ baa du kulubi
bumo be amu to nɛ k bee kɔr.
9Kananɛ bɔrɛfu bee jija asɔ na,
aloŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee nya agbo a mur bumo.
10Kumu kpakpaso wuraana
bee kaa ponte to fanɛ ebuluŋ nna,
ama Ebɔrɛ e naa buri bumo be anyii
nɛ bumo be nnɔ bee lo.
11Kananɛ ebuluŋ maa nya shɛŋ
a pɛ a ji nsaa wu na,
aloŋ nɛ bumo alɛ gba beeŋ wu
ŋ ka bumo be mbia nɛ b pesaŋ to.
12Esa ko daŋ kuli ŋ kaŋɛ ma ashiri ko;
e daa maŋ malga kumo awɔrso.
13N daa maŋ tiŋ n di kamɔnchɛ be kanyɛso;
ŋkpal edare bubɔrɔ nɛ n daa ku so.
14Kufu daŋ pɛ ma hale nɛ n daa chicha.
15Kebuniyoyu ko e daŋ lar ma so
nɛ kufu pɛ ma ga hale nɛ awo bibi dii ma.
16Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebuniyoyu na pɛ afu n yili diim, a maŋ naa gbegber to
nɛ m pɛshɛ kumo lee, ma alɛ maŋ pin kusɔ nɛ k la.
Kumo be kaman nɛ n nu ebɔl ko ka kaŋɛ le:
17‘Edimɛdi kikɛ maŋ niŋi Ebɔrɛ
nɛ e to bumo na be anishito.
18Ebɔrɛ maa yirda mbe emalaika
nɛ baa shuŋ mo ebɔrɛso na gba.
19Edimɛdi nɛ b maa chɛr nsaa wu fanɛ
kananɛ kapuya maa chɛr nsaa bure na nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n yirda a?
20Esa beeŋ tiŋ a wɔ ŋkpa to kachipurso,
ama ta a ba kaaseso nɛ e wu n choŋ
nɛ esa kama maŋ nyi gba.
21Dimɛdi be ŋkpa maa chɛr kelar mo to,
Ebɔrɛ baŋ lara efute na, epul to nɛ e wu,
nɛ k daa maŋ daga fanɛ e wu.’ ”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1“Job, shu n fin kechɛto ŋ keni a,
malaika ko beeŋ ba chɛ fo to a?
2Kayurbesa nɛ kukɔrkɔ
e naŋ mɔ ewulpo nɛ e maŋ nyi asheŋ.
3N wu bewulpo ka yili to nɛnɛ kebaawɔtɔ to,
ama kɔnɔsho ka ba bumo nɛ bumo be
laŋ to ebi so nɛ asheŋ bri bumo.
4Bumo be mbia maŋ nya esa nɛ e beeŋ kuŋ bumo;
esa malɛ kikɛ maŋ yili bumo be kaman ashi demujikpa.
5Kumo be kaman nɛ kejimuni wuraana nɛ
basa nɛ akoŋ kɔ ba fuu bumo be adɔjibi
nseŋ gbare bumo be mpetɛsɔ ŋ ki bumo peya.
6Awurfoŋ nɛ anyee ji maa shi
anyi be adɔjibi ka maa wora to.
7Ayai! Edimɛdi gbagba e naa
fin asheŋ a sa bumo be amu;
fanɛ kananɛ ajanwulɛ bee pante edɛ na.
8Job, nɛ ma e daa la fo,
meeŋ ta ma asheŋ m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ
nɛ e chɛ ma to.
9Anyi maaŋ tiŋ m pin asheŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee wora to.
Mo alɛ be emamachisheŋ maŋ kɔ ekar.
10Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba
nɛ adɔsawule bee nya kayul.
11Ebɔrɛ e naa maŋ bebɔlpo so,
nsaa sa basa nɛ baa shu nli kagbenewushi.
12-13Mo e naa melgi basa nɛ b nyi asheŋ ga be ŋkre a buu,
nsaa bɔla benyiashempo be kanyiasheŋ so a pɛ bumo;
saŋɛ na so kusɔ kama nɛ baa wora maa nyalɛ a sa bumo.
14Hale kapiidi gba baa nite nna
a la a la a fin ekpa
fanɛ b ka na tentembiri to na.
15Ama Ebɔrɛ e naa mɔlga basa nɛ asheŋ tir na
ashi kumukpakpaso wuraana be nnɔ to be mmalga
nɛ belempo be eleŋ to
nɛ belempo be kɔrfɛ to.
16Mo e naa sa betirpo tama a shin nɛ
kemaa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so bee ba ekar.
17Kagbenefuli la esa kama nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ
bee niŋi ekpa na peya nna.
Amoso sa maŋ kaŋ keni mbe kefiɛso jiga.
18E beeŋ tiŋ m bar doro nɛ ebesa fo so,
ama mo alɛ beeŋ naŋ chɔɔ fo achuu
nɛ alɔbi na kikɛ n chɛ amo.
19Saŋɛ kikɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ baa lara fo ashi etɔrɔ damta
nɛ a bee bar fo kagbenejija ga ere kikɛ to.
20Ebɔrɛ e naŋ kuŋ fo ashi luwu to jemanɛ kikɛ;
akoŋgboŋ nɛ kena be jemanɛ gba, fo maaŋ wu.
21Mo e naŋ kuŋ fo ashi basa nɛ baa jija fo kutɔ,
nseŋ mɔlga fo ashi kemur kama nɛ k bee ba fo so to.
22Kemur nɛ akoŋgboŋ
be asheŋ maaŋ tir fo ere.
Fo alɛ maaŋ naa ŋana kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi.
23Fo kudɔsawule maaŋ baa kɔ ajembu nɛ afalta;
kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi malɛ maaŋ pɛ fo.
24Feeŋ chena fo laŋ to nɛ kagbenewushi,
nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ wora fo asɔ nɛ fo kɔ.
25Fo kamanebi beeŋ baa shi
a chɔ afitiri nɛ e wɔ durnya kikɛ to.
26Fo ŋkpa beeŋ teŋi so nɛ fo chɛr,
fo alɛ beeŋ baa kɔ eleŋ eyurto
hale n ya fo kachɛ nɛ feeŋ wu.
27Job, an dara asheŋ ere nna nseŋ koya amo n chɛr.
A la kashenteŋ nna, amoso ta amo n shuŋ fo kebaawɔtɔ to.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Ɛlifaz be kamalga to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job tuge Ɛlifaz
be kamalga na to nseŋ kaŋɛ le:
2“K beeŋ baa du kpakpa ga nɛ esa e tiŋ m
pin awurfoŋ nɛ keboltofinfiŋ damta
nɛ a tu ma ere to.
3A shi a chɔ teku ase be shishɛr;
amoso nɛ n daa maŋ fɛ nfɛra pɔɛŋ nseŋ malga na.
4K du fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na ka to
atanyembi nna nɛ amo be kebɔr luri ma eyur to.
Ebɔrɛ ta kufugboŋ nna n lɛ ma so.
5Kurma baŋ nya afitiri a ji,
kumo be kenishi bee bɔlɔ nna.
Kena malɛ gba baŋ nya afitiri wɔlso a we,
k maŋ naa shu.
6Esa bee tiŋ n ji ajibi tataso nɛ nfɔl maŋ wɔ amo to a?
Ŋko ebel mo e wɔ kefule be kefuful na to?
7Kananɛ ma ajibi du nna, e maŋ wɔ ebel.
A maa yɛlga ma gba kuraa.
8-9Ebɔrɛ daŋ nu ma kabɔrɛkule
nseŋ mɔ ma nɛ n wushi
kedaa beeŋ par ma.
10Nɛ e daa beeŋ wora loŋ nna,
ebesa nɛ mee ji ere kikɛ be kaman
n daa beeŋ baa tɛto kagbenefuliso
N nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ du cheembi nna;
ma alɛ maŋ naŋ wora mo kusoe kpakpaso kikɛ.
11Nuso be eleŋ e kraa wɔ ma to,
nɛ a daga fanɛ m baa kraa kɔ tama?
Manɛ bre nɛ men naŋ nya echefoso,
nɛ a daga fanɛ m baa kraa wora kanyiti?
12M maŋ kɔ eleŋ fanɛ kejembu ŋko danyaŋ peper.
13M maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ kikɛ nɛ m mɔlga ma kumu;
kaplɛkama maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ n yɔ n ya nya kechɛto.
14Esa kama nɛ e wɔ le be awurfoŋ to,
hale nɛ e maŋ naa kɔ kabɔrɛŋana
n sa Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ gba;
a daga mo nekpaana ka yili
mbe kaman nna a leŋ mo to.
15Ama menyi nɛ men la n nekpaana ere
bee fule ma nna nsaa du fanɛ mbombi nɛ bɔrɛ
baŋ yili gbrɛbi kikɛ nɛ e wɔlto na.
M maaŋ tiŋ n ta ma egbɛ n lɛ menyi so.
16Eshishɛr bee ti loŋ be mbombi na nna
nɛ amo be nchu maa shibi,
17ketar baŋ wurge nɛ a maaŋ naa kɔ nchu a shile,
nɛ epeŋi malɛ baŋ ber amo so nɛ nchu na feeto.
18Eyawujipo nɛ baa dii enyɔma
baaŋ ta tama n bɛ mbombi ere so,
a fin nchu nɛ b nuu baa foe nna
n ya wu n tɔr keshishɛrsawule so m mur.
19Tɛma be kadegboŋ nɛ Sheba be efuliana so
be eyawujipo nɛ b dii enyɔma
bee kaa bɛ amo so nna a fin nchu nɛ b nuu,
20ama mbombi wɔlso nɛ baa tu,
nɛ bumo be tama a loge nɛ aba e pɔ bumo.
21Menyi alɛ gba du fanɛ
loŋ be mbombi na nna na.
Men ka ba wu awurfoŋ nɛ mee ji na,
nɛ kufu pɛ menyi nɛ menyee fɛ keyige ma n lɛ.
22M maŋ daŋ kule menyi be ekama
fanɛ e sa ma kakɛ kikɛ
23ŋko ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e ka amansherbi
n sa bedoŋ nɛ b ta ma n lɛ.
24To, men ŋini ma kulubi nɛ n wora.
Meeŋ lo ma kɔnɔ to nseŋ nu menyi kutɔ.
25Kashenteŋ bee besa jemanɛ kikɛ nna,
ama kusɔ nɛ menyee kaŋɛ ere maa ŋini shɛŋ.
26Naniere ma kenishi pere nna na,
ama menyee ta ma mmalga fanɛ afu fuloŋ nna.
27Menyi ere beeŋ tiŋ m barga amunibi to n sa abar
ŋko n fa men nekpaana gba n nya amansherbi!
28Men keni ma anishito nɛnɛ,
m maaŋ fule ŋko ŋ ku efɛ n sa menyi.
29Men yige kebaakuu ma kɔnɔ,
nɛ manɛ aloŋ, ma ketre beeŋ jija.
30N nyi kulubi nɛ kelela be mbarga,
m maa ku efɛ nna.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
Manɛ so nɛ kebaawɔtɔ du kpakpa loŋ
1Manɛ nna nɛ kebaawɔtɔ du kpakpa loŋ?
Manɛ nna nɛ anyee ji awurfoŋ loŋ?
2An du fanɛ anya nɛ baa fin kiyoyul
nɛ b chena to n wushi nna;
An la beshumpo nɛ anyee jo
anyi be kakɔka kenishipereso nna.
3Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ ma nchɛ maŋ naa kɔ tɔnɔ n sa ma
nɛ kanyɛso bar ma keboltofinfiŋ damta.
4M baŋ dese kanyɛso kikɛ, mee
kilgi kelaŋ so nna a kule Ebɔrɛ
fanɛ kare e chɛ manaŋ,
ama kumo alɛ maa chɛ manaŋ.
5Achuu nɛ e bee lar nchu nɛ ashushombi
e sɔ ma eyur kikɛ so,
abibi sɔ ma eyur kikɛ nna.
6Ma nchɛ bee duga so manaŋ manaŋ
a chɔ kɔrɛ be kekpaltobi be jese.
7Ebɔrɛ, mee kule fo nna;
sa maŋ teŋ ma so!
Ma ŋkpa baa du fanɛ afu nna,
ma kagbenefuli teŋ fo ekar.
8Anishi nɛ a bee wu ma kabre ere
maaŋ naŋ wu ma kikɛ;
Menyeeŋ keni n fin ma,
ama m maaŋ naa wɔtɔ.
9Kananɛ abɔrɛwɔlpa bee deŋi nsaa choŋ na,
a loŋ nɛ basa bee wu nsaa maŋ naa bɛta a ba.
10Ma alɛ gba maaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba epe,
k maaŋ chɛr basa beeŋ teŋ ma so.
11Amoso m maaŋ tiŋ n lo ma kɔnɔ.
Kagbenejija nɛ ebesa damta to
nɛ mee fubel a bile asheŋ na.
12M maŋ la teku ŋko kusɔ gbeyeso gboŋ
nɛ k wɔ teku chiŋgeliŋ to
nɛ fo ti ma n wɔtɔ a kuŋ ma.
13M baŋ yɔ kelaŋ so,
nsaa tama fanɛ ma ebesa beeŋ ku
14fee ta edare lubi nna a tɔrɔ ma
nɛ kufu bee pɛ ma ga
15hale nɛ mee yɛlga fanɛ
b nyaŋ ma ebɔl to m mɔ gba k bɔ ma so
a chɔ ŋ ka wɔ ŋkpa to.
16Ma ere maŋ naŋ ta ma ŋkpa n tre shɛŋ.
