Kebaawɔtɔ fi ma! Yige ma asheŋ!
Ma kebaawɔtɔ maŋ naa kɔ tɔnɔ n sa ma.
17Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, manɛ nna nɛ dimɛdi be asheŋ tir fo ga
nɛ fo lakal baa wɔ mbe asheŋ woraso so ere?
18Manɛ nna nɛ fee keni dimɛdi
be asheŋ to saŋkikɛ nsaa wora mo a keni
kachipurso nɛ kapaso nɛ kanyɛso ere bre?
19Ama fo maaŋ naŋ kpele fo anishi ma so
nɛ n nya m min echɔl gba a?
20Hale nɛ n wora kulubi gba,
kumo be nnɛ e nya fo?
Manɛ nna nɛ fo lara kenishi n yuu ma loŋ?
Ma asheŋ bee tɔrɔ fo nna a?
21Manɛ nna nɛ fo maŋ tiŋ n ta ma lubi m paŋ ma?
M maaŋ naŋ chɛr nseŋ yɔ eshishɛr to n ya dese.
Fo alɛ beeŋ keni n fin ma, nɛ fo maaŋ wu ma.

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Job mo nekpa Bildad be sososo be kamalga be asheŋ
Bildad
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Bildad nɛ e shi Shuuwa be efuli so na kaŋɛ:
2“Jemanɛ mo nɛ feeŋ yige fo mmalga fuloŋ
nɛ e maŋ kɔ kifi to ere be kebaamalga?
3Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na maa ji esa durmu,
mo alɛ maa wora kusɔ nɛ k maŋ daga.
4Ashere fo mbia na wora n da Ebɔrɛ so nna,
amoso nɛ e gberge bumo kusoe nɛ k daga bumo na.
5Ama nɛ fanɛ fo bɛta n yɔ Ebɔrɛ kutɔ,
nseŋ ya kule Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na;
6ŋko nɛ fanɛ fo la esa nɛ fo niŋi
nɛ kulubi kikɛ maŋ wɔ fo so nna,
kumo ere Ebɔrɛ beeŋ naŋ chɛ fo to
nseŋ shin nɛ fo naŋ nya asɔ nɛ fo paŋ na kikɛ.
7E beeŋ shin nɛ fo echefoso be kebaawɔtɔ
e baa bɔ fo kebaawɔtɔ dra na ga.
8An nanaana daa nyi asheŋ ga,
amoso koya asheŋ bumo kutɔ.
9Anyi maŋ chɛr durnya to, anyi alɛ maŋ nyi shɛŋ.
Anyi maa chɛr kasawule ere so nsaa choŋ fanɛ afu.
10Ama an nanaana na bre beeŋ ŋini fo kasheŋwora,
nɛ fo pin amo to nɛnɛ.
11Agasa maa daŋ a yili kakpa nɛ nchu maŋ wɔ;
amo alɛ maa kɔr kpakpa nɛ k maa petɛ nchu.
12Nɛ fanɛ nchu na malɛ baŋ feeto ndoŋ,
agasa na e naa daŋ afitiri kikɛ kewu.
13Basa nɛ b maŋ nyi Ebɔrɛ du fanɛ agasa nna,
jemanɛ nɛ b maŋ nyi mo na nɛ bumo be tama bee loge.
14Loŋ be basa bee ta bumo be tama a deŋi
kusɔ nɛ k maŋ kɔ eleŋ fanɛ nansa be ketata so nna.
15Nɛ b baŋ ta bumo be egbɛ n lɛ ketata so malɛ,
k maaŋ tiŋ n sɔ bumo to.
16Basa lubi du fanɛ afitiri nɛ a bee nya epeŋi
nɛ bɔrɛchu nɛnɛ nna;
a bee daŋ nɛnɛ nna nɛ amo be nliŋi bee yɔ kufɔ
n sɔ kudɔbi na kikɛ to.
17Loŋ be afitiri na be nliŋi bee luri ajembu to nna
a nya a mur achin a yili nɛnɛ.
18Ama nɛ esa baŋ gberge afitiri na n tia,
b maaŋ naŋ pin fanɛ afitiri daŋ yili ndoŋ ŋ ku so gba.
19Kashenteŋto, kebaawɔtɔ nɛ basa lubi kɔ kikɛ e baa la na.
B maa chɛr nɛ basa ko ba sɔ bumo be kakpa a wɔtɔ.
20An nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ maa kini
esa nɛ basa maa wu kulubi mo so a lɛ,
mo alɛ maa chɛ alubiworapo to.
21Amoso, e beeŋ naŋ shin nɛ fo kagbene e fuli
nɛ fo mushe awɔrso nɛ basa e nu fo asheŋ.
22Ama e beeŋ shin nɛ fo doŋana bre e ji anishinyɔr
nseŋ mur gba kuraa nɛ esa maaŋ naŋ wu bumo kikɛ
hale mbaanaayɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Bildad be kamalga to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ:
2“Kashenteŋ nɛ fo ji.
Dimɛdi kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n ji n lar
Ebɔrɛ be anishito.
3Nɛ anyi nɛ Ebɔrɛ yɔ demujikpa ale kagboŋ gba,
anyi maaŋ tiŋ n ya ji m bri mo.
4Ebɔrɛ nyi asheŋ nsaa kɔ eleŋ ga,
esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n tu mo n ji emɔrɔ m pɔɔ so.
5Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ nya agbo,
e beeŋ tiŋ m pulgi abee nseŋ melgi amo m buu,
nɛ k purgi basa.
6Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ kasawule
nɛ kumo be gbaltɔlase kikɛ a gbuŋgbuŋ to.
7E beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ epeŋi nɛ achɛkpabi
e biri to nɛ kakpa e fuli to ŋ gben.
8Ebɔrɛ nawule e to kuwɔlpa m parga kumo to n sɔ kaplɛkama,
mo alɛ e naa ji teku nɛ kumo to be asɔ kikɛ so eleŋ.
9Ebɔrɛ koŋwule na e to achɛkpabi be yiri yiri awɔlpa to,
Mo e to achɛkpabi nɛ baa tre Shishirigboŋ na nɛ koshi nɛ mbe bibi
nɛ achɛkpabi nɛ a wɔ awɔlpa to be kelargato be kaseto na kikɛ.
10Anyi maaŋ tiŋ m pin Ebɔrɛ be emamachisheŋ
nɛ e bee wora na be kukoŋwule gba to kikɛ.
11Ebɔrɛ baŋ bɔla ma ase a choŋ gba,
m maaŋ wu mo ŋko m pin mbe asheŋ.
12E baŋ ta kusɔ, esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kuŋ mo akpa.
Esa malɛ maaŋ tiŋ m bishi mo fanɛ manɛ nɛ fee wora ere?
13Ebɔrɛ be kagbene baŋ kaa,
e bee mur mo doŋana nɛ baa chɛ
kusɔkpaŋ gboŋgboŋi lubi nɛ k wɔ teku to
nɛ baa tre Reehab na to na nna.
14Nɛ nuso nɛ ma alɛ le beeŋ tiŋ
n ji Ebɔrɛ emɔrɔ ashi ma demu ere to?
15Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ m maŋ wora shɛŋ,
ama kusɔ nɛ meeŋ tiŋ n wora kikɛ e la
kekule Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma demujipo na,
nɛ e wu ma kuwɔr.
16Hale nɛ e sa ma ekpa nɛ m malga gba a,
m maŋ yirda fanɛ e beeŋ nu n sa ma.
17E beeŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ e doro ma n ti so,
nɛ m maŋ wora shɛŋ.
18Pɔɛŋ nɛ meeŋ nya n fute n wushi gba na,
e beeŋ shin nɛ ma awurfoŋ e ti so.
19Nɛ kela fanɛ eleŋ nna, Ebɔrɛ kɔ eleŋ a chɔ ma!
Nɛ kela asheŋ be keji malɛ gba nna,
wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n tre Ebɔrɛ demujikpa?
20Nɛ fanɛ m maŋ wora n da so gba,
ma kɔnɔ to be mmalga beeŋ ji m biri ma.
21Hale esa kikɛ maŋ wu kulubi ma so gba,
ama kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ wora ma
be asheŋ maŋ naa tir ma.
22Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ bee mur basa nɛ b wora n da so
nɛ bumo nɛ b maŋ wora n da so kikɛ nna.
23Nɛ esa lela baŋ wu luwu purgiase gba,
Ebɔrɛ bee chena nna a mushe.
24Ebɔrɛ e sa basa lubi ekpa,
nɛ b sɔ durnya m pugi so;
nseŋ tan demujipoana malɛ.
Nɛ mannɛ Ebɔrɛ e wora loŋ, wanɛ e wora loŋ?
25K du fanɛ ma nchɛ bee choŋ manaŋ manaŋ nna,
nɛ m maŋ naa tama kagbenefuli kikɛ kuraa.
26Ma ŋkpa bee choŋ manaŋ manaŋ nna fanɛ afu na,
k bee yɔ manaŋ manaŋ a chɔ
kusore ka gbelge to n fuu kusɔ gba.
27Jemanɛ ko mee wora ania
fanɛ meeŋ baa leŋ ma kumu to
nseŋ yige kebaamuni to a fubel nna,
28ama ma awurfoŋana na bee da ma kufu nna.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, n nyi Ebɔrɛ ka kraa wu ma fanɛ
esa nɛ e wora n da so nna.
29Nɛ e kraa wu ma fanɛ esa nɛ e wora n da so bre,
manɛ nna nɛ n naa tɔrɔ ma kumu a fin keji n lar?
30Kɔya be yiri kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ
nɛ n tiŋ n ta n fɔr so n nyalɛ so.
31Ebɔrɛ ta ma n lɛ kemaŋ dufɛso to nna,
hale ma asheŋ bee keta
ma asɔbuuso gba nyɔmɔ.
32Ebɔrɛ maŋ la dimɛdi bomin fanɛ ma.
M maaŋ tiŋ n tre mo nɛ e ba demujikpa
nɛ an ji asheŋ.
33Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e tiŋ n ji ma nɛ Ebɔrɛ
be kefɛato be asheŋ ere.
34Esa ko maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e tiŋ n sɔ kedibi
nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a funti ma ere mbe enɔ.
35Esa daa wɔtɔ nɛ e wora loŋ nna,
n daa beeŋ malga n wushi ashi Ebɔrɛ be anishito
nɛ kufu maŋ kɔ ma.
Ama kananɛ asheŋ du naniere,
m maaŋ tiŋ m malga n wushi.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
Job ka fubel ŋ ŋini Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ
1Kebaawɔtɔ lar ma ebɔl!
O Ebɔrɛ, nya asoe n nu ma
kenishipere be nfubel ere.
2O Ebɔrɛ, sa maŋ kaŋ ji m bri ma loŋ!
Manɛ be demu nɛ ma nɛ fo kɔ
nɛ an ji ashi demujikpa?
3Manɛ nna nɛ fo kekini ma n lɛ par fo,
nɛ fo maa wora shɛŋ a laŋɛ basa
lubi be ŋkre bre be kaplɛa so?
4Kananɛ anyi edimɛdi bee keni nsaa wora asheŋ na
nɛ fo, Ebɔrɛ gba bee keni nsaa wora asheŋ a?
5Fo alɛ gba be ŋkpa maŋ wɔ nteŋ
fanɛ anyeya nna a?
6Ama amoso nɛ fee nya manaŋ
a mige to a fin kewu ma kulubi ere a?
7Fo nyi ŋ ka maŋ wora n jija,
ama wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ m malga
ŋ kuŋ ma fo kutɔ?
8Fo gbagba be enɔana nɛ fo ta m pɔr ma.
Ama naniere feeŋ shuli m mur ma a?
9Baa nyiŋi fanɛ fo e pɔr ma
fanɛ kananɛ baa ta ebɔ a pɔr asɔ na.
Amoso sa maŋ naŋ kilgi ma eshishɛr a!
10Fo e wɔtɔ n tuto eleŋ nɛ e tiŋ n di n nio kedampo,
nseŋ shin nɛ n tiŋ n daŋ n nio be epun to.
11Fo e bela ma awibi n chuge abar so
nseŋ wora eblaŋ nɛ kawɔl m buu awibi na so.
12Fo e sa ma ŋkpa nseŋ ŋini
ma fo kasha nɛ k maa loge na.
Fo e naa keni ma so
nɛ n wɔ ŋkpa to na.
13Ama kusɔ nɛ fo ta ŋ ŋana fo kagbene to nde,
ma alɛ nyi k kaa wɔ fo nfɛra to.
14Kumo e la fanɛ, fee keni nna a fin ma kulubi,
saŋɛ na so nɛ fo gberge ma kusoe ŋkpal kumo so.
15M baŋ wora kulubi, mee nya asheŋ fo kutɔ nna,
ama nɛ m baŋ wora kelela bre, m maa nya mbo.
Naniere ma kagbene jija ma ga nɛ anishinyɔr pɛ ma.
16Kanaŋ kama nɛ m pere kenishi n wora asheŋ gba,
fo kraa pete ma nna fanɛ kananɛ ekpampo bee pete buluŋ na,
saŋɛ na so feeŋ ŋini ma fo mamachi be yuku na.
17Jemanɛ kikɛ fee wu ma kulubi nna.
Fo agbo bee wora keshi ma so nna a ti so
nɛ jemanɛ kikɛ fo alɛ bee fin ekpa popɔr
nɛ feeŋ bɔla so ŋ kɔ ma.
18Ebɔrɛ, manɛ nna nɛ fo shin nɛ b kurge ma bre?
A daŋ daga ŋ ka laŋɛ kachɛ nɛ b kurge ma na nna.
19Keshi n nio be epun to n yɔ nchaŋ to
daa beeŋ baa bɔ ma so a chɔ ŋ kaa wɔ ŋkpa to ere.
20Ma nchɛ maŋ naa shi durnya to.
Yige ma nɛ n ji ma kumu gbrɛbi.
21-22K maaŋ chɛr ko nɛ n wu n yɔ
nsaa maŋ naŋ bɛta m ba.
Mee yɔ kakpa nɛ tentembiri plɔ wɔ nna,
kakpa nɛ tama kikɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ n esa na.
Ndoŋ be kefulto e du fanɛ tentembiri na.

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofa be sososo be kamalga be asheŋ
Zofa
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Zofa
nɛ e shi Neeman be efuli so na kaŋɛ le:
2“Esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kplaŋ le be kawuli
be mmalga damta ere so
nɛ e maŋ nya kusɔ ko ŋ kaŋɛ.
3Job, fee fɛ fanɛ anyi maaŋ tiŋ
n tuge fo mmalga ere to nna a?
Esa wɔtɔ nɛ e fɛa fo so ŋkpal fo
mmalga jiga ere so!
4Fee ta fo kumu fanɛ fo maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ
nsaa ji emɔrɔ a kaŋɛ fanɛ fo ere be
asheŋ woraso kikɛ bee par Ebɔrɛ nna.
5Aloko Ebɔrɛ daa beeŋ tuge fo nna!
6E daa beeŋ shin nɛ fo pin
kakpa nɛ kanyiasheŋ shi.
Asheŋ ko du chiŋgeliŋ nna n sa dimɛdi
nɛ e tiŋ m pin amo to.
Fo alɛ daa beeŋ naŋ pin fanɛ
kasogberge nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa fo na
maŋ fo kumo nɛ k daga fo na so.
7Feeŋ tiŋ m pin Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ
be keshi nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ to a?
8Mbe keshi nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ awɔlpa so,
nɛ fo maaŋ tiŋ n fo amo.
Amo alɛ naa du chiŋgeliŋ a chɔ nchaŋ
Mo alɛ naa nyi kusɔ nɛ k bee wora bubuni to
nɛ fo maŋ nyi kumo kikɛ kuraa.
9Mbe keshi nɛ eleŋgboŋ wɔ mpar a chɔ
kasawule nɛ etekuana kikɛ.
10Nɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ ti fo ebu
ŋko n yɛr fo demujikpa,
manɛ nɛ feeŋ tiŋ n wora mo?
11Ebɔrɛ nyi basa nɛ b du jiga,
mo alɛ nsaa wu bumo be asheŋ lubi kikɛ.
12Keshin nɛ ewulpo e pin asheŋ du kpakpa a chɔ
keshin nɛ kurma kpeŋso e nu n sa esa.
13Job, yili fo kagbene kukoŋwule n sa Ebɔrɛ,
nseŋ bɛta n yɔ mo kutɔ kabɔrɛkule to.
14Tuba n lara kulubi ashi fo laŋ to,
hale amo nɛ fo wora ashiri to na gba.
15Nɛ fo wora loŋ, fo maŋ naŋ ji anishinyɔr
fo alɛ beeŋ nya kenyɛn a maaŋ naa wɔ
kufu be kebaawɔtɔ to.
16Kumo be kaman nɛ fo etɔrɔbi ere
kikɛ be asheŋ e lar fo nfɛra to
fanɛ nchu ka bɔla kuturko to n choŋ na.
17Kebaawɔtɔ beeŋ fulto parr a chɔ kapiidi
nɛ tentembiri malɛ e ki fanɛ kachipurso n sa fo.
18Sheŋ maa naa tɔrɔ fo ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to,
Ebɔrɛ beeŋ sa fo tama nɛ fo maŋ naa wɔ kafɔŋ to.
19Fo maaŋ naa ŋana fo doŋana.
Basa damta malɛ beeŋ baa fin kechɛto fo kutɔ.
20Ama basa lubi bre beeŋ paŋ tama nseŋ fo akpa.
Bumo be tama kikɛ beeŋ baa la luwu nna.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Zofa be kamalga to be asheŋ
Job
1-2Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ mo nekpaana na le:
“Menyee fɛ fanɛ men la basa kre anishi ko nna
ashi menyi be atuwebi nɛ men sa ma na to.
3Ama kusɔ nɛ men nyi na nɛ ma alɛ gba nyi,
kumo koŋwule na nɛ ekama gba nyi.
4Jemanɛ kikɛ kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso to nɛ n daa wɔ,
nɛ Ebɔrɛ malɛ daa nu ma kabɔrɛkule.
Ama naniere n nekpaana e naa wora ma eyur to na.
5Nɛ esa baa maŋ wɔ etɔrɔ kikɛ to,
k maŋ du kpakpa n sa mo nɛ kemalga ŋ gbiti
esa nɛ e bee ji awurfoŋ.
6Beyu nɛ basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ
wɔ kayurwushi to nna,
ama kusɔ koŋwule nɛ b yirda
e la eleŋ nɛ b kɔ na.
7Menyi beeŋ tiŋ ŋ koya asɔ damta
ashi mbuibi nɛ asɔbɔya kutɔ.
8Menyi alɛ beeŋ naŋ tiŋ ŋ kule kanyiasheŋ ashi
kasawule so nɛ nchu to be asɔ keniso kutɔ.
9Amo be kekama beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi
kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wora.
10Kusɔ futeso kikɛ be ŋkpa bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nna.
11Men nyi fanɛ asoe nɛ an kɔ a nu mmalga
nsaa kɔ adonduloŋ malɛ a nu ajibi be ebel.
12-13Basakpar kutɔ nɛ anyee koya kanyiasheŋ.
Ama Ebɔrɛ bre kɔ kanyiasheŋ nɛ yuku kikɛ nna.
Basakpar beeŋ tiŋ m pin asheŋ to
ama Ebɔrɛ bre bee pin asheŋ to
nseŋ naa kɔ yuku nɛ e wora amo.
14Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n lɔŋɛ kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ jija,
ŋko n lara basa nɛ e ti ebu ashi kabuti na to.
15Ebɔrɛ e naa pɛ bɔrɛ nɛ ewule bee yili,
mo alɛ naŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ ba ga,
nchu bee sɔ kaplɛkama nna n jija kasawule.
16Jemanɛ kikɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ eleŋ a tiŋ a kɔ a pɔɔ so nna.
Befɛpo nɛ basa nɛ baa fule kikɛ wɔ mbe eleŋ be kaseto to nna.
17Mo e naa suge bewura be kanyiasheŋ,
nsaa shin nɛ bejuŋkparpo bee wora asheŋ fanɛ bewulpo.
18Mo e naa gboŋi bewura kuwura to
nsaa shin nɛ baa nya efɔl a wɔtɔ bumo be nshɛr to
a gberge bumo a yɔ fanɛ anya na.
19Ebɔrɛ e naa lara bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ basa
nɛ b ji eleŋ ga n chɛr na ashi bumo be eyilikpa.
20Mo e naa shin nɛ basa nɛ ekama yirda
be nnɔ bee mɔ bumo,
nsaa suge basakpar be kanyiasheŋ.
21Mo e naa shin nɛ bewurgboŋ bee ji anishinyɔr,
nsaa shin nɛ bumo be yuku bee ba ekar.
22Ebɔrɛ e naa shin nɛ tentembiri bee ki kefulto.
23Mo e naa shin nɛ efuli bee ki efuligboŋ nsaa nya eleŋ,
kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ pɔ amo so m mur amo na.
24Mo e naa shin nɛ efuliana na bewuraana bee ki bewulpo,
nsaa mel to a nite keshishɛrsawule nɛ akpaana maŋ wɔ so na.
25Bewuraana na bee la tentembiri to nna
a nite a jante fanɛ b ka nuu nsa m boo na.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1“N nyi asheŋ nɛ menyee malga ere kikɛ,
ma alɛ pin amo be kekama to.
2Menyi be ekama maŋ kɔ kenyi a chɔ ma.
Menyi alɛ maŋ nyi kusɔ ko nɛ m maŋ nyi kumo.
3Ama Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na
nɛ mee sha nɛ n tu n ji kusɔ nɛ k tu ma ere,
mannɛ menyi.
4Efɛ nawule nɛ menyi ere bee ku a deŋi ma.
Men du fanɛ bechɛpo nɛ b maŋ nyi shɛŋ nna.
5Kanyiasheŋ be kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n wora kikɛ
e la kelo menyi be nnɔ to n chena.
6Men lo to a keni ma nɛ ŋ gbagba a ji ma asheŋ.
7Mmalga nɛ menyee ta a wɔtɔ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ to
8jemanɛ nɛ men sɔ mo so a malga,
nsaa maa ji kashenteŋ na.
9Nɛ Ebɔrɛ mige menyi to ŋ keni
asheŋ beeŋ nyalɛ n sa menyi a?
Menyee tama fanɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n fule Ebɔrɛ
fanɛ kananɛ menyee fule basa na a?
10Nɛ menyi maŋ ji kashenteŋ ashiri to gba,
e beeŋ fɛa menyi so n niŋi menyi asheŋ,
11nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ na e shin nɛ kufugboŋ
e tɔr menyi so nɛ men baa chicha.
12Menyi be aŋasa nɛ menyee bɔ
nɛ emɔrɔ nɛ menyee ji na kikɛ
du fanɛ kalabɛr nɛ afu bee ber a yɔ nna.
13Men lo menyi be nnɔ nseŋ sa ma ekpa nɛ m malga,
kumo be kaman pɔɛŋ nɛ menyi alɛ e malga.
14Kusɔ kama nɛ k nya ma
shi ŋ gbagba be kumu to nna.
15Hale nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha kemɔ ma gba,
ŋ kraa beeŋ yirda mo.
16Kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ mɔlga ma nna na,
ŋkpal manɛ so, esa nɛ e wora n jija kikɛ
maaŋ shuli m ba Ebɔrɛ be anishito nɛ e ji mo demu.
17Men kaŋ asoe n nu ma mmalga nɛnɛ!
18M bela ma demu na ase nɛnɛ nna,
ma alɛ baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ meeŋ ji n lar kumo to.
19Nɛ fo, Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora n jija,
kumo ere meeŋ lo ma kɔnɔ nseŋ wu nɛ k loge.
20Ma Ebɔrɛ, asɔ anyɔ nɛ mee kule fo,
amo be kaman, m maaŋ naaŋ shile ŋ ŋana fo so.
21Amo e la fanɛ yige kebaagberge ma kusoe
nɛ kebaa funti ma nɛ m baa chicha.
22Kumo be kaman nɛ fo semaŋ ma,
nɛ m ba malga n chɛ ma kɔnɔ.
Ŋko fo shin nɛ m malga,
nɛ fo ere e sa ma atuwebi.
23Jande, ŋini ma alubi nɛ n wora,
nɛ m pin amo kikɛ.
24Manɛ nna nɛ fee ŋana ma so
nsaa ta ma fanɛ fo doŋ?
25Kashenteŋto, kebaa funti esa nɛ e maŋ wɔ egbɛ
fanɛ kefantaŋ nɛ afu kɔ a yɔ na e naa par fo a?
26Asheŋ lubi nɛ e maaŋ daga kuraa na,
hale amo nɛ n wora ma kebia to kikɛ
nɛ fo ta a deŋi ma so.
27Fo lara kenishi n yuu ma,
a keni kusɔ kama nɛ mee wora;
hale a karga aya nɛ mee tia kikɛ.
K du nna fanɛ fo ka ta ŋgbɛlɛbi n chɛ ma aya nna.
28Ma eyur baa bɛlge nna ayiyanto
fanɛ kechɛbi nɛ e kaŋkaŋ muu na.”

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1“Dimɛdi be nchɛ maŋ shi durnya to,
amo alɛ nɛ etɔrɔ damta nna.
2Dimɛdi du fanɛ ketoto ŋko kenyɔlɔ nna,
k maa chɛr nɛ k bolo ŋko n wɔl n choŋ.
3Amoso nɛ mee bishi fo, Ebɔrɛ,
fanɛ manɛ nna nɛ fo lara kenishi n yuu ma loŋ
a fin keji ma demu?
4Dimɛdi kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ kulubi
maŋ wɔ mo to.
5Anyi edimɛdi be saŋɛ maŋ shi durnya to,
Fo, Ebɔrɛ na, tea nyi nchɛ nɛ esa beeŋ ji durnya to.
6Manɛ nna nɛ fo maaŋ yige anyi
nɛ an gbagba e fin kagbenefuli n sa anyi be amu,
jemanɛ nɛ an wɔ kegben damta to ere?
7Kedibi nɛ b ku n lɛ gba kraa kɔ tama
fanɛ k beeŋ naŋ purge kachako.
8Kedibi beeŋ tiŋ n wu a yil,
9ama k baŋ nya nchu nɛ k naŋ purge afantaŋ popɔr kaseto.
10Ama anyi edimɛdi kɔr ndibi to,
an baŋ wu asheŋ loge.
11An du fanɛ mbombi nɛ apaana nna,
amo to be nchu baaŋ feeto a bee wɔlto nna.
12Anyi edimɛdi malɛ baaŋ wu,
anyi maaŋ naŋ koso kikɛ,
hale nɛ durnya e fo ekar.
13Jande, Ebɔrɛ, ta ma ŋ ŋana
kasawule be kechimbi to.
Fo agbo kaŋ wushi
nɛ fo nyiŋi n sɔ ma n yige.
14Nɛ esa baŋ wu, e maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m ba ŋkpa to.
Amoso awurfoŋ nɛ mee ji ere kikɛ mee jo ma saŋɛ nna.
15Feeŋ tre ma, nɛ n shuli,
nɛ ma asheŋ a par fo, ma etopo.
16Kumo be kaman nɛ fo baa keni aya nɛ meeŋ baa tia,
ama fo maaŋ baa karga ma alubi a nase.
17Feeŋ ta ma alubi m paŋ ma nseŋ kplaŋ amo so.
Fo alɛ beeŋ kpra ma asheŋ lubi kikɛ n lɛ.
18Kananɛ abee bee buri so a tɔr
nɛ afalta bee bure to
19nɛ nchu bee fɔr ajembu so nsaa sulɔ eshishɛr a yɔ na,
aloŋ nɛ fee shin nɛ edimɛdi be tama bee mur!
20Fo, e naa shin nɛ anyee bel a chɛrga anishiakpa;
kumo be kaman nɛ an wu n choŋ
nsaa maaŋ naa wɔtɔ hale mbaanaayɔ.
21Anyi maa chena a chɛr a wu anyi be mbia
ka nya kemaŋkura ŋko ka ji anishinyɔr ashi kebaawɔtɔ to.
22Anyi maŋ naa nu ebesa kikɛ
n naŋ ti an gbagba peya so;
anyi alɛ maa shu esa kikɛ be keeli,
ama an gbagba peya.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Kusɔ nɛ Ɛlifaz kaŋɛ be asheŋ
Ɛlifaz
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Ɛlifaz
nɛ e shi kade nɛ baa tre Teman na kaŋɛ le:
2-3“Job, nɛ fo daa nyi asheŋ nna,
fo daa beeŋ yige mmalga fuloŋ
nɛ fee malga ere.
4Fo mmalga ere beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ
basa pɔtɛ e lar Ebɔrɛ kaman
nsaa maŋ naŋ yirda mo.
5Fo kɔnɔ to be mmalga e naa ŋini fo asheŋ lubi.
Kamalganyi nɛ fee ta a kuŋ fo kumu bre de.
6M maŋ wɔ nfe nna nɛ n ji fo demu;
fo gbagba be mmalga e naa ji a bri fo.
7Mannɛ fo e la dimɛdi juŋkparso durnya to.
Fo alɛ maŋ chɛr a chɔ abee nɛ Ebɔrɛ to na.
8Ebɔrɛ ka daa wora mbe ŋkre sososo na,
fo daa wɔ ndoŋ a?
Fo nawule e kɔ kanyiasheŋ a?
9Kusɔ ko wɔtɔ nɛ fo nyi kumo
nɛ anyi ere maŋ nyi kumo a?
10Basa nɛ b bel a chɔ fo tuto gba
kutɔ nɛ anyi ere koya kanyiasheŋ.
11Ebɔrɛ gbagba e naa lolo fo na.
Kumo be loŋ maŋ kukwe fo a?
Anyi alɛ gba chɛ mo to m malga
kagbenewushi be mmalga n sa fo.
12Fo kagbene koso m baŋ so ga,
n shin nɛ fo ki esa ŋana so.
13Amoso nɛ fo nya agbo n wɔtɔ Ebɔrɛ
nsaa malga a gbiti mo na.
14Dimɛdi kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e maŋ wora kulubi
nsaa la esa niŋiso Ebɔrɛ be anishito.
15Nɛ Ebɔrɛ maaŋ tiŋ n yirda emalaika
nɛ baa shuŋ mo ebɔrɛso na gba,
16edimɛdi bre nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n yirda a?
Alubi la fanɛ nchu nna n sa anyi edimɛdi
nɛ anyee nuu kapa nɛ kanyɛ.
17Job, kaŋ kusoe n nu kusɔ nɛ n nyi,
nseŋ koya kusɔ ko kumo to.
18Benyiashempo e ŋini ma kashenteŋ
nɛ b koya bumo nanaana kutɔ.
Bumo alɛ maŋ ta ashiri kikɛ ŋ ŋana.
19Bekama nɛ b nya le be kanyiasheŋ ere
malɛ gba e nya kasawule n chena so.
Efuli pɔtɛ so be basa ka bɔla kasawule na so a choŋ ndoŋ,
b maŋ tiŋ n lara bumo be nfɛra ashi Ebɔrɛ so.
20Ama awurfoŋ wɔtɔ karechɛ kikɛ nna
n sa basa nɛ b wɔ alubi be kebaawɔtɔ to.
21Asheŋ nɛ e bee keta kufugboŋ na nawule
be asheŋ nɛ baa nu saŋkikɛ.
Jemanɛ nɛ asheŋ bee nite nɛnɛ a sa bumo na
nɛ beyu nɛ baa suge basa be asɔ na
bee baa kaa suge bumo be asɔ.
22Bumo be kelamba kikɛ e la
tentembiri nɛ kepaŋ tama nɛ luwu.
23Baaŋ baa kulti a fin ajibi fanɛ ejita,
bumo alɛ nsaa nyi fanɛ tentembiri
be kachɛ na taga to.
24Kemurgboŋ, e du fanɛ ewura lempo ka bee shin nɛ e kɔ bumo kena,
a jo nɛ k mur bumo cheche.
25-26Kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ ba basa nɛ b kini Ebɔrɛ
nseŋ lar Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ kaman
n ta akɔsɔ a kɔ Ebɔrɛ nna na.
27Loŋ be basa na beeŋ tiŋ a la
damawuraana nɛ b ji n daŋ,
28ama baaŋ baa ka wɔ nde bureso
nɛ ekama shile ŋ ka to nna.
29Bumo be mpetɛsɔ nɛ kedamaya kikɛ
beeŋ duga so loŋ hale m ba loge
ŋ ka bumo gba kuraa.
30B maaŋ tiŋ ŋ gelge tentembiri kikɛ.
Ebɔrɛ be agbo nɛ k bee suse wuloŋwuloŋ
fanɛ edɛ na beeŋ mur bumo cheche.
31Nɛ b paŋ nfɛra nseŋ ta bumo
be yirda n wɔtɔ asheŋ lubi to bre,
kumo ere asheŋ lubi be kakɔka nɛ baaŋ nya.
32Pɔɛŋ nɛ bumo be kakɔka be saŋɛ na a fo,
bumo be kebaawɔtɔ beeŋ ki fanɛ
kedibi nɛ k bolo a shin nɛ kewu nna.
33Bumo alɛ beeŋ naŋ ki fanɛ kedibi be ayabi
nɛ amo be asɔrso maŋ bel nseŋ chuge n tɔr,
ŋko kedibi sɔrso nɛ kumo be atoto gbaŋgbaŋ n wurge.
34Kashenteŋto, edɛ e naŋ ji bɔrɛkinipoana
nɛ kejimuniwuraana be nwu nɛ bumo be kaman to ebi m mur.
35Ŋkpal manɛ so, b la basa nɛ baa kre asheŋ lubi
nsaa wora amo nna.
Efɛ nɛ kafule malɛ e bɔlɔ bumo be ŋgbene to.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Ɛlifaz be kamalga na to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job tuge Ɛlifaz to ŋ kaŋɛ le:
2“N daŋ kenu le be mmalga ere ŋ ku so,
amo alɛ maa wushi ma kagbene kikɛ.
3Amoso lo fo kɔnɔ nsaa maŋ naŋ kaŋɛ shɛŋ.
Manɛ e kɔ fo nɛ fee sha kamɔrɔji loŋ bre?
4Nɛ fanɛ fo e daa wɔ kebaawɔtɔ nɛ n wɔ kumo to ere,
nɛ ma alɛ wɔ kumo nɛ fo wɔtɔ to ere,
ma alɛ gba daa beeŋ tiŋ a malga kananɛ fee malga ere.
N daa beeŋ tiŋ n nya kusɔ ko m malga ŋ gbiti fo
nseŋ keni fo n fifi kumu fanɛ kananɛ fee wora ere.
5Ama ma ere daa beeŋ malga nna n leŋ fo to
nseŋ lolo fo n wushi fo kagbene.
6Nɛ fanɛ m malga ŋko m maŋ malga gba,
awurfoŋ to nɛ ŋ kraa wɔ a ji ebesa na.
7O Ebɔrɛ, fo bar ma kaseto
nseŋ mur ma laŋ to ebi kikɛ kuraa.
8Fo shin nɛ n nyɔr ŋ ki fanɛ awibi nawule,
nɛ basa bee wu ma nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ
ma alubi so nɛ ŋ ki loŋ.
9Ebɔrɛ nya agbo nna a kɔrfɛ ma kenishipereso,
nseŋ ta anishi n yuu ma so a we anyii to yurkishi so.
10Basa bee gbɛlɛ ma nna nsaa mɛr nnɔ a ŋini ma.
Baa gama nna a kpa ma anishito
etaŋ nsaa wora ma eyurto.
11Ebɔrɛ malɛ e ta ma m bɔɔ basa lubi enɔ,
nɛ jimaŋ nɛ k maa wu kuwɔr ere nya ma e wora loŋ.
12Kusɔ kama daa nite nɛnɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ to nna
pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ to m pɛ ma ebɔl to m buri ma to n lɛ.
Ebɔrɛ lara ma n yili fanɛ kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ
13ta mbe atanyembi n yuu so n to nna.
Mo alɛ maŋ wu ma kuwɔr nseŋ futi ma epun
n lara ma apuntosɔ n lɛ kasawule.
14E baa doro ma ale anyɔ nyɔ nna.
E ba ma so fanɛ enapo nɛ
e nya agbo yurkishi so nna.
15Amoso nɛ n ta bɔtɛ m ba piŋi m buu
nseŋ chena eshishɛrpumpuŋ to a shu
fanɛ ŋ ka bee shu keeli na.
16N shu nna nɛ ma anishi m pere,
hale puŋi m buu so
nɛ m maŋ naa wu nɛnɛ.
17Ama ma alɛ maŋ diewu n wora kulubi ko.
Kebɔrkɔnshi kikɛ maŋ wɔ ma kabɔrɛkule to.
18Nɛ fanɛ n wu gba, mee kule kasawule nna
fanɛ k sa maŋ shin nɛ kushu nɛ mee shu
a fin kashenteŋ ere e ŋana basa so kikɛ.
19Naniere gba, Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ebɔrɛso na
e la ma shɛdajipo nɛ ma ekumpo.
20N nekpaana bre kini ma nna n lɛ,
ama Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee shu a ŋini.
21Kananɛ esa bee kule Ebɔrɛ a sa mo nekpa na
nɛ mee fin esa nɛ e beeŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n sa ma.
22Ŋkpal manɛ so, m maaŋ naŋ ji nfɛ damta
nseŋ wu n yɔ a maaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
Job ka fubel ŋ ŋini Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ
1Ma tama loge nɛ ma jemanɛ malɛ fo n loge,
nɛ ma nchaŋ malɛ kur a dese a jo ma.
2Kusɔ nɛ mee wu kikɛ e la jimaŋ nɛ b diewu
a wora ma eyurto kenishipereso.
3Nɛ fo, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na maŋ chɛ ma to,
wanɛ e naŋ ka kukɔ na n sɔ ma n yige?
4Ŋkpal fo so, n nekpaana kini kenu
kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ na.
Amoso a daga fo shin nɛ b pin
fanɛ b maŋ wora n nyalɛ.
5B ji m bri ma nna ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ baaŋ nya so,
amoso shin nɛ bumo be mbia be anishi e biri bumo.
6Fo, Ebɔrɛ na so nɛ basa nya ma a tege
nsaa tu echɔl a wɔtɔ ma anishito na.
7A ka gbrɛ nɛ n tan,
ŋkpal kushu nɛ kagbenejija damta so.
Ma eyur ere malɛ maŋ naa du
kananɛ k daa du na.
8Basa nɛ b la basa lela kashenteŋto baŋ wu ma
bumo be nnɔ bee mɔ bumo nna
nɛ baa nya agbo a wɔtɔ n nekpaana
nɛ b maa sa Ebɔrɛ bunyaŋ ere.
9Basa niŋiso beeŋ baa wora kusɔ nɛ k daga,
ŋkpal loŋ so baaŋ baa nya eleŋ a ti so.
10Ama n nekpaana ere to be ekama
maŋ kɔ kanyiasheŋ kikɛ mo to.
11Ma nchɛ bee ba ekar nna na,
ma ŋkre kikɛ jija.
Ma alɛ be tama kikɛ loge.
12Ama kusɔ nɛ n nekpaana na beeŋ tiŋ n wora
e la kebaasa ma tama fuloŋ; b maa ji kashenteŋ.
13Ma tama kikɛ e la keyɔ bubuni to,
kakpa nɛ meeŋ ya dese tentembiri to.
14Kumo be kaman nɛ n ta nchaŋ n tre n tuto,
nseŋ ta ashushombi nɛ e beeŋ ji ma na
n tre n nio nɛ n sipocheana.
15Nɛ loŋ nna, ma tama wɔ nnɛ?
Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n wu kumo?
16Tama maaŋ tu ma n yɔ luwu to,
kumo alɛ maaŋ tu ma n yɔ bubuni to.

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildad be kamalga nyɔsopo be asheŋ
Bildad
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Bildad nɛ e shi
Shuuwa be kasawule so na naŋ kaŋɛ le:
2“Job, saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ yige fo mmalga ere bre?
Baa kɔ nfɛra nseŋ shin nɛ anyi ere e malga.
3Fee fɛ nna fanɛ asɔbɔya nɛ a maŋ kɔ nfɛra
e la anyi, ŋko nuso?
4Fo nya agbo nna a doro fo kumu kenyanyaŋɛso na.
Fo kanya agbo na maaŋ tiŋ ŋ gbuŋgbuŋ durnya.
Ebɔrɛ malɛ maaŋ kpal fo so m pulgi abee.
5-6Basa lubi be efitila maa chɛr nsaa duŋ
a ka bumo tentembiri to ashi bumo
be elaŋana to.
7Bumo be aya daa kɔ eleŋ nna ga,
ama naniere e ki aya pɔso.
Bumo gbagba be asheŋ woraso
e shin nɛ b fiti n tɔr.
8Baa nite nna n ya kaa luri ashewu to
nɛ e bee pɛ bumo be aya.
9Bumo alɛ naa nite nna n ya kaa chichi ajigbelɛ so
nɛ e bee pɛ bumo be anakuŋ to kpakpa.
10Ajigbelɛ bee ŋana a dese kasawule to nna,
nɛ ajigbelɛ pul bumo be ekpaana to a jo bumo.
11Kenishipere nɛ k bee keta kufu
bɛ bumo so kaba kama so nna.
12B daŋ dii kedama nna,
ama naniere akoŋ e naa mɔ bumo.
Jɛrbi yil nna a jo bumo kaba kama so.
13Kumo be kaman nɛ luwu gbagba
e ba ji bumo m mur kuraa.
14Baa gberge basa lubi na nna a lar
bumo be elaŋana to nɛ b ya
wu eluwu bumbuŋ nɛ e bee keta kufu.
15Kumo be kaman nɛ bumo be elaŋana
nɛ asɔ kikɛ e chɔɔ m mur ŋ ki nsunɔ.
16Kumo be kaman nɛ b ki fanɛ ndibi
nɛ amo be nliŋi nɛ ayabi kikɛ wu.
17Bumo ere choŋ nɛ ekama teŋ bumo so nna na.
18B lar basa keniso be kasawule so nna na,
nɛ k wora fanɛ b ka lar kefulto to
n ya luri tentembiri to na.
19Bumo ere maaŋ naa kɔ mbia ŋko kaman to ebi
nɛ esa beeŋ keni bumo so n nyiŋi bumo.
20Yili epeŋilarkpa n ya fo epeŋitɔrkpa
esa kama nɛ e nu bumo be asheŋ,
kufugboŋ beeŋ tɔr amodoŋwura so
nɛ e baa chicha.
21Kelamba nɛ k jo basa lubi
nɛ bumo be nnaŋ to ebi
nɛ b maŋ nyi Ebɔrɛ nna na.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Bildad be kamalga na to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ mo nekpa Bildad le:
2“Manɛ nna nɛ fee kɔrfɛ ma nɛ fo mmalga ere bre?
3Ale kudu nna na fo kaa bee malga a gbiti ma.
Nyɔmɔ maŋ kɔ fo a?
4Hale nɛ n wora kulubi gba,
k nya fo nnɛ?
5Fo alelasheŋ so nɛ fee puchi,
a fɛ fanɛ n wora n jija na so
nɛ mee ji awurfoŋ.
6Ama Ebɔrɛ e maŋ wora n nyalɛ
ŋkpal e kaa bee wu ma kulubi so.
7Ŋ ka shu ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora n da ma so,
m maŋ nya esa nɛ e tuge ma.
Ŋ ka shu n fin kechɛto,
esa kikɛ maŋ ji ma asheŋ n sa ma.
8Ebɔrɛ kuŋ ekpa nna nɛ m maaŋ tiŋ n choŋ,
mo alɛ shin nɛ ma ekpa ki tentembiri n sa ma nna.
9E shin nɛ m paŋ ma mpetɛsɔ
nɛ bunyaŋ nɛ ketre lela kikɛ.
10Ebɔrɛ baŋ mur ma kikɛ nna
nɛ m maŋ naa kɔ tama kikɛ kuraa.
11Mbe agbo koso ma so alegaiso nna,
nɛ e bee wora ma fanɛ mo doŋ gbagba na.
12K wora fanɛ e ka shuŋi mbe
benapo kikɛ fanɛ b ba kɔ ma nna,
nɛ b kre m ba kulti ma laŋ n wɔtɔ.
13Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ ŋ gbagba be kanaŋ kini ma n lɛ.
Ŋ ki efɔ basa nɛ b nyi ma kutɔ nna.
14Ŋ kurgepoana shile ŋ ka ma,
nɛ n nekpaana teŋ ma so.
15Basa nɛ n daŋ keta kefɔ ma laŋ to teŋ ma so,
nɛ ma laŋ to be beshumpo kikɛ bee wora ma fanɛ efɔ na.
16M baŋ tre ma nyɛrbi gba,
baa kini keba nna.
17M baŋ fute m buu ma eche gba
e bee shile a ka ma nna.
N niopibi nyɛnsoana gbagba maa
sha kebaamata ma.
18Mbiwurbi gba maa sha kebaamata ma,
nɛ m baŋ taga bumo to baa mushe ma nna
nsaa shile.
19M baa dufɛ nteri kpakpasoana be mmuna so nna,
nɛ basa nɛ mee sha ga malɛ kilgi a kɔ ma.
20N foe eyur to nna ŋ ki fanɛ awibi nawule.
Gbrɛ a ka nɛ n wu.
21N teriana, men baa shu ma so.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ e ber ma n nase na.
22Manɛ e baa nɛ menyi alɛ gba naa kɔrfɛ ma
fanɛ kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee kɔrfɛ ma na?
Awurfoŋ nɛ mee ji ere maŋ kukwe loŋ a?
23B daŋ sibɛ ma mmalga ere n nase kawɔl to
k daa beeŋ par ma ga.
24B daŋ chaŋ amo n deŋi kefalta so nna,
a beeŋ baa dese mbaanaayɔ.
25N nyi ma emɔlgapo Ebɔrɛ na ka wɔ ebɔrɛso,
nɛ asheŋ ere kikɛ be lalaloge
e beeŋ gbelge m ba durnya to m ba mɔlga ma.
26Hale pɔɛŋ nɛ ma eyur ere e mur gba,
ŋ gbagba beeŋ wu Ebɔrɛ kenishiso.
27Kashenteŋto, ŋ gbagba e naŋ wu mo,
ma alɛ bee keni loŋ be kachɛ na ekpa nna.
28N teriana, menyi ere bee fɛ ekpa
nɛ menyeeŋ bɔla so n wu ma kulubi nseŋ mɛaŋ ma nna,
a kaŋɛ fanɛ ma e ta ma kumu n wɔtɔ asheŋ to.
29Ama men baa de demuji nɛ k bee ba menyi so
jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ gberge menyi kusoe na so.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofa ka naŋ malga be asheŋ
Zofa
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Zofa nɛ e shi
Naama be kasawule so na kaŋɛ le:
2“Job, fo mmalga bee chɔ ma kagbene to pasaa;
a daga ŋ ka nya kusɔ ko ŋ kaŋɛ fo naniere.
3Kusɔ nɛ fo malga na la katege nna,
ama ma alɛ gba nyi kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ fo.
4Kashenteŋto fo alɛ gba baa nyi fanɛ dra na kikɛ,
yili jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ to dimɛdi n wɔtɔ durnya to na
5basa lubi be kagbenefuli maa chɛr.
6Baaŋ tiŋ n nya eyilikpagboŋ n ji eleŋ ga,
nɛ k wora fanɛ b kaa bee chute awɔlpa na,
7ama bumo alɛ beeŋ choŋ fanɛ afu ka ta kalabɛr na;
nɛ basa nɛ b daa nyi bumo na e baa bishi abar fanɛ,
nnɛ nɛ b yɔ?
8Basa beeŋ teŋ bumo so fanɛ
kananɛ baa teŋ edareana so na.
9Basa lubi beeŋ foe basa be anishi so ashi mboŋ
nɛ b daa wɔ na nɛ bumo be basa gbagba
a fin bumo ŋ gben.
10Bumo be mbia e naŋ ba ka
asɔ nɛ bumo kurgepoana suge
betirpo kutɔ na be akɔ n sa bumo.
11Basa lubi bee wu a yɔ nchaŋ to nna
nɛ b kraa la mbifɔlbi.
12-13Alubi bee wora basa lubi ebel nna ga
nɛ baa ji amo a nu
amo be ebel fanɛ ajibi na.
14Ama alubi nɛ b min fanɛ ajibi na
beeŋ ki kekera bumo be nnɔ to nɛ kɔrtɔ bumo be epunana to.
15Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ b paŋ
asɔ nɛ b suge beko kutɔ na kikɛ.
16Baaŋ wu nɛ k wora fanɛ
awɔ lubi ka duŋ bumo m mɔ na.
17B maaŋ naŋ nya ekpa n ji asɔ lela nɛ e beeŋ chase;
fanɛ ɔlif be ŋku nɛ kenyipochu nɛ mushoŋchu nɛ
a sɔ kaplɛkama a shile fanɛ lɔr na.
18-19Ŋkpal b ka puni betirpo n suge bumo be nwu so,
bumo be kegben beeŋ to jiga nɛ b maaŋ ji amo be tɔnɔ.
20Kejimuni so, b maa nya asɔ, nɛ a bee kukwe bumo.
21Jemanɛ nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ
nɛ b gbare n sa bumo be amu na,
nɛ bumo be kanyɛ kikɛ beeŋ mur.
22Saŋɛ nɛ b nya kusɔ kikɛ nɛ eyur wushi bumo na
nɛ baaŋ paŋ kusɔ kikɛ nɛ kayurnyaŋ
nɛ awurfoŋ gboŋgboŋi e ba bumo so.
23Jemanɛ nɛ b ji m bɔlɔ epunana na,
nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ mbe agbo
nɛ k bee suse fanɛ edɛ na e ba bumo so.
24Jemanɛ nɛ baaŋ baa shile abɛlso akpa na,
nɛ danyaŋ be atanyembi beeŋ da bumo m mɔ.
25B baŋ gberge atanyembi na m pee,
amo be nnɔso beeŋ baa chise ŋklaŋ a do
nɛ kufugboŋ e luri m bɔlɔ bumo be ŋgbene to.
26Asɔ kama nɛ b gbare n yili na beeŋ mur.
Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ
e ba chɔɔ bumo nɛ bumo be asɔ kikɛ m mur
ashi bumo be elaŋ to.
27Esoso nɛ kasawule kikɛ beeŋ ji shɛda
ŋ gbiti bumo be asheŋ lubi nɛ b wora na.
28Ebɔrɛ be agbo beeŋ ki fanɛ nchugboŋ
m ba sulɔ bumo be asɔ kikɛ n yɔ.
29Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kre n yili n sa
kumukpakpaso wuraana nna na.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Zofa be kamalga to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ:
2“Nɛ fanɛ fee sha kemalga n wushi ma kagbene nna,
kumo ere nu ma kamalga ere.
3Ŋ kaŋ malga n loge,
feeŋ naŋ tiŋ n fara a wora
ma eyur to.
4M maa bile asheŋ a gbiti dimɛdi ko nna,
Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee bile asheŋ a gbiti.
Amoso nɛ maa wora kanyiti na.
5Keni kananɛ ŋ ki.
Ma asheŋ maa chinchiŋ fo
nsaa mɔ fo kɔnɔ a?
6Nɛ ŋ gbagba baa fɛ kusɔ nɛ k tu ma ere be nfɛra,
k bee ta kufu nna a pɛ ma nɛ m baa chicha.
7Manɛ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sa basa lubi ekpa
nɛ baa chena chɛr ga nɛ asheŋ
bee nite nɛnɛ a sa bumo?
8Manɛ nna nɛ bumo be mbia nɛ bumo nanabiana
bee daŋ a tu bumo nɛ b kraa wɔ ŋkpa to?
9Shɛŋ maŋ tir bumo ashi bumo be elaŋana to,
Ebɔrɛ malɛ maa kaa gberge bumo kusoe.
10Bumo be ana bee kurge nna ga,
anabi na malɛ be ekoŋwule gba maa wu.
11Bumo be mbia bee pɛl nna nɛ esa maa keni bumo so,
shɛŋ malɛ maa wora bumo.
12Baa ta echakachaka nɛ ejaŋjilaŋ
nɛ nlopi a boŋ nshɛ a ji eyur nna.
13Kebaawɔtɔ malɛ bee nite nɛnɛ nna a sa bumo,
shɛŋ maa tɔrɔ bumo be nfɛra hale n ya fo
kachɛ nɛ baaŋ wu.
14Ama le nɛ basa lubi na bee kaŋɛ
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na: ‘Yige anyi!
Anyi maa sha kepin fo aparsheŋ.
15Anyi maa nya tɔnɔ kikɛ ashi
kebaakule nɛ kebaabunyaŋ fo to.
16Anyi gbagba be eleŋ so
nɛ asheŋ bee nite nɛnɛ a sa anyi.’
Amoso nɛ ma, Job bre lara ma kumu ashi
loŋ be basa, nɛ bumo be ŋkre lubiana to na.
17Ale afanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ nya agbo
ŋ gberge alubiworapoana kusoe
n shin nɛ b ji jɛrbi?
18Ale afanɛ nɛ e daŋ farnyaŋ bumo to
fanɛ kananɛ afugboŋ bee kpeta amimi a lɛ na?
19Menyi kaa kaŋɛ le: ‘Ebɔrɛ beeŋ gberge
alubiworapoana be mbia kusoe ŋkpal
bumo kurgepoana be asheŋ lubi so.’
Ama le nɛ ma ere kaŋɛ: ‘Ebɔrɛ e gberge
alubiworapoana na gbagba kusoe nɛ b pin
fanɛ bumo gbagba be alubi so nɛ e wora loŋ.’
20Shin nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be agbogboŋ na
e ba alubiworapoana gbagba so nɛ b mur cheche.
21Ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo be luwu be kaman
kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ wora bumo be mbia
be asheŋ maaŋ naa tir bumo.
22Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ
kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora?
Mo e naa ji basa nɛ b yil eyilikpagboŋ demu.
23-24Anyi be beko bee dii kedama nna
nsaa wɔ alenfia to pɔɛŋ nsaa wu.
25Beko bre ketir nɛ ebesa to nɛ baa wu.
26Ama luwu koŋwule nɛ an kikɛ bee wu
nɛ baa puli anyi nɛ ashushombi bee ji anyi.
27N nekpaana, n nyi fanɛ menyee
kre ma ŋkre lubi nna.
28Menyee bishi fanɛ: ‘Basa gboŋ nɛ baa
wora alubi na be elaŋana nɛ b daa wɔ
amo to na naa wɔ nnɛ naniere?’
29Basa kama nɛ b taga to
ŋko nɛ b wɔ kufɔ kikɛ shuli so
30fanɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ nya agbo,
basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ lubi
maa ji jɛrbi.
31Esa kikɛ maa kaŋɛ bumo alubi nɛ b wora,
ŋko a gberge bumo kusoe ŋkpal amo so.
32Kumo be kaman, baa kpaŋ bumo
ashi bumo be nlibuna nna.
33Kasawule gba bee sɔ bumo nɛnɛ nna,
nɛ basa damta damta bee shu bumo be nli.
34Ama mmalga fuloŋ nɛ a maŋ kɔ kifi to
nɛ men kɔ a lolo ma ere na.
Kusɔ kama nɛ menyee kaŋɛ na la efɛ nna.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Ɛlifaz be kamalga sasopo be asheŋ
Ɛlifaz
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Ɛlifaz nɛ e shi
Tɛman be kade to na naŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Manɛ be tɔnɔ nɛ edimɛdi kɔ n sa Ebɔrɛ?
Hale edimɛdi to be benyiashempo gba
maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ n sa mo.
3Nɛ fanɛ fo, Job, maŋ naŋ wora
kulubi ŋ ku so gba,
kumo be loŋ kraa maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ
n sa Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bre.
4Mannɛ fo ka bee ŋana Ebɔrɛ nsaa shuŋ mo so
nɛ e bee kpele fo kusoe a ŋini fo ekpa na.
5Ayai! Mannɛ a loŋ so nna.
Fo asheŋ lubi so nɛ e bee wora loŋ.
6Fo shin nɛ fo niopibi ka fo kekɔ nɛ e ji fo,
mbe asɔbuuso nɛ fo sɔ nɛ e maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ a buu.
7Fo alɛ kini kesa basa nɛ akoŋ nɛ achukoŋ kɔ
ajibi nɛ nchu nɛ b ji nseŋ nuu.
8Fo yuku nɛ eyilikpa nɛ fo ta
n sɔ kasawule ere kikɛ m pugi so.
9Fo kini kechɛ bekulpoche to,
nseŋ kɔrfɛ amunibi n suge bumo be asɔ n ti so.
10Amoso nɛ kufugboŋ ki fanɛ
ajigbelɛ ŋ kulti fo n wɔtɔ
11nɛ k wora fanɛ kaplɛkama ka biri to nɛ fo maa wu,
nɛ nchu bɔlɔ ŋ kulti fo n wɔtɔ na.
12Ebɔrɛ wɔ ebɔrɛso nɛ k wɔ awɔlto
a chɔ achɛkpabi nɛ a wɔ esoso ga nna,
nsaa wu kusɔ kama.
13Fo tama fanɛ tentembiri plɔ beeŋ tiŋ
n ta fo ŋ ŋana Ebɔrɛ so a?
14Awɔlpa nɛ a biri to maaŋ tiŋ m buu
mbe anishi so nɛ e sa maa wu,
saŋɛ nɛ e bee nite a kulti awɔlto ndoŋ na.
15-16Men yige adrasheŋ fuloŋ nɛ alubiworapoana
daŋ yirda nɛ nchu daŋ bɔlɔ m ba sulɔ bumo
n choŋ nɛ b maŋ nyi na be kebɛso.
17Alubiworapo na daŋ kini
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na nna,
a fɛ fanɛ e maŋ tiŋ n wora bumo shɛŋ.
18Ama Ebɔrɛ malɛ daŋ shin nɛ
bumo be nnaŋ to ebi dii kedama nna.
Ma ere maa pin alubiworapoana ere
be kusɔ nɛ baa fɛ bumo be nfɛra to.
19Ebɔrɛ be basa be ŋgbene bee fuli
basa nɛ b kini Ebɔrɛ be kasogberge so nna
nɛ baa ji eyur kagbenefuliso a kaŋɛ le,
20‘An doŋana maŋ naa wɔtɔ,
edɛ malɛ mur bumo be asɔ kikɛ.’
21To, Job, shin nɛ fo nɛ Ebɔrɛ e naŋ nyalɛ abar so
nɛ fo sa maŋ naa ta mo fanɛ fo doŋ.
Nɛ fo wora loŋ, e beeŋ nɛfa fo.
22Sɔ keŋini kama nɛ e bee sa fo na,
nseŋ ta mbe mmalga n wɔtɔ fo kagbene to.
23Nɛ fo baŋ bɛta m ba Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nseŋ lar alubi to,
asheŋ beeŋ nite nɛnɛ n sa fo.
24Amoso lara fo shuwa lela na kikɛ n lɛ
eboŋ nɛ a wɔlto be ataŋɛ to
nseŋ wu amo fanɛ eshishɛr nɛ a maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ.
25Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na
e ki fanɛ shuwa nɛ gbiti lela ga n sa fo.
26Aloŋ nɛ feeŋ nya kagbenefuli
ashi kebaabunyaŋ mo to.
27Ebɔrɛ beeŋ nu fo kabɔrɛkule,
nɛ fo alɛ e wora m bɔlɔ nnɔ naseso
nɛ fo nase n sa mo na so.
28E beeŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ fo kule mo,
nseŋ shin nɛ kefulto e ba fo ekpa so,
nɛ fo baa wora mbe aparsheŋ.
29Nɛ beko tɔr kebaawɔtɔ to gba,
nɛ fo kule Ebɔrɛ n sa bumo
e beeŋ nu fo kekule nseŋ maŋ bumo so.
30Hale basa nɛ b wora n jija gba
beeŋ nya ketampaŋ,
ŋkpal fo ka bee wora Ebɔrɛ kasonu so.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Ɛlifaz be kamalga na to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ mo nekpa Ɛlifaz le:
2“Hale nɛ kabre, ŋ kraa bile asheŋ kenishipereso nna,
ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ ka tɔrɔ ma ga
nseŋ shin nɛ n ji awurfoŋ so.
3Nɛ fanɛ n daa nyi kakpa nɛ Ebɔrɛ wɔ
nɛ kananɛ meeŋ wora n yɔ ndoŋ nna,
n daa beeŋ yɔ mo kutɔ
4n ya tu mo n ji asheŋ,
nseŋ ji mo emɔrɔ kenishipereso.
5Aloŋ nɛ meeŋ pin kusɔ
nɛ e kɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ ma.
6Ebɔrɛ maaŋ kpal mbe eleŋgboŋ so
ŋ kini kenu ma kamalga.
7Ŋkpal manɛ so, m maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ,
mo alɛ beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ,
kulubi kikɛ maŋ bɛ ma,
nɛ n nya ma kumu n ji.
8Ama ŋ keni epeŋilarkpa,
nɛ Ebɔrɛ maŋ wɔ ndoŋ.
Nɛ n naŋ keni epeŋitɔrkpa,
ŋ kraa maŋ wu mo ndoŋ gba.
9Ebɔrɛ bee shuŋ kelargato be esoso nɛ kaseto kikɛ,
ama ŋ kraa maa wu mo ndoŋana gba.
10Ama Ebɔrɛ bre nyi kusɔ kama nɛ mee wora,
mo alɛ baŋ wora ma ŋ keni, e beeŋ wu ma
fanɛ shuwa nɛ eyurpi maŋ wɔ kumo to.
11M maŋ naŋ kini kebɛ mbe mbra kikɛ so,
ma alɛ maa lar mbe ekpaana so kikɛ.
12Kusɔ kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ yili, mee wora kumo nna.
Mbe aparsheŋ nɛ mee bɛ so, mannɛ meya.
13Ebɔrɛ maa chɛrga, esa kikɛ malɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kɔ mo
ŋko ŋ kuŋ mo ekpa nɛ e sa maŋ wora mbe kepar.
14Kusɔ nɛ e kre a laŋɛ ma kaplɛa so
ashi mbe ŋkre damtaana to,
kumo nɛ e beeŋ wora ma.
15Amoso nɛ mbe asheŋ bee keta ma kufu ga na.
M baŋ fɛ ade kikɛ be asheŋ,
kufugboŋ bee pɛ ma nna nɛ m baa chicha.
16Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ ma kenyɛn lar ma to,
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kufugboŋ pɛ ma.
17Ama ŋ kraa maaŋ lo ma kɔnɔ ŋkpal
tentembiri plɔ nɛ k buu ma anishi so ere so.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Manɛ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ maŋ yili demuji be kachɛ?
Manɛ nna nɛ basa nɛ b nyi mo maŋ nyi loŋ be kachɛ na?
2Alubiworapoana tia bumo nɛ bumo braana be nsawule
be egbaŋto be ajembu dulgiso nseŋ nya nsawule damta.
Bumo alɛ naŋ yuri beko be mbolpɔ n ti bumo peya so.
3Baa suge amunibi be ekurma
nsaa sɔ bekulpoche be ana a yili tarma nna.
4Baa kuŋ betirpo ekpa nna
nɛ b sa maa nya asɔ nɛ a la bumo peya.
Bumo alɛ naa nyaŋ bumo nna nɛ baa shile a ŋana.
5Ŋkpal loŋ so, betirpo bee nite keshishɛrsawule so
fanɛ kupuŋ to be ekurma nna a fin kusɔ jiso.
Kaplɛkama maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ b nya ajibi n sa bumo be mbia.
6Betirpo na bee yɔ adɔana nɛ e maŋ la
bumo peya to nna n ya kaa fin ayu nɛ baaŋ ji,
nsaa yɔ alubiworapoana be ndibi sɔrso be adɔana to
n ya kaa shishi asɔrso jiso a ji.
7Kanyɛso baa dese awo to nna nɛ b maŋ buu shɛŋ,
ŋkpal b ka maŋ nya ewajɛbuuso so.
8Bɔrɛgboŋ baa ba, abeelaŋ to nɛ baa shile
n ya kaa ŋana nɛ bɔrɛ na e sa maŋ bri bumo.
9Basa lubi bee suge mbia nɛ bumo tutoana wu nna
ashi bumo nioana kutɔ a ta bumo a ki anya
ŋkpal b ka maŋ tiŋ ŋ ka bumo be akɔ so.
10Kumo be kaman nɛ b nyaŋ mbia na nɛ b ta akoŋ a shuŋ
ayu be adɔana to nɛ b maŋ buu asɔ nɛ e beeŋ baa kuŋ bumo.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, b maŋ kɔ loŋ be asɔbuuso na nɛ b buu.
11Mbia na e naŋ kɔr ɔlif be bibi to n wora ŋku
nseŋ nyaŋ greep be asɔrso malɛ to n wora yabra,
ama achukoŋ e naa mɔ bumo.
12Basa nɛ b doro nɛ bumo nɛ baa wu
ashi ndegboŋana be agbembiana so na
bee shu a fin kechɛto, ama Ebɔrɛ maa wora shɛŋ.
13Basa lubi ko kini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
nɛ e la Kefulto na nna.
B maa pin mo to ŋko a wɔ mbe ekpa to.
14Kakpa baŋ biri to, bemɔpo na bee koso nna
n ya kaa mɔ betirpo nɛ betentaŋasepo.
Kanyɛso saŋko malɛ nɛ b ya kaa yuri.
15Bumo nɛ baa ji kubojua na malɛ
bee jo kaboŋ e biri to nna nɛ b bela asɔ
m buu bumo be amu so saŋɛ na so ekama maaŋ pin bumo.
16Kanyɛso nɛ beyu bee bure a luri basa be elaŋ to,
ama kare baŋ chɛ nɛ b shile ŋ ŋana,
ŋkpal manɛ so, b maa sha kefulto be asheŋ.
17Kanyɛso nɛ baa sha a chɔ kapaso,
ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo nɛ kanyɛso be asɔ
nɛ e bee keta kufu na ji abar keteri nna.
18Alubiworapo na du fanɛ kepɔpɔ nɛ e deŋ
nchu so nɛ nchu na sulɔ amo a yɔ nna.
Amoso Ebɔrɛ be shoduu beeŋ ba bumo be adɔjibi
nɛ ndibi sɔrso be adɔana so nɛ a maŋ tiŋ n wora.
19Kananɛ kenyɔlɔ maa chɛr epeŋi so na,
aloŋ nɛ alubiworapoana gba maaŋ chɛr nseŋ wu n choŋ
nɛ b maaŋ naŋ wu bumo.
20Bumo nioana gba maaŋ naŋ nyiŋi bumo,
ashushombi beeŋ ji bumo m mur fanɛ
kedibi ka bu n tɔr nɛ kaŋkaŋ muu kumo na.
21Ade kikɛ bee wora bumo nna ŋkpal b ka bee ji eleŋ
bekulpoche so nsaa maa wora begbentepo kelela so.
22Ebɔrɛ be yuku na e naa mur basagboŋ na.
Hale nɛ k wora fanɛ asheŋ bee nite nɛnɛ a sa bumo gba,
asheŋ kraa beeŋ bri bumo nɛ b wora asheŋ ŋ gben.
23Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ b baa wɔtɔ
fanɛ shɛŋ ka maaŋ tiŋ n wora bumo na,
ama mo alɛ be anishi wɔ bumo so jemanɛ kikɛ nna.
24Alubiworapoana beeŋ tiŋ n nyalɛ kabre,
ama k maaŋ chɛr ko nɛ bumo be asɔ na e mur cheche.
Baaŋ ba kaseto fanɛ b ka buse afitiri n lɛ na.
25Esa ko beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ
kusɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ ere maaŋ la kashenteŋ a,
nseŋ fɛ fanɛ k maŋ kɔ kifi to a?

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bildad be kamalga sasopo be asheŋ
Bildad
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpa Bildad
nɛ e shi Shuuwa na naŋ kaŋɛ le:
2“Ebɔrɛ shi ga nseŋ daga keŋana,
ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e naa ji kuwura
ebɔrɛso, nɛ kusɔ kama bee nite nɛnɛ ndoŋ.
3Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ ŋ karga emalaika
nɛ bekama nɛ baa shuŋ mo ebɔrɛso na?
Ebɔrɛ be kefulto bee nyaŋɛ kaplɛkama nna.
4Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ mo ere
maŋ wora n jija Ebɔrɛ be anishito.
5Kufɔl nɛ achɛkpabi gba maa fulto parr
Ebɔrɛ bre be anishito.
6Nɛ nuso nɛ dimɛdi bomin,
nɛ e du fanɛ kushushombi,
bre du ga ashi Ebɔrɛ be anishito?”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Bildad be kamalga na to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job malɛ kaŋɛ mo nekpa Bildad le:
2“Fo la echɛtopo nna n sa ma,
etirpo nɛ esa pɔso fanɛ ma le!
3Keni kasotojigboŋ nɛ fo ta n sa
esa nɛ asheŋ tir ga fanɛ ma le!
4Wanɛ e chɛ fo to nɛ fo tiŋ m malga nɛnɛ le ere?
Bildad
5Basa nɛ b wu be ayoyu wɔ bubuni to
tekugboŋ be kaseto nna a chicha kenishipereso.
6Kusɔ kama nɛ k wɔ bubuni to ŋko nɛ k mur
maŋ ŋana Ebɔrɛ bre so.
7Ebɔrɛ e parga awɔlpa nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso na to,
nseŋ shin nɛ durnya shaso nɛ shɛŋ maŋ kɔ kumo to.
8Mo e shin nɛ nchu wɔ bɔrɛwɔlpa to,
ama amo malɛ maa tɔr to ŋkpal amo be egbɛ so.
9Mo koŋwule na e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa
bee buu kufɔl lelemu so nɛ esa maa wu kumo na.
10Ebɔrɛ e chaŋ kefulto nɛ tentembiri
be gbaŋfɔl n deŋi teku so.
11Mo e naa ponte to nɛ awɔlpa
be eshabɔrɛ bee gbuŋgbuŋ to na.
12Ebɔrɛ be eleŋgboŋ nɛ e ta m pulgi teku to,
nseŋ bɔla mbe kanyiasheŋ so ŋ ku teku to be
kusɔbɔya lubi gboŋgboŋi nɛ baa tre Reehab na to.
13Mo e fute n shin nɛ esoso fulto,
nɛ e ta mbe enɔana m mɔ
kusɔkpaŋ nɛ k bee gbeye na.
14Ade bre la Ebɔrɛ be eleŋgboŋ na be ashuŋ wurbi nna na.
To, wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ m pin kananɛ Ebɔrɛ be keshi gbagba du?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Job
1Kede be kaman nɛ Job kraŋ naŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Ma kenishi pere nna ŋkpal
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ ka kini
kewora kusɔ nɛ k daga nseŋ shin nɛ
kebaawɔtɔ ki kekera n sa ma so.
3Ŋ ka baa wɔ ŋkpa to nseŋ kraa
kɔ efute nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa ma ere,
4ma kɔnɔ maaŋ tuge kamalga lubi kikɛ.
Ma kudonduloŋ malɛ maaŋ ku efɛ kikɛ.
5M maaŋ shuli fanɛ kusɔ nɛ men kaŋɛ na bɔla ekpa
hale n ya fo kachɛ nɛ meeŋ wu.
6Ŋkpal manɛ so, karechɛ kikɛ ma nfɛra
bee wora ma nna fanɛ m maŋ wora kulubi.
7Mee kule Ebɔrɛ nna nɛ n doŋana
e ji awurfoŋ ga fanɛ kumu kpakpasowuraana!
8Jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ sɔ basa
nɛ b kini mo na be ŋkpa na,
tama kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ n sa bumo.
9Tɔrɔ be jemanɛ baŋ ba,
Ebɔrɛ maaŋ nu bumo be kekule.
10Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ wora bumo nna.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, b maa sha Ebɔrɛ ŋko kabɔrɛkule.
11Meeŋ ŋini menyi kananɛ Ebɔrɛ be yuku shi,
nseŋ bugi to ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kre.
12Menyi gbagba wu asheŋ ere kenishiso,
nɛ manɛ nna nɛ men naa malga asheŋ
nɛ e maŋ kɔ kifi to?
Zofa
13Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ bee wora
amukpakpaso wuraana nɛ b maa shu basa so nde.
14Baaŋ tiŋ ŋ kurge mbia damta ga,
ama akoŋ ŋko kena e naŋ mɔ bumo be galeŋga.
15Bumo be mbia nɛ baaŋ ji efute malɛ beeŋ lɔ nna n wu.
Bumo be bekulpoche maaŋ nya n shu mbia na be nli gba.
16Amukpakpaso wuraana beeŋ tiŋ
a kɔ amansherbi nɛ asɔbuuso
damta ga fanɛ b ka koli
eshishɛr m biti abar so na.
17Ama Ebɔrɛ be basa e naŋ sɔ asɔbuuso na m buu,
nseŋ chige bumo be amansherbi
damta na to n sa abar.
18Nwu nɛ amukpakpaso wuraana
pɔr na maŋ chɛr kikɛ.
A du fanɛ enansatata
ŋko ndɔtobuuana nna.
19Alubiworapo beeŋ tiŋ n dii
kedama nseŋ ya dese kanyɛso,
ŋklade kachipurso ŋ koso ŋ ki betirpo.
20Kufugboŋ beeŋ pɛ bumo kanyɛso
fanɛ nchu ka bɔlɔ n sɔ kaplɛkama na,
ŋko bɔrɛfugboŋ ka bee ber bumo na.
21Kumo be kaman nɛ epeŋilarkpa be afu tushiso
e ber m ba sulɔ bumo n lar bumo be elaŋana to.
22Jemanɛ nɛ baaŋ wora ania fanɛ
baaŋ shile m mɔlga bumo be amu na,
afu na maaŋ wu bumo kuwɔr kikɛ.
23Kumo be lalaloge nɛ k wora fanɛ afu na
ka bee mushe nsaa wora bumo eyur to
ŋkpal b ka maŋ naa wɔtɔ so na.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
1Mboŋ nɛ baa kur kasawule a lara
shuwa nɛ gbiti wɔtɔ nna,
nɛ kakpa nɛ baa ŋalga amo to
a lɔŋɛ amo so malɛ gba wɔtɔ.
2Kasawule to nɛ baa kur a lara ajembugboŋ,
nsaa bure ajembugboŋ na to a lara
anyembi kpakpaso nɛ danyaŋ peper.
3Basa bee sulɔ efitila nna
a luri kasawule chiŋgeliŋ to tentembiri to
n ya kaa fin abɛlso ere.
4Baa lar kakpa nɛ basa wɔ nna a yɔ kufɔ
n ya kur amaŋ fanɛ abɔrbi na,
nseŋ pɛ efɔl to ŋ gbelge amo to.
5Adɔsawule be kaseto chilili
nɛ baa ta edɛ a bure afalta
6nɛ yawu kpakpaso be ajembu
nɛ baa tre safai na ŋko shuwa nɛ a wɔ amo to na.
7Basa nɛ baa kur kasawule a fin abɛlso bee yɔ
mboŋ nɛ kusore maŋ tiŋ n wu ŋko
ejita maŋ naŋ firgi m bɔla ndoŋ n choŋ nna.
8Mboŋ nɛ ebuluŋ ŋko kusɔbɔya lubi be yiri kikɛ
maŋ naŋ bɔla ŋ kuso na nɛ basa na bee nite.
9Enɔana nɛ dimɛdi kɔ a bure afalta kasawule to
nsaa shin nɛ abee be epul to bee dii efuli.
10Baa bure afalta na nna a fin
yawu kpakpaso be ajembu nɛ abɛlso lela.
11Baa kuŋ kakpa nɛ elɔr bee shi a shile na to nna,
nsaa nya a lara asɔ nɛ a ŋana to.
12Ama nnɛ nɛ esa beeŋ wu kanyiasheŋ?
Nnɛ nɛ anyi beeŋ tiŋ ŋ koya asheŋ be kepinto?
13Esa maaŋ tiŋ n wu kanyiasheŋ edimɛdi to.
Esa kama malɛ maŋ nyi tɔnɔ nɛ k kɔ.
14Kanyiasheŋ maŋ wɔ teku
be kechimbi to gba.
15Esa maaŋ tiŋ n ta shuwa ŋko gbiti
nɛ k maŋ kɔ eyurpi n tɔ kumo.
16Kanyiasheŋ be yawu du kpakpa a chɔ
ajembu lela ŋko shuwa nɛ e maŋ kɔ eyurpi be yawu.
17Kumo be yawu du kpakpa a chɔ
shuwa ŋko asɔ nɛ b ta digi lela n lɔŋɛ be yawu.
18Kanyiasheŋ kɔ yawu a chɔ ajembu lela nɛ baa tre kɔral
nɛ kefitiri bumbuŋ be ajembu lela nɛ baa tre jaspa na,
ŋko ajembu lela peper nɛ baa tre rubi na gba.
19Itiopia be efuli so be ajembu lela nɛ baa tre topas na
nɛ shuwa nɛ e maŋ kɔ eyurpi na kikɛ
be yawu maŋ fo kanyiasheŋ be yawu so.
20To, nnɛ bre nɛ kanyiasheŋ wɔ?
Nnɛ nɛ asheŋ be kepin to wɔ?
21Dimɛdi kikɛ be kenishi maaŋ tiŋ n wu kumo,
mbuibi nɛ a bee firgi ere gba maaŋ tiŋ n wu kumo.
22Luwu nɛ kemur gba nu kumo be asheŋ,
a maŋ nyi kakpa nɛ k wɔ.
23Ebɔrɛ nawule e nyi ekpa nɛ k bee yɔ kanyiasheŋ akpa.
Mo nawule e nyi kakpa nɛ k wɔ.
24Ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e naa wu kusɔ kama
nɛ k wɔ kasawule so.
25Jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ sa afu kumo be eleŋ
nseŋ ku kananɛ teku beeŋ baa sa n sa kumo na
26nseŋ naŋ yili kakpa nɛ bɔrɛ beeŋ baa ba
nɛ ekpa nɛ bɔrɛ beeŋ baa bɔla so a nyɛkpɛ na
27nɛ e wu kanyiasheŋ nseŋ wora kumo
be tɔnɔ nɛ k kɔ ŋ keni nseŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ k walɛ.
28Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ edimɛdi le:
“Kanyiasheŋ e la keta bunyaŋ gboŋ
n sa ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
Nɛ kelar alubi to malɛ la asheŋ be kepin to.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
