Job be lalaloge be kamalga
Job
1Nɛ Job naŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Mee yɛlga fanɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ e baa du
fanɛ kumo nɛ n daa kɔ jemanɛ nɛ
Ebɔrɛ daa keni ma so na.
3Ebɔrɛ daa wɔ ma kutɔ nna jemanɛ kikɛ,
nseŋ daa shin nɛ kakpa bee fulto a sa ma
nɛ mee tiŋ a nite tentembiri to.
4Jemanɛ nɛ asheŋ daa nite nɛnɛ a sa ma na,
Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la n teri kpakpaso na, e daa nɛfa
ma laŋ to ebi kikɛ.
5Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na daa wɔ ŋ kutɔ nna jemanɛ na so,
nɛ ma mbia kikɛ malɛ daŋ kulti ma n wɔtɔ kaplɛkama.
6N daa nya kenyipochu damta ga nna ashi ma ana nɛ mboe to,
nseŋ daa nya ŋku ga ashi ma ɔlif be ndibi be asɔrso to.
7Jemanɛ kikɛ nɛ kadegboŋ na be benimu shɛr
kadegboŋ na be kabuna nɛ ma alɛ gba ya tu bumo n chena,
8mbifɔlbi bee lɔŋɛ a yili ekarso nna,
nɛ basa kpar malɛ e baa koso a yili a bunyaŋ ma.
9Benimuana na bee yige kamalga nna
nsaa ta bumo be enɔana a buu nnɔ so.
10Basagboŋ nɛ basa bee sa bunyaŋ gba bee lo bumo be nnɔ nna.
11Kusɔ kama nɛ n wora ŋko ŋ kaŋɛ
daa par ekama nna nsaa fuli bumo be ŋgbene.
12Jemanɛ kikɛ nɛ betirpo ŋko amunibi bee sha kechɛto,
mee chɛ bumo to nna.
13Bekama nɛ asheŋ pɔɔ so nɛ n chɛ bumo to na nɛfa ma,
ma alɛ daŋ chɛ bekulpoche to nɛ bumo be ŋgbene fuli bumo.
14Jemanɛ kikɛ n daa wora kusɔ nɛ k daga nna,
nsaa maa kpɛa esa kikɛ to.
15N daa wora etanpo nɛ ebobi kelela nna.
16N daa la fanɛ etuto nna n sa betirpo,
nseŋ daa ji asheŋ a chɛ befɔ to ashi demujikpa.
17Nɛ basa lubi ya nyaŋ basa n wɔtɔ a tɔrɔ bumo,
mee kɔ a suge bumo nna nseŋ ju basa lubi na n lɛ.
18N daa fɛ fanɛ meeŋ chɛr fanɛ jita
nseŋ dese ŋ gbagba be ebu to
n wu nɛ kayurwushi nna.
19N daa kɔ eleŋ a yil to nna fanɛ kedibi
nɛ k mur achin n yili m mata nchu nɛ bunyaŋ
bee shi kumo be afantaŋ nɛ ayabi so a wurge kanyɛso nna.
20Ekama daa kpaŋ ma nna jemanɛ kikɛ,
nɛ ma eleŋ malɛ daa maa duga so.
21M baa ji basa asoe to,
baa lo to a nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ na nna.
22Ma alɛ baŋ malga n loge,
b maŋ naa kaŋɛ shɛŋ a ti so.
Ma mmalga daa luri bumo to nna
fanɛ bɔrɛchu ka bee luri kasawule to na.
23B daa suse ma mmalga to nna
fanɛ kananɛ bedɔpo bee suse dɔchubɔrɛ so be nchu na.
24M baŋ mushe n wɔtɔ bumo
jemanɛ nɛ asheŋ maŋ bɔ n sa bumo,
k bee leŋ bumo to nna nsaa sa bumo tama.
25N daa wɔ bumo to nna fanɛ ewura
nseŋ daa malga nɛ baa nu a sa ma
fanɛ ewura ka bee juŋkpar mbe benapo
ŋko fanɛ esa nɛ e bee malga a lulo
basa nɛ b wɔ kagbenejija nɛ kushu to.”

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Naniere mbifɔlbi bee tege ma nna,
ama bumo tutoana daa maŋ la basa nɛ
meeŋ shin nɛ b ti ma njɔnɔ so a keni ma mbolpɔ so gba.
2Bumo alɛ daa la basa nɛ b kɔ eleŋ nna
nɛ n daa maaŋ shuli n ta bumo kushuŋ gba.
3B daa nite a kulti keshishɛrsawule so kanyɛso nna a fin kusɔ nɛ baaŋ ji,
ŋkpal b ka la betirpo jalɛ so.
4Baa nite a shishi afantaŋ nɛ e maŋ wɔ ebel
nɛ ndibi be nliŋi nna a ji.
5Ekama malɛ ju bumo n lar kade na to nna
nsaa ponte bumo so fanɛ b ka la beyu na.
6Abee laŋ nɛ amaŋ nɛ basa kur m mata abee
nɛ mbombi nɛ a wɔlto e ki bumo
peana nɛ b wɔ amo to.
7Ndoŋ nɛ b wɔ a wora awɔr fanɛ ekurma,
bumo alɛ nsaa biti abar so a dese ndibi be afito.
8B ki fanɛ basa fuloŋ nɛ b maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ
nɛ b ju bumo n lar kasawule na so nna.
9Naniere le be basa fuloŋ ere wora nshɛ nna
a boŋ a wora ma eyur to.
10B ta ma fanɛ kejijɛ be esa nna,
a fɛ fanɛ b walɛ so nna a chɔ ma.
Baa kaa yili ma anishito a tu echɔl gba nna.
11Ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ ka shin nɛ awurfoŋ nɛ tɔrɔ ba ma so so,
kusɔ kama nɛ baa sha, kumo nɛ baa wora ma.
12Ŋ ka maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kɔ n sa ma kumu ere gba,
b kraa maa yige kebaakɔ ma.
K du fanɛ b ka sho ajigbelɛ a fin ma kepɛ nna.
13Ŋkpal b ka nyi ŋ ka maŋ kɔ echɛtopo so,
baa wora asheŋ ko nna a shin nɛ ma
awurfoŋ bee wora keshi a ti so.
14Baa shi kaba kama so nna m ba kaa mel ma so,
nsaa biti ma so jemanɛ nɛ n tɔr a dese na.
15Kufugboŋ gboŋi tɔr ma so;
m paŋ ma bunyaŋ nɛ kedamaya kikɛ nna
fanɛ kusɔ ka pante nɛ afu lar na.
16Naniere mee shin nɛ n wu nna na.
Shɛŋ maa sɔ ma ashi ma awurfoŋ to.
17Ma awibi to bee we ma to nna kanyɛso kikɛ,
ebesa nɛ mee nu ma eyur to na maa yige kikɛ.
18Ebɔrɛ be enɔ lempo e pɛ ma kale to,
ma piŋi be kubɔ to nɛ e nyaŋ ŋ keta.
19E ta ma n lɛ edepɔ to nna,
nɛ ŋ kikɛ ki fanɛ depɔ.
20Ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e chɛ ma to,
nɛ e kini, e maŋ tuge ma gba.
Nɛ ŋ koso n yili, ama e baa keni ma nna de.
21Ebɔrɛ maŋ shu ma so kuraa n wu ma kuwɔr.
Mbe eleŋgboŋ nɛ e ta ŋ kɔrfɛ ma.
22E shin nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ ba fuu ma nna n lɛ,
nɛ n tɔr a gbelti.
23K maaŋ chɛr e beeŋ shin nɛ n wu n yɔ bubuni to,
kakpa nɛ ekama beeŋ yɔ kachako na.
24Esa kikɛ maaŋ kini kechɛ basa nɛ b ji jɛrbi
nsaa kule a fin kechɛto to.
25N daŋ tu basa nɛ baa shu n shu,
nseŋ naŋ tu bumo nɛ baa ji awurfoŋ n ji awurfoŋ.
26Ama naniere ma ere ka bee fin kesɔnyige nɛ kefulto,
jɛrbi nɛ tentembiri nɛ n nya.
27Kafɔŋ nɛ ebesa shin nɛ ma apumbi to bee kii to,
karechɛ kama malɛ, awurfoŋ to nɛ n wɔ.
28Awurfoŋ shin nɛ ma kayurwule kilgi m biri, mannɛ epeŋi.
Nɛ ŋ koso n yili basa to a shu a fin kechɛto.
29N daa shu kuwɔr so fanɛ ejiŋkaamu
ŋko egbuŋgbula nna.
30Ma eyur so kikɛ chɔɔ nna a fɔlge so
nɛ ma eyur to bel edɛ a tushi fanɛ edɛ gbagba na.
31Mboŋ nɛ n daa nu kagbenefuli be nshɛ na,
kushu nɛ kagbenejija be awɔr nɛ mee nu ndoŋ.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
Job ka kraa malga be asheŋ
1Ma, Job bɔ ntaŋ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ
m maa ba nɛ ŋ keni eche kayɛlga so kikɛ.
2Ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ bee gberge
benyɛn kama nɛ baa wora loŋ kusoe nna.
3Kashenteŋto, Ebɔrɛ bee shin nɛ
bekama nɛ baa wora alubi bee ji jɛrbi nna.
4Mo alɛ nyi kusɔ kama nɛ mee wora,
nsaa wu keya kama nɛ mee tia.
5Nɛ fanɛ n daŋ ku efɛ n sa esa,
ŋko n fule esa ko ma kebaawɔtɔ to,
6Ebɔrɛ e wora ma ŋ keni,
e beeŋ wu fanɛ kulubi maŋ wɔ ma to.
7Nɛ fanɛ n daŋ foe ekpa wora kusɔ ko nɛ k maŋ niŋi,
ŋko n ta ma kumu n wɔtɔ kulubi ko to,
ŋko n ta ma enɔana n wora kulubi ko nna,
8kumo ere basa pɔtɛ e ji ma adɔjibi
ŋko ma adɔjibi e mur kuraa.
9Nɛ fanɛ n daŋ yɛlga esa ko be eche
nseŋ ya ŋana n sha mo,
10Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ enyɛn pɔtɛ
e suge ma eche ŋ kutɔ.
11Nɛ n daŋ ta esa ko be eche nna,
k daa beeŋ baa la mbushu lubi lubi,
12nɛ k beeŋ mur ma
nseŋ shin nɛ ma adɔjibi e ji edɛ.
13Nɛ fanɛ n daa maŋ wora kusɔ nɛ k daga
n sa ma nyɛrbi nɛ mbita jemanɛ nɛ asheŋ ko
daŋ ba ma nɛ bumo be kefɛato na,
14n daa maaŋ tiŋ n ya yili Ebɔrɛ
be anishito nɛ e ji ma demu nɛ n ji n lar.
15Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ koŋwule na
e to ma nɛ ma nyɛrbi nɛ mbita na kikɛ.
16M maŋ naŋ kini kechɛ betirpo to kikɛ,
ma alɛ maŋ naŋ mɔn bekulpoche kusɔ nɛ baa sha kikɛ.
17Ma alɛ maŋ naŋ ji m mɔɛ
nɛ amunibi bre dese akoŋ kikɛ.
18Ma kebrantiɛ to kikɛ nɛ mee bela amunibi
nsaa chɛ bekulpoche to.
19M baŋ wu esa nɛ e maŋ kɔ asɔbuuso,
20mee sa mo asɔbuuso nɛ b ta ŋ gbagba
be mbolpɔ be afuibi n lue nna.
Kumo be kaman nɛ amodoŋwura e di ma epaŋ ga.
21Nɛ fanɛ n daŋ puni kumunibi ko,
ŋkpal ŋ ka nyi fanɛ
meeŋ tiŋ n ji m bri mo demujikpa so,
22Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ ma mbre
e yili ma abatimu so ŋ ku so n tɔr.
23Ŋkpal ŋ kaa bee ŋana Ebɔrɛ be kasogberge so,
m maaŋ shuli n wora le be asheŋ ere.
24Ma ere maŋ naŋ ta ma yirda
n deŋi kedamaya so kikɛ,
25ŋko a puchi ŋkpal asɔ damta nɛ ŋ kɔ so.
26Ma alɛ maŋ naŋ lar efuli ŋko ŋ ŋana
n shuŋ epeŋi ŋko kufɔl kikɛ ashi ma kebaawɔtɔ to.
27Ebɔrɛ be kaman, m maŋ bunyaŋ kusɔ kikɛ,
ŋko n ta kusɔ ko ma enɔ to n lara sarga n sa kusɔ ko kikɛ.
28Le be alubi ere daa beeŋ tiŋ m bar ma kasogberge,
ŋkpal manɛ so nɛ n daŋ wora amo kumo ere m maŋ ji kashenteŋ
n sa Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na nna na.
29Ma kagbene maŋ naŋ fuli
ŋkpal n doŋana be awurfoŋ so,
ŋko jemanɛ nɛ b ji jɛrbi so.
30Ma alɛ maŋ naŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n fin bumo be luwu
nɛ kebaala kulubi n sa ma kikɛ.
31Esa kikɛ maŋ naŋ di akoŋ ma laŋ to kikɛ.
Ma beshumpo gba nyi ŋ ka bee sɔ befɔ nɛnɛ.
32M maa shin nɛ befɔ nɛ b maŋ kɔ kakpa a luri
bee dese kowushina, ŋkpal manɛ so,
ma laŋ be mbuna bugi nna n sa bumo.
33Basa ko bee ta bumo be alubi a ŋana nna,
ama nɛ ma ere wora kulubi
m maaŋ ta kumo ŋ ŋana kikɛ.
34M maa ŋana kusɔ nɛ basa beeŋ kaŋɛ a laŋɛ ma kaplɛa so,
Ma alɛ maŋ naŋ lo ma kɔnɔ ŋko n ta ma kumu ŋ ŋana ma laŋ to
ŋkpal ŋ ka bee ŋana kufu fanɛ basa beeŋ keni ma jiga so.
35Esa ko maaŋ nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere
nseŋ ji n chɛ ma to a?
Nɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ wu kusɔ ko ma so gba nna,
e malga ŋko n sibɛ kumo n sa ma.
36Saŋɛ na so meeŋ ta kusɔ nɛ e wu ma so na
m mata ma asɔbuuso nɛ ma kasɔto
nɛ ekama e wu kumo.
37Kumo be kaman, meeŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ
kusɔ nɛ n wora kikɛ nseŋ nya kagbene
n yili mbe anishito.
38Nɛ fanɛ n yuri kasawule nɛ mee dɔ so na nna,
ŋko n suge kumo basa nɛ b wɔ kumo kutɔ nna,
39ŋko nɛ fanɛ n ji adɔjibi nɛ e wora
kasawule na so na kikɛ nna
nsaa maŋ sa beshumpo nɛ b dɔ amo na,
40kumo ere Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ afitiri nɛ ewi
a kɔr n sɔ kasawule na kikɛ so,
mannɛ ayu ŋko aboyu.
Job be kamalga be ekar nna na.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Elihu ka nya agbo n wɔtɔ Job mo nekpaana be asheŋ
1Ŋkpal Job ka wu mbe kumu fanɛ e maŋ wora kulubi so, mo nekpaana besa na yige mbe asheŋ nna n sa mo nsaa maŋ naa ji mo emɔrɔ.
2Ama kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Elihu na daa yil a nu kusɔ nɛ k bee wora na kikɛ nseŋ daŋ nya agbo n wɔtɔ Job ŋkpal Job ka daa maŋ wu mbe kumu fanɛ e wora kulubi nseŋ daa bile Ebɔrɛ so. E daa la kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Barakɛl nɛ e shi Buz be kasawule so nseŋ shi Ram be kabuna na pibinyɛn nna. 3Mo alɛ daŋ naŋ nya agbo n wɔtɔ Job mo nekpaana besa na gba nna, ŋkpal b ka daa maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ Job pin kulubi nɛ e wora so, nɛ k ba fanɛ Ebɔrɛ bre e wora n jija na so. 4Elihu daŋ yige basa asa na nna nɛ b malga n sa Job ŋkpal e ka daa la kebibi bumo to so.
5Ama e ka daŋ wu fanɛ basa asa na
daa maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ nɛ b kaŋɛ Job na nɛ e nya agbo
6nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le:
“N la kebifɔlbi nna nɛ menyi alɛ la basakpar,
amoso nɛ n sa menyi bunyaŋ
nsaa maŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ mee fɛ na.
7Ma ere daa fɛ nna fanɛ
basakpar e kɔ kanyiasheŋ.
8Ama n wu fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu
e naa luri dimɛdi to a sa mo kanyiasheŋ.
9Mannɛ kechɛr nfɛ to
e naa shin nɛ esa bee nya kanyiasheŋ,
ŋko a chɛ mo to nɛ e bee pin asheŋ to.
10Amoso, men nu kusɔ nɛ ma alɛ kɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ.
11N wora ania n nu
kusɔ nɛ menyi be ekama malga,
ama menyi be ekama maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ
Job pin fanɛ e maŋ wora n nyalɛ.
12Ŋ kaŋ kusoe n nu menyi be mmalga nɛnɛ,
ama menyi to be ekoŋwule gba maŋ tiŋ n sa
Job kamalga nɛ k shin nɛ e pin e ka wora n foe.
13Men sa maŋ kaŋɛ le:
‘Anyi ere nyi kusɔ nɛ k daga!
Ebɔrɛ e naŋ gberge mo kusoe.’
14Job daa malga a sa menyi nna, mannɛ ma,
ama ma ere daa maaŋ malga
kananɛ men malga ere n sa mo.
15Job, fo mmalga na mɔ bumo kɔnɔ,
b maŋ naa nyi kusɔ nɛ baŋ naŋ kaŋɛ fo.
16Ama a daga fanɛ ma alɛ gba e lo ma kɔnɔ
ŋkpal b ka maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ nɛ b kaŋɛ fo so a?
17Ayai! Meeŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ mee fɛ.
18Ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ damta nɛ ŋ kɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ,
amoso m maaŋ tiŋ n lo ma kɔnɔ.
19Nɛ m maŋ nya ekpa m malga,
meeŋ pante fanɛ kasapuya nɛ k bɔlɔ nsa m pante na.
20M maŋ nya m malga, maaŋ nya ma kumu,
a daga ŋ ka malga.
21M maaŋ malga ŋ kpɛa ekama to,
ma alɛ maaŋ ku efɛ n fur esa ko.
22Ma ere maŋ nyi kananɛ baa ku efɛ a fur basa.
N wora loŋ, Ebɔrɛ nɛ e to ma na
beeŋ gberge ma kusoe epul to.”

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
Elihu be kamalga be asheŋ
1Job, jande nu nfe nɛnɛ!
2Kusɔ nɛ k wɔ ma nfɛra to
nɛ mee shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ na.
3Kagbenefuful nɛ ŋ kɔ a malga na,
kashenteŋ nɛ ma alɛ bee ji.
4Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be Kiyoyu e to ma,
nseŋ sa ma efute nɛ ŋkpa.
5To, nɛ feeŋ tiŋ, fo kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ fo kɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ,
nseŋ bela ase nɛ ma nɛ fo e ji amo.
6Ebɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta m pɔr ma nɛ fo kikɛ.
Ashi mbe anishito, anyi maŋ kɔr abar to.
7Amoso, sa maa ŋana ma
ŋko kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora fo.
8Kusɔ nɛ n nu fo ka kaŋɛ nde:
9“Ma ere maŋ wora n jija.
Kulubi kikɛ maŋ bɛ ma.
10Ama Ebɔrɛ bre e naa wu ma kulubi
nsaa ta ma fanɛ mo doŋ.
11Mo e ta ŋgbɛlɛbi ŋ kre ma aya,
nsaa dara aya kama nɛ mee tia.”
12Ama mee kaŋɛ fo, Job, nna fanɛ fo wora n foe.
Ebɔrɛ e chɔ dimɛdi kikɛ.
13Nɛ nuso nɛ fee ji mo emɔrɔ a kaŋɛ fanɛ
e maa sa dimɛdi be asheŋ bishi so be atuwebi?
14Ekpa damta so nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee bɔla a malga,
ama anyi e maa kaa nu kusɔ nɛ e bee kaŋɛ.
15Saŋko nɛ edimɛdi dese a di kanyɛso,
Ebɔrɛ bee bɔla edare so nna a malga a sa bumo.
16E bee kaa shin nɛ baa nu kusɔ nɛ e bee kaŋɛ nna
nɛ mbe kasokpele malɛ bee ta kufu a pɛ bumo.
17Ebɔrɛ bee malga nna a sa bumo edare to
nɛ k shin nɛ b lar alubi nɛ kamoowu to.
18E maaŋ shin nɛ b mur.
E bee mɔlga bumo luwu to nna.
19Jemanɛ ko Ebɔrɛ bee bɔla kulɔ
nɛ eyur to be ebesa so nna
a ŋini edimɛdi kusɔ nɛ k daga kebaawɔtɔ to.
20Ajibi maa kaa yɛlga belɔpo,
hale ajibi nɛ baa sha ga gba
bee dufɛ bumo be mmuna so nna.
21Bumo alɛ bee kaa foe eyur to nna
hale nɛ bumo be awibi bee lar.
22Nɛ loŋ baŋ wora, baa taga to luwu nna na.
23Ashere Ebɔrɛ be emalaika
ŋgboŋ to ŋgboŋ to nɛ baa nyiŋi
edimɛdi kusɔ nɛ k daga na be eko e naaŋ ba
chɛ bumo to.
24Malaika na beeŋ wu bumo kuwɔr ŋ kaŋɛ
luwu fanɛ e yige bumo, ŋkpal manɛ so,
b teŋ ka alubi na be kukɔ.
25Kumo be kaman nɛ b naŋ nya alenfia,
nseŋ naŋ nya eleŋ ŋ ki fanɛ mbifɔlbi na.
26Kumo be kaman nɛ b kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nu,
nɛ b ta kagbenewushi m bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ,
nɛ e naŋ shin nɛ asheŋ e nyalɛ n sa bumo.
27Loŋ malɛ kaŋ wora, baaŋ kaŋɛ ekama le:
“An daŋ wora alubi nseŋ foe Ebɔrɛ be ekpa so,
ama Ebɔrɛ ta m paŋ anyi
28nseŋ sɔ anyi n yige ashi luwu to
nɛ an kraa wɔ ŋkpa to.”
29Ebɔrɛ bee bugi ekpa nna
a sa anyi be ekama
30nɛ an nya kumɔlga ashi luwu to.
E bee bar anyi mbe kefulto nɛ k bee sa ŋkpa na to nna.
31Amoso, Job, sa maŋ ku ma kamalga na to.
Lo fo kɔnɔ n shin nɛ m malga.
32Nɛ fo kɔ kusɔ ko nɛ fo kaŋɛ,
meeŋ shuli kagbenefuliso fanɛ fo kɔ ekpa.
33Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ,
lo fo kɔnɔ nɛ ŋ ŋini fo kanyiasheŋ.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Elihu naŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Menyi edimɛdi bee fɛ fanɛ men nyi asheŋ nna,
ama men nu ŋ kutɔ!
3Men baŋ da ajibi nɛ e wɔ ebel ŋ keni,
menyee pin amo nna,
ama nɛ men nu kanyiasheŋ be mmalga bre,
menyi maa pin amo ere.
4K ka anyi kutɔ nna nɛ an keni demu na to
nseŋ ji kumo nɛnɛ nɛ k yili kananɛ k daga.
5Job bee ŋini fanɛ e maŋ wora kulubi,
Ebɔrɛ bre e naa kini keji asheŋ
nɛ amo be ekpa so n sa mo.
6Job malɛ naa kaŋɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ
bee tre mo efɛpo nna.
Mo alɛ maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ
nsaa ji awurfoŋ damta na.
7Men daŋ wu esa nɛ e du fanɛ Job a?
E maa sa Ebɔrɛ bunyaŋ kikɛ!
8Mo nɛ alubiworapoana
e naa tu abar a wora asheŋ.
9Ŋkpal manɛ so, e yɛ, esa baa wora
Ebɔrɛ be aparsheŋ e maa nya tɔnɔ kikɛ.
10Men nu nfe, menyi nɛ menyee pin asheŋ to ere!
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shuli n wora kusɔ nɛ k maŋ daga a?
11Ekama be kusɔ nɛ e wora nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee keni so,
nsaa ka amodoŋwura kukɔ.
12Ekpa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na
e tiŋ m bɔla so n wora kulubi.
E bee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so nna a sa ekama.
13Sososo na kikɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ yuku
durnya kikɛ so nsaa keni kumo so.
14Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ sɔ efute nɛ k sa anyi ŋkpa ere
15anyi edimɛdi beeŋ wu nseŋ bɛta n yɔ eshishɛr to.
16Amoso nɛ men nyi asheŋ,
men nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere!
17Menyee ji a bri Ebɔrɛ nɛ e niŋi na nna,
ŋkpal menyi ka bee fɛ fanɛ e kishi kebaaji asheŋ
nɛ amo be ekpa so so.
18Kashenteŋto, Ebɔrɛ e naa ji a bri
bewura nɛ b maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ
nsaa la kumukpakpaso wuraana.
19Ebɔrɛ e to anyi kikɛ kuraa.
Mo alɛ maa keni eko a bɔlɔ kenishi a chɔ eko.
Damawura ŋko etirpo, ewura ŋko ebɔlpo,
kikɛ la kukoŋwule nna ashi mbe anishito.
20Bewura nɛ b ji eleŋ ga gba bee wu kanyɛso,
tentembiri to, jemanɛ nɛ b maa fɛ fanɛ loŋ beeŋ wora,
fanɛ anyi be ekama nna.
21Ebɔrɛ bee wu kusɔ kama nɛ anyee wora.
22Tentembiri plɔ gba maaŋ tiŋ n ta
alubiworapo ŋ ŋana Ebɔrɛ so.
23Amoso Ebɔrɛ maŋ lara kachɛ
nɛ e beeŋ ji demu n yili.
24E maa kule esa ko ekpa nsaa lara bejuŋkparpogboŋ
ashi kejuŋkpar to nseŋ naa ta beko e tal bumo to.
25Ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e nyi kusɔ nɛ baa wora,
mo alɛ e naa lara bumo kiidiso nɛ baa tɔr kuraa.
26E bee gberge bumo kusoe
kakpa nɛ basa beeŋ wu bumo nna
27ŋkpal b ka yige kebaabɛ mo so
nseŋ kplaŋ mbe mbra kikɛ so so.
28Betirpo nɛ b daŋ shu ŋ ŋini Ebɔrɛ
nɛ mo alɛ nu bumo be kushu nseŋ chɛ bumo to.
29Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ maŋ wora shɛŋ gba,
esa ko ŋko efuli ko beeŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi a?
30Ama e kraa gberge bewura
nɛ baa kɔrfɛ bumo be basa kusoe.
31Job, a daga fo kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ fanɛ fo wora n jija,
nseŋ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ fo maaŋ naŋ wora kulubi kikɛ.
32Kumo be kaman nɛ fo kule mo
nɛ e shin nɛ fo pin kulubi nɛ fo wora,
saŋɛ na so, fo maaŋ naŋ wora kumo kikɛ.
33Fo ka kini kewora kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha ere,
fee sha fanɛ mo ere e wora kusɔ nɛ fee sha n sa fo a?
Fo e daga fanɛ fo yili kusɔ ko n sa fo kumu, mannɛ ma.
Naniere, kaŋɛ anyi kusɔ nɛ fee fɛ!
34Job, esa kama nɛ e kɔ nfɛra lela beeŋ tiŋ m pin
35fanɛ kawuli be mmalga nɛ fee malga na,
a maŋ kɔ kanyiasheŋ kikɛ.
36Amoso mee kule Ebɔrɛ nna fanɛ fo ji awurfoŋ ga,
ŋkpal fo ka malga fanɛ alubiworapo so.
37Fo lar Ebɔrɛ kaman nna n ti alubi
nɛ fo wora n da mo so na so.
Anyi kikɛ be anishito nɛ fo keni
Ebɔrɛ jiga n wora mo eyur to.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Elihu naŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Job, fo tama fanɛ fo maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ
ashi Ebɔrɛ be anishito kashenteŋto a?
3Fo maŋ yirda kashenteŋto fanɛ
kewora Ebɔrɛ kasonu kɔ tɔnɔ ga a?
4Meeŋ sa asheŋ nɛ fo nɛ fo
nekpaana bishi na be atuwebi.
5Men keni kananɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa wɔ esoso kufɔ loŋ!
6Nɛ fo wora alubi, k beeŋ tiŋ n tɔrɔ Ebɔrɛ a?
Fo alɛ naŋ wora n da so ale damta gba,
e maaŋ tiŋ n wora mo shɛŋ.
7Nɛ fo la esa niŋiso, manɛ nɛ fee sa mo,
ŋko manɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee fin fo kutɔ?
8Kulubi ŋko kelela kama nɛ fee wora na,
fo braana edimɛdi nɛ fee wora amo.
9Etɔrɔ be jemanɛ ekama bee kule
Ebɔrɛ gboŋgboŋi na nna nɛ e wu
mo kuwɔr nseŋ mɔlga mo.
10Ama Ebɔrɛ nɛ e to bumo na
baŋ chɛ bumo to jemanɛ nɛ asheŋ
ki kpakpa na be kaman baa teŋ mo so nna.
11B maŋ naa bɛta a yɔ Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shin nɛ
an nyi asheŋ a chɔ asɔbɔya nɛ mbuibi na kutɔ.
12Ebɔrɛ maa nu kamoowu wuraana
nɛ alubiworapoana be kabɔrɛkule.
13Nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kini kenu
kabɔrɛkule fuloŋ nɛ baa kule na bre,
14kumo ere e beeŋ kini kenu fo alɛ gba
be kekule nɛ fo maŋ nya kanyiti nsaa fin
fo nɛ mo be keyili demujikpa na.
15Job, fo maŋ wora n nyalɛ ŋkpal fo ka kaŋɛ
fanɛ Ebɔrɛ maa gberge basa nɛ baa wora alubi kusoe so.
16Asheŋ kama nɛ fo malga na kikɛ
bee ŋini fanɛ fo maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ fee kaŋɛ nna.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1Elihu daŋ ta mbe kamalga na
nna n chuge so ŋ kaŋɛ:
2“Nya kanyiti gbrɛbi n sa ma.
Ŋ kraa kɔ kusɔ ko nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ
a laŋɛ Ebɔrɛ be kaplɛa so.
3Kusɔ kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ wora niŋi nna.
Ebɔrɛ gbagba kutɔ nɛ n nya le be kenyi ere.
4Baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ kusɔ kama
nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere la kashenteŋ nna.
5Ebɔrɛ shi ga nsaa kɔ eleŋ ga,
ekama be asheŋ tir n sa mo nna.
Shɛŋ malɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e maa pin kumo to.
6E maa sa alubiworapoana ekpa fanɛ b baa wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ,
e bee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so a sa
basa nɛ beko bee tɔrɔ bumo na.
7Ebɔrɛ e naa keni basa niŋiso so nsaa kuŋ bumo,
mo alɛ nsaa shin nɛ baa wora asheŋ fanɛ bewura,
nseŋ naa shin nɛ basa bee sa bumo bunyaŋ mbaanaayɔ.
8Ama nɛ fanɛ basa wɔ kabuti to
a ji awurfoŋ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ b wora so,
9-10Ebɔrɛ bee shin nɛ baa pin bumo be alubi
nɛ kamoowu be kebaawɔtɔ na nna
nseŋ kpele bumo kusoe fanɛ b bɛta m ba mo kutɔ.
11Nɛ b wora Ebɔrɛ kasonu nsaa shuŋ mo,
asheŋ naa nite nɛnɛ nna a sa bumo
nɛ b naŋ nya kayurwushi bumo be kebaawɔtɔ to.
12Ama nɛ b wora kawulisheŋ
nseŋ kini kenu n sa mo bre,
baaŋ wu luwu besaso n yɔ bubuni to.
13Basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ ashi bumo be ŋgbene to,
kanya agbo e bɔlɔ bumo to.
Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ gberge bumo kusoe gba
b maa kule mo fanɛ e chɛ bumo to.
14Ŋkpal loŋ so baa wu anishinyɔr be luwu nna
jemanɛ nɛ b kraa la mbifɔlbi.
15Awurfoŋ nɛ etɔrɔbi nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee bɔla so
a bugi basa be anishi nsaa ŋini bumo asheŋ.
16Le be jemanɛ ere Ebɔrɛ be kenishi pere nna
nɛ e lara fo ashi tɔrɔ to
nseŋ sa fo kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha yɛlyɛla so.
17Ama naniere fo kaa bee nya fo alubi be kakɔka ere,
18baa da so nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ ta asɔ n fule fo
ŋko kakɛ ko n lɔlɔ fo n wɔtɔ kulubi to.
19Fo eyilikpa nɛ kedamaya maaŋ tiŋ
ŋ kuŋ fo ashi awurfoŋ damta to.
20Fo alɛ e sa maa kule a fin luwu nɛ k du fanɛ tentembiri
a gberge basa a lara bumo be elaŋana to na gba.
21Baa de so nɛ fo maaŋ kilgi n yɔ alubi
nɛ fee fɛ fanɛ amo a bɔ awurfoŋ nɛ fee ji na to.
22Ebɔrɛ be eleŋgboŋ maŋ kɔ ekar.
Eŋinipo kikɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ fanɛ mo.
23Esa kikɛ maa ŋini Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora.
Esa kikɛ malɛ maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi kikɛ.
24Beko kpaŋ Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ e wora so,
a daga fanɛ fo alɛ gba e kpaŋ mo.
25Edimɛdi kikɛ wu kusɔ nɛ e wora,
ama kewora fanɛ kufɔ nɛ b yili n wu amo.
26Anyi maaŋ tiŋ m pin Ebɔrɛ be keshi to,
ŋko n tiŋ ŋ karga mbe nfɛ nɛ e ji.
27Ebɔrɛ e naa shin nɛ bunyaŋ
bee gama a ki bɔrɛwɔlpa.
28Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa bee ba
bɔrɛchu damta a sa edimɛdi kikɛ.
29Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ m pin kananɛ Ebɔrɛ
bee shin nɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa bee salga to a sɔ kaplɛkama,
ŋko kananɛ e wɔ kakpa nɛ e wɔ
nsaa ponte to saŋɛ nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba.
30Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee nyɛkpɛ
a fulto kaplɛkama, hale teku be kaseto gba.
31Ekpa nɛ e bee bɔla so a keni durnya
be efuliana na so nna na.
Bɔrɛchu nɛ e bee sa na e naa wora ajibi a sa anyi.
32Mo e kɔ bɔrɛ be kenyɛkpɛ mbe enɔana to,
nsaa kaŋɛ kumo kakpa nɛ k beeŋ ya yuu
nɛ k ya yu so ndoŋ.
33Bɔrɛ nɛ k bee ponte na
bee ŋini bɔrɛfugboŋ nɛ k bee ba be asheŋ nna,
fanɛ kananɛ kena bee shu a ŋini k ka bee ba na.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1-3M baŋ nu Ebɔrɛ be ebɔl kaa bee muni to
fanɛ bɔrɛ ka ponte, nseŋ wu bɔrɛ ka nyɛkpɛ
ŋ ku awɔlpa to a choŋ, ma kagbene bee ku nna
nɛ kufu e pɛ ma nɛ ma eyur kikɛ e baa chicha.
4Kumo be kaman nɛ ekama e nu mbe ebɔlgboŋ na,
kumo e naa gbri fanɛ bɔrɛ ka ponte na.
Mbe ebɔlgboŋ na baŋ gbri,
shɛŋ maŋ naa ka.
5Ebɔrɛ baŋ ponte ŋ kaŋɛ kesheŋ,
emamachisheŋ nɛ e bee mɔ kɔnɔ
e naa wora.
6Mo e naa shin nɛ kenyɔlɔ bee tɔr kasawule so,
nsaa shin nɛ bɔrɛgboŋ bee ba nɛ mboŋ bee pete.
7Saŋɛ na so basa nɛ e to beeŋ pin mbe kasheŋwora,
nɛ ekama nyam e yige kushuŋ ŋkpal mbe eleŋ so.
8Ndoŋ nna nɛ asɔbɔya e shile n ya ŋana
bumo be edikpaana to.
9Bɔrɛfugboŋ beeŋ shi kelargato be kaseto m ba,
nɛ gbaŋgbaŋ be awo e shi kelargato be esoso m ba.
10Ebɔrɛ baŋ fute, mbe efute bee shin nɛ mbombi
nɛ elɔr kikɛ be nchuana bee wushi a ki fanɛ
abɔrɛjembubi nna.
11-12Ebɔrɛ e naa ponte bɔrɛwɔlpa nɛ e bee shin nɛ
bɔrɛ bee nyɛkpɛ so nɛ e bee sɔ awɔlto
m salga to m buu durnya kikɛ so.
13Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba kasawule so nɛ kakpa bee wushi.
E beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ k ba ŋ gberge basa kusoe,
mo alɛ beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ k ba a ŋini mbe kasha.
14Job, fɛ Ebɔrɛ be emamachisheŋ damta
nɛ e bee wora na be asheŋ nɛnɛ ŋ keni.
15Feeŋ tiŋ m bugi to ŋ kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ k ba
nɛ bɔrɛ be kenyɛkpɛ bee nu Ebɔrɛ
nɛ e nyi kusɔ kikɛ na be kɔnɔ a?
16Fo nyi kusɔ nɛ k kɔ bɔrɛwɔlpa to awɔlto a?
Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nyi kusɔ kikɛ na be emamachisheŋ nna.
17Jemanɛ nɛ keshishɛrsawule so be afu daŋ ber kasawule na so na,
kaboŋ na kikɛ daŋ bel edɛ nna nɛ kaplɛkama wora shruum.
18Ebɔrɛ bre beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa e parga to
m buu so nɛ kakpa e wushi,
ama fo alɛ beeŋ tiŋ n wora loŋ a?
19To, kaŋɛ anyi kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ,
anyi ere be nfɛra wea to nna na.
Anyi maŋ kɔ shɛŋ nɛ an naŋ kaŋɛ.
20A daga ŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ fanɛ mee
sha kemalga mo kutɔ nɛ e mur ma a?
21Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n ta anishi fuloŋ
ŋ keni epeŋi jemanɛ nɛ
bɔrɛwɔlpa maŋ buu kumo so.
22Ama Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be kemaŋkura
fulto a nyɛkpɛ a chɔ epeŋi ga.
23Ebɔrɛ be eleŋgboŋ na shi ga,
anyi alɛ maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kenishiso.
Ama mo alɛ niŋi nna nsaa maa kpɛa edimɛdi to.
24Amoso edimɛdi bee ŋana mo nsaa bunyaŋ mo nna,
ŋkpal manɛ so, e maa keni kamoowu wuraana
nɛ baa fɛ fanɛ b nyi asheŋ ga na a bɔlɔ kenishi.

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka tuge Job to be asheŋ
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bɔla
bɔrɛfu so ŋ kaŋɛ Job le:
2Manɛ nna nɛ fee malga ga loŋ,
saŋɛ nɛ fo mmalga maŋ kɔ shɛŋ amo to?
3To, naniere wora shiriya nɛ ma nɛ fo e ji asheŋ!
Meeŋ bishi fo asheŋ, nɛ fo sa ma amo be atuwebi.
4Ŋ ka daa nase durnya be gbaltɔlase na,
nɛ fo daa wɔtɔ a?
5Wanɛ e chaŋ kumo be mparto nɛ nteŋ to?
M maŋ tama fo ka nyi.
6Manɛ nɛ kumo be kifi yil so?
Wanɛ e pɔr eshabɔrɛ nɛ a kɔ kumo to na?
7Loŋ be kachɛ na be kachipurdidi,
achɛkpabi daa boŋ nshɛ nna,
nɛ ebɔrɛso be emalaika kikɛ daa ji eyur.
8Jemanɛ nɛ n to teku na,
wanɛ e chaŋ kumo be egbaŋ ŋ kuŋ kumo?
9Ma, Ebɔrɛ na, e daŋ ta awɔlpa m buu kumo so fanɛ ketaa,
n shin nɛ tentembiri plɔ buu kumo so.
10Ndoŋ nna nɛ k wora fanɛ ŋ ka
pɔr egbal ŋ kulti teku na n wɔtɔ,
nseŋ shin nɛ k wɔ kumo to fanɛ
ŋ ka ber mbuna so ŋ gba kumo so na.
11Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ kumo le:
“Kakpa nɛ feeŋ tiŋ m ba fo nna na
sa maŋ kaŋ choŋ so ndoŋ.
Kakpa nɛ fo atili lempo na daga e fo nna na.”
12Job, fo daŋ kaŋɛ epeŋi fanɛ k pete kachipurdidi,
nɛ k nu n sa fo a?
13Fo daŋ kaŋɛ karechɛso fanɛ k ba
nɛ kakpa fuli to n lara kumu kpakpaso wuraana
efuli ashi bumo be eŋanakpa a?
14Karechɛ bee shin nɛ abee nɛ ataŋɛ bee lar efuli nna
nɛ baa wu amo fanɛ kananɛ kabaa bee shin nɛ
kusɔbuuso be kananɛ b baa kumo na bee dese nɛnɛ na,
ŋko b ka ta kusɔ n yisi ebɔ wushi so nɛ kumo be nduli
deŋi ebɔ wushiso na so na nna.
15Karechɛ be kefulto bee lara kumukpakpasowuraana
be ashuŋ lubi efuli nna nɛ b maa nya a wora amo.
16Job, fo daŋ yɔ teku be kaseto ŋ ku so a?
Ŋko n nite kumo be kaseto be kasawule so ŋ ku so a?
17Fo daŋ wu kakpa nɛ bubuni wɔ na
be kabuna kenishiso ŋ ku so a?
18Fo nyi kananɛ durnya be mparto sa a?
Kaŋɛ ma, nɛ fo nyi nna na!
19Fo nyi kakpa nɛ kefulto nɛ
tentembiri kikɛ bee shi a ba a?
20Feeŋ tiŋ n juŋkpar amo n yɔ kakpa nɛ e wɔ a?
Fo nyi ekpa nɛ k bee yɔ ndoŋ bre a?
21N nyi geeŋ fanɛ feeŋ tiŋ n wora loŋ,
ŋkpal manɛ so, b kurge fo nna pɔɛŋ
nɛ n to kusɔ kama.
22Fo daŋ yɔ mboŋ nɛ mee yili
abɔrɛjembubi nɛ kunyɔlɔ a?
23N yili amo nna a jo kebagato be jemanɛ
nɛ jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ gberge efuliana na kusoe.
24Nnɛ nɛ bɔrɛ be kenyɛkpɛ bee shi a lar,
ŋko nnɛ nɛ epeŋilarkpa be afu bee shi a ba?
25Wanɛ e chaŋ kubɔr n sa bɔrɛchugboŋ
nseŋ bugi ekpa n sa bɔrɛfugboŋ?
26Wanɛ e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba
keshishɛrsawule nɛ ekama maŋ wɔ so na?
27Wanɛ e naa wurge kasawule wɔlso so nchu
nɛ afitiri bumbuŋ bee kɔr kumo so?
28Wanɛ e la bunyaŋ nɛ bɔrɛ, amo tuto?
29-30Wanɛ e kurge abɔrɛjembubi be yiri kikɛ,
nɛ a bee shin nɛ nchu bee ki fanɛ ajembu
nɛ mbombi nɛ apa be nchu bee wushi a ki abɔrɛjembubi?
31Feeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ achɛkpabi e ba abar so
fanɛ amo nɛ baa tre koshi nɛ mbe bibi nna a?
32Feeŋ tiŋ ŋ ŋini achɛkpabi kusɔ nɛ a beeŋ baa wora,
ŋko n ta achɛkpabi nɛ baa tre Shishirigboŋ nɛ
Shishiribi n yili amo be eyilikpa a?
33Fo nyi mbra nɛ e wɔtɔ n sa awɔlpa to be asɔ a?
Fo alɛ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ mbra na
e shuŋ kasawule so a?
34Feeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ awɔlpa nɛ a shin nɛ bɔrɛgboŋ e ba a?
35Fo e naa kaŋɛ bɔrɛ nɛ k bee nyɛkpɛ a?
Nɛ fo e naa kaŋɛ kumo, k bee nu a sa fo a?
36Fo e naa ŋini ebɔnbɔŋɛ kechali
nɛ ketar be jemanɛ nɛ a bee ba nsaa yɔ a?
37-38Feeŋ tiŋ ŋ karga awɔlpa ŋko n shin nɛ nchu nɛ a wɔ
amo to na e ba bɔrɛ kasawule wɔlso so a?
39Nɛ akoŋ kɔ ebuluŋ, fo e naa chɛ
amo to nɛ a bee nya asɔbɔya a pɛ a ji a?
40Fo e naa kaŋɛ ebuluŋ nɛ a bee
yɔ amo be edikpa a?
41Wanɛ e naa sa ejɔnɔkoso
nɛ amo be bibi ajibi
jemanɛ nɛ akoŋ kɔ amo nɛ
a bee shu a tre ma a fin ajibi na?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka kraa malga be asheŋ
1Fo nyi jemanɛ nɛ kebee so be mboe nɛ echibir bee kurge a?
Fo daŋ yili ŋ keni a kaa bee kurge amo be bibi a?
2-3Afɔl afanɛ nɛ a bee dii adampo nsaa kurge?
Fo nyi saŋɛ nɛ a bee kurge a?
4Amo be bibi maa chɛr nsaa nya eleŋ
nsaa yige amo nioana be kebɛ so n ya ka ji amo be amu so
nsaa maŋ naa bɛta a ba amo nioana kutɔ ashi kupuŋ to.
5Wanɛ e naa tuge kupuŋ to be ekurma afɔl so
nɛ a bee nya amo be amu a nite a kulti?
6Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nawule e naa chɛ emo to
nɛ a bee tiŋ a wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ nfɔl wɔ kumo be shishɛr to na.
7Kupuŋ to be ekurma ere barga ndegboŋ nna
a wɔ kupuŋ to wɔfɔ ŋkpal a ka maa sha awɔr so.
Amo alɛ maaŋ shuli nɛ esa e pɛ amo n ta amo n shuŋ.
8Ama a bee nite a kulti abee so nna
a fin afitiri bumbuŋ a ji.
9Kupuŋ to be kena beeŋ shuli
m ba kaa wɔ fo kenalu to nsaa shuŋ a sa fo a?
10Feeŋ tiŋ n ta kubɔ to be kebarga
n wɔtɔ kumo n shin nɛ k dɔ a?
Ŋko n shin nɛ k gberge katekpa
m pumpuŋ kudɔ to a?
11Feeŋ shuli n to eyur n lɛ kumo so nɛ k ta eleŋgboŋ
nɛ k kɔ na n shuŋ ashuŋ kpakpaso n sa fo a?
12Feeŋ shuli n yirda kumo nɛ k sulɔ fo
ayu teŋiso m bar fo nɛ fo wɔtɔ mpuro to a?
13Nyiŋgbeŋ bee ber atɛ to manaŋ manaŋ ga,
ama kumo alɛ maaŋ tiŋ n firgi n fo tɔkɔrkɔ so.
14Nyiŋgbeŋ bee yige kumo be afule nna
a nase kasawule nɛ kasawule na e bel amo edɛ.
15K maŋ nyi fanɛ esa ŋko kusɔbɔya ko
beeŋ tiŋ n chichi amoso m bure.
16K bee wora nna fanɛ
afule na ka maŋ la kumo peya na.
Kumo alɛ be kegben jiga be asheŋ
maŋ tir kumo.
17Ŋkpal manɛ so, mee to kumo
kusɔbɔya wulpo nɛ k maŋ nyi shɛŋ.
18Ama nɛ k baŋ fara a shile,
k bee choŋ egbaŋɛdiipo so nna nsaa mushe bumo.
19Fo, Job e sa egbaŋɛ eleŋ
ŋko amo be kubɔ so be afuibi na a?
20Fo e shin nɛ a bee tiŋ a tɛ fanɛ abamber a,
ŋko a fute eleŋso a funti basa na a?
21B baaŋ dii egbaŋɛ a yɔ kena to,
a bee mur aya kasawule nna ŋ kpa eshishɛr,
n shile eleŋso n luri kena na to.
22A maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ baa tre kufu,
amo alɛ maa wu tokobi nsaa shile kumo.
23Amo be bediipo be akɔsɔ bee kpla
abar nna nsaa nyɛkpɛ epeŋi so.
24Egbaŋɛ bre maaŋ tiŋ n yili boeŋ.
Kena to be mbel baŋ shu,
a bee yarase a yɔ kena to nna.
25Kabel baŋ shu, baa fute eleŋso nna.
Baa nu kena be asheŋ kufɔ nna,
nsaa nu amo be bediipoana be mmalga.
26Jemanɛ nɛ kɔl bee firgi a yɔ kelargato be kaseto
ketarso na, fo e ŋini kumo nɛ k keparga atɛ n firgi a?
27Fo e naa kaŋɛ kusore nɛ k bee firgi esoso
nsaa tɔ kumo be kesha abee be awɔlto a?
28K bee ta kebee be awɔlto nna a ki kumo pe,
nɛ kebee na be afalta na e baa kuŋ kumo.
29Ndoŋ nɛ k bee shi a keni kufɔ nɛ tatato,
nsaa wu kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ nya m pɛ n ji.
30Ejɔnɔkoso bee bar asɔ nɛ e bee pɛ nna
nɛ emo be bibi e baa chala a mel amo so a ji.

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka kraa malga asheŋ
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ Job le:
2“Ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na,
ama fo, Job malga ŋ kasar ma ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ
m maŋ wora n nyalɛ.
To, sa ma mmalga nɛ m bishi fo na be atuwebi naniere.”
Job ka tuge Ebɔrɛ be kamalga to be asheŋ
3Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le:
4“Ma alɛ e la wanɛ nɛ n tiŋ n tuge fo mmalga?
Mee wora ma kɔnɔ kare nɛ m malga ŋ kasar fo.
5N daŋ malga kela koŋwule ŋko ale anyɔ ko nna,
ama m maaŋ naŋ malga kikɛ.”
6Kede be kaman nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ ko ber m ba
nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bɔla kumo to
ŋ kaŋɛ Job le:
7“Kilgi fo anishito n shoŋi ma nseŋ sa ma
asheŋ bishiso ere be atuwebi!
8Fee sha nɛ fo ŋini fanɛ m maa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so.
Ma e maŋ wora n nyalɛ, fo ere e wora n nyalɛ, ŋko?
9Fo eleŋ fo ma eleŋ so a?
Fo ebɔl beeŋ tiŋ m ponte to fanɛ meya a?
10Kumo ere shin nɛ ekama e wu kemaŋkura
nɛ yukugboŋ nɛ fo kɔ na.
11Keni basa nɛ baa maŋ bumo be amu so,
nseŋ shin nɛ fo kanya agbogboŋ e bar
bumo kaseto nɛ ŋ keni!
12To, bar bumo nɛ kumukpakpaso wuraana
kaseto nseŋ chichi bumo so kakpa nɛ b wɔ na!
13Ta kesaŋɛ ŋ ŋmea bumo be ekama nseŋ gama bumo
n ya puli nchaŋ to!
14Nɛ fo tiŋ n wora ade kikɛ, ŋ gbagba beeŋ shuli so
fanɛ fo e kɔ kashenteŋ.
15Keni churu le.
Ma e to kumo nɛ fo kikɛ.
Ama afitiri nawule nɛ k bee ji fanɛ kena.
16Keni kananɛ k pɔl eyur to
nsaa kɔ eleŋ aya ase loŋ.
17Kumo be kodu yil nna fanɛ
kakubadibi,
nɛ kumo be ebɛaŋ malɛ pɔlto nɛnɛ.
18Kumo be awibi be eleŋ du fanɛ
danyaŋ peper ŋko kebɛlso nna.
19Ma e to kumo nɛ k kɔ eleŋ a chɔ
ma asɔ toso kikɛ,
ama ŋ kraa chɔ kumo eleŋ.
20Abee to nɛ k bee nya afitiri a ji
nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ a ka na malɛ e baa wɔ ndoŋ a pel.
21-22Ndibi nɛ a yil lɔrkar be kiyoyul to
nɛ k bee dese a wushi nsaa ŋana
agasa nɛ a yil kakpa nɛ k bee pete nchu na to.
23Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na bee da nchu a buu kumo gba,
k bee dese boeŋ nna a maa lɔ kufu.
24Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ m buu kumo be anishi so m pɛ kumo?
Ŋko n ta kusɔ ŋ kɔl kumo be kamuna to m pɛ kumo?”

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka kraa malga asheŋ
1Feeŋ tiŋ n ta kɔrɔtɔ be dariwa m pɛ
kusɔbɔya gboŋ lubi nɛ k wɔ teku to nna a?
Ŋko ŋ kre kumo be kɔnɔ afɔl n nase a?
2Feeŋ tiŋ n futi kumo be kamuna n wɔtɔ kumo efɔl a?
Ŋko n ta dariwa n da kumo be ketaya m bɔl a?
3K beeŋ shuli ŋ kule fo fanɛ fo wu kumo kuwɔr a?
Ŋko m malga boeŋ boeŋ n sa fo a?
4K beeŋ shuli fanɛ k beeŋ baa la
fo kenya mbaanaayɔ a?
5Feeŋ tiŋ n chɛ kumo afɔl fanɛ kabuibi
n sa fo mbia nɛ b keta a pɛl a?
6Eyawujipo beeŋ shuli n ji kumo be kebɛ a?
Baaŋ shuli ŋ kuya kumo to n fa a?
7Esa beeŋ tiŋ n da kumo kekpa
ŋko n to kumo malfa m mɔ a?
8Fo baŋ tu kumo ŋ kɔ kela koŋwule,
fo maaŋ naŋ shuli n tu kumo ŋ kɔ kikɛ.
9Esa kama nɛ e wu kusɔkpaŋ lubi gboŋgboŋi na
kenishiso bee paŋ mbe kenyɛn nna nseŋ tɔr kasawule.
10Nɛ esa kikɛ maŋ kɔ eleŋ nɛnɛ nɛ e tiŋ
n tu kumo ŋ kɔ,
kumo ere wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n tu ma ŋ kɔ?
11Ma e naa yili asheŋ a sa durnya kikɛ,
ma alɛ maŋ ji esa kikɛ be kukɔ.
12Shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ ko a laŋɛ kusɔkpaŋ lubi
gboŋgboŋi ere be aya be kaplɛa so
nseŋ bugi kumo be keshi nɛ eleŋ be asheŋ to ŋ kaŋɛ fo.
13Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n luu kumo be kawɔl,
ŋko n ta kebarga n wɔtɔ kumo be kɔnɔ to.
14Esa kikɛ maŋ shuli m bugi kumo be kɔnɔ,
ŋkpal manɛ so,
kumo be kɔnɔ to be anyi bee keta kufu nna.
15Abɛlso be asɔ kuŋkumuso e buu
kumo be kaman kikɛ so.
Amo alɛ pɛ abar nna a kɔ eleŋ fanɛ kejembu.
16Kekama pɛ kumo barkasa to be kpakpa nna,
afu gba maaŋ tiŋ n luri amo be kefɛato.
17Amo alɛ naŋ pɛ abar nna ga
nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ m marga amo ashi abar so.
18Kusɔkpaŋ lubi gboŋgboŋi ere
baŋ kpa kamuna to, edɛ e naa lar.
Kumo be anishi malɛ bee kpa edɛ nna
fanɛ epeŋi ka pete na.
19Edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ e naa lar kumo be kɔnɔ to,
a shin nɛ edɛ be adondulombi bee parga to a sɔ kaplɛkama.
20Edishi malɛ bee lar kumo be kamuna to nna,
fanɛ kapuliya fuloŋ ka bɛ asure so nɛ edishi bee kaa kumo to na.
21K baŋ fute, kakpa bee suse edɛ nna,
ŋkpal edɛ be adondulombi kaa bee lar
kumo be kɔnɔ to so.
22Kumo be kubɔ kɔ eleŋ ga,
nɛ ekama nɛ e tu kumo,
kufu bee pɛ mo nna nɛ e baa chicha.
23Kumo be kawɔl be kaplɛkama maŋ du pɔtɔ pɔtɔ,
kumo kikɛ baa du kpakpa nna fanɛ kebɛlso na.
24Kumo be kagbene so du kpakpa ga nna
fanɛ kuboo.
25Kusɔkpaŋ lubi gboŋgboŋi ere
baŋ lara kumo be kumu efuli
kufu bee pɛ belempo gba nna
nɛ b baa shile.
26Tokobi ŋko kekpa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ
n doro kumo kikɛ.
27Danyaŋ ŋko abɛlso be akɔsɔ
du fanɛ agasa ŋko ndibi wuso
nna n sa kumo.
A maaŋ tiŋ n wora kumo shɛŋ.
28Atanyembi maa shin nɛ k bee shile,
ŋkpal manɛ so, k maa ŋana amo.
Ketababu be kejembu malɛ du
fanɛ kuyu be kewabi nna n sa kumo.
29Kaprɛ bre du fanɛ kegasa nna n sa kumo,
basa baa kpa kumo akpa, k bee mushe bumo nna.
30K baa gbeye depɔ to, kumo be epun so
be afɔfɔ nɛ a du fanɛ mpɛlanfu na
bee kori depɔ nna nsaa nase kubɔr.
31Nɛ k baŋ muni nchu be kechimbi to malɛ
nchu na bee fɔnɔto nna nɛ teku na to e baga to
fanɛ ŋku ka bɛ edɛ so a falte na.
32Nɛ kumo be kubɔr e baa nyɛkpɛ a bɛ kumo so
nɛ teku be nchu na e ka kupɔpɔ.
33Kupɔrso kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ durnya to
nɛ k kɔ kenyɛn n fo kumo so.
K maa ŋana kufu kikɛ.
34Kumo e la ewura asɔbɔya ŋana so kikɛ to.
Amoso k bee keni amo kikɛ jiga nna.

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
Job ka tuge Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kamalga na to be asheŋ
Job
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job malɛ kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le:
2“Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, n nyi fanɛ fo e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.
Ma alɛ nyi fanɛ feeŋ tiŋ n wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha.
3Fee bishi kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ mee malga ga,
jemanɛ nɛ ma mmalga maŋ kɔ shɛŋ amo to.
Kashenteŋto, asɔ nɛ a baŋ ma kepinto so ga
be asheŋ nɛ m malga.
4Fo kaŋɛ ma fanɛ n lo to n nu fo kutɔ
nseŋ sa asheŋ bishiso nɛ feeŋ bishi ma na
be atuwebi.
5Beko kutɔ nɛ n daŋ nu fo asheŋ,
ama naniere bre ŋ gbagba wu fo kenishiso.
6Amoso nɛ ŋ gbagba be asheŋ bee nu ma agbo
nɛ n tuba nseŋ chena nsunɔ to,
a ŋini kebɔltofinfin nɛ k kɔ ma.”
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka naŋ nɛfa Job be asheŋ
7Job ka malga n loge nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Job mo nekpa, Ɛlifaz nɛ e shi Teman be kadegboŋ to na le: “Kusɔ nɛ ma kayɛrbi Job kaŋɛ a laŋɛ ma kaplɛa so na la kashenteŋ nna, ama n nya agbo nna n wora fo nɛ fo nekpaana benyɔ na, ŋkpal men ka kini keji kashenteŋ na so. 8Amoso mee sha fanɛ men ta egbolu ashunu nɛ ekpakpa ashunu n ya sa Job nɛ e ta amo n yili men be katelamu to n lara sarga chɔɔso nɛ k beeŋ par ma. Kumo be kaman nɛ ma kayɛrbi Job e kule Ebɔrɛ n sa menyi nɛ n sɔ mbe kekule na nsaa maaŋ naŋ wora menyi kusɔ nɛ k daga menyi ŋkpal menyi be kawuli so. Menyi maŋ malga kusɔ nɛ k daga a laŋɛ ma kaplɛa so fanɛ kananɛ ma kayɛrbi Job bre wora na.”
9Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job mo nekpaana besa na, Ɛlifaz nɛ Bildad nɛ Zofa, wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ bumo na, nɛ Ebɔrɛ sɔ Job be kekule nɛ e kule n sa bumo na.
Asheŋ ka nyalɛ n sa Job be asheŋ
10Job ka kule Ebɔrɛ n sa mo nekpaana na be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ shin nɛ e naŋ nya asɔ nɛ e daa kɔ nseŋ paŋ amo na be kekama be ntuŋ anyɔso nseŋ naŋ dii kedama ga n ti so. 11Kumo be kaman nɛ Job wora kejigboŋ n sa mo niopibiana kikɛ nɛ mo teri draana kikɛ ashi mbe laŋ to. B daŋ ba wushi mo kagbene nseŋ lolo mo nna a laŋɛ etɔrɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ sa ekpa nɛ a ba mo so na kikɛ be kaplɛa so nna. Bumo be ekama daŋ sa mo amansherbi nɛ shuwa be kepinibi nna.
12Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ nɛfa Job a chɔ kananɛ e daŋ nɛfa mo dra na. E daŋ naŋ sa mo mbolpɔ ŋgboŋ kuduana nɛ enyɔma ŋgboŋ ashe nɛ egbolu dɔso be benyɔ nyɔ be ntuŋ kagboŋ nɛ ekurma kagboŋ nna.
13E daŋ naŋ sa Job bibinyɛn ashunu nɛ bibiche asa nna. 14Nɛ Job nase mo pibiche sososo na Jimaima nseŋ nase enyɔsopo na Keziya nɛ esasopo na malɛ Kɛren Happuk. 15Eche kikɛ daa maŋ wɔ kasawule na so nɛ e walɛ kebita n fo Job be bibiche asa na so. Bumo tuto malɛ daŋ yige kapetɛ nna n sa bumo nɛ bumo danyɛnsoana na.
16Ade kikɛ be kaman, Job daŋ ji nfɛ kalfa nɛ adena nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu. E daŋ nya benanabiana nna hale n ya fo bumo nɛ b bɛ so benasopo gba. 17E daŋ bel nɛnɛ nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
SOSOSO
(Nshɛ 1—41)
Kashenteŋ be kagbenefuli be asheŋ
1Kagbenefuli la bekama nɛ b maa sɔ
alubiworapoana be kasotoji,
ŋko a kute alubiworapoana to
a wora asheŋ,
ŋko a tu basa nɛ b maŋ kɔ saŋɛ
a sa Ebɔrɛ na peya nna.
2Bumo be kagbenefuli bee shi
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be keŋini
be kebaawɔtɔ to nna;
nɛ kumo be loŋ malɛ
wɔ bumo be nfɛra to
kapa nɛ kanyɛ.
3Loŋ be basa du fanɛ
boŋkarase be ndibi
nɛ a bee sɔr asɔrso
saŋɛ nɛ k daga na nna.
Amo be afantaŋ maa
gbaŋgbaŋ kikɛ.
Kusɔ kama nɛ baa wora
bee nite nɛnɛ nna a sa bumo.
4Ama mannɛ loŋ nɛ k du
n sa alubiworapoana bre.
Bumo ere du fanɛ asɔ be afɔfɔ
nɛ afu bee foŋ n ya kaa lɛ nna.
5Ebɔrɛ be demujiachɛ na,
alubiworapoana kikɛ beeŋ ji n tɔr.
Ebɔrɛ beeŋ barga bumo
ashi basa nɛ baa ŋana mo
nsaa wora asheŋ
nɛ a niŋi ekpa na kutɔ.
6Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa kuŋ
loŋ be basa nsaa ŋini bumo ekpa.
Ama alubiworapoana bre be ekpa
kɔ bumo nna a yɔ kemur to.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
and his chosen king.
3They say, “Let's cut the ropes
and set ourselves free!”
4In heaven the Lord laughs
as he sits on his throne,
making fun of the nations.
5The Lord becomes furious
and threatens them.
His anger terrifies them
as he says,
6“I've put my king on Zion,
my sacred hill.”
7 I will tell the promise
that the Lord made to me:
“You are my son, because today
I have become your father.
8Ask me for the nations,
and every nation on earth
will belong to you.
9 You will smash them
with an iron rod
and shatter them
like dishes of clay.”
10Be smart, all you rulers,
and pay close attention.
11Serve and honor the Lord;
be glad and tremble.
12Show respect to his son
because if you don't,
the Lord might become furious
and suddenly destroy you.
But he blesses and protects
everyone who runs to him.
translation_text:
Ebɔrɛ be ewura laraso be asheŋ
1Manɛ nna nɛ efuliana na
bee kre ŋkre lubi loŋ?
Manɛ nna nɛ amo be basa
bee kre asheŋ fuloŋ?
2Nɛ manɛ nna nɛ amo be bewura
nɛ bejuŋkparpoana bee wora kɔnɔ
a kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
nɛ mbe esa lara so na?
3Le nɛ baa kaŋɛ:
“Men shin nɛ an suge anyi be amu
ashi bumo be enɔ to,
nseŋ nya anyi be amu a ji.”
4Ebɔrɛ tase mbe kuwurputi so
esoso nna ŋ kplaŋ bumo so,
nsaa mushe bumo.
5Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ fɛa bumo so agbo so,
nɛ kufu pɛ bumo ga, nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo le:
6“M buu ma ewura nna n chena Zayɔn
nɛ k la ma kebee cheembi na so
ashi Jerusalɛm to.”
7Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ le:
“Meeŋ bɔ kɔnɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
nase n sa ma na be kubɔya.”
E yɛ: “Fo e la m pibinyɛn na;
kabre, ŋ ki fo tuto.
8Amoso kule ma,
nɛ n ta efuliana ere kikɛ n sa fo;
nseŋ shin nɛ durnya ere kikɛ
e ki feya.
9Feeŋ ta fo kebɛlso be kuwurkpabi
n ji amo so kuwura.
Fo alɛ beeŋ bure amo to
fanɛ ebɔ be kapuya na
10Amoso menyi bewura e kaŋ asoe
n nu le be kefiɛso ere;
Menyi, durnya to be bejuŋkparpo
e koya le be asheŋ ere.
11Men ta kufu nɛ kechicha chicha
a shuŋ Ebɔrɛ, nseŋ shin nɛ
men be ŋgbene e fuli.
12Men baa jɔŋɛ a bunyaŋ mo pibi na,
nɛ mannɛ aloŋ e beeŋ nya agbo
epul to m mur menyi.
E bee nɛfa nsaa kuŋ bekama
nɛ baa shile a yɔ mo kutɔ na nna.”

english_text:
(Written by David when he was running from his son Absalom.)
An Early Morning Prayer
1 I have a lot of enemies, Lord.
Many fight against 2me and say,
“God won't rescue you!”
3But you are my shield,
and you give me victory
and great honor.
4I pray to you, and you answer
from your sacred hill.
5I sleep and wake up refreshed
because you, Lord,
protect me.
6Ten thousand enemies attack
from every side,
but I am not afraid.
7Come and save me, Lord God!
Break my enemies' jaws
and shatter their teeth,
8because you protect
and bless your people.
translation_text:
Saŋɛ nɛ Ewura David bee shile mo pibinyɛn Absalɔm be kena na nɛ e boŋ kashɛ ere.
1N nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
ŋ kɔ bedoŋ damta ga.
Basa damta e naa kɔ ma.
2Baa malga a gbiti ma nna
a kaŋɛ le:
“Ebɔrɛ maaŋ mɔlga mo.”
3Ama, fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na,
e naa kuŋ ma saŋkikɛ.
Fo e naa shin nɛ mee kɔ a pɔɔ so,
nsaa shin nɛ mee nya
bunyaŋgboŋ nɛ keleŋto.
4N shu n tre fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na;
nɛ fo nu ma kushu
ashi fo kebee cheembi na so.
5Saŋkama nɛ n dese a di,
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
bee keni ma so nna,
a kuŋ ma kanyɛ na kikɛ.
6Hale bedoŋ kagboŋ kulti ma gba,
m maa lɔ kufu.
7Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, mɔlga ma.
Gberge ma doŋana kusoe,
n shin nɛ bumo be eleŋ e yɔɔ,
nɛ b sa maŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ ma so.
Fɛta ma doŋana be atayamu,
nseŋ gbaŋ bumo be anyi.
8Kekuŋ shi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nna.
Enyɛnpe nɛfa fo basa.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.)
An Evening Prayer
1You are my God and protector.
Please answer my prayer.
I was in terrible distress,
but you set me free.
Now have pity and listen
as I pray.
2How long will you people
refuse to respect me?
You love foolish things,
and you run after
what is worthless.
3The Lord has chosen
everyone who is faithful
to be his very own,
and he answers my prayers.
4 But each of you
had better tremble
and turn from your sins.
Silently search your heart
as you lie in bed.
5Offer the proper sacrifices
and trust the Lord.
6There are some who ask,
“Who will be good to us?”
Let your kindness, Lord,
shine brightly on us.
7You brought me more happiness
than a rich harvest
of grain and grapes.
8I can lie down
and sleep soundly
because you, Lord,
will keep me safe.
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ be asheŋ
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
nɛ fo la ma ekumpo,
nu ma kekule.
N daa wɔ tɔrɔ to nna
nɛ fo chɛ ma to.
Amoso wu ma kuwɔr
nseŋ nu ma kekule.
2Saŋɛ mo nɛ menyi basa ere
beeŋ yige ma katege?
Saŋɛ mo nɛ menyeeŋ yige
asheŋ fuloŋ be kasha,
nɛ kebaaju a buu efɛ so?
3Men nyi fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na,
ta basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ niŋiso nna
ŋ ki mbe mbia;
saŋkama nɛ n shu n tre mo,
e bee nu ma kekule nna.
4Men ta kufu nɛ kechicha chicha
n lar men be alubi to.
Men keni men be ŋgbene to nɛnɛ,
saŋɛ nɛ men nawule dese kelaŋ so na.
5Men lara sarga nɛ k daga
n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na,
nseŋ yirda mo.
6Basa damta bee kule
Ebɔrɛ nna a kaŋɛ le:
“Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛfa anyi,
nseŋ wu anyi kuwɔr.”
7Kagbenefuli nɛ fo sa ma na chɔ
kumo nɛ aboyu damta be keburi
ŋko nsa damta be kenya
bee sa basa ga.
8Mee dese nna a di nɛ kagbenewushi,
ŋkpal manɛ so, fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
nawule e naa kuŋ ma.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use flutes.)
A Prayer for Help
1Listen, Lord, as I pray!
Pay attention when I groan.
2You are my King and my God.
Answer my cry for help
because I pray to you.
3Each morning you listen
to my prayer,
as I bring my requests to you
and wait for your reply.
4You are not the kind of God
who is pleased with evil.
Sinners can't stay with you.
5No one who boasts can stand
in your presence, Lord,
and you hate evil people.
6You destroy every liar,
and you despise violence
and deceit.
7Because of your great mercy,
I come to your house, Lord,
and I am filled with wonder
as I bow down to worship
at your holy temple.
8You do what is right,
and I ask you to guide me.
Make your teaching clear
because of my enemies.
9 Nothing they say is true!
They just want to destroy.
Their words are deceitful
like a hidden pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
10Punish them, God,
and let their own plans
bring their downfall.
Get rid of them!
They keep committing crimes
and turning against you.
11Let all who run to you
for protection
always sing joyful songs.
Provide shelter for those
who truly love you
and let them rejoice.
12Our Lord, you bless those
who live right,
and you shield them
with your kindness.
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ
Kekuŋ be kabɔrɛkule be asheŋ
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ;
nu ma kekule;
nɛ ma kushuto.
2Ma Ebɔrɛ nɛ ma ewura,
nu ma kushu.
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
mee kule fo nna,
chɛ ma to.
3Kachipurso kikɛ
fee nu ma kekule nna.
Mee ta ma asheŋ tirso nna
a ba kaa nase fo anishito,
nsaa jo fo atuwebi.
4Alubi maa par fo.
Fo alɛ nɛ alubiworapo
maaŋ tiŋ n chena abar so.
5Ŋkpensheŋ wura maaŋ tiŋ
n yili fo anishito.
Fo kishi basa
nɛ baa wora alubi ga.
6Feeŋ mur befɛpo kikɛ.
Fo kishi kumukpakpaso
nɛ kafule ga.
7Ama ŋkpal fo kuwɔrwu ka shi so,
meeŋ tiŋ m ba fo bɔrɛlambu to;
m ba gbir bunyanso,
m maŋkura fo.
8Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, juŋkpar ma
ŋkpal fo ka bee wora asheŋ niŋiso so.
Ŋini ma fo ekpa niŋiso na,
ŋkpal ŋ ka kɔ bedoŋ damta so.
9M maaŋ tiŋ n yirda
kusɔ nɛ ma doŋana bee kaŋɛ.
Esa be kejija nɛ baa fin.
Efɛ e bɔlɔ bumo be mmalga to
fanɛ kemaŋ chiŋgeliŋ nɛ asɔ buu so.
Bumo be adonduloŋ malɛ bee ku
efɛ nawule nna.
10Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, shin nɛ b ji n tɔr.
Shin nɛ bumo gbagba be ŋkre
e shin nɛ b mur.
Ju bumo ashi fo anishito,
ŋkpal bumo be alubi nɛ
kumukpakpaso so.
11Ama bumo nɛ baa fin kekuŋ
ashi fo kutɔ na bre be ŋgbene
bee fuli bumo nna,
nɛ baa boŋ nshɛ kagbenefuliso
saŋkama.
Baa kuŋ bumo nɛ baa sha fo na;
Shin nɛ bumo be ŋgbene
e baa fuli bumo ŋkpal fo so.
12Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
fee nɛfa bekama nɛ baa wora
fo kasonu nsaa wora asɔ nɛ niŋi nna.
Fee kuŋ bumo nna fanɛ kananɛ
kebɛlso be kusɔ kuŋso
bee kuŋ benapo na.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.
)
A Prayer in Time of Trouble
1 Don't punish me, Lord,
or even correct me
when you are angry!
2Have pity on me and heal
my feeble body.
My bones tremble with fear,
3and I am in deep distress.
How long will it be?
4Turn and come to my rescue.
Show your wonderful love
and save me, Lord.
5If I die, I cannot praise you
or even remember you.
6My groaning has worn me out.
At night my bed and pillow
are soaked with tears.
7Sorrow has made my eyes dim,
and my sight has failed
because of my enemies.
8 You, Lord, heard my crying,
and those hateful people
had better leave me alone.
9You have answered my prayer
and my plea for mercy.
10My enemies will be ashamed
and terrified,
as they quickly run away
in complete disgrace.
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ
Tɔrɔ to be kabɔrɛkule be asheŋ
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
sa maŋ nya agbo ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ
n wora n jija,
nseŋ gberge ma kusoe agbo so.
2Wu ma kuwɔr nseŋ sa ma eleŋ;
ŋkpal manɛ so,
ma eyur kikɛ chɛl ma nna
3nɛ mee shin nɛ n wu.
Saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ chɛ ma to,
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ?
4Enyɛnpe, ba mɔlga ma.
Wu ma kuwɔr,
nseŋ mɔlga ma ashi luwu to.
5M baŋ wu,
m maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n fur fo,
ŋko n nyiŋi fo asheŋ.
6Kebɔltofinfin e naa mɔ ma.
Kanyɛso kikɛ, ma anishichubi
bee pɔ ma gedo nɛ kaputi nna.
7N doŋana shin nɛ
kagbenejija pɛ ma,
nɛ n shu nɛ ma anishi puŋi
a maŋ naa wu nɛnɛ.
8Basa lubi, men shile ma so!
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na,
nu ma kushu.
9E nu ma kekule nseŋ wu ma kuwɔr,
n wora ma asheŋ tirso n sa ma.
10Anishinyɔr beeŋ pɛ ma doŋana kikɛ
nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo ga nɛ b wulto,
nseŋ pal kaman n ta nyɔmɔ n shile n yɔ.

english_text:
(Written by David.
He sang this to the Lord because of Cush from the tribe of Benjamin.)
The Lord Always Does Right
1You, Lord God,
are my protector.
Rescue me and keep me safe
from all who chase me.
2Or else they will rip me apart
like lions attacking a victim,
and no one will save me.
3I am innocent, Lord God!
4I have not betrayed a friend
or had pity on an enemy
who attacks for no reason.
5If I have done any of this,
then let my enemies
chase and capture me.
Let them trample me to death
and leave me in the dirt.
6Get angry, Lord God!
Do something!
Attack my furious enemies.
See that justice is done.
7Make the nations come to you,
as you sit on your throne
above them all.
8Our Lord, judge the nations!
Judge me and show that I
am honest and innocent.
9 You know every heart and mind,
and you always do right.
Now make violent people stop,
but protect all of us
who obey you.
10You, God, are my shield,
the protector of everyone
whose heart is right.
11You see that justice is done,
and each day
you take revenge.
12Whenever your enemies refuse
to change their ways,
you sharpen your sword
and string your bow.
13Your deadly arrows are ready
with flaming tips.
14An evil person is like a woman
about to give birth
to a hateful, deceitful,
and rebellious child.
15 Such people dig a deep hole,
then fall in it themselves.
16The trouble they cause
comes back on them,
and their heads are crushed
by their own evil deeds.
17I will praise you, Lord!
You always do right.
I will sing about you,
the Lord Most High.
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ be asheŋ
1N nyɛnpe nɛ ma Ebɔrɛ,
m ba fo kutɔ nna nɛ fo kuŋ ma,
nseŋ mɔlga ma.
Sɔ ma n yige ashi basa nɛ b ju
a buu ma so na kutɔ.
2Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ baaŋ kpɛa ma to
fanɛ buluŋ ka kpɛa kusɔbɔya to na.
Esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n sɔ ma
ama fo nawule.
3Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
nɛ n wora kulubi n da
esa ko so,
4ŋko n lar nlɔpo kikɛ kaman,
ŋko ŋ kɔ n sɔ n doŋ be asɔ
nɛ e maŋ wora shɛŋ;
5nɛ n wora asɔ ere be kekama,
kumo ere fo shin nɛ
ma doŋana e ju ma n pɛ.
Shin nɛ b chichi ma so m mɔ
nseŋ yige ma n lɛ shishɛr to.
6Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
nya agbo ŋ kpa n niŋi to
n tu ma doŋana nɛ b nya agbo ga na;
yili to n shin nɛ kashenteŋji e di efuli.
7Shin nɛ basa kikɛ e shɛr fo anishito
nɛ fo yili esoso n ji bumo so kuwura.
8Fo e la durnya kikɛ be demujipo na.
Amoso Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
shin nɛ n ji n lar;
ŋkpal ŋ kaa bee ji kashenteŋ,
a maŋ wora n jija so.
9Fo la Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee wora
asheŋ nɛ a niŋi nna,
a nyi esa be kagbene to
nɛ mbe nfɛra to be asheŋ kikɛ.
Shin nɛ alubiworapo e yige
alubi be kebaawora,
nseŋ kuŋ basa lela ashi alubi to.
10Fo, Ebɔrɛ e la ma ekumpo.
Fo e naa kuŋ
kagbene koŋwulewurana kikɛ.
11Fee ji asheŋ nɛ amo
be ekpa so nna,
nsaa nya agbo karechɛ kikɛ
ŋkpal alubi so.
12Nɛ alubiworapo maŋ tuba
ashi mbe alubi to,
fo yee fo tokobi nna
nseŋ gberge fo keta to;
13fo ta kudur lubi nna n daŋɛ
fo atanyembi nɛ fo gberge
alubiworapoana kusoe.
14Basa di alubi be dampo,
nseŋ bela ase nɛ b kurge
kafulesheŋ nɛ kumukpakpaso.
15Ama bumo gbagba
e naŋ kilgi n tɔr amaŋ chiŋgeliŋ
nɛ b kur n nase beko na to.
16Bumo gbagba be alubi beeŋ laŋɛ
n deŋi bumo be amu so,
nɛ kananɛ baa tintiŋ basa
a shin nɛ baa wora asheŋ na
e laŋɛ bumo so.
17Mee chɔrɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ga
ŋkpal e ka bee wora asheŋ
nɛ amo be ekpa so so.
Meeŋ boŋ kashɛ n di
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ
nɛ e wɔ esoso na epaŋ.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.
)
The Wonderful Name of the Lord
1Our Lord and Ruler,
your name is wonderful
everywhere on earth!
You let your glory be seen
in the heavens above.
2 With praises from children
and from tiny infants,
you have built a fortress.
It makes your enemies silent,
and all who turn against you
are left speechless.
3I often think of the heavens
your hands have made,
and of the moon and stars
you put in place.
4 Then I ask, “Why do you care
about us humans?
Why are you concerned
for us weaklings?”
5 You made us a little lower
than you yourself,
and you have crowned us
with glory and honor.
6 You let us rule everything
your hands have made.
And you put all of it
under our power—
7the sheep and the cattle,
and every wild animal,
8the birds in the sky,
the fish in the sea,
and all ocean creatures.
9Our Lord and Ruler,
your name is wonderful
everywhere on earth!
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ be asheŋ
Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura nɛ dimɛdi be bunyaŋ be asheŋ
1Enyɛnpe, anyi be Ebɔrɛ,
fo keshi nɛ fo mamachi
be aworbi wɔ durnya ere
be kaplɛkama;
nɛ fo kemaŋkura wɔ esoso.
2Hale mbi popɔrbi nɛ mbiwurbi
kikɛ bee boŋ nshɛ a di fo epaŋ.
Fo kuŋ fo kumu
ashi fo doŋana be enɔ to.
Fo alɛ maaŋ sa
fo doŋ kikɛ kashuli.
3N baŋ keni awɔlpa nɛ fo to,
nɛ kananɛ fo ta kufɔl nɛ
achɛkpabi n yili amo be eyilikpa,
4kusɔ nɛ mee bishi e la fanɛ:
“Manɛ bre e baa la dimɛdi
nɛ mbe asheŋ tir fo,
nɛ fee fɛ mbe asheŋ loŋ?”
5Fo nawule e chɔ dimɛdi
ashi fo asɔ toso kikɛ to.
Fo alɛ e sa mo
kemaŋkura nɛ bunyaŋ.
6Nseŋ shin nɛ e ki fo
asɔ toso kikɛ to be ejuŋkparpo.
Fo ta asɔ kikɛ fanɛ
7mbolpɔ nɛ ana
nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya,
8nɛ mbuibi nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ
nɛ teku to be asɔ kikɛ
m bɔɔ mo enɔ nna.
9Enyɛnpe anyi be Ebɔrɛ,
fo keshi nɛ fo mamachi be aworbi
wɔ durnya ere be kaplɛkama nna.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “The Death of the Son.”)
Sing Praises to the Lord
1I will praise you, Lord,
with all my heart
and tell about the wonders
you have worked.
2God Most High, I will rejoice;
I will celebrate and sing
because of you.
3When my enemies face you,
they run away and stumble
and are destroyed.
4You take your seat as judge,
and your fair decisions prove
that I was in the right.
5You warn the nations
and destroy evil people;
you wipe out their names
forever and ever.
6Our enemies are destroyed
completely for all time.
Their cities are torn down,
and they will never
be remembered again.
7You rule forever, Lord,
and you are on your throne,
ready for judgment.
8You judge the world fairly
and treat all nations
with justice.
9The poor can run to you
because you are a fortress
in times of trouble.
10Everyone who honors your name
can trust you,
because you are faithful
to all who depend on you.
11You rule from Zion, Lord,
and we sing about you
to let the nations know
everything you have done.
12You did not forget
to punish the guilty
or listen to the cries
of those in need.
13 Please have mercy, Lord!
My enemies mistreat me.
Keep me from the gates
that lead to death,
14and I will sing about you
at the gate to Zion.
I will be happy there
because you rescued me.
15 Our Lord, the nations fell
into their own pits,
and their feet were caught
in their own traps.
16You showed what you are like,
and you made certain
that justice is done,
but evil people are trapped
by their own evil deeds.
17The wicked will go down
to the world of the dead
to be with those nations
that forgot about you.
18The poor and the homeless
won't always be forgotten
and without hope.
19Do something, Lord!
Don't let the nations win.
Make them stand trial
in your court of law.
20Make the nations afraid
and let them all discover
just how weak they are.
translation_text:
Ewura Deevid be kashɛ be asheŋ
Ebɔrɛ be kapandi be kashɛ
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, meeŋ bugi
ma kagbene kikɛ n fur fo,
nseŋ kaŋɛ etumasesheŋ
nɛ fo wora kikɛ.
2Ma kagbene beeŋ fuli ma
nɛ n ji eyur ŋkpal fo so.
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ,
meeŋ boŋ kashɛ
n di fo ketre epaŋ.
3N doŋana baŋ wu fo,
baa kilgi nna a shile,
nsaa fiti a tɔr a wu.
4Eshenteŋjipo e la fo
nɛ fee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so.
Fo ji ma asheŋ kashenteŋ be ekpa so
n ŋini fanɛ n ji n lar.
