amo be kananɛ a sa so.
18Nɛ fanɛ ŋ karga fo nfɛra gba,
e beeŋ baa chɔ teku ase be eshishɛr.
M baŋ di n tiŋi kelaŋ so gba,
ma nɛ fo e kraa la.
19O Ebɔrɛ, fo daa beeŋ shuli m mɔ
kumukpakpasowuraana nna
nseŋ kuŋ ma ashi bumo be kamɛaŋ to,
k daa beeŋ par ma ga.
20Baa kaa malga mmalga lubi
a gbiti fo nna nsaa jija fo ketre.
21O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, ma alɛ gba kishi
bekama nɛ b kishi fo nseŋ kini fo,
n lar fo kaman na nna.
22Yurkishi nawule nɛ ŋ kɔ a sa bumo;
n ta bumo nna fanɛ ma doŋana.
23O Ebɔrɛ, mige ma to ŋ keni,
m pin ma kagbene to;
wora ma ŋ keni
m pin ma nfɛra fɛso.
24Sa maŋ shin nɛ m baa bɔla
ekpa lubiana so a wora asheŋ,
ama baa juŋkpar ma ashi fo
ekpa nɛ k dese mbaanaayɔ na so.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
A Prayer for the Lord's Help
1Rescue me from cruel
and violent enemies, Lord!
2They think up evil plans
and always cause trouble.
3 Their words bite deep
like the poisonous fangs
of a snake.
4Protect me, Lord, from cruel
and brutal enemies,
who want to destroy me.
5Those proud people have hidden
traps and nets
to catch me as I walk.
6You, Lord, are my God!
Please listen to my prayer.
7You have the power to save me,
and you keep me safe
in every battle.
8Don't let the wicked succeed
in doing what they want,
or else they might never
stop planning evil.
9They have me surrounded,
but make them the victims
of their own vicious lies.
10Dump flaming coals on them
and throw them into pits
where they can't climb out.
11Chase those cruel liars away!
Let trouble hunt them down.
12Our Lord, I know that you
defend the homeless
and see that the poor
are given justice.
13Your people will praise you
and will live with you
because they do right.
translation_text:
Kekule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kechɛto be asheŋ
1O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, mɔlga ma ashi
kumukpakpasowuraana be enɔ to!
Nseŋ kuŋ ma ashi bedoŋ
nyaŋnyaŋso kutɔ.
2Ŋkre lubi e wɔ bumo be ŋgbene to,
nɛ baa bar kebagato karechɛ kikɛ.
3Bumo be nnɔ to be mmalga
du fanɛ awɔ lubi be kubɔr
ashi esa be eyur to nna.
4O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, baa kuŋ ma ashi
kumukpakpasowuraana nɛ bedoŋ
nyaŋnyaŋso nɛ baa fin ma
kemur na be enɔ to.
5Kamoowuwuraana ŋana nna
n sho ajigbelɛ nɛ ashewu ma
ekpa to a fin ma nɛ b pɛ.
6O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, fo e la ma Ebɔrɛ.
Jande nu ma kekule nseŋ chɛ ma to!
7O Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ,
fo la ma emɔlgapo lempo,
fo e naa kuŋ ma ashi kekɔ
nɛ bedoŋ bee kɔ ma kikɛ to.
8O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ
kumukpakpasowuraana e nya
kusɔ nɛ baa sha.
Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ b maaŋ yige
kebaakre asheŋ lubi.
9Shin nɛ basa nɛ b kulti ma n wɔtɔ
be mmalga lubi e laŋɛ n ji bumo.
10Shin nɛ kedɛmurmur e tɔr
bumo be amu so.
Ta bumo n lɛ edepɔmaŋ to
nɛ b lar ŋ gben.
11Sa maŋ shin nɛ basa nɛ baa
ku asheŋ a deŋi beko e nya kusɔ
nɛ baa sha kasawule ere so kikɛ.
Shin nɛ asheŋ lubi e ba basa
nyaŋnyaŋso so m mur bumo cheche.
12Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, n nyi fanɛ fo
e naa kɔ a sa betirpo,
nsaa shin nɛ betentaŋasepo
bee nya asɔ nɛ a daga bumo.
13Kashenteŋto, basa nɛ bumo
be asheŋ woraso niŋi beeŋ baa
wɔ fo kutɔ a kpaŋ fo ketre na.

english_text:
(A psalm by David.)
A Prayer for the Lord's Protection
1I pray to you, Lord!
Please listen when I pray
and hurry to help me.
2 Think of my prayer
as sweet-smelling incense,
and think of my lifted hands
as an evening sacrifice.
3Help me to guard my words
whenever I say something.
4Don't let me want to do evil
or waste my time doing wrong
with wicked people.
Don't let me even taste
the good things they offer.
5Let your faithful people
correct and punish me.
My prayers condemn the deeds
of those who do wrong,
so don't let me be friends
with any of them.
6Everyone will admit
that I was right
when their rulers are thrown
down a rocky cliff,
7and their bones lie scattered
like crushed rocks
on top of a grave.
8You are my Lord and God,
and I look to you for safety.
Don't let me be harmed.
9Protect me from the traps
of those violent people,
10and make them fall
into their own traps
while you help me escape.
translation_text:
Kaaseso be kabɔrɛkule be asheŋ
1O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
fo nɛ mee shu a tre;
nya manaŋ m ba chɛ ma to!
Jande nu ma kekule ere.
2Nu ma kekule fanɛ
duwu be efɛa belbelso,
nseŋ wu ma enɔana
nɛ m maŋ so ere fanɛ kaaseso
be sarga nɛ mee lara a sa fo.
3O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, chɛ ma to,
nɛ jemanɛ kikɛ nɛ meeŋ bugi
ma kɔnɔ, meeŋ baa de mmalga
nɛ a beeŋ lar kumo to so.
4Baa lara ma kagbene ashi
asheŋ lubi be kebaawora to
nɛ ma kebaatu basa lubi
a wora asheŋ gela gela to.
Sa maŋ shin nɛ m baa tu bumo
a ji bumo be kejigboŋana gba.
5Shin nɛ fo basa niŋiso
e baa ŋini ma ekpa;
ŋ kaŋ wora n foe
nɛ b gberge ma kusoe.
M maaŋ shin nɛ basa lubi
e maŋkura ma kikɛ,
ŋkpal manɛ so, mee kule
Ebɔrɛ nna a gbiti bumo.
6Jemanɛ nɛ bumo be bewuraana
beeŋ shi abee be awɔlto n tɔr to na,
nɛ basa beeŋ pin fanɛ asheŋ
nɛ m malga na la kashenteŋ nna.
7Kananɛ baa baŋɛ ndibi to
wurwurbi na nɛ bumo be awibi
beeŋ buri to n dese
nchaŋ be nnɔ ase.
8Ama ma ere be anishi yuu fo
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na so nna,
a fin fanɛ fo baa kuŋ ma
nsaa maŋ shin nɛ n wu!
9O Ebɔrɛ, baa kuŋ ma ashi ajigbelɛ
nɛ basa lubi bee sho ma to.
10Shin nɛ bumo gbagba e tɔr
bumo be ajigbelɛ to, nseŋ shin nɛ
ma ere e bɔla amo ase n choŋ
nɛ shɛŋ maŋ wora ma.

english_text:
(A special psalm and a prayer by David when he was in the cave.)
A Prayer for Help
1 I pray to you, Lord.
I beg for mercy.
2I tell you all my worries
and my troubles,
3and whenever I feel low,
you are there to guide me.
A trap has been hidden
along my pathway.
4Even if you look,
you won't see anyone
who cares enough
to walk beside me.
There is no place to hide,
and no one who really cares.
5I pray to you, Lord!
You are my place of safety,
and you are my choice
in the land of the living.
Please answer my prayer.
I am completely helpless.
6Help! They are chasing me,
and they are too strong.
7Rescue me from this prison,
so I can praise your name.
And when your people notice
your wonderful kindness to me,
they will rush to my side.
translation_text:
Kekule Ebɔrɛ be kechɛto be asheŋ
1Mee shu a tre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nna;
a kule mo fanɛ e wu ma kuwɔr.
2Mee ta ma nfubel kikɛ nna a bar mo;
nsaa kaŋɛ mo ma etɔrɔ kikɛ be asheŋ.
3M baa pɔ aba kiyoyu to,
mo e naa ŋini ma kusɔ nɛ
k daga fanɛ n wora.
Bedoŋ ŋana n sho ma kejigbelɛ
ashi ekpa nɛ mee nite so nna.
4M baŋ keni ŋ kulti, mee wu fanɛ
esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e chɛ ma to,
esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e kuŋ ma.
Ma asheŋ malɛ maŋ tir esa kikɛ.
5Fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na,
nɛ mee kule nɛ fo chɛ ma to!
Fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ma ekumpo.
Fo nawule nɛ mee fute a yigeso
ashi ma kebaawɔtɔ to.
6Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, nu ma kushu
nɛ mee shu a fin fo kechɛto ere.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, asheŋ gben ma nna na.
Mɔlga ma ashi ma doŋana be enɔ to;
b chɔ ma eleŋ ga nɛ m maaŋ tiŋ bumo.
7Lara ma ashi ebesa nɛ kafɔŋ to;
saŋɛ na so, meeŋ kpaŋ fo
ashi fo basa be nshɛr to,
ŋkpal kelela nɛ fo wora ma so.

english_text:
(A psalm by David.)
A Prayer in Time of Danger
1Listen, Lord, as I pray!
You are faithful and honest
and will answer my prayer.
2 I am your servant.
Don't try me in your court,
because no one is innocent
by your standards.
3My enemies are chasing me,
crushing me in the ground.
I am in total darkness,
like someone long dead.
4I have given up hope,
and I feel numb all over.
5I remember to think about
the many things you did
in years gone by.
6Then I lift my hands in prayer,
because my soul is a desert,
thirsty for water from you.
7Please hurry, Lord,
and answer my prayer.
I feel hopeless.
Don't turn away
and leave me here to die.
8Each morning let me learn
more about your love
because I trust you.
I come to you in prayer,
asking for your guidance.
9Please rescue me
from my enemies, Lord!
I come to you for safety.
10You are my God. Show me
what you want me to do,
and let your gentle Spirit
lead me in the right path.
11Be true to your name, Lord,
and keep my life safe.
Use your saving power
to protect me from trouble.
12I am your servant.
Show how much you love me
by destroying my enemies.
translation_text:
Kekule Ebɔrɛ be kechɛto be asheŋ
1Jande Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
nu ma kekule!
Nu ma kushu nseŋ wu ma kuwɔr.
Bɔla fo kashenteŋji nɛ kebaawɔtɔ
niŋiso so n sɔ ma n yige.
2Sa maŋ ji ma, fo kayɛrbi demu;
ŋkpal manɛ so, esa kikɛ be kebaawɔtɔ
maŋ niŋi ashi fo anishito.
3Bedoŋ bee ju ma nna a kulti
nɛ mee tɔr a koso.
Tentembiri mina to nɛ n wɔ,
fanɛ esa nɛ e wu a dese nchaŋ to
dra dra kikɛ na.
4Ŋkpal loŋ so ma tama kikɛ loge nna,
nɛ ma kagbene jija ma m baŋ so.
5Mee nyiŋi asheŋ nɛ fo wora
nfɛ damta nɛ a choŋ na kikɛ nna
nsaa fɛ amo be asheŋ.
6M maŋ ma enɔana so
ashi kabɔrɛkule to a shoŋi fo nna,
Kananɛ kasawule wɔlso bee sha
nchu na nɛ ma kiyoyu gba
bee shu a fin fo.
7Jande Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
nu ma kabɔrɛkule manaŋ!
Ma tama kikɛ loge.
Sa maŋ pal kaman n sa ma.
Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ meeŋ ya ti
bumo nɛ b teŋ wu n yɔ
bubuni to na so.
8Ŋkpal ŋ ka ta ma yirda
n deŋi fo so so,
shin nɛ m baa nyiŋi fo kasha
nɛ k maa loge na be asheŋ
kachipurso kikɛ.
Mee kule fo nna nɛ fo ŋini ma
ekpa nɛ meeŋ baa bɔla so
a wora asheŋ.
9O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, mɔlga ma
ashi bedoŋ be enɔ to,
ŋkpal manɛ so, fo kutɔ
nɛ mee ba nsaa nya kekuŋ.
10Fo e la ma Ebɔrɛ.
Ŋini ma kusɔ nɛ fee sha
fanɛ n wora, nseŋ shin nɛ fo
Kiyoyu nɛ e du boeŋ na e baa
juŋkpar ma ekpa kikɛ so.
11Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, baa kɔ a kuŋ ma
fanɛ kananɛ fo nase kɔnɔ na.
Bɔla fo kumɔlga be eleŋ na so
m mɔlga ma ashi etɔrɔ to.
12Ŋkpal fo kasha nɛ k maa loge
nɛ fo kɔ n sa ma so,
mɔ ma doŋana kikɛ nseŋ mur
bekama nɛ baa kɔrfɛ ma na;
ŋkpal manɛ so, n la fo kayɛrbi nna.

english_text:
(By David.)
A Prayer for the Nation
1I praise you, Lord!
You are my mighty rock,
and you teach me
how to fight my battles.
2You are my friend, my fortress,
where I am safe.
You are my shield,
and you made me the ruler
of our people.
3 Why do we humans mean anything
to you, our Lord?
Why do you care about us?
4We disappear like a breath;
we last no longer
than a faint shadow.
5Open the heavens like a curtain
and come down, Lord.
Touch the mountains
and make them send up smoke.
6Use your lightning as arrows
to scatter my enemies
and make them run away.
7Reach down from heaven
and set me free.
Save me from the mighty flood
8of those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth.
9In praise of you, our God,
I will sing a new song,
while playing my harp.
10By your power, kings win wars,
and your servant David is saved
from deadly swords.
11Won't you keep me safe
from those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth?
12Let's pray that our young sons
will grow like strong plants
and that our daughters
will be as lovely as columns
in the corner of a palace.
13May our barns be filled
with all kinds of crops.
May our fields be covered
with sheep by the thousands,
14and every cow have calves.
Don't let our city be captured
or any of us be taken away,
and don't let cries of sorrow
be heard in our streets.
15Our Lord and our God,
you give these blessings
to all who worship you.
translation_text:
Kekule Ebɔrɛ n sa efuli be asheŋ
1Meeŋ kpaŋ fo, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ!
Fo e la ma kefalta gboŋ.
Fo alɛ e naa ŋini ma kananɛ
meeŋ baa kɔ kena.
2Fo e la n teri shaso
nɛ ma ekumpo lempo,
Fo nɛ mee shile a mata
nsaa nya ma kumu.
Fo e la ma kebɛlso be kusɔ kuŋso,
fo alɛ e shin nɛ mee ji kuwura
anyi be basa so.
3O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, wanɛ e la dimɛdi,
nɛ fee keni a wu mo;
nɛ mbe asheŋ tir fo le ere bre?
4Dimɛdi baa du fanɛ afu futeso nna;
mbe nchɛ bee choŋ nna fanɛ kiyoyul.
5O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, bugi esoso
be kuwɔlpa fanɛ patisa
ŋ gbelge m ba;
Beta abeeana na,
nɛ edishi e kaa amoso.
6Shin nɛ bɔrɛ e nyɛkpɛ
m pesaŋ fo doŋana to;
To fo atanyembi
m bar kebagato bumo to,
nɛ b lara aya n shile.
7Shi esoso ndoŋ n teŋi fo enɔ to
m pɛ ma n chule ashi nchu
be kechimbi to n sɔ ma n yige;
mɔlga ma ashi efuli pɔtɛ
be basa be enɔana to.
8Bumo e la befɔ nɛ b maa ji
kashenteŋ nsaa ku efɛ
a bɔ ntaŋ na.
9O Ebɔrɛ, meeŋ boŋ
kashɛ popɔr ŋ kpaŋ fo;
meeŋ laŋ jaŋjilaŋ
m boŋ kashɛ n sa fo.
10Fo e naa shin nɛ bewura
bee kɔ a pɔɔ so,
fo e naa kɔ a mɔlga fo kayɛrbi,
Ewura Deevid ashi kena to.
11Jande kɔ m mɔlga ma alɛ gba
ashi befɔ fɛpoana nɛ b maa
ji kashenteŋ na be enɔ to.
12An kule Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e shin nɛ anyi
be mbrantiɛbia e baa du fanɛ ndibi
nɛ a daŋ yili a kɔ eleŋ;
nɛ anyi be bibiche malɛ e baa
du fanɛ eshabɔrɛ nɛ b pɔr n ji
kuwurlambu kebita na.
13Shin nɛ anyi be mpuro
e bɔlɔ adɔjibi be yiri kikɛ
nɛ anyi be mbolpɔ e kurge ga
n salga n sɔ kaplɛkama,
14n shin nɛ anyi be ana gba
e kurge ga.
Sa maŋ shin nɛ amo be kekama
e gboŋi kedampo n lɛ kikɛ.
Sa maŋ shin nɛ bedoŋ e kɔ m pɔɔ
anyi be kadegboŋ na so,
ŋko m pɛ anyi be beko n yɔ
kenyaya to efuli wɔfɔ so.
Fo alɛ e sa maŋ shin nɛ an nu
kagbenejija be kushu ashi anyi
be abɔrbi so kikɛ.
15Kagbenefuli la bekama nɛ le be asheŋ
bee wora bumo to na peya nna.
Kagbenefuli la bekama nɛ bumo
be Ebɔrɛ la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya nna.

english_text:
(By David for praise.)
The Lord Is Kind and Merciful
1I will praise you,
my God and King,
and always honor your name.
2I will praise you each day
and always honor your name.
3You are wonderful, Lord,
and you deserve all praise,
because you are much greater
than anyone can understand.
4Each generation will announce
to the next your wonderful
and powerful deeds.
5I will keep thinking about
your marvelous glory
and your mighty miracles.
6Everyone will talk about
your fearsome deeds,
and I will tell all nations
how great you are.
7They will celebrate and sing
about your matchless mercy
and your power to save.
8You are merciful, Lord!
You are kind and patient
and always loving.
9You are good to everyone,
and you take care
of all your creation.
10All creation will thank you,
and your loyal people
will praise you.
11They will tell about
your marvelous kingdom
and your power.
12Then everyone will know about
the mighty things you do
and your glorious kingdom.
13Your kingdom will never end,
and you will rule forever.
Our Lord, you keep your word
and do everything you say.
14When someone stumbles or falls,
you give a helping hand.
15Everyone depends on you,
and when the time is right,
you provide them with food.
16By your own hand you satisfy
the desires of all who live.
17Our Lord, everything you do
is kind and thoughtful,
18and you are near to everyone
whose prayers are sincere.
19You satisfy the desires
of all your worshipers,
and you come to save them
when they ask for help.
20You take care of everyone
who loves you,
but you destroy the wicked.
21I will praise you, Lord,
and everyone will respect
your holy name forever.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka la esa nsaa wu kuwɔr be asheŋ
1Meeŋ maŋ fo so nseŋ kpaŋ fo,
ma Ebɔrɛ nɛ ma Ewura;
Ma alɛ beeŋ maŋkura
fo ketre saŋkama.
2Meeŋ baa kpaŋ fo karechɛ kikɛ
nsaa maŋkura fo ketre
hale mbaanaayɔ.
3Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shi ga,
nseŋ daga fanɛ b baa
kpaŋ mo saŋkama.
Ekama maaŋ tiŋ m pin
mbe kishi na to.
4Kekurgeto kama to ebi beeŋ ji
fo emamachisheŋ nɛ a bee
mɔ kɔnɔ na be asheŋ n sa
bumo be kaman to ebi.
5Baaŋ baa malga fo kemaŋkura
be kela be asheŋ.
Bumo alɛ beeŋ baa fɛ fo asheŋ
woraso nɛ a bee mɔ kɔnɔ na
be asheŋ jemanɛ kikɛ.
6Basa beeŋ baa malga fo
asheŋgboŋ be asheŋ
nsaa ber fo keshi be kubomboŋ
a sa beko.
7Baaŋ baa ji fo alelasheŋ
damta be asheŋ a sa beko
nsaa boŋ nshɛ kagbenefuliso
a laŋɛ fo asheŋ niŋiso
be kaplɛa so.
8Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na la eshapo
nɛ e bee wu kuwɔr nna,
mo alɛ maa nya agbo manaŋ manaŋ;
mbe kasha maa chɛrga kikɛ.
9Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee wora
ekama kelela nsaa kɔ kashagboŋ
a sa mbe asɔ to so kikɛ nna.
10O Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,
fo asɔ to so kikɛ beeŋ kpaŋ fo,
nɛ fo basa kikɛ e di fo epaŋ.
11Baaŋ baa ji fo kuwurji
be kemaŋkura be asheŋ;
bumo alɛ beeŋ baa malga
fo eleŋgboŋ be asheŋ.
12Saŋɛ na so edimɛdi kikɛ
beeŋ pin fo ashuŋgboŋ
nɛ fo kuwurji be kemaŋkura
nɛ kela be asheŋ.
13Fo kuwurji wɔtɔ nna mbaanaayɔ;
k maŋ kɔ ekar,
fo alɛ bee ji kuwura nna,
yili kenana ko n ya fo
kenana ko to ebi so nna.
An Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, fo e naa wora
a bɔlɔ fo nnɔ naseso so nsaa wora
kusɔ kama nɛ fo kaŋɛ feeŋ wora.
14Fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa chɛ
bumo nɛ b wɔ tɔrɔ to to,
nsaa niŋi bumo nɛ b tɔr to.
15Asɔ futeso kikɛ bee keni
fo anishito nna nɛ fo sa
amo ajibi jemanɛ nɛ k daga.
16Fo e naa bugi enɔ to a sa
kusɔ futeso kikɛ kumo be
asheŋ tirso yila yila so.
17Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be
kesheŋ wora kikɛ niŋi nna,
mo alɛ kɔ kasha nna
n sa mbe asɔ to so kikɛ.
18E wɔ bekama nɛ baa tre mo
kagbene koŋwule so na kutɔ nna.
19Mo alɛ bee sa bekama nɛ baa
bunyaŋ mo na asɔ nɛ a tir bumo nna
nsaa nu bumo be kekule a mɔlga
bumo ashi etɔrɔ to.
20Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee kuŋ bekama
nɛ baa sha mo na nna,
ama kumukpakpasowuraana bre,
e bee mur bumo nna.
21Jemanɛ kikɛ ma ere beeŋ
kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na;
ekama e sa mbe ketre cheembi na
bunyaŋ mbaanaayɔ.

english_text:
Shout Praises to the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
With all that I am,
I will shout his praises.
2I will sing and praise
the Lord God
as long as I live.
3You can't depend on anyone,
not even a great leader.
4Once they die and are buried,
that will be the end
of all their plans.
5The Lord God of Jacob blesses
everyone who trusts him
and depends on him.
6 God made heaven and earth;
he created the sea
and everything else.
God always keeps his word.
7He gives justice to the poor
and food to the hungry.
The Lord sets prisoners free
8and heals blind eyes.
He gives a helping hand
to everyone who falls.
The Lord loves good people
9and looks after strangers.
He defends the rights
of orphans and widows,
but destroys the wicked.
10The Lord God of Zion
will rule forever!
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Kekpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na awɔrso be asheŋ
1Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Meeŋ ta ma kagbene kikɛ
ŋ kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
2Meeŋ boŋ nshɛ ŋ kpaŋ
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na saŋɛ nɛ
n wɔ ŋkpa to ere.
3Men sa maŋ ta menyi be yirda
n wɔtɔ edimɛdi be bejuŋkparpo to.
Dimɛdi bomin kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ
m mɔlga esa.
4B baŋ wu baa bɛta a
yɔ shishɛr to nna;
Loŋ be kachɛ na bumo be
ŋkre kikɛ bee ba ekar nna.
5Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la an nananyɛn
Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ na bee nɛfa ekama
nɛ e yirda mo nseŋ ta mbe kumu
n to mo so na nna.
6Ebɔrɛ e to esoso nɛ kasawule;
mo e to teku nɛ kumo to
be asɔ kikɛ nyam.
Jemanɛ kikɛ e bee wora a bɔlɔ
mbe nnɔ naseso so nna.
7Mo e naa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so
a sa betirpo nsaa sa bumo nɛ
akoŋ kɔ kusɔ jiso.
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa lara basa
nɛ b ti ebu ashi kabuti to.
8Mo koŋwule na e naa bugi
etanpo be anishi.
Mo e naa pɛ bumo nɛ b tɔr to
a niŋi to a yili nsaa sha basa
nɛ bumo be kebaawɔtɔ niŋi.
9Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa keni befɔ so,
nsaa ji a chɛ amunibi nɛ bekulpoche to;
ama kumukpakpasowuraana bre,
e bee mur bumo nna.
10Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, nɛ e la Jerusalɛm
be Ebɔrɛ na, bee ji kuwura nna
mbaanaayɔ!
Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!

english_text:
Sing and Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Our God is kind,
and it is right and good
to sing praises to him.
2The Lord rebuilds Jerusalem
and brings the people of Israel
back home again.
3He renews our hopes
and heals our bodies.
4He decided how many stars
there would be in the sky
and gave each one a name.
5Our Lord is great and powerful!
He understands everything.
6The Lord helps the oppressed,
but he smears the wicked
in the dirt.
7Celebrate and sing!
Play your harps
for the Lord our God.
8He fills the sky with clouds
and sends rain to the earth,
so that the hills
will be green with grass.
9He provides food for cattle
and for the young ravens,
when they cry out.
10The Lord doesn't care about
the strength of horses
or powerful armies.
11The Lord is pleased only
with those who worship him
and trust his love.
12Everyone in Jerusalem,
come and praise
the Lord your God!
13He makes your city gates strong
and blesses your people.
14God lets you live in peace,
and he gives you
the very best wheat.
15As soon as God speaks,
the earth obeys.
16He covers the ground with snow
like a blanket of wool,
and he scatters frost
like ashes on the ground.
17God sends down hailstones
like chips of rocks.
Who can stand the cold?
18At his command the ice melts,
the wind blows,
and streams begin to flow.
19God gave his laws and teachings
to the descendants of Jacob,
the nation of Israel.
20But he has not given his laws
to any other nation.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Keboŋ kashɛ ŋ kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be asheŋ
1Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Keboŋ nshɛ ŋ kpaŋ an
Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na walɛ ga.
Kekpaŋ mo wɔ ebel ga
nseŋ daga loŋ.
2Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee lɔŋɛ
Jerusalɛm nna a pɔr;
nsaa bɛta mbe basa nɛ b daŋ pɛ
n yɔ kenyaya to ashi efuli pɔtɛ
wɔfɔ so na a ba epe.
3Mo e naa ti kagbenejijawuraana
kagbene nsaa chɛ bumo be alɔana.
4Mo e yili kananɛ achɛkpabi
beeŋ ba sa awɔlpa so
nseŋ nase amo be kekama
ketre a tre kumo.
5An Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shi alegaiso
nsaa kɔ eleŋ ga.
Mo alɛ bee pin kusɔ kama to nna.
6Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa chɛ bebɔlpo to,
nsaa bar kumukpakpasowuraana kaseto.
7Men boŋ nshɛ ŋ kpaŋ
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na;
men laŋ ejaŋjilaŋ m boŋ
nshɛ n sa anyi be Ebɔrɛ na.
8Mo e naa shin nɛ abɔrɛwɔlpa
bee salga to a buu kaplɛkama so;
nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba kasawule so
a shin nɛ afitiri bee kɔr abee so.
9Mo e naa sa asɔbɔya kusɔ jiso
nsaa bela ejɔnɔkoso fɔlbi
jemanɛ kikɛ nɛ a shu n tre mo.
10Mannɛ egbaŋɛ be eleŋ nɛ
benapo lempoana be asheŋ e naa
par Ebɔrɛ nsaa fuli mbe kagbene.
11Basa nɛ baa bunyaŋ mo
nɛ bumo nɛ bumo be yirda
wɔ mbe kasha nɛ k maa
chɛrga na so be asheŋ e naa
par mo nsaa fuli mbe kagbene.
12O Jerusalɛmebi, men kikɛ e maŋ
Enyɛnpe menyi be Ebɔrɛ na so
nseŋ kpaŋ mo!
13Mo e shin nɛ menyi be kadegboŋ
be mbunagboŋ na kɔ eleŋ;
mo alɛ e naa nɛfa menyi be basa.
14Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ men wɔ
kayurwushi to ashi
menyi be efuli so na.
Mo e naa sa menyi ajibi lela.
15Ebɔrɛ malɛ baŋ malga kenishipereso,
k bee sɔ durnya kikɛ to manaŋ nna.
16Mo e naa shin nɛ kunyɔlɔ
bee sɔ kaplɛkama,
nɛ bɔrɛfurbi malɛ bee ba
fanɛ kalabɛr na.
17Mo e naa shin nɛ abɔrɛjembubi
bee wurge to fanɛ awarabi na.
Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n chena awo
nɛ e bee shin nɛ k bee ba na to.
18Mo koŋwule na e naa malga
nɛ afu bee ber,
nɛ abɔrɛjembubi na bee ŋalga
a ki nchu a shile mbombi to na.
19Ebɔrɛ e ta mbe mbraana
nɛ keŋiniana n sa mbe basa
nɛ b la an nananyɛn Jeekɔb
nɛ e daa wɔtɔ dra dra na
be kaman to ebi;
bumo e ki Israɛl be efuli so
be basa na.
20E maŋ wora le n sa efuli pɔtɛ
kama so be basa;
b maŋ nyi mbe mbraana gba.
Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!

english_text:
Come Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Shout the Lord's praises
in the highest heavens.
2All of you angels,
and all who serve him above,
come and offer praise.
3Sun and moon,
and all of you bright stars,
come and offer praise.
4Highest heavens, and the water
above the highest heavens,
come and offer praise.
5Let all things praise
the name of the Lord,
because they were created
at his command.
6He made them to last forever,
and nothing can change
what he has done.
7All creatures on earth,
you obey his commands,
so come praise the Lord!
8Sea monsters and the deep sea,
fire and hail, snow and frost,
and every stormy wind,
come praise the Lord!
9All mountains and hills,
fruit trees and cedars,
10every wild and tame animal,
all reptiles and birds,
come praise the Lord!
11Every king and every ruler,
all nations on earth,
12every man and every woman,
young people and old,
come praise the Lord!
13All creation, come praise
the name of the Lord.
Praise his name alone.
The glory of God is greater
than heaven and earth.
14Like a bull with mighty horns,
the Lord protects
his faithful nation Israel,
because they belong to him.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Durnya kikɛ ka daga kekpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be shɛŋ
1Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Menyi nɛ men wɔ ebɔrɛso na,
men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
2Menyi Ebɔrɛ be emalaika kikɛ,
nɛ ebɔrɛso be beshumpo kikɛ,
men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
3Kufɔl nɛ epeŋi, e baa kpaŋ mo.
Achɛkpabi nɛ e bee nyɛkpɛ
gba e baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
4Ebɔrɛso nɛ k wɔ awɔlto chilili,
nɛ awɔlto be nchuana kikɛ,
e baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
5Men shin nɛ le be asɔ ere kikɛ
e baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ketre.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e malga eleŋso
n to amo kikɛ kuraa.
6Mo koŋwule na e malga eleŋso
nɛ amo be kekama ere nya kumo
be eyilikpa a yil mbaanaayɔ na.
Mbe atande maa chɛrga kikɛ.
7Kasawule so be asɔ keniso kikɛ,
e baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
Teku to be asɔbɔya gboŋgboŋi kikɛ,
nɛ kumo to be asɔ keniso kikɛ
e baa kpaŋ mo.
8Bɔrɛ be kenyɛkpɛ nɛ abɔrɛjembubi
nɛ kunyɔlɔ nɛ awɔlpaana
nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋana nɛ amo kikɛ bee
nu a sa mo na e baa kpaŋ mo.
9Abeegboŋana nɛ abeebiana kikɛ,
nɛ ndibi sɔrsoana nɛ kupo to
be ndibi kikɛ e baa kpaŋ mo.
10Kowu nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya
be yiri kikɛ;
asɔbɔya wurbi be yiri kikɛ
nɛ mbuibi kikɛ e baa kpaŋ
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
11Durnya to be efuliana
kikɛ so be bewuraana,
bewurbi nɛ durnya to be
kenimujipoana kikɛ,
12mbrantiɛbia nɛ besuŋgurbi kikɛ,
basakpar nɛ mbiwurbi kikɛ
e baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
13Asɔ to so kikɛ e baa kpaŋ
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ketre.
Men baa kpaŋ mbe ketre na nawule.
Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura shi ga a chɔ
esoso nɛ kasawule so kikɛ peya.
14Mo e shin nɛ mbe efuli nya eleŋ,
saŋɛ na so, mbe basa, Israɛlebi kikɛ,
nɛ bumo be asheŋ wɔ mbe kagbene to na,
beeŋ baa kpaŋ mo.
Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!

english_text:
A New Song of Praise
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Sing him a new song of praise
when his loyal people meet.
2People of Israel, rejoice
because of your Creator.
People of Zion, celebrate
because of your King.
3Praise his name by dancing
and playing music on harps
and tambourines.
4The Lord is pleased
with his people,
and he gives victory
to those who are humble.
5All of you faithful people,
praise our glorious Lord!
Celebrate and worship.
6 Praise God with songs
on your lips
and a sword in your hand.
7Take revenge and punish
the nations.
8Put chains of iron
on their kings and rulers.
9Punish them as they deserve;
this is the privilege
of God's faithful people.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Kapandi be kasha be asheŋ
1Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Men boŋ kashɛ popɔr n sa
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na;
men baa kpaŋ mo ashi kakpa
nɛ mbe basa nɛ baa ji kashenteŋ
a sa mo shɛr abar so na.
2Israɛl be basa, men shin nɛ menyi
be ŋgbene e fuli menyi ŋkpal menyi
be etopo na so;
menyi Jerusalɛm to be basa malɛ e ji
eyur ŋkpal menyi be ewura so!
3Men ta echakachaka nɛ ejaŋjilaŋ
a boŋ nshɛ nsaa cha a dele
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ketre.
4Ŋkpal manɛ so, mbe basa be asheŋ
bee par mo nna.
Mo alɛ bee ta kemaŋkura nna
a buu bekama nɛ baa bar bumo
be amu kaseto so nsaa mɔlga bumo.
5Ebɔrɛ be basa kama nɛ b nya
le be kemaŋkura ere e shin nɛ
bumo be ŋgbene e baa fuli bumo
nɛ b baa boŋ nshɛ a ji eyur
kapa nɛ kanyɛ kikɛ.
6B baa kpaŋ Ebɔrɛ awɔrso
jemanɛ nɛ b ta bumo be etokobi
jiso m bɔɔ enɔ a yɔ
7nɛ b ya kɔ m pɔɔ efuli pɔtɛana
be basa so ŋ gberge bumo kusoe;
8nseŋ naa kpaŋ mo jemanɛ nɛ baŋ pɛ
efuli pɔtɛana na be bewuraana
nɛ bumo be benimuana nseŋ wɔtɔ
bumo ŋgbɛlɛbiana na.
9Saŋɛ na so baaŋ gberge efuli
pɔtɛana na be basa kusoe
fanɛ kananɛ Ebɔrɛ yili kumo na.
Ebɔrɛ be basa laraso cheembi kikɛ
be kemaŋkura nna na.
Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!

english_text:
The Lord Is Good to His People
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Praise God in his temple.
Praise him in heaven,
his mighty fortress.
2Praise our God!
His deeds are wonderful,
too marvelous to describe.
3Praise God with trumpets
and all kinds of harps.
4Praise him with tambourines
and dancing,
with stringed instruments
and woodwinds.
5Praise God with cymbals,
with clashing cymbals.
6Let every living creature
praise the Lord.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Ebɔrɛ ka walɛ n sa mbe basa be asheŋ
1Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Men baa kpaŋ Ebɔrɛ ashi
mbe bɔrɛlambu to!
Men baa kpaŋ mo ebɔrɛso ashi
mbe kakpa lempo na!
2Men baa kpaŋ mo ŋkpal asheŋ
gboŋgboŋi nɛ e wora so.
Men naa kpaŋ mo ŋkpal e ka
shi m baŋ so so.
3Men baa ta mbel nɛ alaŋsɔ
be yiri kikɛ
a kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
4Men baa laŋ ŋkure a cha
a kpaŋ mo,
nsaa ta ejaŋjilaŋ nɛ nlopi gba
a kpaŋ mo.
5Men baa ta echakachaka nɛ
abɛlso be alaŋsɔ be yiri kikɛ
a laŋ a kpaŋ Ebɔrɛ.
6Asɔ keniso kikɛ e baa kpaŋ
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!
Men baa kpaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na!

english_text:
How Proverbs Can Be Used
1 These are the proverbs
of King Solomon of Israel,
the son of David.
2Proverbs will teach you
wisdom and self-control
and how to understand
sayings with deep meanings.
3You will learn what is right
and honest and fair.
4From these, an ordinary person
can learn to be smart,
and young people can gain
knowledge and good sense.
5If you are already wise,
you will become even wiser.
And if you are smart,
you will learn to understand
6proverbs and sayings,
as well as words of wisdom,
and all kinds of riddles.
7 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of knowledge.
Only a fool rejects wisdom
and good advice.
Warnings against Bad Friends
8My child, obey the teachings
of your parents,
9and wear their teachings
as you would a pretty hat
or a lovely necklace.
10Don't be tempted by sinners
or listen 11when they say,
“Come on! Let's gang up
and kill somebody,
just for the fun of it!
12They're well and healthy now,
but we'll finish them off
once and for all.
13We'll take their valuables
and fill our homes
with stolen goods.
14If you join our gang,
you'll get your share.”
15Don't follow anyone like that
or do what they do.
16They are in a big hurry
to commit some crime,
perhaps even murder.
17They are like a bird
that sees the bait,
but ignores the trap.
18They gang up to murder someone,
but they are the victims.
19The wealth you get from crime
robs you of your life.
Wisdom Speaks
20 Wisdom shouts in the streets
wherever crowds gather.
21She shouts in the marketplaces
and near the city gates
as she says to the people,
22“How much longer
will you enjoy
being stupid fools?
Won't you ever stop sneering
and laughing at knowledge?
23Listen as I correct you
and tell you what I think.
24You completely ignored me
and refused to listen;
25you rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
26“So when you are struck
by some terrible disaster,
27or when trouble and distress
surround you like a whirlwind,
I will laugh and make fun.
28You will ask for my help,
but I won't listen;
you will search,
but you won't find me.
29No, you would not learn,
and you refused
to respect the Lord.
30You rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
31“Now you will eat the fruit
of what you have done,
until you are stuffed full
with your own schemes.
32Sin and self-satisfaction
bring destruction and death
to stupid fools.
33But if you listen to me,
you will be safe and secure
without fear of disaster.”
translation_text:
Aŋasa be tɔnɔ be asheŋ
1Israɛl be ewura Sɔlɔmɔn nɛ e la Deevid pibinyɛn na be aŋasa nde.
2Aŋasa ere beeŋ chɛ fo to nɛ fo nya kanyiasheŋ nɛ kasonu nsaa tiŋ a pin mmalga chiŋgeliŋ be afito.
3A beeŋ chɛ fo to nɛ fo nya
kebaawɔtɔ to be kanyiasheŋ
nsaa kɔ kashenteŋji a tiŋ
a wora asɔ nɛ a daga.
A beeŋ shin nɛ fo baa wɔ
kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso to
nsaa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so.
4Aŋasa ere beeŋ tiŋ n sa
esa nɛ e maa pin asheŋ to
manaŋ manaŋ kanyiasheŋ;
nseŋ sa mbifɔlbi kenyi, n chɛ bumo to
nɛ b baa wora asheŋ nɛ a kɔ tɔnɔ.
5A bee sa benyiashempo
kenyi nna a ti so,
nsaa chɛ bekoyapo to
nɛ baa tiŋ a lara asɔ
nɛ a daga kewora;
6nsaa tiŋ a pin aŋasa
nɛ ablɔmbi nɛ mmalga chiŋgeliŋ
nɛ benyiashempo be mmalga be
atrɔmbi nɛ amo be afito.
Mbrantiɛbia be kasotoji be asheŋ
7Kabɔrɛŋana e la kenyi be sososo.
Ewulpo e naa kini
kanyiasheŋ be kekoya
nɛ kebela be kasogberge.
8M pibinyɛn, kaŋ kusoe n nu
fo tuto be kusɔ nɛ e bee kaŋɛ fo,
nsaa maŋ kplaŋ
fo nio be ŋini gba so.
9Ŋkpal manɛ so
bumo be keŋini na
beeŋ sa fo da lela,
fanɛ kananɛ neemu
ŋko kubɔtoshembi
bee sa esa kela na.
10M pibinyɛn,
belubiworapo baa fule fo
a ŋin fo a wɔtɔ alubi to,
fo sa maa sa bumo kashuli.
11Nɛ b baŋ kaŋɛ fo le:
“Ba tu anyi nɛ an ya ŋana
n dese ekpakar n fin
esa ko m mɔ kenyanyaŋɛso,
12n shin nɛ bumo nɛ b kɔ eleŋ
nɛ alenfia
na e ki bubuni n luri nchaŋ to.
13An wora loŋ anyeeŋ nya
yawukpakpaso be asɔ lela
be yiri yiri,
nɛ an be ebuana e bɔlɔ asɔ
nɛ an suge
fanɛ b ka kɔ kena n suge asɔ na.
14Amoso ba ti anyi so,
saŋɛ na so anyi nɛ fo
beeŋ barga kusɔ kama
nɛ an nya na to.”
15M pibinyɛn,
sa maa tu loŋ be basa
a wora asheŋ.
Baa ji a gelge bumo.
16Ŋkpal manɛ so,
saŋkikɛ, baa jujo nna
nɛ b wora alubi.
Kemɔ esa maŋ la shɛŋ bumo kutɔ.
17Kebaa sho kabuibi kejigbelɛ
nɛ e jɔŋ a keni fo
la asheŋ fuloŋ nna!
18To, loŋ be basa lubi na
bee sho bumo gbagba be amu
ajigbelɛ nna.
B yɛ basa nɛ baa pugi a jo,
ama bumo gbagba be amu
nɛ baa kilgi a mɔ.
19Kayu to nɛ beyu bee paŋ
bumo be ŋkpa.
Loŋ nɛ basa kama
nɛ baa nyaŋɛ to a buu
basa kikɛ bee loge to.
Kanyiasheŋ be asheŋ;
20Men nu nfe,
kanyiasheŋ e wɔ agbembi so
nɛ kebɛ to a tre awɔrso na.
21K wɔ nde be mbunagboŋ
nɛ basa bee bɔla to a lar
nsaa luri na ase nna
a ponte a tre awɔrso a kaŋɛ le:
22“Ewulpo, fee sha fanɛ
fo baa la ewulpo saŋkikɛ nna
nsaa keni kenyi jiga a?
Fo kini kenyi be kekoya nna a?
Saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ fara a koya asheŋ?
23Fo daa nu ma kefiɛ so nna,
ndafanɛ meeŋ sa fo kasotoji lela
nseŋ bugi kagbene
n ŋini fo kusɔ nɛ n nyi.
24Saŋkama mee tre fo
a kaŋɛ fanɛ fo ba ma kutɔ
ama fo kplaŋ ma so
nseŋ kini kenu n sa ma.
25Fo kplaŋ ma kasotoji kikɛ so,
nseŋ kini fanɛ fo maaŋ shin nɛ
n niŋi fo ekpa.
26Amoso, fo baŋ luri tɔrɔ to,
meeŋ mushe fo.
Awurfoŋgboŋ baŋ tu fo,
meeŋ wora fo eyurto.
27Tɔrɔ nɛ awurfoŋ
beeŋ ba fo so
fanɛ afugboŋ ka ber
m bar etɔrɔ
nɛ ebesa nɛ kebaawɔtɔ kekra na.
28Loŋ be saŋɛ na,
feeŋ shu n tre ma, kanyiasheŋ,
ama m maaŋ tuge fo.
Feeŋ fin ma kenishipereso
ama fo maaŋ wu ma.
29Fo yɛ kenyi maŋ la shɛŋ
nseŋ kini kewora
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kasonu.
30Fo kini ma kasotoji
nsaa maŋ shin nɛ
n niŋi fo ekpa.
31Amoso feeŋ ji
kusɔ nɛ fo du na be asɔrso,
nɛ fo gbagba be aworbi
e kilgi a bishi fo.
32Ewulpo be kawuli
e naa bar mo luwu,
nɛ kekini kenyi be kekoya malɛ
bee yɛr esa kemur to.
33Ama esa kama nɛ e bee
wora ma kasonu beeŋ nya kekuŋ.
E maaŋ ba lɔ kufu
fanɛ kusɔ lubi ko beeŋ wora mo.”

english_text:
Wisdom and Bad Friends
1My child, you must follow
and treasure my teachings
and my instructions.
2Keep in tune with wisdom
and think what it means
to have common sense.
3Beg as loud as you can
for good common sense.
4Search for wisdom
as you would search for silver
or hidden treasure.
5Then you will understand
what it means to respect
and to know the Lord God.
6 All wisdom comes from the Lord,
and so do common sense
and understanding.
7God gives helpful advice
to everyone who obeys him
and protects those
who live as they should.
8God sees that justice is done,
and he watches over everyone
who is faithful to him.
9With wisdom you will learn
what is right
and honest and fair.
10Wisdom will control your mind,
and you will be pleased
with knowledge.
11Sound judgment and good sense
will watch over you.
12Wisdom will protect you
from evil schemes
and from those liars
13who turned from doing good
to live in the darkness.
14Most of all they enjoy
being mean and deceitful.
15They are dishonest themselves,
and so are all their deeds.
Wisdom and Sexual Purity
16Wisdom will protect you
from the smooth talk
of a sinful woman,
17who breaks her wedding vows
and leaves the man she married
when she was young.
18The road to her house leads
down
to the dark world
of the dead.
19Visit her, and you will never
find the road to life again.
20Follow the example
of good people
and live an honest life.
21If you are honest and innocent,
you will keep your land;
22if you do wrong
and can never be trusted,
you will be rooted out.
translation_text:
Kanyiasheŋ be tɔnɔ be asheŋ
1M pibinyɛn,
baa koya asɔ nɛ mee ŋini fo
nsaa nyiŋi asɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ
fo baa wora na saŋkikɛ.
2Baa bugi asoe
a koya kanyiasheŋ
nsaa pin asheŋ to.
3Baa kɔ a fin kenyi
nɛ asheŋ be kepinto.
4Baa fin kenyi kenishipereso
fanɛ kananɛ feeŋ fin gbiti
nɛ yawu kpakpaso
be asɔ nɛ a ŋana na.
5Fo wora loŋ,
kumo ere feeŋ pin
kusɔ nɛ k la kabɔrɛŋana
nsaa tiŋ a pin Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ to.
6Ŋkpal manɛ so,
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
e naa sa kanyiasheŋ.
Mo kutɔ nɛ kenyi
nɛ asheŋ be kepinto bee shi.
7Mo e naa chɛ basa nɛ
baa wora asheŋ niŋiso to
nsaa kuŋ bumo.
8Mo e naa kuŋ basa nɛ
baa wora asheŋ nɛ a daga,
nsaa ŋini bekama nɛ baa shuŋ mo
nɛ kagbene koŋwule na ekpa.
9Nɛ fee nu ma mmalga,
feeŋ pin kusɔ nɛ k walɛ
nɛ kusɔ nɛ k niŋi ekpa
nɛ kusɔ nɛ k daga fanɛ
fo baa wora.
10Kanyiasheŋ beeŋ luri
m bɔlɔ fo to,
nɛ fo kenyi e bɔlɔ fo kenishi.
11Fo lakal nɛ asheŋ be kepinto
beeŋ baa kuŋ fo.
12Kanyiasheŋ e naŋ kuŋ fo
ashi asheŋ lubi be kewora to;
nseŋ mɔlga fo ashi basa nɛ
bumo be mmalga bee bar asheŋ to.
13Loŋ be basa e kini
kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso
nsaa wɔ tentembiri be alubi
be kebaawɔtɔ to na.
14Bumo, nɛ alubi be kewora
bee wora ebel
nɛ bumo be ŋgbene
bee fuli alubi so na.
15Bumo be asheŋ woraso
e maa bɔla ekpa,
nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ n yirda bumo na.
16Kanyiasheŋ beeŋ mɔlga fo
ashi beche nɛ baa lar
bumo kulana be mman
a ta kɔnɔ belbelso
a fule benyɛn a ji na kutɔ.
17Loŋ be beche
e naa yige
bumo be etumbanyɛn
nsaa kplaŋ kakil to be ŋkre be kɔnɔ
nɛ b nase Ebɔrɛ
be anishito na so na.
18Ekpa nɛ k bee yɔ
loŋ be beche pe na
bee yɛr basa luwu
nɛ kemur to nna.
19Esa kama nɛ e yɔ loŋ be eche pe
maŋ naa bɛta a yɔ epe,
ŋko a bɔla ekpa
nɛ k bee yɛr esa ŋkpa to na.
20Amoso a daga fanɛ fo baa kute
basa lela be aworbi to nna;
nsaa wɔ kebaawɔtɔ niŋi so to.
21Ŋkpal manɛ so basa
nɛ baa wora asheŋ niŋiso
nɛ basa nɛ b maŋ kɔ mpulɔ
e naaŋ nya
anyi be kasawule ere so a wɔtɔ.
22Ama Ebɔrɛ beeŋ lara basa lubi
nɛ basa nɛ b maa ji kashenteŋ
ashi kasawule ere so.

english_text:
Trust God
1My child, remember
my teachings and instructions
and obey them completely.
2They will help you live
a long and prosperous life.
3Let love and loyalty
always show like a necklace,
and write them in your mind.
4 God and people will like you
and hold you in high esteem.
5With all your heart
you must trust the Lord
and not your own judgment.
6Always let him lead you,
and he will clear the road
for you to follow.
7 Don't ever think that you
are wise enough,
but respect the Lord
and stay away from evil.
8This will make you healthy,
and you will feel strong.
9Honor the Lord by giving him
your money and the first part
of all your crops.
10Then you will have
more grain and grapes
than you will ever need.
11 My child, don't turn away
or become bitter
when the Lord corrects you.
12 The Lord corrects
everyone he loves,
just as parents correct
a child they dearly love.
The Value of Wisdom
13God blesses everyone
who has wisdom
and common sense.
14Wisdom is worth more
than silver;
it makes you much richer
than gold.
15Wisdom is more valuable
than precious jewels;
nothing you want
compares with her.
16In her right hand
Wisdom holds a long life,
and in her left hand
are wealth and honor.
17Wisdom makes life pleasant
and leads us safely along.
18Wisdom is a life-giving tree,
the source of happiness
for all who hold on to her.
19By his wisdom and knowledge
the Lord created
heaven and earth.
20By his understanding
he let the ocean break loose
and clouds release the rain.
21My child, use common sense
and sound judgment!
Always keep them in mind.
22They will help you to live
a long and beautiful life.
23You will walk safely
and never stumble;
24you will rest without a worry
and sleep soundly.
25So don't be afraid
of sudden disasters
or storms that strike
those who are evil.
26You can be sure that the Lord
will protect you from harm.
27 Do all you can for everyone
who deserves your help.
28Don't tell your neighbor
to come back tomorrow,
if you can help today.
29Don't try to be mean
to neighbors who trust you.
30Don't argue just to be arguing,
when you haven't been hurt.
31Don't be jealous
of cruel people
or follow their example.
32The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is dishonest,
but he lets good people
be his friends.
33He places a curse on the home
of everyone who is evil,
but he blesses the home
of every good person.
34 The Lord sneers at those
who sneer at him,
but he is kind to everyone
who is humble.
35You will be praised
if you are wise,
but you will be disgraced
if you are a stubborn fool.
translation_text:
Mbrantiɛbia be kasotoji be asheŋ
1M pibinyɛn, sa maŋ kaŋ teŋ
asɔ nɛ mee ŋini fo na so.
Baa nyiŋi asɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo fanɛ
fo baa wora na saŋkikɛ.
2Asɔ nɛ mee ŋini fo na
beeŋ sa fo ŋkpa tenteŋ,
nɛ nɛfa.
3Sa maŋ shin nɛ kebaayɛ a wora
e baa barga fo kikɛ.
Chɛ kumo n shɛga
fo kubɔ to fanɛ kubɔtoshembi,
n shin nɛ k bɔlɔ fo kagbene to
a dii efuli ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to.
4Ŋkpal manɛ so
nɛ fo baa wora loŋ,
fo asheŋ beeŋ baa bɔlɔ Ebɔrɛ
nɛ dimɛdi kikɛ kenishi.
5Ta fo kagbene kikɛ nyam
n yirda Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
Sa maa ta fo tama a deŋi
kusɔ nɛ fo nyi so.
6Baa nyiŋi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
ashi kusɔ kama nɛ fee wora to,
nɛ e baa lɔŋɛ ekpa nɛ fee bɔla so
kananɛ k daga a sa fo.
7Sa maa fɛ fanɛ
fo nyi asheŋ ga.
Baa nu a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
nsaa gelge alubi.
8Nɛ fo baa wora loŋ,
k beeŋ baa du fanɛ
kudur lela nna a chɛ fo,
nsaa wushi fo eyur to be ebesa.
9Baa ta fo kanya
nɛ fo sososo be adɔjibi
a bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.
10Nɛ fee wora loŋ,
fo mpuro beeŋ baa bɔlɔ a wurge
nɛ fo nsapuya gba
e baa bɔlɔ
asɔ nuuso popɔr a wurge.
11M pibinyɛn, sa maa kini
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kebela
be kasogberge
ŋko mbe kefiɛso be keŋini.
12Ŋkpal manɛ so,
basa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee sha
nɛ e bee niŋi ekpa,
fanɛ kananɛ etuto
bee wora mo pibi shaso na.
13Kagbenefuli la
ekama nɛ e ki enyiashempo,
ŋko ekama nɛ e nya
asheŋ be kepinto
be nfɛra na peya nna.
14Ŋkpal manɛ so
kanyiasheŋ kɔ tɔnɔ
a chɔ shuwa nɛ gbiti.
15Kanyiasheŋ kɔ tɔnɔ
a chɔ abitasɔ kikɛ.
Fo maaŋ tiŋ n ta shɛŋ shɛŋ
m ber kanyiasheŋ.
16Kanyiasheŋ e naa sa
esa ŋkpa tenteŋ,
nɛ kedamaya nɛ kemaŋkura.
17Kanyiasheŋ beeŋ sa fo
kebaawɔtɔ belbelso,
nseŋ ŋini fo ekpa lela
nɛ feeŋ baa bɔla so a wora asheŋ
ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to.
18Bekama nɛ b kɔ kanyiasheŋ na,
be ŋgbene bee fuli bumo nna.
Bumo be kanyiasheŋ bee sa bumo
ŋkpa tenteŋ nna.
19Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kanyiasheŋ
nɛ e ta n to durnya,
nseŋ ta mbe kenyi
n wora awɔlpaana
n yili kakpa nɛ a wɔ.
20Mbe kanyiasheŋ
e shin nɛ eboŋana bee shile,
nɛ awɔlpa bee bar
bɔrɛchu kasawule so.
21M pibinyɛn,
baa kɔ fo kanyiasheŋ
nɛ fo lakal to kpakpa.
Sa maŋ shin nɛ a shile fo kikɛ.
22Ŋkpal manɛ so,
amo e naŋ sa fo
kagbenefuli be ŋkpa
nɛ k wɔ ebel.
23Kanyiasheŋ nɛ lakal
beeŋ kuŋ fo,
nɛ fo maaŋ foe ekpa.
24Kanyiasheŋ beeŋ shin nɛ
fo ya dese nɛ kufu e baa kɔ fo,
ŋko a di a yeŋi a tiŋi.
25Ŋko a fɔŋ etɔrɔ purgiso
nɛ a bee kaa ba basa lubi so
fanɛ afugboŋ na so.
26Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
beeŋ baa kuŋ fo ashi etɔrɔ to.
E maaŋ shin nɛ fo tɔr
kejigbelɛ kama to.
27Saŋkama nɛ feeŋ tiŋ,
fo chɛ bekama
nɛ baa fin kechɛto to.
28Nɛ feeŋ tiŋ n chɛ fo kurgepo to,
fo chɛ mo to,
sa maŋ shin nɛ e jo
nɛ kare e chɛ pɔɛŋ.
29Sa maa kre fo kurgepo
nɛ e yirda fo ŋkre lubi.
30Ŋko ŋ ku asheŋ n deŋi
esa kama,
nɛ e maŋ wora fo kulubi kikɛ.
31Sa maa yɛlga
basa lubi be aworbi,
ŋko a wora
bumo be asheŋ woraso.
32Ŋkpal manɛ so,
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kishi
basa nɛ baa wora alubi be asheŋ ga,
ama e yirda basa
nɛ bumo be aworbi niŋi na bre nna.
33Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be shoduu
wɔ basa lubi pe nna,
nɛ mbe nɛfa malɛ wɔ basa lela pe.
34Mo nɛ basa
nɛ baa maŋ bumo be amu so
maŋ kɔ shɛŋ,
ama e bee shu basa
nɛ baa bar bumo be amu ase
bre so nna.
35Benyiashempo bee nya
ketre lela nna,
ama bewulpo bre
bee ji nyɔmɔ nna
a ti bumo be anishinyɔr so.

english_text:
Advice to Young People
1My child, listen closely
to my teachings
and learn common sense.
2My advice is useful,
so don't turn away.
3When I was still very young
and my mother's favorite child,
my father 4said to me:
“If you follow my teachings
and keep them in mind,
you will live.
5Be wise and learn good sense;
remember my teachings
and do what I say.
6“If you love Wisdom
and don't reject her,
she will watch over you.
7The best thing about Wisdom
is Wisdom herself;
good sense is more important
than anything else.
8If you value Wisdom
and hold tightly to her,
great honors will be yours.
9It will be like wearing
a glorious crown
of beautiful flowers.”
The Right Way and the Wrong Way
10My child, if you listen
and obey my teachings,
you will live a long time.
11I have shown you the way
that makes sense;
I have guided you
along the right path.
12Your road won't be blocked,
and you won't stumble
when you run.
13Hold firmly to my teaching
and never let go.
It will mean life for you.
14Don't follow the bad example
of cruel and evil people.
15Turn aside and keep going.
Stay away from them.
16They can't sleep or rest
until they do wrong or harm
some innocent victim.
17Their food and drink
are cruelty and wickedness.
18The lifestyle of good people
is like sunlight at dawn
that keeps getting brighter
until broad daylight.
19The lifestyle of the wicked
is like total darkness,
and they will never know
what makes them stumble.
20My child, listen carefully
to everything I say.
21Don't forget a single word,
but think about it all.
22Knowing these teachings
will mean true life
and good health for you.
23Carefully guard your thoughts
because they are the source
of true life.
24Never tell lies or be deceitful
in what you say.
25Keep looking straight ahead,
without turning aside.
26 Know where you are headed,
and you will stay
on solid ground.
27Don't make a mistake by turning
to the right or the left.
translation_text:
Tɔnɔ nɛ kanyiasheŋ kɔ be asheŋ;
1Ma mbinyɛnso,
men baa nu asɔ nɛ,
men tuto bee ŋini menyi na;
men baa bugi asoe a nu amo,
saŋɛ so menyeeŋ pin amo to nɛnɛ.
2Asɔ nɛ a walɛ
nɛ mee ŋini menyi;
amoso men baa nyiŋi amo.
3Ŋ kaa daa la kebibi
nsaa la n tuto
nɛ n nio be ebinyɛn koŋwule na,
4n tuto daa ŋini ma
asheŋ nna a kaŋɛ ma le:
“Baa nyiŋi asɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ na,
nsaa maa teŋ amo so.
Baa bɛ asɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ
fo na so nseŋ nya ŋkpa tenteŋ.
5Nya kanyiasheŋ nɛ lakal,
n sa maŋ teŋ ŋko ŋ kplaŋ
asɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo na so.
6Sa maŋ kplaŋ kanyiasheŋ so,
nɛ k kuŋ fo,
baa sha kumo, nɛ k baa keni fo so.
7Kanyiasheŋ e chɔ
kusɔ kama nyam,
amoso fin kanyiasheŋ nɛ lakal.
8Baa sha kanyiasheŋ
nɛ k ta fo ŋ ki esa gboŋ.
Pɛ kumo to kpakpa
nɛ k bar fo kemaŋkura.
9Kumo e naŋ ki fanɛ kemaŋkura,
be kuwurwuro m buu fo.
10M pibinyɛn,
kaŋ kusoe kenishipereso
n nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo ere,
nseŋ nya ŋkpa tenteŋ.
11Ŋ ŋini fo kanyiasheŋ,
nɛ kananɛ feeŋ baa kɔ
kebaawɔtɔ niŋi so.
12Nɛ fo kɔ kanyiasheŋ,
shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ kagle fo ekpa to.
Fee shile gba fo maaŋ fiti n tɔr.
13Baa nyiŋi asɔ nɛ fo
koya na saŋkikɛ,
nsaa kɔ amo to kpakpa,
ŋkpal manɛ so kusɔ nɛ fo koya
e la fo ŋkpa.
14Sa maa yɔ mboŋ nɛ
basa lubi bee yɔ,
ŋko a koya basa lubi
be aworbi.
15Baa gelge loŋ be ekpa,
nseŋ lar alubi to.
Kini alubi be kewora,
nseŋ m pɛ fo ekpa a yɔ.
16Basa lubi bre
baŋ maŋ wora kulubi,
b maaŋ tiŋ n di.
B maaŋ tiŋ n di nɛ b maŋ wora
kulubi ŋ gbiti esa ko.
17Asheŋ lubi nɛ kelantokɔ,
du nna fanɛ
ajibi nɛ nchu n sa bumo.
18Ama ekpa nɛ belelaworapo
bɔ so na bre
du nna fanɛ karechɛ so
be epeŋi na.
K bee fulto nna a ti so
hale nɛ kare e ya chɛ
nɛ kaboŋ e fulto parr.
19Ama belubiworapo bre
be ekpa
biri to nna fanɛ tentembiri plɔ.
Baa fiti a tɔr,
ama b maa wu asɔ nɛ baa fiti na.
20M pibinyɛn, bugi asoe
nɛnɛ n nu
kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo ere.
Kaŋ kusoe n nu
ma mmalga ere.
21Sa maŋ shin nɛ
ma mmalga na e barga fo.
Baa nyiŋi amo
nseŋ ta amo n wɔtɔ
fo kagbene to saŋkama.
22Ŋkpal manɛ so a beeŋ sa
esa kama nɛ e pin amo to
ŋkpa nɛ alenfia.
23Baa da fo nfɛra fɛso so,
ŋkpal manɛ so
amo e naa ŋini fo kebaawɔtɔ.
24Sa maŋ malga kusɔ kama nɛ
kashenteŋ maŋ wɔ kumo to.
Fo nɛ efɛsheŋ nɛ mmalga nɛ
a bee shin nɛ
basa bee wora a foe ekpa
e sa maa kɔ shɛŋ.
25Baa keni tenini
nseŋ ta kashenteŋji
nɛ kebaa teŋ a wora
be kebaawɔtɔ a yɔ anishito.
Sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ anishinyɔr e ji fo
nɛ fo kurgi fo kumu n yuu to kikɛ.
26Baa chena a fɛ asheŋ nɛnɛ,
nsaa kre kusɔ kama
nɛ fee sha kewora
be asheŋ nɛnɛ
pɔɛŋ nsaa wora kumo.
Aloŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ fee wora
beeŋ nite nɛnɛ.
27Baa gelge kulubi
nsaa nite teteri,
Sa maa kpele ekpa
niŋiso na kikɛ.”

english_text:
Be Faithful to Your Wife
1My son, if you listen closely
to my wisdom and good sense,
2you will have sound judgment,
and you will always know
the right thing to say.
3The words of an immoral woman
may be as sweet as honey
and as smooth as olive oil.
4But all that you really get
from being with her
is bitter poison and pain.
5If you follow her,
she will lead you down
to the world of the dead.
6She has missed the path
that leads to life
and doesn't even know it.
7My son, listen to me
and do everything I say.
8Stay away from a bad woman!
Don't even go near the door
of her house.
9You will lose your self-respect
and end up in debt
to some cruel person
for the rest of your life.
10Strangers will get your money
and everything else
you have worked for.
11When it's all over,
your body will waste away,
as you groan 12and shout,
“I hated advice and correction!
13I paid no attention
to my teachers,
14and now I am disgraced
in front of everyone.”
15You should be faithful
to your wife,
just as you take water
from your own well.
16And don't be like a stream
from which just any woman
may take a drink.
17Save yourself for your wife
and don't have sex
with other women.
18Be happy with the wife
you married
when you were young.
19She is beautiful and graceful,
just like a deer;
you should be attracted to her
and stay deeply in love.
20Don't go crazy over a woman
who is unfaithful
to her own husband!
21The Lord sees everything,
and he watches us closely.
22Sinners are trapped and caught
by their own evil deeds.
23They get lost and die
because of their foolishness
and lack of self-control.
translation_text:
Kesakalea be keji be kefiɛso be asheŋ
1M pibinyɛn,
bugi asoe nɛnɛ n nu
ma kanyiasheŋ
be mmalga
nɛ a bee sa lakal ere.
2Amo e naaŋ sa fo da lela,
nseŋ shin nɛ fo mmalga e baa
ŋini fanɛ fo kɔ kenyi.
3Eche nɛ lar mo kul be kaman
be kɔnɔpurbi
beeŋ tiŋ a du mɔlmɔlbi
fanɛ ŋku,
nɛ kumo be kepipe e baa wɔ ebel
fanɛ mushoŋchu na,
4ama fo baŋ di mo n loge,
ebesa nɛ n daa nyi nna
e naa bɛ kumo so.
5Fo bɛ mo so
e beeŋ yɛr fo bubuni to,
ŋkpal manɛ so ekpa nɛ e bɔ so na
bee yɔ luwu to nna.
6E maŋ bɔ ekpa nɛ
k bee yɔ ŋkpa to na,
ama mo alɛ maŋ nyi kumo be loŋ,
ŋkpal manɛ so
e maŋ kɔ epe.
7Amoso m pibinyɛn,
bugi asoe nɛnɛ n nu.
Sa maŋ teŋ
kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere so.
8Baa gelge loŋ be beche na.
Sa maa ji a taga bumo to kuraa.
9Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, feeŋ paŋ
fo bunyaŋ nɛ kemaŋkura,
nɛ basa lubi
e nya ekpa m mɔ Juwebi;
10nɛ befɔ e ta asɔ lela
nɛ fo gben n nya na kikɛ.
11Fo ŋkpa be lalaloge,
feeŋ dese a shuto,
nɛ fo eleŋ nɛ eyur kikɛ
e fo amo be ekar.
12Loŋ be jemanɛ na so
nɛ fo kaŋɛ le:
“Manɛ e ba nɛ n daa maŋ koya?
Manɛ nna nɛ
m maŋ shuli n sɔ keŋini?
13N daa maŋ nu n sa
ma beŋinipoana;
n daŋ kplaŋ bumo so nna.
14Kabre ma e ŋaba
basa kikɛ be anishito na!
15Amoso shin nɛ fo laŋ to be ajibi
e baa kukwe fo.
16Mbia nɛ fo nɛ bejipoche
beeŋ kurge na,
maaŋ lar tɔnɔ n sa fo.
17Shin nɛ fo gbagba be mbia
e daŋ n chɛ fo to,
mannɛ basa pɔtɛ be mbia.
18Amoso shin nɛ fo kagbene
e baa fuli
fo kebiato be eche so.
Shin nɛ mbe asheŋ
e baa par fo.
19E walɛ kebita nna
a du shreembi fanɛ chibir na,
amoso shin nɛ mbe
kebita e baa sa fo kagbenefuli.
Shin nɛ mbe kasha
e baa bɔlɔ fo kenishi.
20M pibinyɛn, manɛ e ba
nɛ fee ta fo kasha
n ya kaa sa eche pɔtɛ?
Manɛ e ba nɛ enyɛn ko
be eche be kebita
bee par fo a chɔ fo eche peya?
21Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
bee wu kusɔ kama
nɛ fee wora.
Kaplɛkama nɛ fee yɔ
e bee wu fo.
22Esa lubi be alubi
du fanɛ kegba,
nɛ mo gbagba
bee kilgi a tɔr to
nɛ k bee pɛ mo nna.
23Loŋ be basa bee wu nna
ŋkpal b ka maŋ kɔ kamootiŋ so.
Bumo gbagba be kawulisheŋ
e naa yɛr bumo nchaŋ to.”

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
Kawulisheŋ be asheŋ
1M pibinyɛn,
nɛ fo nase kɔnɔ
fanɛ feeŋ yili
esa ko be katelamu
ŋ ka mbe kukɔ bre,
2fo gbagba be kɔnɔ to
be mmalga kre fo nna na;
nɛ fo kɔnɔ naseso na
e kilgi m pɛ fo.
3M pibinyɛn, ŋkpal fo ka tɔr
amodoŋwura be enɔ to so,
kananɛ feeŋ wora n nya
fo kumu nde.
Nya manaŋ n ya kule
amodoŋwura fanɛ
e ta kukɔ na m paŋ fo.
4Sa maŋ ta loŋ be kesheŋ na
n wora ewɔji,
ŋko ŋ kplaŋ kumo so
a dese a di.
5Wora ania n lar
kesheŋ na to manaŋ,
fanɛ kananɛ kusɔbɔya
ŋko kabuibi nɛ e wɔ
kejigbelɛ to bee wu ekpampo
nsaa kɔ a fin
kumɔlga kumo be kumu na.
6Betɔlpo, men keni
kananɛ atutulombi
bee wora asheŋ so,
ŋ koya kebaawɔtɔ.
7B maŋ kɔ bejuŋkparpo
ŋko bewura
ŋko basa nɛ baa ji bumo
be edemu a sa bumo,
8ŋkeshin nɛ bumo alɛ bee fin
bumo be ajibi ketarso nna
a yili pɔɛŋ nɛ kechali e fo.
9Etɔlpo, nuso be ewushi
nɛ fee sha nɛ fo wushi?
Saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ tiŋi edi to
ŋ koso n shuŋ?
10Kusɔ nɛ etɔlpo bee kaa kaŋɛ
e la fanɛ;
shin nɛ n di gbrɛbi,
ŋko shin nɛ n chena
n wushi gbrɛbi.
11Ama saŋɛ nɛ e dese a di na
nɛ ketir bee nyaŋ mo
a wɔtɔ fanɛ
beyu ka ta adoŋsɔ ŋ kuŋ
esa ekpa n suge mbe asɔ na.
12Basa lubi nɛ basa fuloŋ
e naa nite a ku efɛ.
13Baa kaa wora basa
anishi nna
ŋko a ta bumo be eyur be mba
a malga basa kutɔ
a fule bumo.
14Baa wora loŋ nna
nsaa kɔ nfɛra lubi a kre asheŋ
a bar kebagato
basa to kaplɛkama.
15Ŋkpal loŋ so
tɔrɔ nɛ k bee yɛr basa
kemur to na,
beeŋ tɔr bumo so
m mur bumo
saŋɛ nɛ b maa tama kumo na.
16Asɔ ashunu nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
kishi ga na nde:
17Kamoowu
nɛ kudonduloŋ fɛpo
nɛ enɔ nɛ k bee mɔ
basa nɛ b maŋ wora n da so,
18nɛ nfɛra fɛso lubi
nɛ basa nɛ alubi be kewora
maa choŋ bumo so
19nɛ shɛdajipo nɛ e bee ku efɛ
a deŋi abar so
nɛ edebɔrpo nɛ
e bee ta beteri be amu
a ŋmɛa abar.
Kesakalea be asheŋ
20M pibinyɛn, baa bɛ
kusɔ nɛ fo tuto kaŋɛ fo so,
nsaa maa kplaŋ asɔ nɛ
fo nio ŋini fo so.
21Shin nɛ bumo be mmalga
e baa wɔ fo
nfɛra to saŋkama
fanɛ a ka la kubɔtoshembi
a di fo na.
22Shin nɛ a baa ŋini fo ekpa;
nsaa kuŋ fo kanyɛso.
Saŋkama nɛ fo di n tiŋi,
fo shin nɛ a baa ji fo asoeto.
23Ŋkpal manɛ so fo nio
nɛ fo tuto be keŋini
du fanɛ kefulto nna n sa fo;
nɛ bumo be kasogberge malɛ
bee sa fo kebaawɔtɔ lela.
24Bumo be keŋini na
e naaŋ kuŋ fo
ashi esa pɔtɛ be eche
be kayɛlga
be mmalga belbelso to.
25Sa maŋ kpal
loŋ be beche be kebita so
n yɛlga bumo;
ŋko n shin nɛ
bumo be kayɛlga so
be kekeni fo,
e shin nɛ fo sha bumo.
26Sakaleche be yawu maŋ fo
bodobodo be amansherbi so,
ama esa be eche be kasha
beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ fo luri
tɔrɔ gboŋgboŋi to.
27Esa beeŋ tiŋ n chɔɔ edɛ
n wɔtɔ mbe kusɔbuuso to,
nɛ kusɔbuuso na maaŋ chɔɔ a?
28Ŋko esa beeŋ tiŋ n ta aya fuloŋ
n nite ajanwulɛ so
nɛ a maaŋ chɔɔ mo a?
29To, loŋ koŋwule na
nɛ k du n sa
esa kama nɛ
e di mo barkasa be eche.
Esa kama nɛ e wora loŋ
maaŋ paŋ kasogberge kikɛ.
30Basa maa sha beyu be asheŋ;
hale eyu yuri ajibi n ji
ŋkpal akoŋ so gba,
nɛ b pɛ mo,
31baaŋ gberge mo kusoe
n shin nɛ e ka kusɔ nɛ
e yur na be kukɔ
ale ashunu.
Hale kumo be loŋ
beeŋ shin nɛ e paŋ
kusɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ gba,
baaŋ shin nɛ e wora loŋ.
32Enyɛn kama nɛ e bee sha
mo braana be beche
maŋ kɔ nfɛra nna na.
Mo alɛ gbagba be kumu nɛ
e baa jija na.
33Kebri nɛ ŋaba e
naa jo loŋ be esa.
Mo alɛ nɛ anishinyɔr
e naa baa la saŋkikɛ.
34Ŋkpal manɛ so
kedata be agbo lubi ga,
nɛ enyɛn bee bishi
kumo be kuwule
a maa wu kuwɔr kuraa.
35Sheŋ malɛ maa tiŋ a ka
kedata be agbo be kukɔ.
Kakɛ kama maŋ wɔtɔ
a wushi kedata be agbo.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
Sakaleche be kasokpele be asheŋ
1M pibinyɛn,
baa nyiŋi asɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo na.
Sa maŋ teŋ kusɔ nɛ
ŋ kaŋɛ fo na so kikɛ.
2Baa wora asɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ na
nseŋ ji efute tenteŋ;
Baa de so,
nsaa bɛ ma keŋini na so
fanɛ kananɛ esa bee kuŋ
kusɔ nɛ e bee sha ga na.
3Baa kɔ asɔ nɛ
ŋ ŋini fo na to saŋkikɛ,
n shin nɛ a baa wɔ
fo kagbene to.
4Ta kanyiasheŋ ŋ
ki fanɛ fo sipoche,
nseŋ ta lakal malɛ
ŋ ki fo teri kpakpaso.
5Amo e naŋ kuŋ fo
ashi fo braana be beche,
nɛ beche nɛ b kɔ
kesakalea so
be mmalga belbelso to.
Sakaleche be asheŋ
6Kachako nɛ n jule ŋ keni
ma ebu be tokuro to,
7n wu mbrantiɛbia damta
nɛ b maa pin asheŋ to
manaŋ manaŋ,
nseŋ keni bumo to
n wu ewulpo ko.
8E daa na kubɔrbi so nna
a mata kakpa
nɛ eche ko daa wɔ,
nseŋ bɔla eche na be kawu ase.
9Kaaseso e daa la,
nɛ kaboŋ birito.
10Nɛ kache na mɛato
kesakalea so
n lar n yɔ mo kutɔ.
Mbe nfɛra daa yil
kananɛ e beeŋ wora
n nya kabrantiɛbia na n yɔ
mbe laŋ to nna.
11Eche na daŋ paŋ
anishinyɔr nna,
nsaa nite kubɔrbi so saŋkikɛ
a malga awɔrso.
12Saŋko e bee yili
kebonfu ko to nna a jo,
saŋko malɛ kubɔrbi so,
saŋko malɛ kebɛ to.
13E ka ya tu kebinyɛnbi na
nɛ e pɛ mo to,
m pepe mbe kɔnɔpurbi
nseŋ keni mbe anishito diimbi
ŋ kaŋɛ le:
14“Kabre nɛ m mɔ
asɔbɔya n lara sarga;
eblaŋ wɔ ma laŋ to.
15Amoso nɛ n lar a fin fo
nseŋ keni n wu fo nfe!
16Ma alɛ ta ljipt be efuli so
be ago peper
be asɔ deseso nna
n deŋi ma gedo so.
17Nseŋ ta etulale nɛ baa tre
mir nɛ alowe
nɛ Sinamɔn na
ŋ ŋmenyaŋ kumo kikɛ so.
18Amoso, baa ba
nɛ an ya sha abar
nseŋ ji anyi be amu
hale nɛ kare e ya chɛ.
19Ma kul maŋ wɔ epe,
e yɔ kade wɔfɔ ko nna.
20E ta amansherbi damta
nna n yɔ.
Bɔkwe anyɔ pɔɛŋ e beeŋ ba.”
21Kache na ta
mmalga belbelso nna,
n fule mo, m pɛ mo
nɛ e shuli n sa mo.
22Nseŋ bɛ mo so epul na to
fanɛ kananɛ baa keta kusɔbɔya
a yɔ nɛ b ya mɔ,
ŋko kananɛ chibir bee shile a luri
kejigbelɛ to nɛ k bee pɛ kumo,
23nɛ b ya too ketanyembi
n wɔtɔ kumo be kagbene to
m mɔ na.
Kebinyɛnbi na daa du nna fanɛ
kabuibi nɛ e bee yɔ
kejigbelɛ to.
E daa maŋ nyi fanɛ
kenishipere to nɛ
e bee yɔ na.
24Amoso, naniere,
ma mbinyɛnsobi,
men nu nfe.
Men kaŋ kusoe n nu
kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere.
25Men sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ
men be ekama
be kagbene e yɔ
loŋ be eche so.
Men sa maa sa
loŋ be beche kashuli.
26Eche na shin nɛ
benyɛn damta
paŋ bumo be eyilikpa.
Esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ karga basa
nɛ e shin nɛ b mur.
27Fo baa yɔ mo pe,
kumo ere luwu be ekpa
nɛ fo bɔ na.
Mo pe e la ekpa shimbi
nɛ k bee yɔ luwu to.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Kanyiasheŋ ka walɛ be asheŋ
1Nu nfe,
kanyiasheŋ e naa tre na.
Lakal e naa kaŋɛ awɔrso
fanɛ fo nu n sa mo na.
2K wɔ abee so nna
nseŋ mata ekpakar
nɛ ŋkpancheri.
3Kade be kabunagboŋ
nɛ baa bɔla a luri kade to na
ase nɛ k wɔ a tre a kaŋɛ:
4“Dimɛdi kikɛ nɛ e wɔ
kasawule so nɛ mee kaŋɛ na.
5Menyee wora abibisheŋ nna a?
Men nya kenimufɛra.
Men wuli nna ŋko?
Men wora nfɛra.
6Men kaŋ kusoe n nu
ma mmalga lela ere.
Kusɔ kama nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi na
niŋi ekpa nna.
7Kashenteŋ nɛ mee ji,

8Kusɔ kama nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ
la kashenteŋ nna,
efɛ ŋko kafulesheŋ kikɛ
maŋ wɔ kumo to.
9K baŋ di efuli nna
n sa esa kama nɛ
e bee pin asheŋ to,

10Lara ma keŋini ere

Baa fin kenyi
a chɔ shuwa lela.
11Kanyiasheŋ kɔ tɔnɔ

Dimɛdi be kusɔ shaso kikɛ
maaŋ tiŋ n ta kumo be kumu

12Ma, kanyiasheŋ,

13Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
be kesa bunyaŋ

Kamoowu nɛ ŋkpensheŋ,
nɛ asheŋ lubi nɛ efɛ be mmalga

14Ma e naa kre ŋkre

15Ma e naa chɛ bewurjipo to

16Ma e naa chɛ

17Mee sha bumo nɛ

Esa kama nɛ e bee fin ma

18Ŋ kɔ kedamaya,

19Kusɔ nɛ feeŋ nya ma kutɔ
bɔ shuwa

20Ekpa niŋi so,

21Mee sa bumo nɛ baa sha

nsaa shin nɛ asɔ lela bee bɔlɔ

22Ma nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
juŋkpar n to.

Ŋ ka fara

n ta amo n yili

Ebɔrɛ to kasawule,

29nseŋ ponte ŋ kaŋɛ nchu na
fanɛ a sa maŋ bɔlɔ n dii

30N daa wɔ mo kutɔ nna fanɛ

Ma kagbene bee fuli ma nna

31Ma kagbene fuli durnya so,

32Naniere, mbifɔlbi,

Men wora asɔ nɛ
ŋ kaŋɛ ere nɛ a shin nɛ

33Men nu kusɔ nɛ mee

34Bekama nɛ baa ba

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Kanyiasheŋ nɛ kawuli be asheŋ
1Kanyiasheŋ pɔr kumo be ebu nna
n yili eshabɔrɛ ashunu so.
2Nseŋ shin nɛ b mɔ
kusɔbɔya n wora kejigboŋ;
nseŋ ta asɔ
nɛ amo be efɛa bee dufɛ viim
n wɔtɔ nsa to n yili.
3Nseŋ shuŋi mbe mbita fanɛ
b ya yili kade be mboŋ jeŋgreŋ
m ponte n tre basa ŋ kaŋɛ:
4“Menyi nɛ men maa pin asheŋ to
manaŋ manaŋ na e luri m ba.”
Nseŋ kaŋɛ bewulpo malɛ le:
5“Men ba ji ma ajibi
nseŋ nu nsa belbelso
nɛ n wora n yili na.
6Men lar basa nɛ
b maa pin asheŋ to
manaŋ manaŋ na be katuŋ to
nseŋ ji efute.
Men shin nɛ asheŋ be kepin to
e baa ŋini menyi ekpa.”
7Fo baa ŋini esa nɛ
e kɔ mpuchi ekpa,
katege nɛ fee fin a sa fo kumu na.
Nɛ fo fiɛ esa lubi so,
feeŋ luri tɔrɔ to.
8Sa maŋ kaŋ fiɛ
esa nɛ e bee puchi so,
fo baŋ wora loŋ,
e beeŋ kishi fo.
Ama fo baŋ ŋini enyiashempo bre
ekpa e beeŋ sa fo bunyaŋ.
9Kusɔ kama nɛ fo
kaŋɛ enyiashempo,
bee sa mo kanyiasheŋ nna a ti so.
Kusɔ kama malɛ
nɛ fo kaŋɛ basa nɛ
baa wora asheŋ niŋiso,
bee sa bumo kenyi nna a ti so.
10Nɛ fee sha kanyiasheŋ,
fo fara a ŋana Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.
Nɛ fo baa nyi Ebɔrɛ cheembi na,
feeŋ baa pin asheŋ to.
11Kanyiasheŋ beeŋ shin nɛ
fo ŋkpa e teŋi so.
12Fo nyiasheŋ,
feeŋ ji kumo be tɔnɔ;
Fo kpal kamoowuso
ŋ kini kanyiasheŋ
feeŋ ji awurfoŋ.
13Kawuli du fanɛ
eche nɛ e maa pin
asheŋ to manaŋ manaŋ
nsaa da asheŋ a wea abar to nna.
14E bee chena mbe kabuna to
ashi kaboŋ jeŋgreŋ nɛ
baaŋ wu mo nna,
15a tre a kaŋɛ basa nɛ baa choŋ le:
16“Basa nɛ b maa pin
asheŋ to manaŋ manaŋ,
e luri m ba.”
Nsaa kaŋɛ bewulpo malɛ le:
17“Keyuri nchu wɔ ebel,
ama ajibi nɛ fo ŋana n ji
e wɔ ebel a chɔ amo”
18Basa nɛ baa nu mbe kafulesheŋ
maŋ nyi fanɛ
bekama nɛ b luri mbe laŋ to kikɛ
bee yɔ bubuni to nna.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Ewura Sɔlɔmɔn be aŋasa
1Ewura Sɔlɔmɔn be aŋasa nde:
Kebia nyiashempo
bee bar mo tuto nɛ mo nio
kumu saŋɛ nna,
ama kebia wulpo bre
bee wɔtɔ bumo ebesa to nna.
2Kapuni be kedamaya
maa lar tɔnɔ a sa esa
ama kashenteŋji bre
bee mɔlga esa be ŋkpa nna.
3Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ maaŋ shin nɛ
basa lela e di akoŋ,
Mo alɛ maaŋ shin nɛ
alubiworapoana e nya
kusɔ nɛ baa sha.
4Ntɔl bee bar esa ketir nna,
ama kepere kenishi n shuŋ
bre bee shin nɛ esa bee
dii dama nna.
5Enyiashempo bee teŋi
asɔ saŋɛ nɛ a bel nna,
ama k la anishinyɔr nna fanɛ
esa e baa dese a di
kasɔteŋi be jemanɛ.
6Basa lela bee nya nɛfa nna;
ama nfɛra lubi e ŋana
a wɔ esa lubi
be mmalga be kaman.
7Basa lela be alela so
nɛ baa nyiŋi bumo,
ama b maa nyiŋi
belubiwurapo bre kikɛ.
8Basa nɛ b kɔ lakal
bee sɔ kasotoji nna,
ama basa nɛ baa malga
kawuliso bre
maa chɛr nsaa tɔr.
9Beshenteŋjipo bee nya kekuŋ nna,
nɛ shɛŋ maa gbuŋgbuŋ bumo;
ama kebirkɔnshiwura be asheŋ
beeŋ lar efuli.
10Esa nɛ e bee dɔ
a buu kashenteŋ so
bee wɔtɔ basa ebesa to nna,
ama esa nɛ e maa fɛ nfɛra
pɔɛŋ nsaa malga
maa chɛr nsaa tɔr.
11Esa lela be mmalga du fanɛ
kebuye nna a sa ŋkpa,
ama kamɔ be nfɛra lubi
e ŋana a wɔ esa lubi
be mmalga be kaman.
12Kekishi bee bar kamɔrɔji
nɛ kebagato nna,
ama kasha bre bee kplaŋ
aworandeso kikɛ so nna.
13Esa be mmalga e naa ŋini fanɛ
e la enyiashempo,
ama ewulpo bre
daga kasogberge nna.
14Enyiashempo bee fin kenyi nna
a ti so saŋkikɛ,
ama ewulpo be mmalga
e naa da mo a lɛ.
15Kedamaya bee kuŋ
damawuraana nna
fanɛ kananɛ baa pɔr egbal
a kuŋ kade na,
ama ketir bre maa kuŋ betirpo.
16Alela be kakɔka
e la ŋkpa tenteŋ,
ama alubi bre bee shin nɛ
esa bee wora alubi nna a ti so.
17Basa nɛ baa shuli a sɔ keŋini
be kasogberge beeŋ ji efute,
ama bumo nɛ b maa shuli
kewora n jija bre
be lalaloge maa kaa walɛ.
18Esa kama nɛ kekishi wɔ mo to
la efɛpo nna.
Ewulpo e naa ta
b yɛ b yɛ a shuŋ.
19Fo baa malga ga
fo maa kra malga a foe.
Nɛ fo nyi asheŋ
fo maaŋ baa malga ga.
20Esa lela be mmalga
du fanɛ gbiti nna,
ama esa lubi maa sa
esa nfɛra nɛ k kɔ tɔnɔ.
21Esa lela be mmalga
kɔ tɔnɔ nna n sa basa damta,
ama kawuli beeŋ tiŋ m mɔ fo.
22Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e naa ta
esa e ki damawura.
Kepere kenishi n shuŋ
maaŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ fo dii dama.
23Ewulpo nɛ alubi be kewora
bee wora ebel.
Kanyiasheŋ e naa par benyipo bre.
24Basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ niŋiso
bee nya kusɔ nɛ baa sha nna,
ama kusɔ nɛ belubiworapo bre
maa sha nɛ baa nya ga.
25Afugboŋ bee ba nna
m ba kaa ber alubiworapoana a lɛ,
ama beshenteŋjipo bre
bee nya kumɔlga nna saŋkama.
26Sa maŋ shin nɛ etɔlpo
e wora shɛŋ n sa fo,
mbe asheŋ wora so kikɛ
du nna fanɛ fo ka ji dorobi
nɛ anyi bee nyiri fo;
ŋko edishi ka luri fo anishito nna.
27Wora Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kasonu
nseŋ ji efute n chɛr.
Kumu kpakpasowura
bee wu nna nɛ mbe saŋɛ maŋ naŋ fo.
28Basa lela be kanya
bee bar kagbenefuli nna,
ama belubiworapo bre
maaŋ nya kusɔ nɛ baa tama kikɛ.
29Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ
bee kuŋ beshenteŋjipo nna,
nsaa mur bumo nɛ
baa wora alubi.
30Basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ nɛ a niŋi
bee nya kekuŋ
saŋkikɛ nna,
ama belubiworapo bre
maaŋ ji efute n chɛr kasawule so.
31Basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ nɛ a niŋi
bee malga
kanyiasheŋ be mmalga nna,
ama baaŋ kuŋ
mmalga lubi wora bre ekpa.
32Basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ nɛ a niŋi
e nyi asheŋ lela
nɛ a daga kemalga,
ama asheŋ besaso nɛ belubiworapo
bre bee malga saŋkama.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kishi
kapuni be kasɔkarga ga.

nsaa ji anishinyɔr.

bee sa esa kanyiasheŋ nna.

7Belubiworapo nɛ tama e naa wu,

nɛ k deŋ bumo be kedamaya so

8Basa cheembi bee nya kekuŋ

mbe kade to ebi be ŋgbene

ama basa lubi bre be mmalga

12Ewulpo e naa ji beko be asheŋ,
enyiashempo bre bee loto nna.
13Esheŋjipo kikɛ maŋ kɔ ashiri,
ama feeŋ tiŋ n yirda

14Efuli nɛ k maŋ kɔ
bejuŋkparpo nyiashempo

15Nɛ fo yili kajinamu
n sa esa nɛ fo maŋ nyi,

16Eche nɛ e bee bugi enɔ a kɛ
bee nya kemaŋkura nna,

Etɔlpo maaŋ dii dama kikɛ,

beeŋ dii dama.
17Nɛ fee wora kelela
fo kumu nɛ fee wora a sa.

18Belubiworapo maa nya tɔnɔ kikɛ,

19Esa kama nɛ e yili
mbe kagbene to fanɛ

mbe kagbene to fanɛ
e beeŋ wora alubi bre
maaŋ ji efute n chɛr kikɛ.
20Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kishi

baaŋ gberge belubiworapo kusoe,

asheŋ niŋiso bre

22Eche nɛ e walɛ kebita
nsaa maŋ kɔ da
du fanɛ shuwa be kepinibi nna

23Asɔ kama nɛ basa lela bee fin
bee ki asɔ lela nna.

k bee pɛ basa agbo nna.
24Kakɛ maa loge asɔ.
Beko bee kɛ ga,

25Fo baa bugi enɔ a kɛ

Chɛ beko to
nɛ beko malɛ e chɛ fo to.

kɔnɔ nna,

bee nya asheŋ lela nna,

bumo be tama n deŋi
bumo be kanya so

a ba bumo be laŋ to ebi so
maaŋ nya kapetɛ n ji kikɛ.

30Kecheembiya bee sa ŋkpa nna,
ama kumu kpakpaso
be kebaawɔtɔ bre bee mɔ nna.

kelela be kakɔka durnya ere to,
