1-2On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
3 Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing. 4But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work, 5 just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
6 Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. 7I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple. 8All silver and gold belong to me, 9and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace.
The Past and the Future
10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Lord God All-Powerful told the prophet Haggai 11to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
12Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice?
“Of course not,” the priests answered.
13 Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?”
“Of course they would,” the priests answered.
14So the Lord told Haggai to say:
That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me. 15But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple, 16you recalled what life was like in the past. When you wanted 200 kilograms of wheat, there were only 10, and when you wanted 50 jars of wine, there were only 20. 17I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
18Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like. 19Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead.
God's Promise to Zerubbabel
20That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
21Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth 22and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other. 23But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_text:
Bɔrɛlambu popɔr na be kela be asheŋ
1-2Loŋ be kafɛ nyɔsopo na be kufɔl shunusopo be kachɛ adunyɔ nɛ kako na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ bɔla anebi Heegai so ŋ kaŋɛ Zerubabel nɛ e la Juda be efuli so be gomena nɛ Joshuwa nɛ e la bɔrɛmatapo nimuso na nɛ basa na kikɛ le: 3“Menyi to be eko beeŋ tiŋ n nyiŋi kananɛ bɔrɛlambu na be kela daa du a? Nuso nɛ k naa du n sa menyi naniere? K maŋ naa la shɛŋ n sa menyi, ŋko? 4Ama ekama e sa maŋ pɔ aba. Menyi ere e baa shuŋ kushuŋ na de, ŋkpal manɛ so, n wɔ menyi kutɔ. 5Kɔnɔ koŋwule be ŋkre nɛ ma nɛ men nanaana daŋ kre jemanɛ nɛ b daŋ lar Ijipt be efuli so na nɛ ŋ kraa bɛ so na. Ma alɛ be Kiyoyu kraa wɔ menyi to, amoso men sa maa lɔ kufu.
6K maaŋ chɛr, meeŋ naŋ gbuŋgbuŋ ebɔrɛso nɛ kasawule so nɛ teku nɛ kasawule wɔlso kikɛ. 7Meeŋ baga efuliana na kikɛ to n shin nɛ b bar asɔ lela nɛ baa sha ga na nfe, nɛ ma kemaŋkura e bɔlɔ bɔrɛlambu ere kikɛ to. 8Durnya to be shuwa nɛ gbiti kikɛ la meya nna. 9Bɔrɛlambu popɔr ere beeŋ lar kebita a chɔ kedra na, nɛ n shin nɛ ma basa e nya kayurwushi nɛ kedamaya nfe ashi.” Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e malga na.
Dra na nɛ echefoso be asheŋ
10Ewurgboŋ Dariɔs ka ji kuwura ashi Pɛshiya be efuli so be kafɛ nyɔsopo to be kufɔl kpanusopo to be nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ ana na nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ anebi Heegai le: 11“Bishi bɔrɛmatapoana na atuwebi nɛ b kɔ a laŋɛ asheŋ bishiso nɛ mee sha kebishi ere be kaplɛa so: 12Nɛ fanɛ esa pɛ mbe piŋi tenteŋ be kɔnɔso m bɔɔ eblaŋ nɛ k du cheembi ŋkpal b ka ta kumo n lara sarga n sa Ebɔrɛ so, nɛ piŋi tenteŋ na beta bodobodo ŋko ajibi daŋɛso ŋko yabra ŋko ajibi pɔtɛ ko, loŋ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ amo alɛ gba e ki cheembi a?”
Ndoŋ nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na kaŋɛ: “Ayai, loŋ maaŋ tiŋ n wora.”
13Ndoŋ nna nɛ Heegai bishi bumo, “Nɛ fanɛ esa wora eyurpi ŋkpal e ka beta ebuni so nseŋ beta ajibi, loŋ be ajibi na gba wora eyurpi a?”
Nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na kaŋɛ, “Mm, a wora eyurpi.”
14Ndoŋ nna nɛ Heegai kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ, aloŋ koŋwule na nɛ k du a laŋɛ basa ere nɛ efuli na kikɛ be kaplɛa so ŋ kutɔ. Kusɔ kama nɛ baa wora nɛ asɔ kama nɛ baa ta a lara esarga na kikɛ maŋ walɛ so.”
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka nase nɛfa be kɔnɔ be asheŋ
15Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ: “Menyi maŋ wu kusɔ nɛ k wora menyi na a? Pɔɛŋ nɛ men fara bɔrɛlambu na be kelɔŋɛ m pɔr 16ekama nɛ e daa yɔ aboyu nɛ e buri n nase ase daa tama kenya aboyu fanɛ ebɔtɛ anyɔ nna, ama e daa nya bɔtɛ koŋwule nna. Esa beeŋ yɔ yabra to a tama kenya ekɔlba kalfa be bɔlɔ bɔlɔ, ama e bee nya ekɔlba adena nna. 17Ma e daa shin nɛ bunyaŋ bee tɔr menyi be adɔjibi so nɛ e bee puu nsaa jija na, ama men kraŋ kini ketuba n lar menyi be alubi to. 18Kabre e la kufɔl kpanusopo na be nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ ana, kachɛ nɛ men tɔl bɔrɛlambu na be gbaltɔlase n loge. Yili kabre a yɔ, men baa dara kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ baa wora menyi to. 19Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ aboyu maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ ndibisɔrso na malɛ be kekama maŋ naŋ sɔr asɔrso kikɛ, ama yili kabre a yɔ meeŋ nɛfa menyi.”
Enyɛnpe na ka nase kɔnɔ n sa Zerubabel be asheŋ
20Kamɔnchɛ na gbagba nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ sa Heegai kubɔya nyɔsopo fanɛ, 21e kaŋɛ Zerubabel nɛ e la Juda be efuli so be gomena na le: “Mee sha kegbuŋgbuŋ ebɔrɛso nɛ kasawule so kikɛ nna. 22Ma alɛ beeŋ gboŋi bewura nseŋ m mur bumo be kuwurjiana. Meeŋ melgi bumo be egbaŋɛturko m buu nseŋ shin nɛ bumo be egbaŋɛ e wu nɛ bediipo na malɛ e kilgi a mɔ abar. 23Ama kaŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Zerubabel fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e lara mo nɛ e ji kuwura ma ketre to.” Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e malga na.

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1 I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo.
In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
2-3Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you. 4Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
5Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever. 6But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.”
First Vision: Horses and Riders
7-8 On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him. 9An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?”
“I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
10At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
11Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
12At this, the angel said, “Lord All-Powerful, for 70 years you have been angry with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. When are you ever going to have mercy on them?”
13The Lord's answer was kind and comforting. 14So the angel told me to announce:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem. 15For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned. 16And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again. 17I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion.
Second Vision: Animal Horns
18Next, I saw four animal horns. 19-21The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?”
His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.”
Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?”
He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka tre mbe basa fanɛ b bɛta m ba mo kutɔ be asheŋ
1Ewurgboŋ Dariɔs ka ji Pɛshiya be efuli so be kuwura be kafɛ nyɔsopo to be kufɔl burwasopo to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta kubɔya ere n sa anebi Zakareya nɛ e la Berekia pibinyɛn nsaa la Ido mo nanabi na. 2-3Le nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kaŋɛ anebi Zakareya fanɛ e kaŋɛ basa na: “Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ nya agbo nna n wɔtɔ men nananyɛnana, ama nɛ men bɛta m ba ŋ kutɔ meeŋ sɔ menyi nseŋ chɛ menyi to. 4Men sa maa wora fanɛ men nanaana na. Dra na kikɛ nɛ anebiana na ta ma kubɔya na n sa bumo fanɛ b sa maa wɔ kebaawɔtɔ lubi to. Ama b daa maŋ nu n sa ma ŋko n wora ma mmalga kasonu. 5Men nanaana na nɛ anebiana na kikɛ maŋ naa wɔ ŋkpa to. 6N daŋ bɔla anebiana nɛ b la ma nyɛrbi na so nna n sa men nanaana ma mbraana nɛ kefiɛso be mmalga, ama b daa maŋ tuge ma, nɛ kumo be kasogberge ba bumo so. Kumo be kaman nɛ b chɛrga bumo be nfɛra nseŋ shuli so fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e sa bumo kasogberge nɛ k daga bumo, fanɛ kananɛ ŋ kre kumo na.”
Anebi na ka ku egbaŋɛ be bɔrɛdare be asheŋ
7Ewurgboŋ Dariɔs ka ji kuwura na be kafɛ nyɔsopo be kufɔl kudukakosopo nɛ baa tre Shebat na be nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ ana nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ sa ma kubɔya edare to kanyɛso. 8Ashi edare na to n daŋ wu esa ko ka dii gbaŋɛ peper nna m ba yili ndibi ko be afito ashi ketaŋɛ ko to, nɛ egbaŋɛ peper kpaw nɛ bepeper kunɔkunɔ nɛ befuful ko malɛ yil mbe kaman. 9Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika nɛ e bee bugi asheŋ to a sa ma na le: “Manɛ nɛ egbaŋɛ ere bee ŋini?”
Nɛ e kaŋɛ ma: “Meeŋ ŋini fo kusɔ nɛ e bee ŋini.” 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn nɛ e daa yil ndibi na be afito na kaŋɛ ma le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shuŋi bumo fanɛ b ya nite n dara durnya ŋ keni.” 11Kumo be kaman nɛ egbaŋɛdiipo na ba kaŋɛ malaika nɛ e yil ndibi na be afito na le: “An nite ŋ kulti durnya kikɛ nseŋ wu fanɛ kakpa kikɛ wora shruum nna a dese kagbenewushi so.” 12Nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, fo ka nya agbo n wɔtɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ nde nɛ a wɔ Juda be efuli so na be nfɛ adushunu nde. Saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ wu bumo kuwɔr?”
13Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta kagbenewushi be mmalga nɛ e kɔ kechɛto n sa malaika na. 14Nɛ malaika na malɛ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ m ber kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ na be kubomboŋ. E yɛ: “Mee sha Jerusalɛm nɛ k la ma kadegboŋ cheembi na alegaiso, 15ama n nya agbo nna n wɔtɔ efuliana nɛ a wɔ kayurwushi to na ŋkpal manɛ so, n daŋ nya agbo gbrɛbi nna n wɔtɔ ma basa, nɛ loŋ be efuliana shin nɛ ma basa be awurfoŋ wora keshi n ti so. 16Amoso nɛ m bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm to nɛ m ba wu kadegboŋ na kuwɔr na. Baaŋ naŋ lɔŋɛ ma bɔrɛlambu na nɛ kadegboŋ na m pɔr.”
17Kumo be kaman nɛ Malaika na naŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Ma ndegboŋana na beeŋ naŋ dii dama. Ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ chɛ Jerusalɛm to nseŋ naŋ sɔ kumo ŋ ki ŋ gbagba be kadegboŋ.”
Alambɛ be bɔrɛdare be asheŋ
18Ade be kaman nɛ n naŋ ku bɔrɛdare ko n wu asɔbɔya be alambɛ ana ko. 19Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika nɛ e bee malga ŋ kutɔ na le: “Alambɛ ere be kefito a?”
Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Alambɛ na bee ŋini durnya to be efuli lempoana nɛ a shin nɛ Juda nɛ Israɛl nɛ Jerusalɛm to be basa pesaŋ to na nna.”
20Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini ma ebɔyɛpo ana ko. 21Nɛ m bishi le: “Manɛ nɛ ebɔyɛpo ere ba nɛ b ba wora?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ ma le: “B ba nna nɛ b ba funti nseŋ kɔ m pɔɔ efuli pɔtɛana nɛ a daŋ kɔ m pɔɔ Juda so n shin nɛ kumo be basa pesaŋ to na so nna.”

english_text:
Third Vision: A Measuring Line
1This time I saw someone holding a measuring line, 2and I asked, “Where are you going?”
“To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
3The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him 4and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall. 5The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.”
A Call to Action
6The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds. 7Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
8Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion:
Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him. 9And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
10City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you. 11When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful. 12Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
13Everyone, be silent!
The Lord is present
and moving about
in his holy place.
translation_text:
Efɔl karga asɔ be bɔrɛdare be asheŋ
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ n naŋ ku bɔrɛdare n wu kanyɛn ko nɛ e kɔ efɔl karga asɔ to. 2Nɛ m bishi mo le: “Nnɛ nɛ fee yɔ?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Mee yɔ nɛ n ya karga Jerusalɛm so, m pin kumo be nteŋ nɛ mpar nna.”
3Edare na to nɛ n wu malaika nɛ e malga ŋ kutɔ na ka bee yɔ nɛ malaika nyɔsopo ko malɛ ba shɛr mo to 4nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Shile n ya kaŋɛ kabrantiɛbia nɛ e kɔ efɔl karga asɔ to na fanɛ Jerusalɛm to be basa nɛ asɔbɔya beeŋ ba wora keshi ga nɛ b maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m pɔr egbal gba ŋ kulti kumo. 5Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nase kɔnɔ fanɛ mo gbagba beeŋ ki fanɛ edɛ be egbal ŋ kulti kadegboŋ na a kuŋ kumo nsaa la kumo be kemaŋkura ashi kumo to.”
B ka tre basa nɛ b pɛ n yɔ kenyaya to m ba epe be asheŋ
6-7Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ mbe basa le: “Ma e daŋ pesaŋ menyi to n sɔ kaplɛkama. Ama naniere men shile Babilɔn be efuli nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso na so m bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm to.” 8Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na shuŋi ma fanɛ n ya kaŋɛ efuli kama so ebi nɛ b daŋ kɔ m pɔɔ menyi nɛ men wɔ Jerusalɛm to so nseŋ sɔ menyi be asɔ na e la fanɛ,
Jerusalɛm du fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be kenishi nna. Kusɔ kama nɛ esa kama baŋ wora Jerusalɛm, mo nɛ amodoŋwura wora na. 9Amoso Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba e naaŋ kɔ menyi nɛ men be benapo nseŋ shin nɛ basa nɛ b daa shuŋ menyi na e kɔ m pɔɔ menyi so nseŋ suge menyi be asɔ kikɛ. Aloŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na gbagba e shuŋi ma.
10Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le: “Jerusalɛmebi! Men boŋ nshɛ kagbenefuliso, ŋkpal manɛ so, mee ba nna nɛ ma nɛ menyi e ba kaa wɔtɔ!”
11Loŋ be saŋɛ na efuli damtaana beeŋ ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ m ba ki mbe basa. E beeŋ ba chena menyi to nɛ men pin fanɛ mo e shuŋi ma menyi kutɔ. 12Juda beeŋ naŋ laŋɛ ŋ ki Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya ashi mbe kasawule cheembi so nɛ Jerusalɛm e ki kadegboŋ mo nɛ e bee sha ga.
13Ekama e wora shruum ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito, ŋkpal manɛ so, e koso kakpa cheembi nɛ e wɔ na nna a ba.

english_text:
Fourth Vision: Joshua and Satan
1 I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him. 2 But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
3Joshua's clothes were filthy. 4So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
5I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
6After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
7If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me. 8 Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
9Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country. 10 Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_text:
Joshuwa nɛ Setani be asheŋ
1Nɛ n naŋ ku bɔrɛdare n wu bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Joshuwa nɛ e yil Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be malaika kutɔ nɛ Setani malɛ yil Joshuwa be jisoso m mata mo e shin nɛ e ku asheŋ n deŋi mo. 2Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika na kaŋɛ Setani le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e fiɛ fo so, Setani! Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ mbe kasha wɔ Jerusalɛm so na e fiɛ fo so. Kanyɛn ere du fanɛ kadɛdibi nɛ b pee edɛ to nna.”
3Joshuwa daŋ buu asɔ biriso nna a yil ndoŋ. 4Ndoŋ nna nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ basa nɛ b daa yil ndoŋ na le: “Men lara kanyɛn ere be asɔ biriso nɛ e buu ere.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ Joshuwa malɛ le: “N lara fo alubi ashi fo so, ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ sa fo asɔbuuso popɔr nɛ fo buu.”
5Kede be kaman nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ basa na fanɛ b ta neemu popɔr m mɛa Joshuwa be kumu so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta asɔbuuso popɔr m buu mo nɛ malaika na yil a keni.
6Nɛ malaika na leŋ Joshuwa to ŋ kaŋɛ le: 7Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Nɛ fo baa wora ma mbraana kasonu nsaa shuŋ ashuŋ nɛ meeŋ baa sa fo bre, meeŋ shin nɛ fo baa keni ma bɔrɛlambu na nɛ kumo be kelɔnɛ so. Ma alɛ beeŋ baa nu fo kabɔrɛkule fanɛ kananɛ mee nu emalaika nɛ b wɔ ŋ kutɔ ere be kabɔrɛkule na.” 8Amoso fo, Joshuwa nɛ fo la bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ fo braana bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b wɔ nfe, e nu nɛnɛ. Menyi so nɛ echefoso be asheŋ lela kikɛ beeŋ bɔla so m ba, ŋkpal loŋ so mee sha kelara ma kayɛrbi nɛ e la ma ewura laraso na efuli nna. 9Kejembu nɛ ŋ kɔ a nase Joshuwa be anishito ere kɔ mba ashunu nna. Meeŋ sibɛ kusɔ ko n deŋi kumo so nseŋ ta kachɛ koŋwule n lara kasawule ere so ebi be alubi ashi bumo so. 10Kachɛ na kaŋ fo ekama beeŋ kela n tre mo kurgepoana nɛ b ba chena n ji kekurge kagbenewushiso ashi bumo be ndibi sɔrso be afito.

english_text:
Fifth Vision: A Lampstand and Olive Trees
1The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep. 2Then he asked, “What do you see?”
“A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames. 3 One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container. 4But, sir, what do these mean?”
5Then he asked, “Don't you know?”
“No sir,” I replied.
6 So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel:
I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit. 7Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
8The Lord spoke to me again and said:
9Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful. 10 Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone.
Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
Kefitilatɔl be bɔrɛdare be asheŋ
1Ndoŋ nna nɛ malaika nɛ e daa malga ŋ kutɔ na laŋɛ m ba tiŋi ma fanɛ ŋ ka daa di na, 2nseŋ bishi ma le: “Manɛ nɛ fo wu?”
Nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: “N wu shuwa be kefitilatɔl nɛ ŋku wɔ kurwa to a bɛ kumo be esoso nɛ efitila ashunu wɔ kumo so. Efitila na be kekama kɔ kumo be kechɛbi be kaboŋ nna. 3Ɔlif be ndibi anyɔ ko daa yil m mata kefitilatɔl na be mba anyɔ so nna.” 4Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika na le: “Ade ere be kifito e la manɛ?”
5Nɛ e bishi ma le: “Fo maŋ nyi a?”
Nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: “M-m kowurnyɛn, m maŋ nyi.”
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka nase kɔnɔ n sa Zerubabel be asheŋ
6Kumo be kaman nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ fanɛ n ta Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be kubɔya ere n sa Zerubabel. E yɛ: “Feeŋ pɔɔ fo doŋana so ama mannɛ kena to be eleŋ ŋko kuwibi to be eleŋ nɛ feeŋ ta ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so. Ma Kiyoyu na be eleŋ so nɛ feeŋ ta m pɔɔ so.” 7Kusɔ kama nɛ k du fanɛ kebee a kagle fo to beeŋ foe fo anishito. Feeŋ lɔŋɛ bɔrɛlambu na m pɔr. Kachɛ nɛ feeŋ ta lalaloge be berkishi m mɔ kapɔr na so na, basa na kikɛ beeŋ boŋ to awɔrso ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa kumo! Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa kumo!”
8Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: 9“Zerubabel e nase bɔrɛlambu na be gbaltɔlase, mo alɛ beeŋ pɔr kumo n loge. Nɛ loŋ kaŋ wora, ma basa beeŋ pin fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, e shuŋi fo bumo kutɔ.
10Bekama nɛ b keni kananɛ asheŋ fara gbrɛ gbrɛbi kabre ere jiga na kaŋ wu kejembu nɛ kumo be asheŋ tir ga ere ka bɔɔ Zerubabel enɔ na, baaŋ ji eyur kagbenefuliso
Kumo be kaman nɛ malaika na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: Efitilatɔl ashunu na e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anishi ashunu nɛ a bee keni a wu kusɔ kikɛ durnya ere kikɛ to na.”
11Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika na le: “Manɛ nɛ ɔlif be ndibi anyɔ nɛ a yil m mata kefitilatɔl na be bena nɛ jisoso na malɛ bee ŋini? 12Manɛ nɛ ɔlif be ndibi be ayabi anyɔ nɛ a mata shuwa be asɔ kulkulso tentembi anyɔ nɛ ɔlif be ŋku bee bɔla amo to a lar na malɛ bee ŋini?”
13Nɛ malaika na bishi ma le: “Fo maŋ nyi amo be afito a?”
Nɛ n yɛ: “M-m kowurnyɛn, m maŋ nyi.”
14Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ: “A yili nna n sa basa anyɔ na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ b duga ŋku n do bumo be amu so nseŋ lara bumo n yili fanɛ b baa shuŋ mo ere Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la durnya kikɛ be Enyɛnpe na.”

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
Kawɔl sibɛso nɛ k bee firgi na be asheŋ
1Kede be kaman nɛ n naŋ to kenishi ŋ keni n wu kawɔl sibɛso ko ka bee firgi afu to. 2Nɛ malaika na bishi ma kusɔ nɛ n wu, nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “N wu kawɔl sibɛso ka bee firgi afu to nna. Kumo be nteŋ to sa fanɛ ayadra adesa nɛ kumo be mparto malɛ sa fanɛ ayadra kuduanu nna.”
3Ndoŋ nna nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ ma: “B sibɛ kɔnɔsho nɛ k beeŋ ba durnya be kasawule so kikɛ nna n wɔtɔ kumo to. Kawɔl sibɛso na be kaba ko so bee kute kananɛ baaŋ lara eyu kikɛ ashi kasawule so nna, nɛ kaba nyɔsopo malɛ bee kute kananɛ baaŋ ju esa kama nɛ e bee bɔ ntaŋ a ku efɛ be asheŋ nna. 4Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ e beeŋ shin nɛ kɔnɔsho ere e luri eyu nɛ ekama nɛ e bee bɔ ntaŋ a ku efɛ kikɛ be elaŋana to nseŋ shir elaŋ na so hale nɛ a ya mur cheche.”
Eche nɛ e wɔ kelantaŋɛ to na be asheŋ
5Kumo be kaman nɛ malaika na naŋ lar ŋ kaŋɛ ma le: “Keni awɔlto, kusɔ pɔtɛ ko bee ba!”
6Nɛ m bishi mo: “Manɛ nna?”
Nɛ e kaŋɛ ma: “K la kelantaŋɛ nɛ k yili n sa basa nɛ b wɔ kasawule so kikɛ be alubi nna.”
7B ka bugi kelantaŋɛ na be buuso nɛ b ta epal n lɔŋɛ na nɛ n wu fanɛ eche ko e daa tase kumo to! 8Nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ: “Kache ere yili n sa kumu kpakpaso nna.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ ŋin kelantaŋɛ na be buuso m buu so kpakpa.
9Ŋ ka naŋ maŋ kumu so ŋ keni esoso nɛ n wu beche anyɔ ko nɛ b kɔ tɔkɔrkɔ be atɛ lempo ka firgi m ba ŋ kutɔ m ba fuu kelantaŋɛ na n firgi a yɔ. 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika nɛ e daa malga ŋ kutɔ na le: “Nnɛ nɛ b kɔ kelantaŋɛ na a yɔ?”
11Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Babilɔn be efuli so nɛ b kɔ kumo a yɔ nɛ b ya pɔr lambu n ta kumo n wɔtɔ nɛ basa e baa bunyaŋ kumo ndoŋ.”

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
Egbaŋɛturko ana na be asheŋ
1Kede be kaman nɛ n naŋ ku bɔrɛdare ko gba n wu egbaŋɛturko ana ko ka shi danyaŋ be abee anyɔ ko be kefɛato a ba. 2Gbaŋɛ peper e daa gberge sososo be gbaŋɛturko na nɛ gbaŋɛ lembir malɛ daa gberge kenyɔsopo na. 3Egbaŋɛ fuful e daa gberge gbaŋɛturko sasopo na nɛ egbaŋɛ muchɛr muchɛr malɛ daa gberge kenasopo na. Egbaŋɛ na kikɛ daa gberge amo eleŋso nna. 4Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi malaika na: “Gafrache, egbaŋɛturko ere be kifito a?”
5Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “A yili nna n sa ayoyu ana nɛ a shi Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la Enyɛnpe durnya kikɛ so na kutɔ m ba na.”
6Egbaŋɛ lembir na daa gberge gbaŋɛturko na nna a yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso be kaba so na, nɛ egbaŋɛ fuful na malɛ daa yɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so nɛ bemuchɛr muchɛr na malɛ daa yɔ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so.
7Egbaŋɛ lempoana na ka daŋ lar m ba na b daa fin keyɔ durnya be efuli kama so kenishipereso nna. Ndoŋ nna nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ egbaŋɛ na le: “Meeŋ ya nite ŋ kulti durnya be efuli kikɛ so!” Nɛ b nu nseŋ yɔ. 8Kumo be kaman nɛ malaika na boŋ to ŋ kaŋɛ ma “Egbaŋɛ nɛ a yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso be kaba so na e shin nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be agbo wushi.”
Joshuwa be kuwurwuro be asheŋ
9Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: 10-11“Sɔ shuwa nɛ gbiti be ŋkɛ ashi Helda nɛ Tobija nɛ Jedaya nɛ b la basa nɛ b shi Babilɔn be efuli so m bɛta na kutɔ n wora kuwurwuro. Kumo be kaman nɛ fo nɛ bumo e yɔ Josaya nɛ e la Zefanaiya pibinyɛn na pe n ya ta kuwurwuro na m buu bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Joshuwa nɛ e la Jehozadak pibinyɛn na. 12Kumo be kaman nɛ fo kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: ‘Kanyɛn ko beeŋ shi kakpa nɛ fo wɔ ere n lar fanɛ keyimu ka pete na m ba lɔŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛlambu na m pɔr. 13Mo e naŋ pɔr kumo n nya kemaŋkura fanɛ ewura na nseŋ ji mbe basa so kuwura. Mo nɛ bɔrɛmatapo ko beeŋ wora kɔnɔkoŋwule n chɛ abar to n shuŋ kayurwushiso.’ 14Kuwurwuro na beeŋ baa la kanyiŋi be kusɔ bɔrɛlambu na to n sa Heldai nɛ Tobija nɛ Jedaya nɛ Josaya nɛ e la Zefanaiya pibinyɛn na.”
15Basa beeŋ shi efuli wɔfɔ so m ba chɛ to n lɔŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛlambu na m pɔr. B kaŋ lɔŋɛ kumo m pɔr n loge na nɛ feeŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e shuŋi ma. Fo baa wora Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na be mbraana kikɛ kasonu, ade kikɛ beeŋ wora m bɔlɔ so ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka maa sha ekishi nɛ k maŋ shi kagbene to be asheŋ
1Ewurgboŋ Dariɔs ka ji Pɛshiya be efuli so be kuwura be kafɛ nasopo to be kufɔl kpanusopo nɛ baa tre Keslɛv na be kachɛ nasopo to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta kubɔya n sa ma, Zakareya. 2Bɛtɛl be kade to ebi daŋ shuŋi Shareza nɛ Regɛm-Mɛlɛk nɛ bumo be benyɛn ko nna fanɛ b yɔ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛlambu to n ya kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be nɛfa n sa bumo 3nseŋ naŋ bishi bɔrɛmatapoana na nɛ anebiana na le be kesheŋ bishiso ere: “An baa kraa shu nli nsaa kishi kufɔl nusopo na to fanɛ kananɛ an wora nfɛ damta ŋkpal b ka daŋ bure bɔrɛlambu na so a?”
4Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na ta kubɔya ere n sa ma. 5E yɛ: “Kaŋɛ efuli na so ebi nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na fanɛ mannɛ ma ere be kemaŋkura so nɛ b daa kishi nsaa shu nli kufɔl nusopo nɛ keshunusopo na to nfɛ adushunu nɛ a choŋ na. 6B ka daa ji a nuu na bre ma so nɛ b daa wora loŋ a?”
7Kubɔya koŋwule ere nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ bɔla anebi juŋkparsoana na so m bɔ n sa basa nɛ b daa wɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ nde nɛ a kulti kumo na to saŋɛ nɛ b daŋ dii dama nsaa wɔ kayurwushi to na. Loŋ be jemanɛ na, basa damta daŋ chena kelargato be kaseto be keshishɛrsawule na nɛ abeesawule nɛ a wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so na so nna.
Kusoe kpakpaso ka bar basa be kepɛ n yɔ efuli pɔtɛ so be asheŋ
8Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ sa ma le be kubɔya ere. 9E yɛ: “Dra dra na kikɛ nɛ n ta atande ere n sa ma basa ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: ‘Men baa wora asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so, men baa la basa nsaa wora kelela nsaa wu abar kuwɔr. 10Men sa maa kɔrfɛ bekulpoche nɛ amunibi nɛ befɔ nɛ b chena menyi to nɛ betentaŋasepo. Menyi alɛ e sa maa fɛ nfɛra lubi a laŋɛ men braana be kaplɛa so ashi menyi be ŋgbene to.’ ”
11Ama ma basa ta ŋkpensheŋ nna m pal kaman n sa ma nseŋ ti bumo be asoe ŋ kini kenu n sa ma. B daŋ kplaŋ ma so nna 12nseŋ wora bumo be ŋgbene kpakpa fanɛ awarabi nsaa maa kaŋ asoe a nu mmalga nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be Kiyoyu bɔla anebi juŋkparsoana so n ta n sa bumo na ŋko a bɛ ma mbra so. Amoso n daŋ nya agbo nna ga n wɔtɔ bumo. 13Ŋkpal b ka daŋ kini kenu n sa ma jemanɛ nɛ n daa malga bumo kutɔ na so, nɛ ma alɛ gba maŋ nu bumo be kekule. 14N daŋ pesaŋ bumo to nna n ya lɛ efuli pɔtɛana so fanɛ kananɛ afugboŋ bee pesaŋ asɔ to n ya kaa lɛ na, nɛ bumo be kasawule lela na dese fuloŋ nɛ esa kikɛ daa maŋ naa wɔ kumo so.

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
22Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness. 23When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e ka beeŋ naŋ nɛfa Jerusalɛm be asheŋ
1Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ ta kubɔya ere n sa ma, Zakareya. 2E yɛ: “Ŋ ka bee sha Jerusalɛm nɛ kumo to be basa alegaiso so, bumo doŋana be asheŋ bee nu ma agbo nna. 3Meeŋ naŋ bɛta m ba chena Zayɔn be kebee na so ashi Jerusalɛm to. Aloŋ nɛ ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ Jerusalɛm la ma beyirdapo be kadegboŋ nna nɛ Zayɔn malɛ la ma kebee cheembi. 4Basa belso nɛ baa keta akpabi a nite beeŋ naa gama a chena abar so ashi Jerusalɛm to 5nɛ mbinyɛnsobi nɛ bechesobi malɛ e sɔ agbembi so a pel.
6Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ: Basa nɛ baaŋ ka efuli na so beeŋ baa fɛ fanɛ loŋ maaŋ tiŋ n wora, ama kumo be kewora maŋ du ma so kpakpa. 7Meeŋ mɔlga ma basa ashi efuliana nɛ a wɔ epeŋilarkpa nɛ epeŋitɔrkpa na 8nseŋ bɛta bumo m ba chena Jerusalɛm to. Baaŋ ba kaa la ma basa nɛ ma alɛ e baa la bumo be Ebɔrɛ nsaa ji kuwura bumo so kashenteŋ nɛ kumo be ekpa so.”
9Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ nde: “Mmalga nɛ ma anebiana na daŋ malga jemanɛ nɛ b daa tɔl ma bɔrɛlambu na be gbaltɔlase na nɛ menyee nu na, amoso men baa kɔ kenyɛn nsaa maa pɔ aba. 10Pɔɛŋ nɛ b pɔr bɔrɛlambu na nɛ esa kikɛ daa maa kɔ amansherbi nɛ e tiŋ m ber basa paa ŋko n haya asɔbɔya nɛ b shuŋ n sa mo. Esa kama malɛ daa maa tiŋ a kuŋ mbe kumu ashi mo doŋana be enɔ to. N daŋ shin nna nɛ basa fɛaŋ abar so a wɔtɔ nna. 11Ama naniere bre, m maaŋ naŋ gberge menyi basa gbrɛbi nɛ men ka ere kusoe fanɛ kananɛ n daŋ wora bedarapo na jemanɛ nɛ k choŋ na. 12Meeŋ shin nɛ men dɔ n duu menyi be asɔduuso kayurwushiso. Menyi be afeelebi nɛ e bee sɔr asɔrso nɛ baa tre greeps na beeŋ sɔr nɛnɛ, nɛ bɔrɛ e ba ga nɛ men be kasawule e wora adɔjibi nɛnɛ. Ma efuli so be basa nɛ baaŋ ji efute na nɛ meeŋ nɛfa le be ekpa so. 13Efuli pɔtɛana be basa bee shoduu menyi Juda nɛ Israɛl be efuliana so ebi nna, ama meeŋ mɔlga menyi nseŋ shin nɛ men ki nɛfa be basa. Men baa kɔ kenyɛn nsaa maa lɔ kufu.”
14Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ: “Men nanaana ka daŋ shin nɛ n nya agbo na, n daŋ kre fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ b ji jɛrbi nna nseŋ shin nɛ loŋ wora. 15Ama naniere mee kre kenɛfa Jerusalɛm to nɛ Juda be efuli so ebi nna. Amoso men sa maa lɔ kufu. 16Asɔ nɛ a daga fanɛ men baa wora e la kebaaji abar kashenteŋ nsaa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so ashi menyi be demujikpaana saŋɛ na so kayurwushi beeŋ baa wɔ menyi to. 17Men sa maa kre kebaawora abar kulubi. Men sa maa bɔ ntaŋ a ji efɛ be eshɛda. Ŋ kishi le be alubiana ere kikɛ nna.”
18Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le. 19E yɛ: “Ekishi nɛ menyee kishi kufɔl nasopo nɛ kenusopo nɛ keshunusopo nɛ kudusopo to na beeŋ ki kayurji nɛ kagbenefuli be nchɛgboŋ n sa Juda be efuli so ebi. Amoso a daga fanɛ men baa sha kashenteŋ nɛ kayurwushi.”
20Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ: “Jemanɛ ko bee ba nɛ basa damta e shi efuli pɔtɛana so be ndegboŋ damta to m ba Jerusalɛm to. 21Bumo nɛ b shi kadegboŋ koŋwule to beeŋ kaŋɛ abar le: ‘Anyee yɔ nna nɛ an ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ kule mo nɛ e nɛfa anyi. Amoso men ba nɛ an yɔ!’ 22Basa damta beeŋ shi efuligboŋana so m ba Jerusalɛm to m ba bunyaŋ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ kule mo fanɛ e nɛfa bumo. 23Loŋ be jemanɛ na so, eyiri pɔtɛ nɛ efuli pɔtɛana so be basa kudu beeŋ pɛ Israɛl be esa koŋwule be kale to nsaa kaŋɛ mo le: Shin nɛ an bɛ fo so a yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an nu fanɛ Ebɔrɛ wɔ men kutɔ nna.”

english_text:
Israel's Enemies Will Be Punished
1 This is a message
from the Lord:
His eyes are on everyone,
especially the tribes
of Israel.
So he pronounces judgment
against the cities
of Hadrach and Damascus.
2Judgment will also fall
on the nearby city
of Hamath,
as well as on Tyre and Sidon,
whose people are clever.
3Tyre has built a fortress
and piled up silver and gold,
as though they were dust
or mud from the streets.
4Now the Lord will punish Tyre
with poverty;
he will sink its ships
and send it up in flames.
5 Both Ashkelon and Gaza
will tremble with fear;
Ekron will lose all hope.
Gaza's king will be killed,
and Ashkelon emptied
of its people.
6A mob of half-breeds
will settle in Ashdod,
and the Lord himself
will rob Philistia of pride.
7No longer will the Philistines
eat meat with blood in it
or any unclean food.
They will become part
of the people of our God
from the tribe of Judah.
And God will accept
the people of Ekron,
as he did the Jebusites.
8God says, “I will stand guard
to protect my temple from those
who come to attack.
I know what's happening,
and no one will mistreat
my people ever again.”
The Lord Tells about the Coming King
9 Everyone in Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
Your king has won a victory,
and he is coming to you.
He is humble
and rides on a donkey;
he comes on the colt
of a donkey.
10 I, the Lord, will take away
war chariots and horses
from Israel and Jerusalem.
Bows that were made for battle
will be broken.
I will bring peace to nations,
and your king will rule
from sea to sea.
His kingdom will reach
from the Euphrates River
across the earth.
The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
11 When I made a sacred agreement
with you, my people,
we sealed it with blood.
Now some of you are captives
in waterless pits,
but I will come to your rescue
12and offer you hope.
Return to your fortress,
because today I will reward you
with twice what you had.
13I will use Judah as my bow
and Israel as my arrow.
I will take the people of Zion
as my sword
and attack the Greeks.
The Lord Will Protect His People
14Like a cloud, the Lord God
will appear over his people,
and his arrows will flash
like lightning.
God will sound his trumpet
and attack in a whirlwind
from the south.
15The Lord All-Powerful
will protect his people,
and they will trample down
the sharpshooters
and their slingshots.
They will drink and get rowdy;
they will be as full as a bowl
at the time of sacrifice.
16The Lord God will save them
on that day,
because they are his people,
and they will shine on his land
like jewels in a crown.
17How lovely they will be.
Young people will grow there
like grain in a field
or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_text:
Demuji nɛ k bee ba Israɛl mo doŋana so be asheŋ
1Kubɔya nɛ k shi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ nde: E yɛ, mbe anishi yuu edimɛdi kikɛ so nna, fɔŋfɔŋ eyiri yiri nɛ b wɔ Israɛl be efuli so na. Mo alɛ naŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ mbe demuji na beeŋ ba Hadrak nɛ kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Damaskɔs na ashi Siriya be efuli so na so.
2Kumo be kaman mbe demuji beeŋ ba Hamaf be kade nɛ k mata Hadrak na gba so. Nde nɛ baa tre Tayɛ nɛ Sidɔn nɛ amo to be basa nyi kasheŋ wora ga na gba maaŋ lar demuji na to.
3Tayɛ be basa pɔr ebu lempo jeŋgreŋ ko a kuŋ bumo be amu nna nseŋ gbare shuwa nɛ gbiti m biti abar so fanɛ eshishɛr na! 4Ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ suge asɔ kama nɛ Tayɛ ebi na kɔ na. E beeŋ shin nɛ bumo be asɔ lela nɛ b kɔ na e mur teku to nɛ edɛ e ji kade na m mur cheche.
5Filisti be efuli so be basa nɛ b wɔ kade nɛ baa tre Ashkɛlɔn na beeŋ wu kusɔ nɛ k wora na nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo nɛ ebesa damta e ji basa nɛ b wɔ Gaza be kadegboŋ to na. Aloŋ e naŋ wora Ekrɔn be kadegboŋ to ebi gba. Bumo be tama beeŋ loge, ŋkpal b ka nyi fanɛ bumo alɛ gba beeŋ kɔ n tɔr so. Gaza beeŋ paŋ kumo be ewura nɛ Ashkɛlɔn e ki kade bureso a dese fuloŋ. 6Eyiri bubɔrɔ e naŋ ba sɔ Ashdɔd be kade na n chena, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba e shin nɛ Filistiebi na e ŋaba a maaŋ naa tiŋ m puchi kikɛ. 7Filistiebi na maaŋ naa we eblaŋ nɛ a kraa kɔ ŋklaŋ amo to ŋko a ji ajibi nɛ baa kishi. Bekama nɛ baaŋ ji efute na beeŋ ki ma basa a du fanɛ Juda be yiri to be kabuna ko be basa. Ekrɔnebi malɛ beeŋ ki ma basa fanɛ kananɛ Jebusiebi ki na. 8Ebɔrɛ yɛ: “Meeŋ baa kuŋ ma kasawule nɛ benapo nɛ baa kulti a mɔ basa na maaŋ nya kumo so m bɔla choŋ. M maaŋ sa kumukpakpasowuraana ekpa nɛ b naa kɔrfɛ ma basa. N wu awurfoŋ nɛ ma basa ji na kikɛ.”
Zayɔn be ewura popɔr na be asheŋ
9Ekama nɛ e wɔ Jerusalɛm to
e baa ji eyur nsaa wora awɔr kagbenefuliso!
Ŋkpal manɛ so menyi be ewura kɔ m pɔɔ so
nsaa ba menyi kutɔ;
e du boeŋ nna nseŋ dii kurmafɔlbi a ba.
10Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ:
“Meeŋ lara kena to be egbaŋɛturko
nɛ egbaŋɛ ashi Israɛl be efuli so nɛ Jerusalɛm to.
Ata nɛ b lɔŋɛ ŋkpal kena so na
beeŋ buri to.
Meeŋ bar kayurwushi efuliana na so,
nɛ menyi be ewura e
yili teku ko ase a ji kuwura n ya fo teku nyɔsopo ase.
Mbe kuwurji beeŋ shi Yufreetes be Lɔr na ase
n ya fo durnya be ekar kikɛ.”
Kenaŋ laŋɛ Ebɔrɛ be basa m ba be asheŋ
11Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ:
“Ŋkpal ma nɛ menyi be kɔnɔkoŋwule
be ŋkre nɛ b ta esarga be ŋklaŋ m mɔ kumo so na so,
meeŋ lara menyi be basa ashi kenyaya nɛ k du
fanɛ kemaŋ chiŋgeliŋ nɛ k maŋ kɔ nchu na to.
12Men bɛta m ba menyi be kumɔlga
be kakpa lempo na nseŋ nya tama.
Ŋkpal manɛ so, kabre meeŋ laŋɛ asɔ
nɛ men daa kɔ na be ntuŋ anyɔso n sa menyi.
13Meeŋ ta Judaebi fanɛ enapo be keta na,
nseŋ ta Israɛlebi malɛ fanɛ ma atanyembi.”
Ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ ta Zayɔn be basa
fanɛ ma tokobi, ŋ kɔ Griikebi kena.
14Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ba buu
mbe basa so fanɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa,
nseŋ to mbe atanyembi
fanɛ bɔrɛ ka nyɛkpɛ na.
Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ beeŋ foŋ mbe kabel
nseŋ bɔla bɔrɛfu to n shi kelargato
be kaseto m ba.
15Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ baa kuŋ mbe basa,
nɛ b kɔ m pɔɔ bumo doŋana so m mur bumo.
Baaŋ baa wora awɔr kena to fanɛ basa boo so
nseŋ shin nɛ ŋklaŋ e lar bumo doŋana be eyurana so
a shile fanɛ kananɛ bɔrɛmatapo bee chulgi
sarga be asɔbɔya be ŋklaŋ a wurge bɔrɛsure na so na.
16Kamɔnchɛ na Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na
e naŋ mɔlga mbe basa fanɛ kananɛ
mbolpɔkpapo bee mɔlga mbe mbolpɔ
ashi kenishipere to na.
Baaŋ baa nyɛkpɛ mbe kasawule so
fanɛ kuwurwuro so be amaŋkanibi na.
17Baaŋ baa walɛ kebita kashenteŋto!
Mbifɔlbi beeŋ daŋ a kɔ eleŋ nɛnɛ
ŋkpal b ka beeŋ nya aboyu damta a ji
nsaa nya yabra popɔr a nuu so.

english_text:
A Bright Future for Judah and Israel
1I, the Lord, am the one
who sends storm clouds
and showers of rain
to make fields produce.
So when the crops need rain,
you should pray to me.
2 You can't believe idols
and fortunetellers,
or depend on the hope
you receive from witchcraft
and interpreters of dreams.
But you have tried all of these,
and now you are like sheep
without a shepherd.
3I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am fiercely angry
with you leaders,
and I will punish you.
I care for my people,
the nation of Judah,
and I will change
this flock of sheep
into charging war horses.
4From this flock will come leaders
who will be strong
like cornerstones and tent pegs
and weapons of war.
5They will join in the fighting,
and together they will trample
their enemies like mud.
They will fight,
because I, the Lord,
will be on their side.
And they will crush
the enemy cavalry.
6I will strengthen
the kingdoms of Judah
and Israel.
And I will show mercy
because I am the Lord,
their God.
I will answer their prayers
and bring them home.
Then it will seem as though
I had never rejected them.
7Israel will be like
a tribe of warriors
celebrating with wine.
When their children see this,
they will also be happy
because of me, the Lord.
8I will give a signal
for them to come together
because I have rescued them.
And there will be as many
as ever before.
9 Although I scattered my people
in distant countries,
they won't forget me.
Once their children are raised,
they will return—
10I will bring them home
from Egypt and Assyria,
then let them settle
as far as Gilead and Lebanon,
until the land overflows
with them.
11My people will go through
an ocean of troubles,
but I will overcome the waves
and dry up the deepest part
of the Nile.
Assyria's great pride
will be put down,
and the power of Egypt
will disappear.
12I'll strengthen my people
because of who I am,
and they will follow me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka nase kumɔlga be kɔnɔ be asheŋ
1Men kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bɔrɛchu kechali so. Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee mɔl a ba, a shin nɛ kasawule so bee nya kayul nɛ asɔduu bee kɔr a wora nɛ edimɛdi bee nya a ji. 2Basa bee yɔ agbir to nɛ bekpalpo kutɔ nna, ama asheŋ fuloŋ nɛ efɛsheŋ nɛ baa nya ashi bumo kutɔ. Beko bee kute edare be afito, ama bumo alɛ bee fule basa nna a sa bumo kagbenewushi fuloŋ. Ŋkpal loŋ so basa bee nite a kulti fanɛ mbolpɔ foeso nna. Asheŋ maa nyalɛ a sa bumo ŋkpal b ka maŋ kɔ esa nɛ e bee keni bumo so so.
3Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “N nya agbo nna n wora befɔ nɛ baa ji kuwura ma basa so nsaa shin nɛ ŋ gberge bumo kusoe. Juda be efuli so be basa na la ma basa nna, nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ baa keni bumo so. Baaŋ baa du fanɛ ma kena to be egbaŋɛ lempo nna. 4Bewura nɛ bejuŋkparpo nɛ gomena be ekrachi nimuso nɛ b kɔ eleŋ beeŋ shi Juda be yiri to n lar. 5Juda be basa beeŋ sɔ kelempo fanɛ benapo nɛ b kɔ m pɔɔ bumo doŋana so nsaa chichi bumo so fanɛ ekpa to be depɔ na. Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka wɔ bumo kutɔ so, baaŋ kɔ m pɔɔ bedoŋ nɛ b dii egbaŋɛ a kɔ gba so.
6Meeŋ sa Juda be basa eleŋ,
nseŋ mɔlga Israɛl be basa.
Meeŋ wu bumo kuwɔr
nseŋ bɛta bumo kikɛ m ba epe.
Baaŋ baa du fanɛ basa nɛ m maŋ naŋ kini ŋ ku so nna.
Ma e la Enyɛnpe bumo be Ebɔrɛ na;
ma alɛ beeŋ nu bumo be kabɔrɛkule.
7Israɛl be basa na beeŋ baa kɔ eleŋ fanɛ benapo,
nsaa kɔ kagbenefuli fanɛ eyabra nuupo.
Bumo be kaman to ebi beeŋ baa nyiŋi
kekɔmpɔɔso ere nɛ bumo be ŋgbene a fuli
ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wora so.
8Meeŋ tre ma basa m ba gama abar so,
ma alɛ beeŋ mɔlga bumo nseŋ shin nɛ
b wora keshi a du fanɛ kananɛ b daa sa na.
9Hale ŋ ka shin nɛ b pesaŋ to
a wɔ efuli pɔtɛana so ere gba,
b kraa nyiŋi ma asheŋ ashi
mboŋ wɔfɔ na nna.
Bumo nɛ bumo be mbia beeŋ ji efute
nseŋ gama abar so m bɛta m ba epe.
10Meeŋ ya keta bumo n shi
Ijipt nɛ Asiriya be efuliana so m ba epe,
nɛ b ba chena bumo gbagba be kasawule so.
Meeŋ shin nɛ b chena Giliad nɛ
Lebanɔn be nsawule gba so,
n sɔ amo kikɛ so.
11B kaŋ bɔla bumo be etɔrɔbi
nɛ e du fanɛ teku ere to a choŋ,
ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ yɔɔ atili na
nseŋ shin nɛ Nail be lɔr nɛ k wɔ Ijipt be efuli so na
be kechimbi to be nchu e feeto.
Meeŋ shin nɛ Asiriyaebi be kamoowugboŋ na e ba kaseto,
nɛ Ijiptebi e paŋ bumo be eleŋgboŋ na.
12Meeŋ naŋ wɔtɔ ma basa eleŋ to,
nɛ b baa bunyaŋ ma nsaa wora ma kasonu.
Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e malga na!”

english_text:
Trouble for Israel's Enemies
1Lebanon, open your gates!
Let the fire come in
to destroy your cedar trees.
2Cry, you cypress trees!
The glorious cedars have fallen
and are rotting.
Cry, you oak trees of Bashan!
The dense forest
has been chopped down.
3Listen! Shepherds are crying.
Their glorious pastures
have been ruined.
Listen! Lions are roaring.
The forests of the Jordan Valley
are no more to be found.
Worthless Shepherds
4The Lord my God said to me:
Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter! 5The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
6Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
7So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.” 8In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them. 9Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
10On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people. 11The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord. 12-13 I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly 30 pieces of silver.
Then the Lord said, “Throw the money into the treasury.” So I threw the money into the treasury at the Lord's temple. 14Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
15Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd. 16Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
17You worthless shepherd,
deserting the sheep!
I hope a sword
will cripple your arm
and blind your right eye.
translation_text:
Belempo nyaŋnyaŋso be ketɔr be asheŋ
1Lebanɔnebi men bugi menyi be mbuna,
nɛ edɛ e chɔɔ menyi be ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na!
2Seprɛs be ndibi, men baa shu nsaa boŋ to
ŋkpal manɛ so, sida be ndibi tɔr;
kemaŋkura be ndibi na kikɛ mur!
Bashan be ndibigboŋ, men baa shu nsaa boŋ to;
ŋkpal b ka ku kupogboŋ na to be ndibi
damta na kikɛ n lɛ so!
3Men nu mbolpɔkpapoana ka bee shu awɔrso;
ŋkpal bumo be mbolpɔ be ejikpa lela na ka mur so!
Men nu ebuluŋ ka bee munto;
ŋkpal Jɔɔdan be lɔrkar be kupogboŋ lela na ka mur so!
Mbolpɔkpapo anyɔ ko be asheŋ
4Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe ma Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma nde: “Ta fo kumu ŋ ki fanɛ mbolpɔkpapo nɛ baa shin nɛ b mɔ mbe mbolpɔ. 5Basa nɛ b tɔ bumo na bee mɔ bumo nna nsaa ta bumo be amu a ji. Nɛ basa nɛ baa fa mbolpɔ na malɛ bee kaŋɛ le: ‘Mee di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ ŋkpal ŋ ka dii dama so!’ Mbolpɔkpapoana na gbagba maa shu mbolpɔ na so.”
6Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “M maaŋ naŋ shu ekama so ashi durnya ere to. Ŋ gbagba beeŋ ta basa na m bɔɔ bumo braana nɛ bewurjipoana enɔ nɛ b mur durnya ere cheche nɛ m maaŋ mɔlga kumo ashi bumo be enɔ to.”
7Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ ŋ ki mbolpɔ nɛ b kɔ a yɔ nɛ b ya mɔ na be ekenipo, nseŋ ta akpabi anyɔ ŋ keta a kpa bumo na. N daa tre kuko ‘Kushuso’ nsaa tre kuko malɛ ‘Kɔnɔkoŋwule’ nna. 8Kufɔl koŋwule to nɛ n nya agbo n ju mbolpɔkpapo asa ko nɛ b daŋ kishi ma asheŋ ga na. 9Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mbolpɔ na le: “M maaŋ naa la menyi be ekenipo. Bumo nɛ baaŋ wu, b wu. Bumo nɛ baaŋ mur malɛ e mur. Bumo nɛ baaŋ ka malɛ e baa pɛ abar a we.” 10Kumo be kamɔnchɛ nɛ m bu kekpabi nɛ mee tre ‘Kushuso’ na to, a ŋini fanɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ efuliana na kikɛ kre na ku to. 11Amoso kumo be kamɔnchɛ kikɛ nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na ku to. Basa nɛ baa tɔ mbolpɔ a fa na daa keni ma nna, nseŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bɔla kusɔ nɛ n wora ere so nna a malga a sa bumo. 12Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Nɛ menyee sha, menyeeŋ tiŋ n ta ma kakɔka n sa ma. Ama nɛ menyi maaŋ sa, men baa kɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b sa ma gbiti be ndarbi adesa fanɛ amo e la ma kakɔka.
13Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le: “Ta amo n ya wɔtɔ bɔrɛlambu na be lɔkɔ na to.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ n ta gbiti be ndarbi adesa nɛ b fɛ fanɛ amo e daga ma na n ya wɔtɔ bɔrɛlambu be lɔkɔ na to. 14Kede be kaman nɛ n naŋ bu kekpabi nyɔsopo nɛ mee tre ‘kɔnɔkoŋwule’ na to, nɛ Juda nɛ Israɛl be kekurgeji ku to.
15Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le: “Naŋ laŋɛ ŋ ki mbolpɔkpapo nɛ e maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ kikɛ na. 16Ŋkpal manɛ so n lara mbolpɔkpapo ko fanɛ e ba kaa keni ma mbolpɔ so, ama mo shɛŋ maaŋ baa wɔ bumo nɛ baaŋ foe na to ŋko nɛ e nite n fin bewurbi na ŋko n chɛ bumo nɛ baa lɔ na ŋko ŋ kpa bumo nɛ b kɔ alenfia na n yɔ keji to. Ama bedanso na nɛ e beeŋ baa mɔ a we a ka awibi. 17Asheŋ maaŋ nyalɛ n sa loŋ be mbolpɔkpapo jiga nɛ e yige mbe mbolpɔ n lɛ na! Mbe eleŋ kikɛ beeŋ mur ashi kena to. Mbe kabre beeŋ wu, nɛ mbe jisoso be kenishi malɛ e tan!”

english_text:
Victory for Jerusalem
1This is a message from the Lord about Israel:
I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans. 2I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked. 3But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it.
When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem, 4I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah. 5Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
6At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
7But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself. 8I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader. 9I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem.
Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
10 I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born. 11On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo. 12Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan, 13Levi, Shimei, 14and all other families as well.
translation_text:
Jerusalɛm ka beeŋ nya kumo be kumu kachako so be asheŋ
1Kubɔya nɛ k shi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ a laŋɛ Israɛl be kaplɛa so na nde. Mo e to esoso nseŋ tɔl durnya n yili kumo be gbaltɔlase so, nseŋ sa dimɛdi ŋkpa na. 2E yɛ: “N yili kumo nna fanɛ Jerusalɛm e ki fanɛ yabra kurwa nɛ efuliana nɛ a mata kumo na e nuu m boo. Kananɛ baaŋ kre kena m ba kulti Jerusalɛm n wɔtɔ na, aloŋ nɛ baaŋ wora Juda be efuli na kikɛ so. 3Ama loŋ be jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, meeŋ shin nɛ Jerusalɛm e ki fanɛ kejembu gbɛgbɛso, nɛ efuli kama so ebi maaŋ tiŋ n fifir kumo. Bekama nɛ b wora ania nɛ b fifir kumo beeŋ doro bumo be amu. 4Loŋ be kachɛ na meeŋ shin nɛ kufugboŋ ko e tɔr gbaŋɛ kikɛ so nɛ eboŋ e tɔr amo be bediipoana so. Ma e naaŋ baa keni Juda be basa so. Meeŋ shin nɛ bumo doŋana be egbaŋɛ e tan. 5Kumo be kaman nɛ Juda be efuli so be mbunaana na be basa e kaŋɛ bumo be amu le: ‘Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa sa mbe basa nɛ b wɔ Jerusalɛm to na eleŋ.’
6Jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, meeŋ shin nɛ Juda be efuli so be benimuana na e ki fanɛ edɛ ashi kupo to ŋko aboyu nɛ a wɔl a yil to. Baaŋ mur efuliana nɛ e kulti bumo na kikɛ. Ama shɛŋ maaŋ wora basa nɛ b wɔ Jerusalɛm be kadegboŋ na to na bre.
7Ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naŋ shin nɛ Juda be benapo e juŋkpar ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so, saŋɛ na so kemaŋkura nɛ ewura Deevid be kaman to ebi nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ Jerusalɛm to beeŋ nya na maaŋ baa chɔ Juda be efuli so be basa nɛ b ka na peya. 8Loŋ be jemanɛ na, ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naaŋ baa kuŋ bekama nɛ b wɔ Jerusalɛm to, nseŋ shin nɛ bumo to be bepɔshipo gba e baa kɔ eleŋ fanɛ ewura Deevid. Ewura Deevid be kamanebi beeŋ baa juŋkpar bumo fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be malaika gbagba na. 9Ma alɛ beeŋ mur efuli kama nɛ k beeŋ wora ania fanɛ k beeŋ kɔ Jerusalɛm kena.
10Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ kuwɔrwu nɛ kabɔrɛkule be kiyoyu e gbelge m ba ewura Deevid be kamanebi nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ Jerusalɛm to na kikɛ so. Baaŋ to kenishi n wu esa nɛ b da mo kekpa m mɔ na nseŋ shu mbe keeli fanɛ kananɛ baa shu ebi koŋwule be keeli na, nseŋ wora kuwɔr be asheŋ fanɛ esa nɛ e paŋ mbe wurkoŋnyɛn na. 11Kushu nɛ k beeŋ baa wɔ Jerusalɛm to loŋ be kamɔnchɛ na beeŋ baa shi pasaa. K beeŋ baa du fanɛ b ka daa shu Hadad Rimɔn be keeli ashi Megido be keplasawule so na nna. 12-14Kasawule na so be esa kikɛ ashi kanaŋ kama to beeŋ shu keeli. Benyɛn na bee barga bumo be amu ashi beche na to nna a shu. Ewura Deevid nɛ Neetan nɛ Livai nɛ Shimei be nnaŋ to ebi nɛ nnaŋ mo nɛ e ka na kikɛ to ebi gba be benyɛn nɛ beche beeŋ barga to a shu ntuŋ so.”

english_text:
Getting Rid of Idols and False Prophets
1In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
2The Lord All-Powerful says:
When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them. 3If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
4Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet. 5Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
6And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.”
A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
7 The Lord All-Powerful said:
My sword, wake up! Attack
my shepherd and friend.
Strike down the shepherd!
Scatter the little sheep,
and I will destroy them.
8Nowhere in the land
will more than a third of them
be left alive.
9Then I will purify them
and put them to the test,
just as gold and silver
are purified and tested.
They will pray in my name,
and I will answer them.
I will say, “You are my people,”
and they will reply,
“You, Lord, are our God!”
translation_text:
Kelar agbir nɛ anebi fɛpoana be asheŋ to be asheŋ
1Nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Jemanɛ ko bee ba nɛ kebuye ko e ba kaa bul nchu n fɔr ewura Deevid be kaman to ebi nɛ Jerusalɛm to be basa be alubi nɛ eyurpisheŋ kikɛ n lɛ. 2Jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, meeŋ mur agbirana be atre kasawule na so nɛ esa maaŋ naa nyiŋi amo be asheŋ gba kuraa. Ma alɛ beeŋ lara anebi fɛpoana na nɛ eyurpisheŋ be kiyoyu gba kasawule na so. 3Esa kama kaŋ naa kaŋɛ fanɛ mo ere bee wu abɔrɛsheŋ to nna a kaŋɛ, mo tuto nɛ mo nio gbagba e naŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e daga luwu, ŋkpal e ka ku efɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kamalga nɛ e bee malga so. Nɛ e kraŋ kini a malga mo nio nɛ mo tuto gbagba e naaŋ da mo tokobi m mɔ. 4Loŋ be jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, anebi kikɛ maaŋ naa puchi mbe ebɔrɛdare so ŋko a wora anebi be aworbi ŋko a buu anebi be epiŋi a fule basa. 5Ama kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ kaŋɛ e la fanɛ, ‘Ma ere maŋ la anebi. Ma kebia to kikɛ edɔpo e la ma hale m ba fo kabre.’ 6Kumo be kaman nɛ esa naŋ bishi mo le: Nɛ manɛ e kpɛa fo eyur so le ere? E beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ, ‘N teri ko be laŋ to nɛ n nya amo.’ ”
B ka mɔ mbolpɔkpapo nɛ mbolpɔ pesaŋ to be asheŋ
7Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ: “Tokobi, koso ŋ kɔ mbolpɔkpapo nɛ e bee shuŋ a sa ma na m mɔ mo nɛ mbolpɔ na e yeŋ to m pesaŋ to. Saŋɛ na so meeŋ nya ŋ kɔ ma basa. 8Kasawule na so be basa na be ntuŋ asa to be ntuŋ anyɔ beeŋ wu m mur nɛ katuŋ koŋwule nawule e ka. 9Katuŋ koŋwule nɛ b ka na gba, meeŋ wora bumo ŋ keni nseŋ lɔŋɛ bumo so fanɛ kananɛ baa ta shuwa ŋko gbiti a wɔtɔ edɛ to a lɔŋɛ amo so na. Kumo be kaman pɔɛŋ nɛ baaŋ kule ma nɛ n nu n sa bumo nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b la ma basa nna, nɛ bumo alɛ e bugi to ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, e la bumo be Ebɔrɛ.”

english_text:
War and Victory
1The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people. 2But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
3The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle. 4He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west. 5Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
6It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold. 7And the Lord has decided when it will happen—this time of unending day.
8 In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. 9Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
10-11 From Geba down to Rimmon south of Jerusalem, the entire country will be turned into flatlands, with Jerusalem still towering above. Then the city will be full of people, from Benjamin Gate, Old Gate Place, and Hananel Tower in the northeast part of the city over to Corner Gate in the northwest and down to King's Wine Press in the south. Jerusalem will always be secure and will never again be destroyed.
12Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out. 13The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other, 14-15until even the people of Judah turn against those in Jerusalem. This same terrible disaster will also strike every animal nearby, including horses, mules, camels, and donkeys. Finally, everything of value in the surrounding nations will be collected and brought to Jerusalem—gold, silver, and piles of clothing.
16 Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters. 17No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful. 18-19This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
20-21At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
translation_text:
Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka beeŋ ji kuwura be asheŋ
1Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be demujiachɛ na bee ba. Kamɔnchɛ na nɛ baaŋ muu Jerusalɛm to be asɔ m barga to n sa abar ashi menyi gbagba be anishito. 2Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naŋ gama efuli pɔtɛana na abar so nɛ b ba kɔ Jerusalɛm kena. Baaŋ pɔ kadegboŋ na so nseŋ luri elaŋ to m muu asɔ nseŋ pur beche. Baaŋ pɛ basa na be bargato ŋ ki anya n yɔ efuli pɔtɛana so, ama b maaŋ lara bumo nɛ baaŋ ka na bre kadegboŋ na to. 3Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e lar n ya kɔ efuli pɔtɛana na, fanɛ kananɛ e daŋ wora jemanɛ nɛ k choŋ na. 4Loŋ be jemanɛ na e beeŋ yili ɔlif be kebee nɛ k wɔ Jerusalɛm be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na so nɛ k baŋɛ to anyɔ n tɔr ketaŋɛgboŋ nɛ k yili epeŋilarkpa m ba choŋ epeŋitɔrkpa na. Kumo be kaba koŋwule beeŋ tɔr a laŋɛ kelargato be esoso be kaba so nɛ kaba ko malɛ e tɔr a laŋɛ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so. 5Kumo be kaman nɛ men bɔla ketaŋɛ nɛ kebee na baŋɛ to anyɔ n dese n ya fo kakpa nɛ baa tre Azɛl na n shile. Kananɛ men nanaana daŋ shile saŋɛ nɛ kasawule daŋ gbuŋgbuŋ Juda be ewura Uziya be jemanɛ so na gbagba chap nɛ menyi alɛ gba beeŋ shile m mɔlga menyi be amu. Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ mbe emalaika kikɛ e ba.
6Loŋ be kachɛ na kaŋ fo, kefulto ŋko awo ŋko kenyɔlɔ maaŋ baa wɔtɔ. 7K beeŋ baa la kachɛ nɛ k kɔr nchɛ kikɛ to nna. Karechɛ ŋko kanyɛ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ. Kanyɛ biri gba kakpa kraa beeŋ fulto parr. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nawule e nyi saŋɛ nɛ loŋ beeŋ wora.
8Kachɛ na kaŋ fo, nchu nɛ a bee sa ŋkpa beeŋ shi Jerusalɛm to a shile. Nchu na be bargato beeŋ baa shile a luri teku nɛ baa tre Teku Wuso na to nɛ bargato malɛ e baa shile a luri kumo nɛ baa tre Mɛditerenia be Teku na to. Ketarso nɛ kechali so kikɛ nɛ nchu na beeŋ baa shile. 9Loŋ be jemanɛ na, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naaŋ baa ji durnya kikɛ so kuwura. Mo nawule be ketre nɛ ekama beeŋ baa nyi nsaa bunyaŋ mo nawule fanɛ Ebɔrɛ.
10Kasawule nɛ k yili Gɛba n dese n ya fo Rimmɔn a laŋɛ Jerusalɛm be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na beeŋ ki fanɛ keshishɛrsawule nɛ baa tre Araba na. Ama Jerusalɛm bre beeŋ baa kraa yil kumo be kakpa nseŋ yili kabuna nɛ baa tre Bɛnjamin be Kabunagboŋ na n salga to n ya fo kumo nɛ baa tre Kukɔlɔ to be Kabunagboŋ, be kakpa nɛ kabuna ko daa wɔ na. K kraa beeŋ yili kakpa nɛ baa tre Hananɛl be Ebu jeŋgreŋ na n salga to n ya fo kakpa nɛ baa wora bewura be eyabra na. 11Basa na beeŋ chena Jerusalɛm to ashi kayurwushi so nɛ k maaŋ naaŋ mur kikɛ.
12Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ kulɔ lubi e tɔr efuli pɔtɛana be basa nɛ baa kɔ Jerusalɛm kena na so. Bumo be eyurana nɛ anishi nɛ adonduloŋ kikɛ beeŋ bɛ a bɛlge nɛ b kraa keni.
13Loŋ be jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ bumo be nfɛra e mel to nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo saŋɛ na so baŋ kilgi n tu abar a kɔ. 14Jemanɛ na so Juda be efuli so be basa beeŋ koso ŋ kɔ ŋ kuŋ Jerusalɛm. Baaŋ kɔ n suge efuli pɔtɛana na be basa be eshuwa nɛ egbiti nɛ asɔbuuso damta. 15Kulɔ lubi koŋwule na beeŋ tɔr Jerusalɛmebi bumo doŋana be egbaŋɛ nɛ ekurmafɔlbi nɛ enyɔma nɛ asɔbɔya be yiri yiri kikɛ nɛ b kɔ ashi bumo be keeyi to so.
16Kumo be kaman nɛ basa nɛ baaŋ ji efute ashi efuli pɔtɛana nɛ b daŋ kɔ Jerusalɛm kena na e baa yɔ Jerusalɛm to kafɛ kikɛ n ya kaa bunyaŋ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na fanɛ bumo be ewura nsaa ji Abuu to be Kachɛgboŋ na. 17Bɔrɛ maaŋ naŋ ba efuli kama so ebi nɛ b kini keyɔ Jerusalɛm to n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na fanɛ bumo be ewura, be kasawule so kikɛ. 18Nɛ fanɛ Ijiptebi gba kini keji Abuu to be Kachɛgboŋ na, kulɔ lubi nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ b k tɔr efuli pɔtɛana nɛ kini mo na so na beeŋ pɛ bumo alɛ gba. 19Kasogberge nɛ k beeŋ ba Ijipt be efuli nɛ efuli pɔtɛana nɛ a kini keji Abuu to be Kachɛgboŋ na so nna na.
20Jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, baaŋ sibɛ ‘Baa du cheembi n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na’ n deŋi egbaŋɛ be adulombi so, nɛ bɔrɛlambu na to be mpuliya daŋɛso na e baa du cheembi fanɛ echeenshi cheembi nɛ a yil bɔrɛsure na ase na. 21Baaŋ ta mpuliya daŋɛso kikɛ ashi Jerusalɛm to nɛ Juda be efuli so kikɛ m bɔɔ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na enɔ nɛ e wora amo cheembi. Basa nɛ baa lara esarga na beeŋ ta amo a daŋɛ esarga be eblaŋ. Jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, eyawujipo maaŋ naa wɔ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛlambu na to.

english_text:
1I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel.
The Lord's Love for Israel
2 Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob 3instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam. 4Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.”
But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
5Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.”
Judgment against Priests
6I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
7You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
8 But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you. 9I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
10I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings. 11From dawn until dusk my name is praised by every nation on this earth, as they burn incense and offer the proper sacrifices to me. 12But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
13You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these? 14Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
translation_text:
1Kubɔya nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta n sa kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Malakai fanɛ e sa Israɛl be basa nde.
Kasha nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kɔ n sa Israɛl be asheŋ
2E yɛ: “Israɛlebi, saŋkama, ma kasha wɔ menyi so nna ga.”
Ama le nɛ bumo alɛ daŋ kaŋɛ: “Ekpa mo so nɛ fo ŋini anyi kasha?”
Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Isɔɔ nɛ Jeekɔb la esa nɛ mo sipo nna, ama Jeekɔb nɛ mbe kaman to ebi nɛ n lara a sha ga, 3nsaa maa sha Isɔɔ nɛ mbe kaman to ebi malɛ be asheŋ nseŋ mur bumo be abee so be efuli na nɛ k ki ejiŋkaamu pe.”
4Hale nɛ Isɔɔ be kaman to ebi nɛ b la Edɔm be efuli so ebi na kaŋɛ le gba: “Anyi be nde kikɛ mur, ama anyi alɛ beeŋ naŋ lɔŋɛ m pɔr amo.” Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malɛ beeŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Nɛ men lɔŋɛ m pɔr amo gba meeŋ naŋ bure amo nɛ basa e baa tre ndoŋ ‘Belubiworapoana be efuli nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be agbo wɔ kumo so mbaanaayɔ.’ ”
5Israɛl be basa beeŋ wu kumo nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be eleŋ bee ji a baŋ Israɛl be efuli gba so nna!”
Enyɛnpe na ka maŋ sa bɔrɛmatapoana kashuli be asheŋ
6Le nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na: “Kebia bee bunyaŋ mo tuto nna nɛ kayɛrbi malɛ bee sa mo nyɛnpe bunyaŋ. N la men tuto nna, nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ menyi maa bunyaŋ ma? N la men nyɛnpe nna, nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ menyi maa sa ma bunyaŋ? Men keni ma jiga, ama menyi alɛ kraa bishi fanɛ nuso nɛ an keni fo jiga? 7Ŋkpal men ka ta ajibi nɛ a maŋ daga keta n lara sarga n deŋi ma bɔrɛsure so so.
Kede be kaman nɛ men bishi: ‘Ekpa mo so nɛ an maŋ sa fo bunyaŋ?’ Men ka maŋ keni ma bɔrɛsure m bɔlɔ kenishi so. 8Men ka bee ta asɔbɔya nɛ b tan ŋko asɔbɔya nɛ baa lɔ ŋko bumo nɛ bumo be ayaana wu a lara sarga a sa ma na, men fɛ fanɛ loŋ walɛ a? Men ta loŋ be asɔbɔya n ya sa men be gomena e beeŋ kini amo, mo alɛ maaŋ chɛ menyi to.”
9Nɛ menyi bɔrɛmatapoana kule Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e wu anyi kuwɔr e beeŋ nu menyi be kekule a? Nɛ k baŋ ba loŋ, kumo ere menyi e bar kumo. 10Enyɛnpetale yɛ: “Men be eko daŋ ti ma bɔrɛlambu na be akuloŋ k daa beeŋ par ma. Saŋɛ na so men maaŋ baa jija saŋɛ a lara esarga chɔɔso fuloŋ a deŋi ma bɔrɛsure so, ŋkpal manɛ so ma kagbene maŋ fuli menyi so. Hale men ta men be esarga m ba sa ma gba, meeŋ kini amo. 11Durnya ere to be basa damta beeŋ bunyaŋ ma. Baaŋ baa chɔɔ duwu a sa ma nsaa lara esarga nɛ a bee bɔlɔ kenishi a sa ma. Bumo kikɛ bee bunyaŋ ma ketre gboŋ na nna. 12Ama menyi ere jija ma ketre nna ŋkpal men ka maa tre ma bɔrɛsure na shɛŋ nsaa ta ajibi nɛ men maa sha gba a lara sarga a deŋi kumo so so. 13Kumo be kaman le nɛ men kraa kaŋɛ: ‘Ebɔl lar anyi ere nna.’ Men wɔtɔ gba nna a kpa mmuna to a wɔtɔ ma. Kayu be asɔbɔya nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ b la ebobi nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ baa lɔ nɛ men ta a lara sarga a sa ma. Men fɛ fanɛ meeŋ shuli n sɔ amo nna a? 14Kɔnɔsho e baa wɔ ekama nɛ e bee puni nsaa ta asɔbɔya nɛ a maŋ daga m ba kaa lara sarga a sa ma, saŋɛ so nɛ e nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e beeŋ ta kusɔbɔya lela nɛ k wɔ mbe asɔbɔya to m ba lara sarga n sa ma na so. Ŋkpal manɛ so ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ewurgboŋ, nɛ efuli kama so ebi bee ŋana ma.”

english_text:
True and False Priests
1I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests. 2You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests. 3I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
4 I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi. 5 I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name. 6He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
7You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 8But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi. 9So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike.
A Broken Agreement
10Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors? 11You people in Judah and Jerusalem have been unfaithful to the Lord. You have disgraced the temple that he loves, and you have committed the disgusting sin of marrying the worshipers of other gods. 12I pray that the Lord will no longer let those who are guilty belong to his people, even if they eagerly decide to offer the Lord a gift.
13And what else are you doing? You cry noisily and flood the Lord's altar with your tears, because he isn't pleased with your offerings and refuses to accept them. 14And why isn't God pleased? It's because he knows that each of you men has been unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young. You promised that she would be your partner, but now you have broken that promise. 15Didn't God create you and your wife to become like one person? And why did he do this? It was so you would have children, and then lead them to become God's people. Don't ever be unfaithful to your wife. 16The Lord God All-Powerful of Israel hates anyone who is cruel enough to divorce his wife. So take care never to be unfaithful!
17You have worn out the Lord with your words. And yet, you ask, “How did we do that?”
You did it by saying, “The Lord is pleased with evil and doesn't care about justice.”
translation_text:
1Le nɛ Enyɛnpetale daŋ kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na: “Ŋ kɔ le be kenishipere be kamalga ere nna a sa menyi bɔrɛmatapoana ere: 2Men shin nɛ menyi be asheŋ woraso e baa sa ma bunyaŋ. Men baa maa nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ menyi, meeŋ shin nɛ kɔnɔsho a pɛ menyi. Asɔ kama nɛ a la nɛfa n sa menyi na gba, meeŋ sho amo kɔnɔ. Kashenteŋto, n tiŋ n sho amo kɔnɔ gba, ŋkpal men ka maŋ ta ma mmalga kenishipereso so.” 3Meeŋ gberge men be mbia kusoe nseŋ ta asɔbɔya nɛ menyee ta a lara esarga na be ebin ŋ gbiti menyi be anishito. Kumo be kaman nɛ ma nɛ menyi maa naa kɔ shɛŋ. 4Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ kenishipere be mmalga nɛ ŋ kɔ a sa menyi na, saŋɛ na so ma nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b la Livai be kaman to ebi na be kɔnɔ naseso be ŋkre na maaŋ jija.
5N daŋ nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ meeŋ sa bumo ŋkpa nɛ kebaawɔtɔ lela. Ma alɛ daŋ wora loŋ nna, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ta bunyaŋ n sa ma. Kumo be saŋɛ na malɛ b daa sa ma bunyaŋ nna nsaa ŋana ma. 6Kashenteŋ nɛ kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso be asheŋ nɛ b daa fɛ, manɛ asheŋ lubi. Ma nɛ bumo daa wɔ abar so kagbene wushiso nna. Mannɛ asheŋ nɛ e niŋi nawule nɛ b daa wora, ama b daŋ chɛ basa damta gba to nɛ b yige alubi be kebaawora. 7Menyi bɔrɛmatapoana e daga men ka bee malga Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ nɛ basa e baa ba men kutɔ nɛ men ŋini bumo Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ nɛ b pin mo nɛnɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so menyi so nɛ Enyɛnpetale bee bɔla a malga a sa basa.
8Ama menyi bɔrɛmatapoana na kini kashenteŋ be ekpa na naniere. Men be keŋini gba shin nɛ basa damta bee wora alubi nna.
