11Ebɔrɛ daa bɔla Pɔɔl so nna a wora emamachisheŋ popɔr damta ga. 12B daa ta Pɔɔl be antikiana nɛ mbe kushuŋ to be asɔbuuso gba nna n ya kaa sa belɔpo nɛ a bee shin nɛ basa na be alɔ nɛ ayoyu lubiana malɛ gba bee lar bumo to. 13Juwebi ko gba daa na a kilgi to a ju ayoyu lubi nseŋ wora ania nɛ b ta Enyɛnpe Yesu be ketre gba n wora loŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ayoyu lubi na: “Yesu nɛ Pɔɔl bee bɔ mbe kubɔya na be ketre to nɛ mee kaŋɛ menyi na, men lar esa ere to.” 14Bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ baa tre Skiva na be mbinyɛnbi ashunu e daa wora loŋ na. 15Nɛ kiyoyu lubi na kaŋɛ bumo: “N nyi Yesu nsaa nyi Pɔɔl be asheŋ nɛ basa mo malɛ e la menyi alɛ?” 16Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn nɛ kiyoyu lubi na wɔ mo to na nyaŋɛ to m buu bumo n doro bumo nseŋ kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to n lɛ nɛ b lar mbe kowu na to n delge so n shile n choŋ. 17Juwebi nɛ nnyamase nɛ b daa wɔ Ɛfeses na kikɛ ka nu kumo nɛ kufu pɛ bumo kikɛ ga nɛ b sa Enyɛnpe Yesu be ketre kemaŋkura ga. 18Nɛ beyirdapoana na be bedamta ba basa to m ba kaa bugi bumo gbagba be afito a kaŋɛ alubi nɛ b wora. 19Bumo be bedamta nɛ b daŋ ta ŋkilgi be nwɔl ŋ koya ŋkilgi na daŋ bar amo kikɛ abar so m ba chɔɔ amo basa kikɛ be anishito. B ka daŋ ber nwɔl na be amansherbi a daa wɔ pɔŋ ŋgboŋ adesa. 20Ŋkpal le be asheŋgboŋ ere so Enyɛnpe be kubɔya na daŋ sɔ kakpa kikɛ nna nɛ basa damta bee yirda a ti so.
Kolu ka ku Ɛfeses be asheŋ
21Asheŋ nɛ a wora na be kaman nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na shin nɛ Pɔɔl yili kumo mbe kagbene to fanɛ e beeŋ bɔla Masɛdonia nɛ Griis to n ta n yɔ Jerusalɛm. Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “A daga fanɛ, ŋ kaŋ yɔ ndoŋ, n fo Rom gba.” 22Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shuŋi mbe bechɛtopo anyɔ ko Masɛdonia nseŋ kraa wɔ Eeshia be kasawule so. Mbe bechɛtopo na e daa la Timoti nɛ Irastes.
23Jemanɛ na so nɛ kenishipere be kayurnyaŋ koso Ɛfeses ŋkpal Enyɛnpe be ekpa na so. 24Gbitibɔyɛponyɛn ko e daa wɔ Ɛfeses nɛ baa tre mo Demitrias. E daa ta egbiti nna a lɔŋɛ asɔ nɛ a du fanɛ kegbirche Aatemis be ebu. Mbe beshumpo daa nya tɔnɔ ga ashi kushuŋ na to. 25Ndoŋ nna nɛ e tre mbe beshumpoana na nɛ bekama nɛ bumo alɛ gba daa shuŋ loŋ be kushuŋ na m ba shɛr ŋ kaŋɛ: “Men nyi fanɛ kushuŋ ere e naa nyalɛ anyi. 26Menyi alɛ gba bee wu nseŋ naa nu kusɔ nɛ kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Pɔɔl na wɔtɔ a wora. E wɔtɔ nna a kaŋɛ basa fanɛ agbirana nɛ baa lɔŋɛ na maŋ la ebɔrɛana kikɛ. Mo alɛ tiŋ n shin nɛ basa damta ashi Ɛfeses nfe nɛ Eeshia be kasawule ere so be basa damta shuli fanɛ mbe kamalga na la kashenteŋ nna. 27Nɛ an maŋ de so, basa beeŋ jija anyi be kushuŋ ere be ketre. Kumo alɛ be kaman, nɛ an maŋ de so, basa beeŋ ba kaa fɛl kegbirche Aatemis be ebu na nɛ mbe ketre maaŋ naŋ dii kikɛ. Men keni, kegbirche nɛ basa kikɛ bee bunyaŋ ashi Eeshia be efuli ere so na nɛ baa sha kewora loŋ na.”
28Jimaŋ na ka nu asheŋ nɛ Demitrias malga na nɛ agbo pɛ bumo nɛ b fara a ponte a kaŋɛ: “Ɛfesesebi be kegbirche Aatemis e la elempo.” 29Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebagato na sɔ kade na to kikɛ nɛ jimaŋ yenso na nyaŋ Gayes nɛ Aristaakes, Masɛdonia be basa anyɔ ko nɛ bumo nɛ Pɔɔl daa na na ŋ gberge bumo n yɔ kade na be nshɛrkpa. 30Pɔɔl gbagba daa sha keyɔ jimaŋ na be anishito nna ashi nshɛr na to nɛ beyirdapoana na ju mo. 31Nɛ efuli na so be benimuana nɛ b daa la Pɔɔl mo teriana na gba shuŋi ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ ba nshɛrkpa na to. 32Jemanɛ ere so kikɛ nɛ nshɛr na kikɛ bee baga to, nɛ ekama bee gbar a juge to, ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo be bedamta gba daa maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ b shɛr ndoŋ nɛ b wora. 33Basa na be beko daa tama fanɛ Alɛkzaanda be asheŋ nna, ŋkpal Juwebi na ka daŋ shin nɛ e ya yili anishito na so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Alɛkzaanda wora jimaŋ na enɔ a sha kemalga m mɔlga mbe kumu ashi jimaŋ na kutɔ. 34B ka pin fanɛ e la Juw nna nɛ bumo kikɛ ponte awa anyɔ a kaŋɛ kusɔ koŋwule nɛ b daŋ fara ŋ kaŋɛ na: “Ɛfesesebi be kegbirche Aatemis e la elempo.” 35Jimaŋ na wora awɔr na loŋ nɛ kade na to be krachigboŋ na ya tiŋ n lɔlɔ bumo nɛ b lo to nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Ɛfesesebi, ekama nyi fanɛ Ɛfeses e naa keni kegbirche Aatemis be ebu na nɛ kejembu cheembi nɛ k shi ebɔrɛso n tɔr na so. 36Esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n chɛ kumo be loŋ, amoso, men wushi eyur boeŋ n sa maŋ kuse n wora asheŋ brembreŋ. 37Basa nɛ men bar nfe ere maŋ yuri kegbirlambu na to be kusɔ kama, bumo alɛ maŋ malga kulubi ŋ gbiti anyi be kegbirche na. 38Nɛ Demitrias nɛ mbe beshumpo nɛ esa ko kɔ abar gba nna, baaŋ tiŋ n yɛr amodoŋwura benimuana na kutɔ nchɛ nɛ baa kaa lar a chena demujikpa na to na nɛ bumo nɛ amodoŋwura ya kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ b wora abar. 39Ama nɛ fanɛ men kraa sha kusɔ ko n ti so, kakpa nɛ baaŋ ji loŋ be demu e la ndetobia be nshɛr nɛ mbra na bee ŋini na to. 40Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ anyi maŋ de so, Romebi na beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ k wora ere la kelantokɔ nna. Le be kebagato ere maŋ kɔ kifi. Anyi alɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ k bar le be kebagato ere.” 41Krachi na ka malga n loge nɛ e shin nɛ basa na pesaŋ to n yɔ epe.

english_text:
Paul Goes through Macedonia and Greece
1When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia. 2As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece 3and stayed there for three months.
Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia. 4With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus. 5They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there. 6After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week.
Paul's Last Visit to Troas
7On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning. 8In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps. 9A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
10Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.” 11After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left. 12Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy.
The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
13Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there. 14When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene. 15The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus. 16Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost.
Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
17From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him. 18When they got there, he said:
You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia. 19Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble. 20When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you. 21I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
22I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there. 23In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem. 24 But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
25I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again. 26I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you! 27I have told you everything God wants you to know. 28Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
29I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you. 30Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers. 31Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
32I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people. 33I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes. 34You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends. 35By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
36After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed. 37Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him. 38They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.”
Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_text:
Pɔɔl ka naŋ bɛta n yɔ Masɛdonia nɛ Griis be asheŋ
1Basa na be kebagato na ka baŋ loge nɛ Pɔɔl tre beyirdapoana na n ta mmalga damta n leŋ bumo to ga nseŋ kela bumo nseŋ ta n yɔ Masɛdonia n ya yɔ ndoŋ be ndeana na to 2n ya kaa ta mmalga damta a leŋ beyirdapoana na to. 3Ade be kaman nɛ e yili ndoŋ n yɔ Griis n ya ji afɔl asa ndoŋ. E daŋ naa bela ase nna nɛ e luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n yɔ Siriya nseŋ nu Juwebi na ka bee sha kemɔ mo nɛ e naŋ bɛta m bɔla Masɛdonia. 4Mo nɛ Pires nɛ e shi Beriya na pibi Sopata nɛ Aristaakes nɛ Sɛkundes nɛ b shi Tɛsalɔnika na nɛ Gayes nɛ e shi Dɛbi na nɛ Timoti nɛ Eeshia be efuli so ebi Tikikes nɛ Trɔfimes na e daŋ yɔ. 5Bumo e daŋ juŋkpar n ya kaa jo anyi ashi Trowas. 6Bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi be Kejigboŋ na be jemanɛ ka choŋ nɛ an yili Filipai n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n ji nchɛ anu nseŋ ya tu bumo Trowas nɛ an kikɛ ji bɔkwe ndoŋ.
Pɔɔl be lalaloge be kechɔrɔ Trowas be bebɛsopo be asheŋ
7Bɔkwe be kachɛ juŋkparso be kanyɛso ko an shɛr m bɔ enɔ n wɔtɔ kɔnɔkoŋwuleso be kawiejibi na to nɛ Pɔɔl kpal e ka beeŋ lar kade na to kumo be ŋklade na so m bɔ kubɔya na loŋ nɛ kiidiso ya fo. 8Ndia damta ko malɛ e daa wɔ esoso be ebu nɛ an daŋ shɛr na to. 9Kabrantiɛbia ko daa tase tokuro so nɛ baa tre mo Yutikes. Ŋkpal Pɔɔl ka malga n chɛr na so nɛ edi laa mo nɛ e fara a di hale n ya di n choŋ so n shi esoso be ebu sasopo na to m ba tɔr kasawule nɛ b ba nɛ b ba ta mo nɛ e wu. 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl gbelge n ya teŋi mbe kumu to n dese mo so nseŋ ta mbe enɔana m mea mo nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Men sa maa fɔŋ so, e kɔ ŋkpa.” 11Kumo be kaman nɛ Pɔɔl naŋ bɛta n dii n yɔ esoso be ebu na to n ya buri bodobodo to n we. Pɔɔl ka malga bumo kutɔ loŋ hale nɛ epeŋi ya pete nɛ e yige bumo nseŋ yɔ. 12Ndoŋ nna nɛ b keta kabrantiɛbia na ŋkpa to n yɔ epe. Bumo be ŋgbene daŋ fuli bumo ga ŋkpal loŋ so.
Pɔɔl ka shi Trowas n yɔ Mailites be asheŋ
13Ndoŋ nna nɛ an juŋkpar n yɔ ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n ta n yɔ Asɔs, kakpa nɛ an daa yɔ nɛ an ya ta Pɔɔl na. E ka daŋ bɔla aya so n yɔ ndoŋ na so nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ an wora loŋ. 14E ka tu anyi Asɔs nɛ an ta mo n wɔtɔ ekuloŋ na to n ta n yɔ Mitilini 15n ya yili ndoŋ n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to n di ŋ klade m ba baŋ Kiyɔs so n choŋ. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an ta n yɔ Samɔs n naŋ klade n yɔ Mailites. 16Pɔɔl daa sha kekpar Ɛfeses so nna n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daa maŋ naa sha kenaŋ n chɛr Eeshia be efuli so. E daa kuse nna nɛ e ya fo Jerusalɛm ta a ba Pɛntekɔst be kachɛgboŋ na, nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ nna na.
Pɔɔl ka kela Ɛfeses be asɔri to be benimuana be asheŋ
17Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl yili Mailites n shuŋi kabɔ fanɛ e ya kaŋɛ ndoŋ be asɔriebi be benimuana fanɛ b shɛr mo to. 18B ka ba nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Men nyi kebaawɔtɔ nɛ n daa kɔ a wɔ menyi kutɔ na yili kachɛ nɛ n fara m ba Eeshia be efuli ere so na m ba fo kabre. 19N daa shuŋ ma kushuŋ nna fanɛ kebɔrɛnya nsaa yɔɔ ma kumu saŋkama a wɔtɔ a nya kagbenejija a shu nchɛ nchɛ to ŋkpal Juwebi be nia nɛ b daa kre ma na so. 20Men nyi fanɛ saŋɛ nɛ n daŋ bɔ kubɔya na n sa menyi nseŋ ŋini menyi asheŋ basa to nɛ menyi peana na, n daa maŋ ta kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ chɛ menyi to ŋ ŋana menyi so kikɛ. 21Juwebi nɛ nnyamase kikɛ nɛ n daŋ fiɛ so kpakpa fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to a bɛ Ebɔrɛ so nseŋ yirda an Nyɛnpe Yesu. 22Naniere malɛ, kenu n sa Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na so nɛ mee yɔ Jerusalɛm a maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ ya wora ma ndoŋ na. 23Kusɔ nɛ m baa nyi e la fanɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na bee fiɛ ma so kade kama to fanɛ kabuti nɛ etɔrɔ bee jo ma saŋko. Ama amo alɛ maŋ tir ma, ŋkpal manɛ so, m maa ta ŋ gbagba be ŋkpa ere fanɛ k la kusɔ ko ma kutɔ. 24Kusɔ nɛ k tir ma e la kananɛ meeŋ tiŋ n loge Enyɛnpe Yesu be kushuŋ nɛ e sa ma na. Kumo alɛ e la kebɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ na be baru lela na. 25N yɔ menyi be ekama ere nyam kutɔ n ya bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be asheŋ n sa menyi, ama naniere n nyi fanɛ menyi be ekama maaŋ naŋ wu ma kikɛ. 26Amoso, m baa bugi asheŋ to nna a kaŋɛ menyi kabre nna fanɛ: Nɛ menyi be ekama baŋ foe ekpa, mannɛ ma e bar kumo, 27ŋkpal manɛ so, m maŋ ta kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ yili fanɛ e beeŋ wora na ŋ ŋana menyi so. 28Men baa de men gbagba be amuana so nsaa de basa nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na ta m bɔɔ menyi enɔ na so. Men baa keni Ebɔrɛ be asɔriebi nɛ e ta ŋ ki mo peya ashi mo gbagba Pibinyɛn be luwu na so fanɛ kananɛ asɔbɔyakpapo bee keni mbe asɔbɔya so na. 29Ŋkpal manɛ so, n nyi fanɛ ŋ kaŋ yɔ, befɛpo damta beeŋ ba menyi to m ba fin kemur asɔriebi na fanɛ kananɛ kuntuŋ bee luri mbolpɔ to a mur amo na. 30Menyi to be beko malɛ gba beeŋ koso kachako ŋ ku efɛ n shin nɛ beyirdapoana na e bɛ bumo so. 31Amoso, men baa da so a nyiŋi kananɛ n daŋ shu n fiɛ menyi so kenishipereso kapa nɛ kanyɛ nfɛ asa a ŋini menyi be ekama asheŋ na. 32Naniere, Ebɔrɛ be enɔ to nɛ mbe kuwɔr be kakɛ be kubɔya na be kebaawɔtɔ to nɛ mee ta menyi a wɔtɔ to na. Kubɔya na e naaŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ menyi be kenyi e wora keshi n ti so n naŋ shin nɛ men nya nɛfa nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a jo nɛ e sa mbe basa cheembi na. 33M maŋ yɛlga esa kama be gbiti ŋko shuwa ŋko asɔbuuso. 34Menyi gbagba nyi fanɛ ma enɔana ere nɛ n daŋ ta n shuŋ n nya asɔ nɛ a daga fanɛ ma nɛ m braana na e nya. 35M bɔla kusɔ kama to ŋ ŋini menyi fanɛ kebaashuŋ le ere nɛ anyee chɛ bepɔshipo to nsaa nyiŋi Enyɛnpe Yesu gbagba be mmalga nɛ e kaŋɛ na: ‘Kakɛ kɔ kagbenefuli a chɔ kesɔ.’ ”
36Pɔɔl ka malga n loge nɛ mo nɛ bumo kikɛ gbir ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ. 37Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo kikɛ ba kaa nyaŋ mo a mata bumo be amu kashaso a kela mo nsaa shu. 38Kusɔ nɛ k daŋ baa jija bumo be ŋgbene ga e daa la kananɛ e kaŋɛ fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ wu mo kikɛ na. Ade be kaman nɛ b shuŋi mo n lar ekpa n yɔ ekuloŋgboŋ nɛ e beeŋ luri na akpa.

english_text:
Paul Goes to Jerusalem
1After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara. 2We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
3We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo. 4We found the Lord's followers and stayed with them for a week. The Holy Spirit had told them to warn Paul not to go on to Jerusalem. 5But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed. 6Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
7We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day. 8 The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles, 9and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
10 We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea. 11He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.” 12After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
13But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
14Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
15Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem. 16Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning.
Paul Visits James
17When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us. 18Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present. 19Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles. 20Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul:
My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses. 21But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
22What should we do now that our people have heard you are here? 23 Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God. 24Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
25 Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
26The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them.
Paul Is Arrested
27When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him. 28They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.” 29 Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
30The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut. 31The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot. 32So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered.
As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. 33The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done. 34Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress. 35As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him. 36The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!”
Paul Speaks to the Crowd
37When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?”
“How do you know Greek?” the commander asked. 38“Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led 4,000 terrorists into the desert?”
39“No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
40The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_text:
1An ka kela bumo n loge nɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ na to m bɔla nchu so n ta tinini loŋ n ya fo Kɔs ŋ klade n yɔ Rodes n ya shi ndoŋ n yɔ Patara. 2Ndoŋ nɛ an ya nya ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k bee shin nɛ k yɔ Fenisha nɛ an luri kumo to n yɔ. 3An ta loŋ m ba kaa wu Saipres nseŋ yige kumo anyi be bena so n lɛ nseŋ ta n yɔ Siriya n naŋ ta n ya yili Tayɛ, kakpa nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na daa sha keyaa lara kumo be esulɔ. 4Ndoŋ nɛ an ya wu beyirdapoana ko n ji bɔkwe bumo kutɔ nɛ b bɔla Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na be eleŋ to ŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl fanɛ e sa maŋ yɔ Jerusalɛm. 5Ama anyi be keyige bumo n yɔ be saŋɛ ka ba fo nɛ an lar bumo kutɔ ndoŋ. Bumo kikɛ nɛ bumo be beche nɛ mbia e daŋ shuŋi anyi n lar kadegboŋ na to nɛ an kikɛ ya gbir shishɛr so ashi teku na ase ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ. 6Kumo be kaman nɛ an kela abar ŋkeŋ shin nɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ na to nɛ bumo alɛ bɛta n yɔ epe.
7An ka naŋ fara anyi be enite na nɛ an lar Tayɛ n yɔ Petɔlemeeyis n ya ji kachɛ koŋwule ndoŋ n chɔrɔ bekurgepoana na. 8Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an lar ndoŋ n yɔ Sizariya n ya luri baru lela malgapo Filip pe. E daa la basa ashunu nɛ bebɛsopoana na daŋ lara Jerusalɛm na be eko nna. 9E daa kɔ mo gbagba be mbichebi kurgeso bena. B daa la anebicheana nna a wɔtɔ a maŋ kil. 10An daŋ wora nchɛnnyɔ nɛ anebi ko nɛ baa tre Agabes na ya shi Judiya m ba. 11E ka ba anyi kutɔ nɛ e ba ta Pɔɔl be kreso ŋ kre mo gbagba be aya nɛ enɔana nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Le nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na kaŋɛ: ‘Le nɛ Jerusalɛm to be Juwebi na beeŋ kre kreso ere wura nseŋ ta mo m bɔɔ nnyamase enɔ.’ ” 12An ka nu loŋ nɛ anyi nɛ basa na kule Pɔɔl fanɛ e sa maŋ naŋ yɔ Jerusalɛm. 13Nɛ e bishi bumo: “Manɛ so nɛ menyee wora le ere nsaa shu le a jija ma kagbene? Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Yesu so meeŋ shuli fanɛ b mɔ ma ashi Jerusalɛm to gba, a bishi kekre ma ndoŋ.” 14An daa maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ e chɛrga mbe nfɛra, amoso, an daŋ yige mo nna nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Kusɔ kama nɛ Enyɛnpe yili e wora loŋ.”
15An ka wora nchɛnnyɔ ndoŋ nɛ an bela ase n yɔ Jerusalɛm. 16Anyi nɛ Sizariya be bebɛsopo na be beko e daŋ yɔ nɛ b keta anyi n yɔ anyi be kowurnyɛn Meneesɔn pe. E daŋ shi Saipres nna a la ebɛsopo ashi mbe kebiato kikɛ.
Pɔɔl ka ya chɔrɔ Jeems be asheŋ
17An ka ba Jerusalɛm nɛ bekurgepoana na bugi kagbene n sɔ anyi kagbenefuliso 18Kumo be ŋklade nɛ anyi nɛ Pɔɔl yɔ nɛ an ya chɔrɔ Jeems. Saŋɛ na so nɛ asɔriebi be benimuana na kikɛ wɔ ndoŋ. 19Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl chɔrɔ bumo nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo asɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bɔla mo so n wora nnyamase to kikɛ nyam. 20B ka nu mbe kamalga na nɛ bumo kikɛ di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “Fo wu ai, ekurgepo, Jerusalɛm ere to be Juwebi damta gba ki beyirdapo naniere, ama bumo alɛ kraa mɔ bumo be amu nna a bɛ Mosis be mbra na so. 21Basa kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ fo wɔtɔ nna a ŋini Juwebi nɛ b wɔ nnyamase be efuliana so nna fanɛ b yige kebaabɛ Mosis be mbra na so. B yɛ fo yɛ, b sa maa ku bumo be mbia atutu, bumo alɛ e sa maa bɛ Juwebi be edaŋkare na so. 22Bumo be kenu fanɛ fo ba malɛ baŋ fuli nna, amoso, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ wora? 23Wora kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ fo ere. Benyɛn ana ko nase kɔnɔ n sa Ebɔrɛ a wɔ nfe. 24Ya ti bumo so nɛ b fɔr fo nɛ bumo be eyurpi n lɛ nseŋ shin nɛ fo ka bumo be eyurpi be kefɔr n lɛ be kukɔ n sa bumo nɛ b tiŋ n shin nɛ b she bumo be amu. Loŋ nɛ ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ asɔ nɛ b nu na kikɛ la efɛ nna, ŋkpal fo gbagba ka bee bɛ Mosis be mbra na so so. 25To, nnyamase nɛ b ki bebɛsopo na malɛ, an sibɛ kawɔl n shuŋi bumo fanɛ b sa maŋ naa ji nlɔŋɛjibi ŋko ŋklaŋ ŋko a we kusɔbɔya kama nɛ b maŋ teŋ, nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b baa gelge kubojuaji gba.” 26Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl shin nɛ mo nɛ basa na yɔ ŋ klade n ya wora bumo be kefɔr n lɛ be daŋkaresheŋ na nseŋ shin nɛ e yɔ bɔrɛlambu na to n ya kaŋɛ kachɛ nɛ baa loge eyurpi be kefɔr n lɛ be daŋkare na nseŋ lara basa na be ekama be sarga.
B ka pɛ Pɔɔl ashi bɔrɛlambu na to be asheŋ
27Nchɛnshunu na ka taga to nɛ Eeshia be kasawule so be Juwebi ko wu Pɔɔl bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ we n wɔtɔ jimaŋ na kikɛ nseŋ nyaŋ Pɔɔl 28m ponte ŋ kaŋɛ: “Israɛlebi, men ba chɛ to. Kanyɛn nɛ e na kaplɛkama a ŋini basa kikɛ asheŋ nɛ a bee da Israɛlebi nɛ Mosis be mbra na nɛ bɔrɛlambu na so e ba nfe hale m bar nnyamase bɔrɛlambu na to nɛ b ba jija kumo kananɛ k du cheembi na.” 29B ka daŋ wu Trɔfimes nɛ e shi Ɛfeses nɛ Pɔɔl kade na to so nɛ b daŋ tama fanɛ Pɔɔl daŋ keta mo nna n luri bɔrɛlambu na to. 30Ndoŋ nna nɛ kadegboŋ na to ebi kikɛ luri kebagato to nɛ basa na kikɛ shile m ba abar so m ba nyaŋ Pɔɔl ŋ gberge mo n lar bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ ti bɔrɛlambu na be mbuna epul na to. 31Jimaŋ yenso na daa sha kemɔ Pɔɔl nna nɛ esa ko ya kaŋɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na fanɛ Jerusalɛmebi nyaŋɛ to. 32Epul na to nɛ enimu na lara ekrachi ko nɛ benapo ko nɛ b bɛ mo so n nya manaŋ n yɔ jimaŋ na to. B ka baŋ wu mo nɛ benapo na nɛ b yige Pɔɔl be kebri. 33Nɛ enimu na yɔ Pɔɔl kutɔ n ya shin nɛ b pɛ mo nseŋ shin nɛ b ta ŋgbɛlɛbi anyɔ ŋ kre mo. Kumo be kaman nɛ e bishi: “Nuso be esa e la kanyɛn ere, nɛ manɛ nɛ e wora?” 34Ndoŋ nna nɛ jimaŋ na gbar n juge to. Kebagato na be keshi na so benapo be enimu na daa maŋ tiŋ m pin kusɔ nɛ k baŋ wora, amoso, e daŋ shin nɛ mbe benapo keta Pɔɔl nna n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to. 35Ebu na be kabondiikpa nawule nɛ b daŋ fo nɛ benapo na maŋ mo so ŋkpal kananɛ jimaŋ yenso na nyaŋɛ to na so. 36Bumo kikɛ daa shil nna a buu mo a ponte a kaŋɛ: “Men mɔ mo.”
Kananɛ Pɔɔl malga ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu be asheŋ
37B ka daa shin nɛ b ta Pɔɔl n luri kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to nɛ e malga benapo be enimu na kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ: “Jande, shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ ko.” Nɛ benapo be enimu na bishi mo: “Fee nu Griik to a? 38Kumo ere, mannɛ fo e la Ijipt be kanyɛn nɛ e daŋ koso jemanɛ ko so a kɔ mbe abane kena nseŋ keta benapo yenso ŋgboŋ ana n luri kiyi to nna ŋko?” 39Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “N la Juw nna ashi Silisia be Taases nɛ k maŋ la kade fɔmbi na. Jande shin nɛ m malga n sa basa ere.” 40Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na sa Pɔɔl ekpa nɛ e yili ebu na be kabondiikpa nseŋ wora basa na enɔ nɛ b la to nɛ e malga Hibruw to ŋ kaŋɛ:

english_text:
1“My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!” 2When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
3 I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
4 I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women. 5The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
6 One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me. 7I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
8“Who are you?” I answered.
The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.” 9Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
10I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?”
Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.” 11The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
12In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there. 13He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!”
At once I could see. 14Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice. 15You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard. 16What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
17After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision 18of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
19I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you. 20 Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
21But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
22The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.” 23They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air.
Paul and the Roman Army Commander
24The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
25While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
26When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
27The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”
“Yes,” Paul answered.
28The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.”
But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
29The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
Paul Is Tried by the Council
30The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.

1“M braana nɛ n tutoana, men lo to n nu ma kamalga nɛ mee sha kemalga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu ashi menyi kutɔ ere.” 2B ka nu e ka bee malga Hibruw to nɛ bumo kikɛ wora shruum a chɔ sososo b ka fara n lo to na nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: 3“N la Juw nna ashi Silisia be Taases, ama Jerusalɛm to nfe nɛ b bela ma nɛ Gameelial daa la ma eŋinipo. Kananɛ k daga fanɛ esa e bɛ an nanaana be mbra na so na nɛ b daŋ ŋini ma nɛ n ta ma kumu m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nɛ n shuŋ mbe kushuŋ fanɛ kananɛ menyi kikɛ nfe ere bee wora na. 4N daŋ tɔrɔ basa nɛ b bɛ le be ekpa ere na so hale a sha kemɔ bumo kikɛ. Beche nɛ benyɛn kikɛ nɛ n daŋ pɛ n shin nɛ b ti ebu. 5Bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ nshɛrwuraana na kikɛ e la ma shɛdajipoana. Bumo kutɔ nɛ n daa sɔ nwɔl a yɔ bekurgepo Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Damaskɔs na kutɔ nɛ b sa ma ekpa nɛ m pɛ loŋ be basa na ŋ kre bumo ŋgbɛlɛbi m ba Jerusalɛm to nfe m ba kaa shin nɛ baa gberge bumo kusoe.
Pɔɔl ka malga kananɛ e ba ki ebɛsopo be asheŋ
6Kachako ŋ ka wɔ loŋ be enite na to m ba kaa taga to Damaskɔs kapaso ko nɛ kefultogboŋ ko nyaŋɛ n shi ebɔrɛso m ba yuu ma so. 7Ndoŋ nna nɛ n tɔr kasawule nseŋ nu ebɔl ka bee bishi ma: ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, manɛ e ba nɛ fee tɔrɔ ma?’ 8Nɛ m bishi: ‘Fo wanɛ, Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ e kaŋɛ: ‘Ma Nazarɛt be Yesu nɛ fee tɔrɔ na.’ 9Ma nɛ basa nɛ b daa la na daŋ wu kefulto na, ama b daa maŋ nu esa nɛ e daŋ malga n sa ma na be ebɔl na. 10Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi: ‘Nɛ nuso nɛ meeŋ wora Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ Enyɛnpe na kaŋɛ ma: ‘Niŋi to ŋ koso n luri Damaskɔs nɛ b kaŋɛ fo kusɔ kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ fo wora.’ 11Ŋkpal kefultogboŋ na so n daŋ tan nna, amoso, m braana na e daŋ pɛ ma enɔ to n luri Damaskɔs to. 12Kanyɛn ko daa wɔtɔ a la abɔrɛshenshapo a bɛ anyi be mbra na so nɛ baa tre mo Ananiyas. Damaskɔs to be Juwebi na kikɛ daa sa mo bunyaŋ nna. 13Mo e daŋ ba yili ma kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ ma: ‘Ekurgepo Sɔɔl, naŋ bɛta a wu.’ Epul na malɛ to nɛ n naŋ nya ma anishi n wu mo. 14Nɛ e kaŋɛ: ‘An nanaana be Ebɔrɛ na e lara fo fanɛ fo pin kusɔ nɛ e bee sha kewora nseŋ shin nɛ fo wu mbe Kenya cheembi na n naŋ shin nɛ fo nu mbe ebɔl na. 15Ŋkpal manɛ so, feeŋ ki mbe shɛdajipo ŋ kaŋɛ basa kikɛ mbe kusɔ nɛ fo wu nɛ kusɔ nɛ fo nu be asheŋ. 16Amoso, sa maŋ naŋ jo, koso n shin nɛ b bɛr fo kabɔrɛbɛr a ti Yesu be ketre na nɛ Ebɔrɛ e fɔr fo alubi n lɛ.’
B ka tre Pɔɔl nnyamase to be asheŋ
17Kumo be kaman nɛ m bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm m ba kaa kule Ebɔrɛ bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ ku bɔrɛdare n wu Enyɛnpe Yesu nɛ e kaŋɛ ma: 18‘Nya manaŋ n lar Jerusalɛm, ŋkpal manɛ so, nfe be basa ere maaŋ yirda ma shɛda nɛ fee sha keji n sa bumo ere.’ 19Nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Enyɛnpe, b baa nyi geeŋ ŋ ka daŋ yɔ nshɛrbuana to n ya pɛ basa nɛ b yirda fo na nseŋ bri bumo. 20Saŋɛ nɛ baa mɔ fo shɛdajipo Stiven na nɛ ma alɛ gba yil a keni mbe bemɔpo na be asɔbuuso so nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ kashenteŋto e daga luwu.’ 21Nɛ Enyɛnpe kaŋɛ ma: ‘Lar nɛ n shuŋi fo kufɔ kufɔ nnyamase kutɔ.’ ”
22Pɔɔl ka bee malga asheŋ na kikɛ nɛ basa na bee nu. Ama e ka ba malga keyɔ nnyamase na kutɔ be asheŋ nɛ b fara a ponte ga a kaŋɛ: “Men lara mo durnya ere to. Men mɔ mo!” 23B daŋ baa ponte to nna a kpa bumo be nle a lɛ nsaa jɔ shishɛr a lɛ esoso. 24Nɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na shin nɛ mbe benapo ba keta Pɔɔl n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to nseŋ shin nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b kuya Pɔɔl so nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ Juwebi na bee boŋ to a malga a gbiti mo loŋ na. 25B ka kre mo nɛ b kuya mo so nɛ Pɔɔl bishi enapo nimusobi ko nɛ e daa yil ndoŋ na le: “Ekpa wɔtɔ fanɛ b kuya Rom be efuli so be esa so nɛ b maŋ ji mo demu ŋ keni a?” 26Enapo nimusobi na ka nu loŋ na nɛ e yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ n ya bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fo yɛ fo wora ere? Kanyɛn na la Rom be esa nna.” 27Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na yɔ Pɔɔl kutɔ n ya bishi mo: “Kaŋɛ ma, Rom be esa e la fo a?” Nɛ Pɔɔl shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm.” 28Nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ: “Amansherbi damta nɛ ŋ ka n sa abane pɔɛŋ nseŋ ki Rom be esa.” Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ma ere, b kurge ma Rom be esa nna.” 29Epul na to nɛ basa nɛ b daa sha nɛ b bishi Pɔɔl asheŋ na bɛta kaman nɛ kufu pɛ benapo be enimu na gba ŋkpal e ka pin Pɔɔl ka la Rom be esa nɛ ŋkpal e ka shin nɛ b ta ŋgbɛlɛbi ŋ kre mo so so.
30Benapo be enimu na daa sha kepin kusɔ nɛ k baŋ ba nɛ Juwebi na nɛ Pɔɔl daŋ baa kɔ abar loŋ nna. Amoso, kare ka chɛ nɛ e shin nɛ b saŋɛ Pɔɔl be ŋgbɛlɛbi na nseŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ nshɛrwuraana na kikɛ shɛr nɛ e shin nɛ Pɔɔl ba yili bumo be anishito.

english_text:
1Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
2Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth. 3 Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
4The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
5 Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
6 When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
7As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides. 8 The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these, 9and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
10The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
11That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.”
A Plot To Kill Paul
12-13The next morning more than 40 Jewish men got together and vowed that they would not eat or drink anything until they had killed Paul. 14Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul. 15You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
16When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it. 17So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
18The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
19The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
20He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him. 21But please don't do what they say. More than 40 men are going to attack Paul. They have made a vow not to eat or drink anything until they have killed him. Even now they are waiting to hear what you decide.”
22The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.”
Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
23The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have 200 soldiers ready to go to Caesarea. Take along 70 men on horseback and 200 foot soldiers with spears. 24Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
25The commander wrote a letter that said:
26Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
27Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
28I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council 29and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
30As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
31The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris. 32The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way. 33When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
34The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia. 35The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_text:
1Nɛ Pɔɔl keni nshɛrwuraana na diimbi nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, hale kabre ma kagbene to maa wora ma shikashika Ebɔrɛ be anishito fanɛ m maŋ kɔ kebaawɔtɔ cheembi.” 2Ndoŋ nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Ananiyas shin nɛ basa nɛ b daŋ yili n taga to Pɔɔl na ŋmɛa Pɔɔl be kɔnɔ. 3Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ mo: “Kebirkɔnshiwura ere! Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ŋmɛa fo kɔnɔ loŋ. Fo yɛ fo chena nfe nna nɛ fo bɔla ekpa nɛ mbra na bee ŋini na so n ji demu, ama ma nɛ fee shin nɛ baa ŋmɛa n naa wora a da mbra na so na.” 4Nɛ basa nɛ b yili n taga to Pɔɔl na kaŋɛ mo: “Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ fee tege ere a?” 5Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, n daa maŋ nyi fanɛ e la bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ: ‘Sa maŋ kaŋ malga kamalga lubi ŋ gbiti fo basa be enimu.’ ” 6Pɔɔl ka wu fanɛ basa na be beko la Esadusiana nna nɛ beko malɛ la Efarisiana nɛ e malga awɔrso n sa nshɛrwuraana na ŋ kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, Farisinyɛn e kurge ma nɛ ma alɛ naa la Farisi. Baa ji ma demu nfe ere nna, ŋkpal ŋ ka kɔ tama kpakpaso fanɛ bumo nɛ b wu na ka beeŋ tiŋi luwu to so.” 7E ka malga loŋ epul na to nɛ Efarisiana na nɛ Esadusiana na fara a bile nɛ basa na kikɛ barga to ntuŋ anyɔ so. 8Ŋkpal manɛ so, Esadusiana bee kaŋɛ fanɛ basa maaŋ tiŋi luwu to nseŋ naa kaŋɛ fanɛ emalaika ŋko ayoyu maŋ wɔtɔ, ama Efarisiana daŋ yirda amo asa na kikɛ. 9Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo be kaponte na naŋ dii ga nɛ mbraŋinipoana nɛ b la Efarisiana na be beko niŋi to n yili m ponte eleŋso ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ b maŋ shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Anyi ere maŋ wu kulubi kikɛ kanyɛn ere so. Ashere kiyoyu ko ŋko malaika e malga mo kutɔ kashenteŋto na.” 10Bumo be kolu na daŋ nyaŋɛ to ga hale basa na be kegberge Pɔɔl n tuge to be asheŋ pɛ benapo be enimu na kufu ga. Nɛ e shin nɛ mbe benapo luri basa na to ŋ keta Pɔɔl n lar bumo to n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to.
11Kumo be kamɔnchɛ be kanyɛso nɛ Enyɛnpe ba yili Pɔɔl kutɔ nseŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Baa kɔ kenyɛn. Kananɛ fo ji ma shɛda ashi Jerusalɛm to ere nɛ fee naŋ yɔ Rom malɛ n ya wora.”
Juwebi ka kre Pɔɔl be kemɔ be nia be asheŋ
12Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Juwebi na shɛr ŋ kre bumo be nia nseŋ sa Ebɔrɛ kɔnɔ fanɛ b baa maŋ mɔ Pɔɔl b maaŋ ji ajibi, bumo alɛ maaŋ nuu shɛŋ. 13Basa nɛ b daŋ yili kusɔ ere le na kikɛ daa chɔ basa adena. 14B ka sa kɔnɔ na n loge nɛ b yɔ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ benimuana na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ bumo: “An ba abar so nna m ba sa kɔnɔ kpakpaso fanɛ an baa maŋ mɔ Pɔɔl, an maaŋ ji shɛŋ. 15Amoso, menyi nɛ nshɛrwuraana na e kute n shuŋi kabɔ nɛ e ya kaŋɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na fanɛ e shin nɛ b bar Pɔɔl menyi kutɔ nɛ e ba malga nɛ men pin mbe demu na to nɛnɛ. Saŋɛ na so nɛ anyee jo mo ekpa to n nya mo m mɔ nɛ e maŋ fo nfe.”
16Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl mo sipoche pibi nu bumo be nia na nseŋ ya luri kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to n ya kaŋɛ Pɔɔl kesheŋ na. 17Nɛ Pɔɔl tre benapo be benimuwurbiana na be eko ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Keta kabrantiɛbia ere n yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ. E bee sha kekaŋɛ mo kusɔ ko nna.” 18Nɛ benapo be enimubi na juŋkpar ŋ keta mo n yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo: “Pɔɔl kabutipo na e tre ma ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ ŋ keta kabrantiɛbia ere m ba fo kutɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e kɔ kusɔ ko nna nɛ e kaŋɛ fo.” 19Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na gbagba pɛ kabrantiɛbia na be enɔ to nseŋ keta mo n lar ekarso m bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha kekaŋɛ ma?” 20Nɛ e yɛ: “Juwebi na yili kumo fanɛ baaŋ kute ŋ kule fo echefo fanɛ fo keta Pɔɔl m ba nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ nɛ e malga nɛ b pin mbe demu na to nɛnɛ. 21Ama kplaŋ bumo so, ŋkpal manɛ so, basa ko chɔ basa adena ŋ ŋana a jo mo. Amo be basa na kikɛ bɔ ntaŋ nna fanɛ b maŋ mɔ Pɔɔl, b maaŋ ji ajibi, bumo alɛ maaŋ nuu shɛŋ. B bela ase nɛ b wora loŋ nsaa jo nɛ b nu kusɔ nɛ feeŋ kaŋɛ.” 22Nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kikɛ fanɛ fo e kute le be kesheŋ ere n sa ma kikɛ.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ kabrantiɛbia na yɔ.
B ka keta Pɔɔl n yɔ Gomena Filiks kutɔ be asheŋ
23Kumo be kaman nɛ benapo be enimu na tre mbe benapowurbi benyɔ ko ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Men shin nɛ benapo alfa anyɔ nɛ egbaŋɛdiipoana be benapo adushunu nɛ akpawuraana be benapo alfa anyɔ e bela ase nɛ men yɔ Sizariya. Menyeeŋ koso nfe kerfi akpanu kanyɛ ere. 24Men fin egbaŋɛ n sa Pɔɔl nɛ e dii nɛ men keni mo so nɛnɛ n yɛr mo nɛ alenfia n ya sa Gomena Filiks.” 25Kumo be kaman nɛ benapo be enimu na sibɛ kawɔl ŋ kaŋɛ:
26“Ma, Klawdias Lisias e naa sibɛ kawɔl ere a sa fo, ebunyampogboŋ Gomena Filiks na. Mee chɔrɔ fo. 27Juwebi e daŋ nyaŋ kanyɛn ere a sha kemɔ mo nɛ n nu fanɛ e la Rom be esa nna nseŋ keta ma benapo n ya mɔlga mo bumo kutɔ. 28N daa sha kenu kusɔ nɛ e wora bumo nna, 29ŋkpal loŋ so ŋ keta mo n yɔ nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ n ya wu fanɛ e maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ nɛ k daga mbe luwu ŋko kabuti. Bumo gbagba be mbraana be emɔrɔsheŋ nɛ b kɔ a wu mo kulubi. 30Ma alɛ nu fanɛ Juwebi na bee kre mbe kemɔ be nia nna, amoso nɛ n shin nɛ b kɔ mo a ba fo kutɔ na. Ŋ kaŋɛ basa nɛ bumo nɛ mo kɔ abar na fanɛ b ba kaŋɛ fo alubi nɛ e wora.”
31Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na wora asɔ nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ bumo na kikɛ ŋ keta Pɔɔl kanyɛso na kikɛ hale n ya fo Antipatris. 32Kumo be ŋklade nɛ aya so be benapo na yili Antipatris m bɛta n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to ŋ ka egbaŋɛdiipoana nɛ bumo nɛ Pɔɔl e baa yɔ. 33B ka fo Sizariya nɛ b ta kawɔl na n sa gomena na nseŋ ta Pɔɔl m bɔɔ mo enɔ. 34Gomena na ka kraŋ kawɔl na nɛ e bishi Pɔɔl efuli na so be kaba mo nɛ e shi. E ka pin fanɛ Silisia nɛ e shi 35nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Basa nɛ baa wu fo kulubi na kaŋ ba, meeŋ keni fo demu na to.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ benapo na ta Pɔɔl n yɔ kowu nɛ Hɛrɔd daŋ pɔr na to n ya kaa keni mo so.

english_text:
Paul Is Accused in the Court of Felix
1Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul. 2So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him:
Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off. 3All of us are always grateful for what you have done. 4I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
5This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes. 6-8When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
9The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said.
Paul Defends Himself
10The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began:
I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
11It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough. 12Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself. 13There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
14I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets. 15I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil. 16And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
17 After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices. 18This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
19Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now. 20Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council. 21 The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
22Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.” 23He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him.
Paul Is Kept under Guard
24Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus. 25But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.” 26After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
27Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_text:
Juwebi na ka kaŋɛ fanɛ Pɔɔl wora kulubi be asheŋ
1Kumo be nchɛ anu be kefɛato nɛ bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Ananiyas nɛ benimu ko nɛ mbraŋinipo nɛ baa tre Tetales yɔ Sizariya n ya kaŋɛ Gomena Filiks ashi demujikpa na kulubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora. 2B ka tre Tetales, nɛ e ba fara le a kaŋɛ alubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora: “Ebunyampogboŋ, ŋkpal fo kanyiasheŋ so nɛ fo tiŋ n juŋkpar anyi n shin nɛ an nya kagbenewushi saŋɛ kikɛ m ba fo mbre nɛ asheŋ lela damta tiŋ n wora anyi be efuli ere so nɛ kumo be ketre dii na. 3Saŋkama kumo be loŋ bee par anyi ga kaplɛkama. Anyee chɔrɔ fo ga ŋkpal loŋ so. 4M maa sha fanɛ m baa kɔ kechɛchɛrase nfe a wora fo, amoso, mee kule fo nna fanɛ fo wora ania n nu anyi be kamalga shiimbi ere. 5An wu fanɛ kanyɛn ere la esa lubi nɛ kabɔlarwura nna. E wɔtɔ nna a yɔ kaplɛkama n ya kaa ta Juwebi a wɔtɔ kebagato to nseŋ naa la basa nɛ baa tre bumo be amu Nazarinebi be katuŋ na to be enimu. 6Ade be kaman nɛ e daa naa sha kejija bɔrɛlambu na to nɛ an pɛ mo. [An daa sha nɛ an bɔla anyi be mbra na so nna n ji mo demu 7nɛ benapo be enimu Lisias ba suge mo eleŋso anyi kutɔ, 8nseŋ yili demu na fanɛ basa nɛ bumo nɛ kanyɛn na kɔ abar e ba fo kutɔ.] Fo gbagba baŋ bishi kanyɛn na, feeŋ pin alubi nɛ e wora na kikɛ nyam.”
9Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juwebi na kikɛ shuli n chɛ Tetales to ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ alubi nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ Pɔɔl wora na kikɛ la kashenteŋ nna.
Pɔɔl ka malga ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu be asheŋ
10Ade be kaman nɛ gomena na wora Pɔɔl enɔ fanɛ e malga nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Fo ka fara a ji efuli ere so ebi demu k chɛr ga kabre. Amoso, k par ma ga ŋ ka bee sha kemalga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu fo anishito ere. 11Yili kachɛ nɛ n yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ n ya bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na m ba fo kabre maŋ naŋ fo nchɛ kuduanyɔ. Nɛ fee sha, fo bishi n nu. 12Juwebi na maŋ wu ŋ ka bee ji esa kikɛ emɔrɔ ashi bɔrɛlambu na to, bumo alɛ maŋ wu ŋ ka bee we a wɔtɔ basa ashi bumo be nshɛrbuana to ŋko kadegboŋ na to be kaplɛkama. 13Bumo alɛ maŋ kɔ shɛŋ nɛ b ta ŋ ŋini fo fanɛ asheŋ nɛ baa malga ere la kashenteŋ nna. 14Kashenteŋto, an nanaana be Ebɔrɛ na nɛ mee bɔla ekpa nɛ b yɛ k la efɛ na so a bunyaŋ. N yirda asɔ nɛ a wɔ Mosis be mbra na to nɛ anebiana na be nwɔl na to kikɛ nyam. 15Tama koŋwule nɛ basa ere kɔ Ebɔrɛ so na nɛ ma alɛ gba kɔ, kumo e la fanɛ basa lela nɛ belubi kikɛ nyam beeŋ ba tiŋi luwu to. 16Amoso, saŋkama mee wora ania nna nɛ m baa kɔ kagbene koŋwule nɛ k maa wora ma shikashika ashi ma nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛ nyiŋgbasa be kebaawɔtɔ to. 17Ŋ ka lar Jerusalɛm kumo be nfɛ damta nde kabre, nɛ n naŋ bɛta n ta amansherbi nɛ n ya kɛ ma basa nseŋ lara sarga. 18Le be kesheŋ ere nɛ n daa wɔ bɔrɛlambu na to a wora nɛ b wu ma. Saŋɛ na so nɛ n wora kefɔr eyurpi n lɛ be daŋkare na be asheŋ n loge. Jimaŋ kikɛ daa maŋ wɔ ma kutɔ, kebagato malɛ kikɛ daa maŋ wɔtɔ. 19Ama Eeshia be efuli so be Juwebi ko malɛ daa wɔtɔ, amoso, a daga fanɛ bumo alɛ gba ka ba nfe m ba kaŋɛ fo alubi nɛ b wu ma so nɛ fanɛ b wu alubi ma so nna na. 20Ŋko fo shin nɛ basa ere e kaŋɛ fo kulubi nɛ b wu ma so, saŋɛ nɛ n daŋ yili nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ na. 21Kusɔ koŋwule nɛ n daŋ ba n yili bumo to ndoŋ ŋ kaŋɛ e la: ‘Menyee ji ma demu kabre nna ŋkpal ŋ ka yirda fanɛ bumo nɛ b wu na kikɛ ka beeŋ tiŋi luwu to so.’ ”
22Ndoŋ nna nɛ Filiks nɛ e daŋ nu Enyɛnpe be ekpa na be asheŋ ga ŋ ku so na shin nɛ b yige demu na be kenu nseŋ shin nɛ e kaŋɛ basa na: “Benapo be enimu Lisias kaŋ ba, meeŋ keni menyi be demu na to.” 23Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ benapo be enimubi nɛ e daa de Pɔɔl so na keta Pɔɔl n ya kaa de mo so. Ama e daŋ sa mo ekpa n shin nɛ mo teriana daa tiŋ a chɛ mo to kanaŋkamaso nɛ b daa sha.
Pɔɔl ka malga n sa Filiks nɛ Drusila be asheŋ
24Kachako malɛ nɛ Filiks keta mbe eche Drusila nɛ e daa la Juw na m ba shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl nɛ e ba malga keyirda Yesu Kristo be asheŋ nɛ e nu. 25Ama Pɔɔl ka ba kaa malga alela be kebaawora nɛ kamootiŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be demujiachɛ be asheŋ nɛ kufu pɛ Filiks nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Feeŋ tiŋ a yɔ naniere. N naŋ nya kachena meeŋ naŋ tre fo.” 26Saŋkama e daa tama fanɛ Pɔɔl beeŋ sa mo amansherbi nna. Amoso, e daa sha kebaatre mo a malga mo kutɔ ga. 27B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ nfɛ anyɔ ba choŋ nɛ Pɔkias Fɛstes ba sɔ mo so a la gomena. Ŋkpal kenya ketre Juwebi na kutɔ so, Filiks daŋ yige Pɔɔl kabuti na to nna nseŋ yɔ.

english_text:
Paul Asks To Be Tried by the Roman Emperor
1Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem. 2There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus 3if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way. 4But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself. 5If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
6Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court. 7As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything. 8Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
9Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
10Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation. 11If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
12After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!”
Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
13A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus. 14They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said:
Felix left a man here in jail, 15and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty. 16I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
17So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in. 18But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would. 19Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
20Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there. 21But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
22Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.”
Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
23The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in 24and said:
King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death. 25I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
26I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write. 27It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_text:
Pɔɔl ka bee sha keyɔ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na kutɔ be asheŋ
1Fɛstes ka ba kasawule na so mbe kachɛ sasopo nɛ e yili Sizariya n yɔ Jerusalɛm. 2Nɛ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ Juwebi be benimuana na ba kaa kaŋɛ mo alubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora. 3Kumo be kaman nɛ b kule Fɛstes fanɛ e wora ania n chɛ bumo to n shin nɛ Pɔɔl e ba Jerusalɛm. B ka daŋ kre Pɔɔl be kemɔ ekpa to be nia so nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ na. 4Nɛ Fɛstes kaŋɛ: “Pɔɔl wɔ kabuti to ashi Sizariya, ma alɛ gbagba maaŋ chɛr nseŋ bɛta n yɔ Sizariya. 5Amoso, men shin nɛ menyi be benimu e tu ma n yɔ Sizariya n ya kaŋɛ alubi nɛ e wora nɛ fanɛ e wora amo nna na.” 6Kumo be kaman nɛ Fɛstes naŋ ji fanɛ nchɛ burwa ŋko nchɛ kudu basa na be kade na to pɔɛŋ nseŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ Sizariya. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ e ya chena mbe kakpa nɛ e ji demu n shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl. 7Pɔɔl ka ba nɛ Juwebi nɛ b shi Jerusalɛm m ba na yili ŋ kulti mo nseŋ malga kenishipereso be asheŋ lubi damta mo nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora, ama bumo alɛ daa maŋ tiŋ ŋ ŋini fanɛ asheŋ nɛ b daa malga na la kashenteŋ. 8Nɛ Pɔɔl malga le ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu: “M maŋ wora shɛŋ n da Juwebi be mbra na ŋko bɔrɛlambu na ŋko Romebi be ewurgboŋ na so.” 9Ŋkpal kenya ketre Juwebi na kutɔ so, Fɛstes daŋ bishi Pɔɔl nna: “Fee sha keyɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ n ya ji fo asheŋ nɛ b yɛ fo wora ere be demu ndoŋ a?” 10Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Romebi be ewurgboŋ na be demujikpa gbagba ere to nɛ m baa yil nɛ b ji ma demu na. Fo gbagba baa nyi fanɛ m maŋ wora Juwebi na shɛŋ. 11Nɛ n daŋ wora kusɔ ko nna n da mbra na so nɛ k daga ma luwu, n daa maaŋ gelge kumo be loŋ. Ama nɛ kashenteŋ maŋ wɔ asheŋ nɛ baa kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora ere to, esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n ta ma m bɔɔ bumo enɔ. Romebi be ewurgboŋ na nɛ mee kule fanɛ e keni ma demu na to.” 12Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛstes bishi mbe beyaasepo kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora Pɔɔl pɔɛŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “Fo yɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni fo demu na to, amoso, mo kutɔ nɛ feeŋ yɔ!”
Fɛstes ka kaŋɛ Ewura Agripa Pɔɔl be asheŋ
13Kede be kaman saŋko nɛ Ewura Agripa nɛ Benis ba Sizariya nɛ b ba chɔrɔ Fɛstes n wora mo ansaŋ nɛ keba. 14B wora nchɛnnyɔ ndoŋ nɛ kachako nɛ Fɛstes kaŋɛ ewura na Pɔɔl be asheŋ fanɛ: “Filiks yige kabutipo ko nfe. 15Ŋ ka yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ Juwebi be bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ benimuana na ba kaŋɛ ma asheŋ lubi nɛ b wu mo so nseŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora n da so. 16Ama ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ Romebi maa shin nɛ baa gberge esa kusoe ŋkpal kulubi kama so she mo nɛ basa nɛ b kɔ abar na ba yili nna geeŋ nɛ e malga n sɔ mbe kumu ashi kulubi nɛ b yɛ e wora na to. 17Bumo kikɛ ka kpal loŋ so m ba nfe nɛ n nya manaŋ kumo be ŋklade n ya chena demujikpa n shin nɛ b bar amo be kanyɛn. 18Ama basa nɛ bumo nɛ mo daa kɔ abar na daa maŋ tiŋ n wu mo kenishipereso be alubi nɛ n daa tama fanɛ baaŋ wu mo na be kekama. 19Bumo gbagba be kabɔrɛshuŋ nɛ ebuninyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Yesu na be emɔrɔana nawule be asheŋ nɛ b daa kɔ. Pɔɔl bee kaŋɛ nna fanɛ amo be kanyɛn na wɔ ŋkpa to. 20N daa maŋ nyi ekpa nɛ meeŋ bɔla so n naŋ nu kusɔ ko n ti so m pin bumo be demu na to nseŋ bishi Pɔɔl fanɛ e bee sha keyɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ b ya keni demu na to a. 21Nɛ Pɔɔl kini nseŋ kule fanɛ benapo e baa keni mo so nfe nseŋ shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni mbe demu na to kacha ko. Ndoŋ nna nɛ n shin nɛ benapo bee de mo so nɛ kachako nɛ e yɔ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na kutɔ.” 22Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Fɛstes: “Ma alɛ gba bee sha fanɛ e malga mbe demu na nɛ n nu.” Nɛ Fɛstes shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “To, echefo feeŋ nu kumo ashi mbe kɔnɔ to.” 23Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Agripa nɛ Benis ba luri nshɛrkpa na bunyanso nɛ basa sa bumo kemaŋkura ga. Bumo nɛ benapo be benimuana na nɛ kade na to be benimuana na e daŋ luri nshɛrkpa na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛstes shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl. 24Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Ewura Agripa nɛ menyi nɛ men wɔ nfe ere, men keni kanyɛn ere nɛ nfe be Juwebiana na nɛ Jerusalɛm to peyaana na kikɛ bee kaŋɛ ma fanɛ e wora alubi nsaa ponte a kaŋɛ fanɛ e maŋ naŋ daga kebaawɔtɔ na. 25Ama ma alɛ maaŋ tiŋ n wu kusɔ nɛ e wora n daga luwu be kasogberge. Mo alɛ naŋ kule fanɛ n shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na gbagba e keni mbe demu na to, amoso, meeŋ shin nɛ b yɛr mo ndoŋ. 26Ama m maŋ kɔ shɛŋ nɛ n sibɛ ŋ kaŋɛ n nyɛnpe na mbe asheŋ. Amoso nɛ m bar mo menyi kutɔ nfe na, fɔnfɔŋ fo, Ewura Agripa kutɔ nɛ n tiŋ n nya kusɔ ko demu na be kaman n sibɛ. 27Ŋkpal manɛ so, a maŋ daga fo ka shin nɛ kabutipo yɔ loŋ, a maŋ sibɛ shɛŋ a ŋini ekama kulubi nɛ e wora.”

english_text:
Paul's Defense before Agrippa
1Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.”
Paul stretched out his hand and said:
2King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me. 3You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
4-5 All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other. 6Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
7Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me. 8 Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
9 I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth. 10I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed. 11I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
12King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests. 13About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me. 14We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
15“Who are you?” I asked.
Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to. 16Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
17The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to. 18I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
19King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven. 20 First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
21That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me. 22But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen. 23 I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
24Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
25But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense. 26None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
27Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
28Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
29Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
30Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up. 31But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
32Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_text:
Pɔɔl ka ba malga ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu Agripa be anishito be asheŋ
1Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “N sa fo ekpa nɛ fo malga ŋ kuŋ fo kumu.” Nɛ Pɔɔl teŋi mbe enɔ to nseŋ fara a malga le a kuŋ mbe kumu:
2“Ewura Agripa, k la kumulela nna ga ŋ ka tiŋ n yili fo anishito nfe kabre nɛ m malga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu ashi asheŋ nɛ Juwebi na ku n deŋi ma kikɛ to. 3Kumo alɛ baŋ kukwe nna ŋkpal kananɛ fo nyi Juwebi be edaŋkareana na nɛ asheŋ nɛ b kɔ a ji abar emɔrɔana na kikɛ nɛnɛ na so. Amoso, mee kule fo fanɛ fo ji kanyiti n nu ma demu ere.
4Juwebi na kikɛ nyi ma kebaawɔtɔ nɛ n daa wɔ to saŋɛ nɛ n daa la kebibi na kikɛ. B nyi fanɛ sososo na ma efuli so nɛ Jerusalɛm to nɛ ŋ ki esa. 5Nɛ baa sha keji kashenteŋ, baaŋ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ dra dra na kikɛ nɛ b pin ŋ ka wɔ katuŋ nɛ k bee bɛ anyi be mbraana na so nɛnɛ a chɔ ntuŋ nɛ a ka na kikɛ na, katuŋ nɛ baa tre Efarisiana be katuŋ na. 6Ama ma e yil nfe kabre nɛ baa ji ma demu ŋkpal ŋ ka kɔ kɔnɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase n sa an nanaana na be tama so. 7Kɔnɔ naseso koŋwule nɛ anyi be basa be nnaŋ kuduanyɔ ebi na bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ kapa nɛ kanyɛ nsaa tama kenya na gbagba chap na. Yiramu, le be tama ere malɛ so nɛ Juwebi na bee ku asheŋ a deŋi ma na. 8Manɛ e ba nɛ menyi Juwebi maaŋ tiŋ n yirda fanɛ Ebɔrɛ bee tiŋi basa luwu to?
9Ma alɛ gba daŋ yili kumo nna fanɛ meeŋ wora kusɔ kama n tiŋ n jija Nazarɛt be Yesu be ketre na. 10Loŋ malɛ nɛ n daŋ wora ashi Jerusalɛm. N daa sɔ a chɛ to nna a kaŋɛ fanɛ bumo be luwu na daga bumo. 11N daa wɔtɔ nna a shin nɛ baa gberge bumo kusoe ashi nshɛrbuana na to nseŋ daa kɔ a fin kananɛ meeŋ wora nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ yirda Yesu na. Agbo daŋ pɛ ma ga ŋkpal bumo so nɛ n yɔ hale nde pɔtɛana to gba nɛ n ya tɔrɔ bumo.”
Pɔɔl ka malga kananɛ e ki ebɛsopo be asheŋ
12Le be kesheŋ nɛ n daŋ kule ekpa ashi bɔrɛmatapowuraana na kutɔ a yɔ Damaskɔs nɛ n ya wora. 13Yiramu, kapaso ko e daa la nɛ n wu kefulto ko ka fuli to a chɔ epeŋi n nyaŋɛ ashi ebɔrɛso m ba yuu ma nɛ basa nɛ an daa na na so. 14Ndoŋ nna nɛ anyi kikɛ tɔr kasawule nɛ n nu ebɔl ko ka bee bishi ma Hibruw to: ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, manɛ e ba nɛ fee tɔrɔ ma? Fo gbagba be kumu nɛ fee doro fanɛ kananɛ kena bee to keya a sela mo nyɛnpe be kekpabi a doro mo gbagba be kumu na.’ 15Nɛ m bishi: ‘Fo wanɛ Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ Enyɛnpe na kaŋɛ: ‘Ma Yesu nɛ fee tɔrɔ na. 16Ama niŋi to ŋ koso n yili. N lar fo so nna nɛ n shin nɛ fo ki ma eshumpo. A daga fanɛ fo ya kaŋɛ basa ma asheŋ nɛ fo wu kabre ere nɛ amo nɛ meeŋ ŋini fo kachako so ere be asheŋ. 17Meeŋ mɔlga fo ashi Israɛl be basa nɛ nnyamase nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ fo yɔ bumo kutɔ ere kutɔ. 18Ya bugi bumo be anishi n shin nɛ b lar bumo be tentembiri na to m ba kefulto to. Shin nɛ b lar Setani be eleŋ to m ba Ebɔrɛ peya to n shin nɛ b yirda ma nɛ n ta bumo be alubi m paŋ bumo nɛ b nya bumo be kakpa ashi Ebɔrɛ be basa laraso na to.’
Pɔɔl ka malga a bɔ Yesu be kubɔya na be asheŋ
19“Amoso, Ewura Agripa, m maŋ kini kenu n sa bɔrɛdare nɛ k shi ebɔrɛso m ba ma kutɔ na. 20Damaskɔs nɛ n fara m bɔ kubɔya na nseŋ yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ Juwebi be efuli so kikɛ nɛ nnyamase to n ya kaa bɔ kubɔya na fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to m ba Ebɔrɛ kutɔ m ba kaa wora asheŋ nɛ a beeŋ ŋini fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to kashenteŋto. 21Ŋ ka wora le ere so nɛ Juwebi na nyaŋ ma ashi bɔrɛlambu na to n fin kemɔ ma na. 22Ama Ebɔrɛ chɛ ma to hale m ba fo kabre nɛ n yili nfe a ji ma shɛda a sa ekama nyam, begboŋi nɛ bewurbi kikɛ na. Kusɔ nɛ mee malga e la kusɔ koŋwule chap nɛ anebiana nɛ Mosis gba kaŋɛ fanɛ k beeŋ wora na. 23Kumo e la fanɛ, a daga fanɛ Kristo na e ji awurfoŋ nseŋ wu n juŋkpar ekama n tiŋi luwu to ŋ ŋini Juwebi nɛ nnyamase fanɛ baaŋ tiŋ n nya kumɔlga, kumo alɛ e la kefulto bumo kutɔ.”
24Pɔɔl ka yili a malga le a kuŋ mbe kumu na nɛ Fɛstes ponte mo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Pɔɔl, keyeŋiyeŋi e kɔ fo na. Fo kawɔl be kenyi damta ere e naa shin nɛ keyeŋiyeŋi tɔr fo so na.” 25Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Yiramu, m maa lɔ nna. Ma nɛ ma nfɛra lela nɛ kashenteŋ be mmalga nɛ mee malga na. 26Ewura Agripa, n tiŋ n ta kenyɛn m malga fo kutɔ nna ŋkpal fo ka nyi asheŋ ere kikɛ so. Ma alɛ bee tama fanɛ fo ta asheŋ na be kekama n wɔtɔ fo kagbene to, ŋkpal manɛ so, asheŋ na daa maŋ wora ŋ ŋana. 27Ewura Agripa, fo yirda anebiana na a? N nyi fo ka yirda bumo.” 28Nɛ Agripa bishi Pɔɔl: “Fo tama fanɛ feeŋ tiŋ n yili epul ere to n shin nɛ ŋ ki Kristo be ebɛsopo a?” 29Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Nɛ fo ki Kristo be ebɛsopo epul ere to ŋko kachako so gba, kusɔ nɛ mee kule Ebɔrɛ e la fanɛ e shin nɛ fo nɛ bumo nɛ b yil nfe kabre a nu kamalga ere e ba ki kananɛ n du ere. Kusɔ nɛ m maa kule nɛ men nya e la kananɛ n wɔ ŋgbɛlɛbi to ere.”
30Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na nɛ gomena na nɛ Benis nɛ basa nɛ b ka na kikɛ koso a yɔ nsaa kaŋɛ abar: 31“Kanyɛn ere maŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ k daga mbe luwu ŋko kabuti.” 32Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Fɛstes: “Nɛ kanyɛn ere daa maŋ kule fanɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni mbe demu ere to nna, an daa beeŋ shin nɛ e lar kabuti ere to.”

english_text:
Paul Is Taken to Rome
1When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners. 2We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
3The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed. 4When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind. 5Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia. 6There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
7We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind. 8We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
9By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past. 10Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.” 11But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
12The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there.
The Storm at Sea
13When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete. 14But soon a strong wind called “The Northeaster” blew against us from the island. 15The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
16We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place, 17but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
18The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard. 19Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear. 20For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
21Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men:
You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss. 22But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
23I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel 24to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.” 25Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised. 26But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
27For 14 days and nights we had been blown around over the Mediterranean Sea. But about midnight the sailors realized we were getting near land. 28They measured and found that the water was about 40 meters deep. A little later they measured again and found it was only about 30 meters. 29The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
30The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship. 31But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.” 32The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
33Just before daylight Paul begged the people to eat something. He told them, “For 14 days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing. 34I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
35After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some. 36They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something. 37There were 276 people on the ship, 38and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter.
The Shipwreck
39Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach. 40They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach. 41But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
42The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping. 43But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore. 44Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_text:
Pɔɔl ka luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to n yɔ Rom be asheŋ
1B ka ba yili kumo fanɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n yɔ Itali nɛ b ta Pɔɔl nɛ kabutipoana ko m bɔɔ Julias enɔ. E daa la Romebi be ewurgboŋ be benapo be katuŋ to be enimubi nna. 2Adramitiam nɛ an daŋ yili n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k daŋ bela ase a yil nɛ k yɔ Eeshia be efuli so be teku be nnɔ ase na to n yɔ. Anyi nɛ Masɛdonia be esa nɛ e shi Tɛsalɔnika nɛ baa tre mo Aristaakes na e daa la. 3Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an fo Saidɔn. Ndoŋ nɛ Julias wora Pɔɔl kelela n shin nɛ e lar n ya chɔrɔ mo teriana nɛ b sa mo asɔ nɛ a daga fanɛ e nya. 4An ka naŋ lar ndoŋ nɛ an kpal afu ko ka daa ber a shɛr anyi to so m bɔla Saipres so be kakpa nɛ afu na daa maa ber eleŋso na. 5An ta loŋ m ba bɔla teku na be mboŋ nɛ a taga to Silisia nɛ Pamfilia be efuliana so na, n naŋ ta ndoŋ m ba fo Maira nɛ k wɔ Lisia na. 6Ndoŋ nɛ benapo be enimubi na ba nya Alɛkzaandria be ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k daa sha keyɔ Itali nɛ e shin nɛ an luri kumo to. 7Ŋkpal afu na so ekuloŋgboŋ na daŋ nite nchu na so nna boeŋ boeŋ loŋ nchɛ damta ko pɔɛŋ nɛ an ba kpar Kenaidas so n yɔ. Ŋkpal kananɛ afu na daa ber a shɛr anyi to na so an daa maŋ tiŋ m bɔla kakpa nɛ an daŋ bɔla so na n yɔ anishito, amoso, Kriit be kepla na so be kakpa nɛ k daŋ kuŋ anyi ashi afu na to nɛ an daŋ bɔla n ya mata Salmoni ŋ kpar so n yɔ. 8An daŋ baŋ kra teku na be kɔnɔ ase nna n ji awurfoŋ loŋ n ya fo kakpa ko nɛ baa tre Ekulonyilikpa Lela Nɛ Kafɔŋ Maŋ Wɔtɔ na. Ndoŋ nɛ Lasiya be kade to daa maŋ wɔ kufɔ.
9An daŋ chɛr ndoŋ ga hale nɛ anyi be kenaŋ pɛ ekpa ya ki kpakpa, ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋɛ na so nɛ kachɛ nɛ baa nyiŋi alubi be keyigempaŋ be asheŋ be daŋkare na gba baŋ so. 10Nɛ Pɔɔl fiɛ bumo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “M braana, n wu fanɛ yili nfe a yɔ, anyi be enite ere be ekpa ere to lubi ga. Ekuloŋgboŋ ere nɛ kumo be esulɔ ere be adamta beeŋ jija nɛ basa gba e mur.” 11Ama benapo be enimubi na daŋ kplaŋ Pɔɔl be kamalga na so nna nseŋ yirda kusɔ nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be befarpoana na be enimu nɛ ekuloŋ na wura na kaŋɛ nna. 12Ndoŋ be ekulonyilikpa na ka daa maa la kakpa lela awo to so, basa na be bedamta daa sha keyige eyilikpa na nna nsaa wɔ ekuloŋgboŋ na to a bɛ teku na so a sha kewora ania n fo Finiks nɛ baaŋ tiŋ nna na. Ndoŋ daa la Kriit be ekulonyilikpa nna a kɔ nnɔ anyɔ, kukoŋwule daa wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be jisoso be kaba so nna nɛ kukoŋwule malɛ daa wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be bena so be kaba so. Ndoŋ nɛ b daa beeŋ tiŋ n shir a wɔ hale nɛ awo na be jemanɛ e ya choŋ.
Afugboŋ ko ka ber teku na so be asheŋ
13Afubi ko ka chela n shi kelargato be kaseto be kaba so m ba nɛ basa na fara a tama fanɛ asheŋ nɛ b daŋ kre fanɛ baaŋ wora na beeŋ nyalɛ n sa bumo. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b gberge ekuloŋgboŋ na be kebɛlso gbɛgbɛso nɛ baa ta a lɛ nchu to nɛ k bee pɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na to a yili na ashi to nseŋ luri ekuloŋgboŋ na to n ta m mata Kriit be teku na be ekarso loŋ a yɔ. 14Ama k maŋ chɛr ko nɛ afugboŋ ko nɛ baa tre epeŋilarkpa be bena so be kaba so be afu na shi kepla na so m ba ber ekuloŋ na 15nɛ k shɛr afu na to kanaŋkamaso ŋ gben nseŋ shin nɛ afu na kɔ anyi be ekuloŋgboŋ na a yɔ. 16An ka bɔla Kawda be kepla na be epeŋitɔrkpa nɛ an luri kakpa ko nɛ k kuŋ anyi gbrɛ ashi afu na to. Ndoŋ nɛ an wora ania ga m ba tiŋ m mɔlga ekulombi nɛ kegboŋi na daa gberge na ashi kebure to. 17B daŋ gberge kumo nna n wɔtɔ kegboŋi na be epunto nseŋ ta efɔlana m bɔla kegboŋi koŋwule na be kaseto ŋ kre kumo kpakpa. Ŋkpal b ka daa lɔ kufu fanɛ baaŋ ya ber Libiya be teku be ekarso be keplagboŋ na to n nia so, b daŋ yɔɔ ekuloŋ na be wajɛ gbɛgbɛso nɛ afu bee ber a yɛr ekuloŋgboŋ na nna nseŋ shin nɛ afu na e baa kɔ ekuloŋ to na a yɔ loŋ. 18Kare ka chɛ nɛ afugboŋ na kraa ber eleŋso nɛ b fara a lara kumo to be esulɔ na a lɛ nchu na to. 19Kare ka naŋ chɛ nɛ bumo gbagba bela ekuloŋ na to be asɔ damta ko nɛ a daŋ daga fanɛ b baa kɔ a shuŋ kumo to na be ako n lɛ nchu na to. 20An daŋ ji nchɛ damta ekuloŋgboŋ na to a maa wu epeŋi nɛ achɛkpabi nɛ afu na malɛ kraŋ baa ber eleŋso, nɛ an ba gben n yige kebaatama anyi be kenaŋ pete be asheŋ.
21Basa na ka ta nchɛ damta loŋ a maa ji shɛŋ nɛ kachako nɛ Pɔɔl koso n yili bumo to ŋ kaŋɛ: “M braana, a daga men ka daŋ bɛ ma kɔnɔ so n daŋ shir Kriit to nɛ an daŋ tiŋ ŋ gelge le be awurfoŋ nɛ jɛrbi nɛ anyee ji ere. 22Ama mee kule menyi nna fanɛ men baa kɔ kenyɛn, ŋkpal manɛ so, menyi be ekama maaŋ paŋ mbe ŋkpa, ekuloŋgboŋ ere nawule e naaŋ mur. 23Ŋkpal manɛ so, ndre kanyɛso Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ma nɛ mee bunyaŋ mo na be malaika kaŋ ba ma kutɔ nna m ba kaŋɛ ma: 24‘Pɔɔl, sa maa lɔ kufu.
