A daga fanɛ fo ya yili Romebi be ewurgboŋ na be anishito. Ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ malɛ nɛ mbe kelela so, basa nɛ fo nɛ bumo wɔ nchu so be enite ere to ere be ekama maaŋ mur.’ 25Amoso, men baa kɔ kenyɛn, ŋkpal manɛ so, n yirda Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ ma na maaŋ chɛrga kikɛ. 26Ama afu ere beeŋ ber anyi n ya lɛ kechɛɛ ko so bre.”
27Anyi be kachɛ kuduanasopo be kanyɛso nɛ afu na wɔtɔ a kpata anyi ashi Eedria be teku so. Kiidiso be jemanɛ ko nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be befarpo na kaŋɛ fanɛ baa tama fanɛ anyee taga to kedeŋi so. 28Ndoŋ nna nɛ b lɛ efɔl gbɛgbɛso nɛ b kɔ a karga nchu be nchiŋ na n wɔtɔ nchu na to n wu fanɛ kakpa nɛ b daa yil na be nchiŋ wɔ ayadra kalfa nɛ adunyɔ. B ka yɔ anishito gbrɛ nɛ b naŋ wora loŋ n wu fanɛ ndoŋ malɛ wɔ ayadra adekpanu. 29B daa lɔ kufu nna fanɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na beeŋ ya dii kefaltagboŋ ko so nseŋ kpal loŋ so n ta abɛlso gbɛgbɛso ana ko n lɛ ekuloŋ na be kamanto n wɔtɔ nchu na to nɛ a ya pɛ ekuloŋ na to n yili nɛ b baa kule Ebɔrɛ a jo nɛ kare ya chɛ. 30Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be befarpo na wora ania nɛ b lar n shile nseŋ yɔɔ ekulombi na to n wɔtɔ nchu na to nsaa kute a wora fanɛ b ka bee sha keta abɛlso gbɛgbɛso na be ako n lɛ n wɔtɔ ekuloŋ na be anishito malɛ na. 31Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ benapo na nɛ bumo be enimubi na: “Befarpo ere baŋ lar ekuloŋgboŋ ere to, men maaŋ lar kikɛ.” 32Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na ku efɔlana nɛ a kre ekulombi na m mata kegboŋi na n shin nɛ k yɔ.
33Kare ka bee taga to kechɛ nɛ Pɔɔl kule basa na kikɛ fanɛ b ji ajibi nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Menyi be nchɛ kuduana nde kabre men ka bee jo a maa ji shɛŋ. 34Jande men ji ajibi n nya eleŋ m mɔlga menyi gbagba be amu. Menyi be ekama maaŋ paŋ mbe kemin koŋwule gba.” 35Pɔɔl ka malga le n loge nɛ e ta bodobodo n di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ bumo kikɛ be anishito nseŋ bu kumo to n fara a we. 36Nɛ basa na ji kenyɛn nɛ bumo be ekama malɛ ji ajibi. 37Anyi kikɛ nyam daa wɔ basa alfa anyɔ nɛ adushunu nɛ ashe ekuloŋgboŋ na to. 38Ekama ka ji n kukwe nɛ b ta ayu nɛ a wɔ ekuloŋgboŋ na to na n lɛ teku na to nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na e fuga so.
Ekuloŋgboŋ na ka bure be asheŋ
39Kare ka chɛ befarpo na maŋ tiŋ m pin teku na be kedeŋi nɛ b fo na. Ama b wu teku na ka ku kasawule n wɔtɔ nchu na be kakpa ko nseŋ naŋ wora kewawa nɛ b yili kumo bumo be ŋgbene to fanɛ b shin nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na e ya fo kasawule na n yili nɛ baaŋ tiŋ nna na. 40Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ku abɛlso gbɛgbɛso ana na be efɔlana na to n shin nɛ abɛlsoana na ka nchu na to nseŋ saŋɛ ekuloŋ na be kamanto be ndibi paŋgelambi nɛ b kɔ a niŋi kumo na malɛ epul na to. Ade be kaman nɛ b maŋ ekuloŋgboŋ na be wajɛ gbɛgbɛso nɛ afu bee ber a yɛr kumo na so ashi ekuloŋgboŋ na be anishito nɛ afu na e ber ekuloŋgboŋ na n yɔ anishito kedeŋi so. 41Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na ya ber kechɛɛsawule ko to nchu na to nɛ kumo be anishito nia nɛ k tia ŋ gben nsaa yil nɛ atiligboŋ ko bee kpata ekuloŋgboŋ na be kamanto eleŋso a bure kumo. 42Nɛ benapo na kre kemɔ kabutipoana na kikɛ nɛ bumo be ekama e sa maŋ laa n dii n shile n yɔ. 43Ama benapo be enimubi na ka daa maa sha nɛ Pɔɔl e wu so, e daŋ ju benapo na ashi loŋ be kesheŋ na to nna nseŋ kaŋɛ basa na be bumo nɛ b daa nyi kalaa na kikɛ fanɛ b fara n tɛ n luri nchu na to a laa a dii. 44Nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na malɛ pɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be ndibi fɛtaso na to m bɛ kaman a ba. Loŋ nɛ ekama daŋ wora n dii nɛ alenfia.

english_text:
On the Island of Malta
1When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta. 2The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
3After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand. 4When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
5Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed. 6The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
7The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days. 8His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
9After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed. 10The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed.
From Malta to Rome
11Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.” 12We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days. 13From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli. 14There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
15Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged.
Paul in Rome
16We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
17Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said:
My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans. 18They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death. 19 The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor.
But I don't have anything to say against my own nation. 20I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
21The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you. 22But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
23They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
24Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not. 25Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet 26 to tell our ancestors,
‘Go to these people
and tell them:
You will listen and listen,
but never understand.
You will look and look,
but never see.
27All of you
have stubborn hearts.
Your ears are stopped up,
and your eyes are covered.
You cannot see or hear
or understand.
If you could,
you would turn to me,
and I would heal you.’ ”
28-29Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
30For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him. 31He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_text:
Kusɔ nɛ k wora Pɔɔl ashi Malta be asheŋ
1An ka dii kedeŋi so nɛ alenfia nɛ an nu fanɛ kepla na nɛ baa tre Malta. 2Ndoŋebi daŋ chɛ anyi to ga. Bɔrɛ daŋ fara nna a ba nɛ awo ko ba nɛ b puga edɛ n sa anyi nɛ an wɔl. 3Pɔɔl ka chala ndibi a wɔtɔ edɛ na to nɛ kuwɔ ko lar ndibi na to ŋkpal kuwuloŋ na so m mea mbe enɔ kpakpa. 4Kepla na so be basa na ka wu kuwɔ na ka chul Pɔɔl be enɔ so nɛ b kaŋɛ abar: “Kanyɛn ere la emɔpo nna, k maŋ kɔ emɔrɔ. E tiŋ n lar nchu na to nɛ alenfia, ama kashenteŋ be ekpa so be ebɔrɛ na maaŋ yige mo nɛ e baa kraa wɔtɔ.” 5Ama Pɔɔl tiŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ kuwɔ na n wɔtɔ edɛ na to nɛ k maŋ tiŋ n doro mo kikɛ. 6B daa dara mo nna a keni kananɛ e beeŋ tiŋ to n tɔr epul na to n wu. Ama b ka jo loŋ n ya gben a maa wu kulubi kikɛ ka bee nya Pɔɔl nɛ b chɛrga bumo be nfɛra nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ ko e la mo.”
7Kakpa nɛ kesheŋ ere daŋ wora Pɔɔl na nɛ kepla na so wura be adɔsawuleana so daa maŋ wɔ kufɔ. Ewura na be ketre e daa la Pablias. E daŋ sɔ anyi kasawule na so nseŋ keta anyi kufɔ nɛnɛ ga nchɛ nsa. 8Pablias mo tuto be eyur daŋ bel edɛ nna nɛ e dese ebu to a lɔ epun to nɛ Pɔɔl luri mbe ebu na to n ta mbe enɔana n deŋi mo so nseŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n sa mo nɛ e nya alenfia. 9Kede be kaman nɛ kechɛɛsawule na so be belɔpo kikɛ ba nɛ e chɛ bumo. 10B daŋ kɛ anyi asɔ damta ga ndoŋ. Kachɛ nɛ an ba kaa lar ndoŋ nɛ b naŋ ta asɔ nɛ anyeeŋ ya kaa sha ekpa to n wɔtɔ anyi be ekuloŋgboŋ na to.
Pɔɔl nɛ mo braana na ka lar Malta n yɔ Rom be asheŋ
11Afɔl asa be kaman nɛ an luri Alɛkzaandria be ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ baa tre kumo Mborobi na to n yɔ. Kepla na so nɛ k daŋ ba kaa wɔ loŋ nɛ awo be jemanɛ ba choŋ. 12Ndoŋ nna nɛ an ta n ya fo Sirakyus be kade to n ji nchɛ asa ndoŋ pɔɛŋ 13nseŋ ta loŋ m ba fo kadegboŋ ko nɛ baa tre Rɛjiam. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ afu ko shi epeŋitɔrkpa be bena so m ber m ba. Kumo be kachɛ nyɔsopo nɛ an fo Putioli be ekulonyilikpa. 14An ka ba wu bebɛsopo ko ndoŋ nɛ b shin nɛ an ji bɔkwe bumo kutɔ. Asheŋ nɛ a daŋ wora anyi anyi be enite na to pɔɛŋ nɛ an ya fo Rom nna na. 15Bekurgepo nɛ b wɔ Rom na ka nu anyi be asheŋ nɛ b lege anyi m ba hale Apias be Kebɛ nɛ kakpa nɛ baa tre Befɔ be Ewushikpa be Nwu Asa na. Pɔɔl ka wu bumo nɛ e nya kenyɛn chɔrɔ Ebɔrɛ ga.
Kusɔ nɛ k wora Pɔɔl ashi Rom be asheŋ
16An ka ba Rom nɛ Romebi be abane be benimuana na shin nɛ Pɔɔl gbagba wɔtɔ a keni mbe kumu so nseŋ shin nɛ b lara enapo nɛ e baa de Pɔɔl so.
17Pɔɔl be kachɛ sasopo ashi Rom nɛ e tre ndoŋ be Juwebi be benimuana na m ba shɛr ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Ŋ kurgepoana, m maŋ wora shɛŋ n da anyi be basa ŋko edaŋkare nɛ an nanaana sa anyi na so nɛ m peebi ti ma ebu ashi Jerusalɛm nseŋ naŋ ta ma m bɔɔ Romebi enɔ. 18Romebi na ka bishi ma asheŋ a maŋ wu kulubi kikɛ nɛ n wora nɛ k daga luwu nɛ b daa shin nɛ b yige ma. 19Nɛ Juwebi na maŋ shuli kumo be loŋ nɛ ŋ gben ŋ kule fanɛ b shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na gbagba e keni ma demu na to, mannɛ fanɛ ŋ kɔ kusɔ ko nna a sha keta n wu m peebi na kulubi. 20Amoso nɛ n tre menyi nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi amo na. Esa nɛ Israɛlebi na bee tama fanɛ e beeŋ ba na malɛ so nɛ ŋgbɛlɛbi ere wɔ ma enɔana to na.” 21Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Esa kama maŋ sibɛ anyi nwɔl ashi Judiya ŋ kaŋɛ anyi fo asheŋ, an kurgepo kama malɛ maŋ shi ndoŋ m bar anyi fo baru lubi ŋko kulubi kama nɛ fo wora be asheŋ. 22Ama kaŋɛ anyi kusɔ nɛ k wɔ fo kumu to, kusɔ nɛ fee fɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an nyi basa ka bee malga kaplɛkama a gbiti katuŋ nɛ fo wɔ na to be basa.” 23Kede be kaman nɛ b sa Pɔɔl kachɛ nɛ baaŋ ba. Kachɛ na ka fo nɛ bumo be bedamta ba kakpa nɛ Pɔɔl daa wɔ na nɛ e baŋ yili chipurso m bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be asheŋ na ŋ ŋini bumo loŋ n ya fo kanyɛso. E daŋ bɛ Mosis be mbra na nɛ anebiana na be nsibɛ na so nna ŋ kɔ ga n fin keshin nɛ basa na yirda Yesu. 24Beko daŋ yirda mbe kamalga na nɛ beko malɛ kini keyirda kumo. 25Pɔɔl ka malga kesheŋ koŋwule ere n loge nɛ b fara a ji abar emɔrɔ a yɔ. Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “Kashenteŋ nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na daŋ shin nɛ anebi Aizaaya daŋ wu ŋ kaŋɛ men nanaana fanɛ e ya kaŋɛ basa na le:
26‘Menyeeŋ nu hale n ya gben, ama men maaŋ pin to.
Menyeeŋ keni hale n ya gben, ama men maaŋ wu shɛŋ.’
27‘Ŋkpal basa ere be ŋgbene ka du kpakpa so
b ti bumo be asoe
nseŋ buu bumo be anishi so.
Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, bumo be anishi beeŋ bugi asheŋ be kewuto
nɛ bumo be asoe e bugi asheŋ be kenuto
nɛ bumo be ŋgbene e bugi asheŋ be kepinto.
Ebɔrɛ yɛ: Loŋ na baaŋ ba ma kutɔ
nɛ n lara bumo ashi bumo be kebaawɔtɔ dra to
n sa bumo kebaawɔtɔ popɔr.’ ”
28Nɛ Pɔɔl naŋ kaŋɛ: “Amoso, men baa nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ shuŋi basa nɛ baa bɔ mbe kumɔlga be kubɔya na nnyamase gba kutɔ. Bumo ere beeŋ bugi asoe n nu.” 29Pɔɔl ka malga asheŋ ere n loge nɛ Juwebi na pesaŋ to a ji abar emɔrɔ kpakpaso a yɔ.
30Pɔɔl be nfɛ anyɔ nɛ e sɔ esa ko be ebu a wɔtɔ a ka ebu na wura. Ndoŋ nɛ e daa wɔ a sɔ basa kama nɛ b daa ba m ba kaa chɔrɔ mo. 31Ndoŋ koŋwule na malɛ nɛ e daa wɔ a bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be kubɔya na a sa basa kenyɛnso a malga kayurwushiso a ŋini Enyɛnpe Yesu Kristo be asheŋ.

english_text:
1From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus.
God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news 2that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures. 3-4This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
5Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith. 6You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
7This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people.
I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
A Prayer of Thanks
8First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith. 9God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
10In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you. 11I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith. 12What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
13 My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places. 14-15It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome.
The Power of the Good News
16 I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles. 17 The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.”
Everyone Is Guilty
18From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth. 19They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them. 20 God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse. 21 They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark. 22They claim to be wise, but they are fools. 23 They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
24So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies. 25They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
26God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural. 27Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
28 Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things. 29They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip, 30say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil.
These people don't respect their parents. 31They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others. 32They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_text:
1Kawɔl ere shi ma Pɔɔl nɛ n la Kristo Yesu be kenya na kutɔ nna. Ebɔrɛ e tre ma nseŋ lara ma ashi ma basa to n shin nɛ ŋ ki mbe eshuŋipo nɛ m ba kaa bɔ mbe baru lela na. 2Dradra na kikɛ nɛ mo ere Ebɔrɛ na bɔla mbe anebiana so nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ cheembi na to n nase kɔnɔ 3fanɛ baru lela na beeŋ ba kaa kute mo Pibinyɛn, an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo nɛ nyiŋgbasa be kaplɛa so nɛ e shi Ewura Deevid be kanaŋ to na be asheŋ. 4Kebaawɔtɔ cheembi be Kiyoyu malɛ be kaplɛa so, Ebɔrɛ ta eleŋgboŋ ŋ ŋini e ka la mo Pibinyɛn saŋɛ nɛ e tiŋi mo luwu to na. 5Mo so nɛ Ebɔrɛ bɔla n wu ma kuwɔr n sa ma ekpa fanɛ m baa la eshuŋipo ŋkpal Yesu koŋwule na be ketre so nɛ efuli kama so ebi e ba yirda mo nseŋ fara a nu a sa mo. 6Menyi, bumo nɛ men wɔ Rom be kade to ere gba ti efuliana nɛ Ebɔrɛ tre fanɛ men ba kaa la Yesu Kristo peya na so. 7Amoso nɛ mee sibɛ kawɔl ere a sa menyi kikɛ nɛ men wɔ Rom be kade to nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha menyi nseŋ tre menyi fanɛ men ba kaa la mo gbagba be basa na. An Tuto Ebɔrɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Yesu Kristo e sa menyi kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ kagbenewushi.
Pɔɔl ka bee di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ nsaa chɔrɔ mo be asheŋ
8Men shin nɛ n fara m bɔla Yesu Kristo so n chɔrɔ ma Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal menyi kikɛ so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, durnya ere to ebi kikɛ baa ji kananɛ menyi be yirda du be asheŋ nna. 9Ebɔrɛ nɛ n ta ma kagbene kikɛ nyam a bɔ mo Pibinyɛn be baru lela na gbagba e la ma shɛdajipo a nyi menyi be asheŋ ka baa wɔ ma kagbene to ashi ma kabɔrɛkule to saŋkikɛ. 10Ma alɛ bee kule Ebɔrɛ nna fanɛ naniere nɛ k par mo, e sa ma ekpa nɛ m ba bɔɔ menyi so. 11M baa sha kewu menyi gbrɛ nna n shin nɛ men nya abɔrɛsheŋ be nɛfa nɛ a bee bɔla Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu na so a ba anyi so na. Loŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ men nya eleŋ kebɛso na to n ti so. 12Kumo e la fanɛ nɛ n tiŋ m ba, menyi be yirda beeŋ leŋ ma to nɛ ma alɛ peya e leŋ menyi alɛ gba to. 13Bekurgepoana, mee sha fanɛ men baa nyi fanɛ saŋɛ damta nɛ ŋ kre keba menyi kutɔ be nia nɛ m ba shin nɛ basa e yirda Yesu kananɛ n shin nɛ nnyamase ko gba wora ashi mboŋ ko na, ama m maŋ nya kumo be ekpa. 14Ŋkpal manɛ so, k du fanɛ ŋ ka ji Griikebi nɛ basa bubɔrɔ nɛ benyiashempo nɛ bewulpo kikɛ abɔrɛsheŋ be keŋini be kukɔ nna. 15Amoso nɛ m baa sha kebɔ baru lela na n sa menyi nɛ men wɔ Rom be kade to gba na.
Baru lela na be eleŋ be asheŋ
16M maa wora baru lela na be anishinyɔr kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, kumo so nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee bɔla a ŋini mbe eleŋ a mɔlga basa kama nɛ baa yirda na. Juwebi e nya kumo be loŋ be ekpa pɔɛŋ nseŋ ta nnyamase, bumo nɛ b maŋ la Juwebi na m bɛ so. 17Ŋkpal manɛ so, baru lela na e naa ŋini kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee nase kumo fanɛ basa e baa la belelapo mbe anishito. Kumo alɛ be sososo kikɛ la yirda nna hale n ya fo ekar. Loŋ gbagba malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ: “Esa kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e la elelapo na beeŋ nya ŋkpa ŋkpal mbe yirda so.”
Ebɔrɛ be agbo nɛ k bee ba basa so be asheŋ
18Ama Ebɔrɛ bugi to ŋ ŋini basa kananɛ mbe agbo beeŋ shi ebɔrɛso m ba basa so ŋkpal alubi nɛ a wɔ bumo be ŋgbene to nɛ amo nɛ a dii efuli na kikɛ so. Bumo e la basa nɛ bumo be alubi na bee buu kashenteŋ na so basa be anishito na. 19Ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ nɛ basa beeŋ ta m pin Ebɔrɛ na baŋ dii efuli nna geeŋ a sa bumo, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ gbagba e bugi amo to n sa bumo. 20Kashenteŋ malɛ nna fanɛ yili jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ to durnya kikɛ na m ba fo mbre, basa beeŋ tiŋ m pin kananɛ mbe edasheŋ nɛ basa maaŋ tiŋ n wu kenishiso na du, kumo e la fanɛ mbe eleŋ nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar na nɛ kananɛ e la Ebɔrɛ kashenteŋto na. Bumo alɛ beeŋ tiŋ m pin amo to, ŋkpal mbe asɔtoso so. Loŋ so, b maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kini mo nseŋ ta bumo be amu n ya ji. 21B nyi Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ, ama bumo alɛ maa ta mo fanɛ Ebɔrɛ a bunyaŋ mo ŋko a chɔrɔ mo. Ama b shin nɛ bumo be nfɛra ki nfɛra fuloŋ nna nɛ bumo be kawuliso be ŋgbene malɛ ki m biri to. 22B yɛ b nyi asheŋ, ama bumo alɛ ki bewulpo nna. 23B ka beeŋ baa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to saŋkama na, b wɔtɔ nna a bunyaŋ asɔ nɛ enyiŋgbasa wora nna nɛ amo be ako duli basa nɛ ako duli mbuibi, ako malɛ duli asɔbɔya nɛ ade malɛ duli asɔ gbeyeso.
24Amoso, Ebɔrɛ malɛ yige bumo be asheŋ nna n sa bumo nɛ b luri kesakalea be ayɛlgasɔ to a wɔtɔ a kɔ abar be eyurana a wora amɔmɔshiasheŋ. 25Kashenteŋ be mmalga nɛ a bee kute Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ na nɛ b kɔ a chɛr efɛ be mmalga a wɔtɔ a bunyaŋ nsaa shuŋ Ebɔrɛ be asɔtoso nsaa yige amo be Etopo na bre, emo nɛ e daga epaŋ be kedi hale mbaanaayɔ na. Amɛn. 26Ŋkpal le be asheŋ ere so Ebɔrɛ yige bumo nna n sa kesakalea be ayɛlgasɔ hale nɛ bumo be beche yige kedi benyɛn n lɛ nsaa kɔ bumo braana beche a di keche nɛ kenyɛn. 27Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ benyɛn na gba bee yige kebaadi beche a lɛ nsaa shin nɛ bumo be ŋgbene bee kaa kesakalea so a wɔ bumo braana benyɛn be kasha to. Benyɛn wɔtɔ nna a kɔ abar kesakalea so a wora amɔmɔshiasheŋ nsaa nya amo be loŋ be tɔnɔ ashi bumo be eyurana to.
28Ade malɛ kikɛ be kaman Ebɔrɛ yige bumo be asheŋ nna n sa bumo ŋkpal b ka kini kenyiŋi kashenteŋ be abɔrɛsheŋ na so nɛ b baa wɔtɔ a wora asheŋ nɛ a maŋ daga kikɛ. 29Ŋkpal b ka kini Ebɔrɛ na so, eda lubi be yiri kikɛ nɛ alubisheŋ nɛ kejimuni nɛ abar be kebaawora alubi e bɔlɔ bumo to. Amo nɛ a bɔlɔ bumo to gba n ti so e la, kayurbesa nɛ kamɔ nɛ nlu nɛ efɛ nɛ kebaafɛ abar asheŋ lubi. Ade malɛ gba be buushi baa kuli bumo braana, 30nsaa malga alubi a gbiti abar a kishi Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ a tege abar nsaa wu bumo be amu. B kɔ mpuchi a fin alubi be ekpa popɔrana a wora alubi nsaa kini kebaanu a sa bumo nioana nɛ bumo tutoana. 31B maŋ nyi asheŋ, bumo alɛ maŋ naa bɛ bumo be nnɔ so ŋko a wu kuwɔr nsaa maa la basa. 32B nyi Ebɔrɛ be mbra na ka bee kaŋɛ fanɛ bekama nɛ b wɔ le be kebaawɔtɔ ere to daga luwu, ama b kraŋ pere kenishi nna a wora amo nsaa leŋ basa pɔtɛ gba to a wɔtɔ loŋ be asheŋ na be kewora to.

english_text:
God's Judgment Is Fair
1 Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things. 2We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way. 3Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse? 4 You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
5But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness. 6 God will reward each of us for what we have done. 7He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever. 8But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil. 9All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles. 10But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles. 11 God doesn't have any favorites!
12Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says. 13God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
14Some people naturally obey the Law's commands, even though they don't have the Law. 15This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned, 16when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says.
The Jews and the Law
17Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God. 18By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right. 19You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark. 20And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
21But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal? 22You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples. 23You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God. 24 It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
25Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised. 26In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised. 27So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
28Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew. 29 To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_text:
Ebɔrɛ be demu be keji be asheŋ
1Amoso, manɛ be ekpa nɛ fo dimɛdi kɔ nsaa tiŋ a wu fo barkasa kulubi? Ŋkpal manɛ so, kanaŋkama nɛ fo du nseŋ wu fo barkasa kulubi, fee ji nna a bri fo gbagba be kumu nna na, ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ koŋwule na nɛ fee wora. 2Nɛ Ebɔrɛ bre bee ji basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ ere demu, an nyi e ka bee ji asheŋ kashenteŋ be ekpa so. 3Ama fo ere dimɛdi, asheŋ nɛ fo kɔ a wu basa kulubi ere gbagba nɛ fee wora, amoso, fee tama fanɛ feeŋ nya ŋ gelge Ebɔrɛ be demuji to a? 4Ŋko fo kpal Ebɔrɛ be kelela ka shi mo to ga na so nna nɛ e ka maa nya manaŋ a gberge basa kusoe na nɛ mbe kanyiti na so so nna a fɛl mo a? Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kelela wɔtɔ nna nɛ fo nya n lar fo alubi to a? 5Ama ŋkpal fo kagbene ka du kpakpa a maa sha kechɛrga na so, fo wɔ fo alubi na to nna a shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ be agbo bee kaa a ti so a jo kachɛ nɛ mbe agbo nɛ mbe demuji kashenteŋ be ekpa so na bee lar efuli na. 6Kusɔ kama nɛ esa wora, Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ka mo kumo be kukɔ. 7Bumo nɛ alelasheŋ be kewora maa gben bumo nɛ baa fin kemaŋkura nɛ bunyaŋ nɛ kebaawɔtɔ nɛ k maŋ kɔ luwu na, e beeŋ sa bumo ŋkpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar na. 8Ama bumo nɛ b wɔ bumo gbagba be aparsheŋ to a kini kashenteŋ na be kebɛso nsaa bɛ alubi so na, Ebɔrɛ be kagbene beeŋ kaa nɛ mbe agbo e ba bumo so. 9Tɔrɔ nɛ kayurnyaŋ beeŋ ba dimɛdi kama nɛ e bee wora alubi so, Juwebi e naaŋ juŋkpar n nya amo pɔɛŋ nɛ nnyamase e bɛ so. 10Ama ekama nɛ e bee wora alelasheŋ, kemaŋkura nɛ bunyaŋ nɛ kagbenewushi beeŋ baa wɔ amodoŋwura so. Juwebi e naaŋ juŋkpar n nya amo pɔɛŋ nseŋ ta nnyamase m bɛ so. 11Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ maa kpɛa basa to.
12Bekama nɛ b maŋ kɔ mbra na nseŋ wora alubi beeŋ lar mbra na be kaman n wu. Bekama malɛ nɛ b wɔ mbra na to nseŋ wora alubi, mbra na to nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ bɔla n ji bumo demu. 13Ŋkpal manɛ so, mannɛ basa nɛ baa nu mbra na nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee nase kumo fanɛ b la belelapo mbe anishito, bumo nɛ baa wora kusɔ nɛ mbra na bee kaŋɛ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ba nase kumo fanɛ b la belelapo. 14Kashenteŋto, nnyamase maŋ kɔ anebi Mosis be mbra na, ama saŋkama nɛ bumo gbagba ta nfɛra nɛ a wɔ bumo to na n wora kusɔ nɛ mbra na bee ŋini, kumo ere bumo be nfɛra na ki mbra na nna n sa bumo na, ama bumo alɛ maŋ kɔ mbra na. 15Bumo be asheŋ woraso na e naa ŋini fanɛ Ebɔrɛ ta asɔ nɛ mbra na bee ŋini na n wɔtɔ bumo be ŋgbene to. Nɛ bumo be elakal gba bee ŋini fanɛ kashenteŋ nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋko bumo be nfɛra maa dese bumo ŋkpal alubi so, saŋko malɛ nɛ a bee yili bumo be kaman. 16To, loŋ malɛ nɛ baru lela nɛ mee bɔ na bee ŋini fanɛ asheŋ beeŋ ba kaa du kachɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ bɔla Yesu Kristo so n yili edimɛdi be wulo be nfɛraana so n ji bumo demu.
Juwebi nɛ mbra na be asheŋ
17To, mannɛ fo e naa tre fo kumu Juw nsaa ta fo yirda a deŋi Mosis be mbra na so a wɔtɔ a ji njɔŋ a kaŋɛ fanɛ fo nɛ Ebɔrɛ be nferinto wɔ ebel na a? 18Mannɛ fo e naa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo nyi kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ esa e wora, fo alɛ naŋ koya ashi mbra na to a nyi kusɔ nɛ k daga esa ka lara na a? 19Mannɛ fo koŋwule na e naa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo e baa la esa nɛ e bee keta betanpo kekpabi nsaa du fanɛ kefulto a sa bumo nɛ b wɔ tentembiri to na a? 20Mannɛ fo koŋwule na e kraa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo e la basa balto be eŋinipo nɛ mbibi be eŋinipo, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo ere be kanyiasheŋ na nɛ kashenteŋ na bee shi mbra na to nna a? 21To, fo nɛ fee ŋini basa pɔtɛ asheŋ, fo maa ŋini fo kumu loŋ be asheŋ na a? Fo e naa malga abɔrɛsheŋ a sa basa fanɛ b sa maa yuri, fo alɛ nsaa yuri a? 22Fo koŋwule na e naa kaŋɛ basa fanɛ b sa maa di bumo braana be beche ŋko a shin nɛ bumo braana be bekul e baa di bumo, fo alɛ nsaa wora loŋ a? Fo kishi agbir, fo alɛ nsaa yuri asɔ ashi amo be ebuana to. 23Fo e wɔtɔ a kɔ mbra na a ji njɔŋ, fo alɛ nseŋ naa shin nɛ fo kemaa bɛ amo so bee bar Ebɔrɛ anishinyɔr. 24Loŋ koŋwule na malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ: “Menyi, Juwebi so nɛ nnyamase bee malga a ji Ebɔrɛ emɔrɔ.”
25Nɛ fee bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ ku kututu, kumo ere fo keku na kɔ kifi, ama nɛ fo maa bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ ku kututu, kenyanyaŋɛso nɛ fo ku na. 26Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ basa nɛ b maŋ ku atutu na baa wora asɔ nɛ mbra na bee ŋini, Ebɔrɛ bee sɔ bumo nna fanɛ bumo nɛ b ku atutu a? 27To, men baa nyi fanɛ basa nɛ b maŋ ku durnya ere to, bumo alɛ nsaa bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so na be kebaawɔtɔ so nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ yili n ji menyi nɛ men ku nseŋ naa kɔ mbra na n ti so na demu. 28Mannɛ kenishiso nɛ baa ta a pin Juw, mannɛ kuku kututu be nwɔl na n lɛ na malɛ e la kashenteŋ be katutuku na. 29Kashenteŋto, dimɛdi be kebaawɔtɔ to e naa ŋini e ka la Juw nɛ kashenteŋ malɛ be keku na la kagbene to be kesheŋ, Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ nna, mannɛ kenishiso be asheŋ nna. Nɛ esa nɛ e ku loŋ na malɛ be kechɔrɔ bee shi Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nna, mannɛ nyiŋgbasa kutɔ.

english_text:
1What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised? 2It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews. 3It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith? 4 No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God,
“Your words
will be proven true,
and in court
you will win your case.”
5If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask. 6But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world? 7Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner. 8You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well.
No One Is Good
9What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said. 10 The Scriptures tell us,
“No one is acceptable to God!
11Not one of them understands
or even searches for God.
12They have all turned away
and are worthless.
There isn't one person
who does right.
13 Their words are like
an open pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
Each word is as deadly
as the fangs of a snake,
14 and they say nothing
but bitter curses.
15 These people quickly
become violent.
16Wherever they go,
they leave ruin
and destruction.
17They don't know how
to live in peace.
18 They don't even fear God.”
19We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty. 20 God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin.
God's Way of Accepting People
21Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses. 22 God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ. 23All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory. 24But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins. 25-26 God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
27What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith. 28We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law. 29Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is! 30 There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith. 31Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_text:
1To, nɛ nuso be kechɔ nɛ Juwebi chɔ basa pɔtɛ? Ŋko manɛ be tɔnɔ nɛ katutuku kɔ? 2Cha, Juwebi baa chɔ basa pɔtɛ ekpa kama so nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ k juŋkpar e la fanɛ bumo nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta mbe mmalga m bɔɔ enɔ. 3Ama nɛ bumo be beko malɛ kini kebugi epunto n sa Ebɔrɛ ai? Loŋ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ malɛ e ki kɔnɔleŋiwura a? 4Kaarɛ fanɛ loŋ e tiŋ n wora. Nɛ nyiŋgbasa bre la efɛpo, Ebɔrɛ bre la kashenteŋjipo nna saŋkama fanɛ kananɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na. A yɛ:
“Fo mmalga to e naa ŋini fo ka kɔ kashenteŋ,
fo alɛ beeŋ baa ji a lar fo edemu to.”
5Kesheŋ bishiso ko malɛ nde fanɛ: “Nɛ fanɛ anyi be asheŋ lubi bee shin nɛ basa bee wu Ebɔrɛ be alelasheŋ, nuso nɛ an naa kaŋɛ ere? An kaŋɛ fanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bar mbe agbo anyi so, e maŋ wora n nyalɛ ŋko?” Nyiŋgbasa be kamɔrɔji be kamalga nɛ mee malga na. 6Kaarɛ, loŋ maŋ kɔ ekpa kuraa, ŋkpal manɛ so, nuso nɛ Ebɔrɛ daa tiŋ a ji durnya ere to ebi demu? 7Ama esa ko malɛ kraa beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n ji emɔrɔ m bishi le: “Nɛ fanɛ ŋkpal ma efɛsheŋ so Ebɔrɛ be kashenteŋ na bee lar efuli nɛnɛ a nya kemaŋkura a ti so, manɛ e naaŋ ba nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora n da so?” 8Le be kamalga koŋwule ere malɛ so nɛ basa ko bee yili so a ku anyi kɔnɔ a kaŋɛ fanɛ loŋ nɛ anyee kaŋɛ na. B yɛ: “Men shin nɛ an baa wora alubi nɛ a baa ki alela.” Loŋ be basa be kasogberge baŋ daga bumo nna.
Dimɛdi ka maŋ du cheembi be asheŋ
9To, naniere, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ anyi chɔ basa pɔtɛ ŋko? Cha, anyi maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ loŋ kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an teŋ wu fanɛ dimɛdi kikɛ, Juwebi nɛ basa pɔtɛ kikɛ wɔ alubi to nna. 10Loŋ malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ:
“Elelapo kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ Ebɔrɛ be anishito,
hale ekoŋwule gba maŋ wɔtɔ.
11Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ a pin asheŋ to,
ekama malɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ a kɔ a fin Ebɔrɛ.
12Ekama nyam kilgi m pal kaman n sa Ebɔrɛ n choŋ,
ekama nyam ki jiga.
Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ a wora kelela,
hale esa koŋwule gba maŋ wɔtɔ.
13Ekama be kɔnɔ du fanɛ b ka kur nchaŋ nna n nase.
Efɛ nɛ bumo be nnɔana na bee ku
mmalga nɛ a bee lar bumo be nnɔana to
du fanɛ wasa ka duŋ esa n lara kɔrtɔ n wɔtɔ mo to na.
14Abar be kebaamelgi kpakpaso e bɔlɔ bumo be nnɔ to a wɔtɔ.
15Bumo be aya malɛ maa chɛr a yɛr bumo basa be kemɔ to.
16Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ b yɔ, kasɔjija be tɔrɔ nɛ baa yige a lɛ basa so.
17B maŋ nyi kagbenewushi be ekpa.
18Bumo alɛ maŋ naa kɔ kabɔrɛŋana.”
19Ama an nyi fanɛ kusɔ kama nɛ mbra na bee kaŋɛ, basa nɛ b wɔ kumo to na to nɛ k de, saŋɛ na so esa kikɛ maaŋ nya kɔnɔ m bugi. Loŋ malɛ e naaŋ shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ e ji durnya kikɛ demu. 20Ŋkpal manɛ so, mannɛ esa nɛ e bee wora mbra be ashuŋ shunso e la esa nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo. Kusɔ nɛ mbra na baa ŋini e la kebaashin nɛ basa e baa pin kulubi be asheŋ.
Kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee shin nɛ mo nɛ basa bee nya kɔnɔkoŋwule be asheŋ
21Ama naniere bre Ebɔrɛ ŋini kananɛ e nase kumo fanɛ basa e baa la belelapo mbe anishito, loŋ be ekpa na malɛ nɛ mbra na maŋ kɔ shɛŋ. 22Loŋ be shɛda nɛ mbra na gba nɛ anebiana na bee ji. Ebɔrɛ malɛ bee bɔla basa be yirda nɛ k deŋ Yesu Kristo so so nna a shin nɛ mo nɛ basa na kikɛ bee nya kɔnɔkoŋwule. Mo alɛ maa kpɛa basa to. 23Ŋkpal manɛ so, ekama nyam wora kulubi a maŋ taga to Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura na. 24Ama ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ esa maa wora shɛŋ nsaa nya na so, asheŋ naŋ nyalɛ n sa basa, ŋkpal kesɔnyige be ekpa nɛ b bɔla Yesu Kristo so m bugi na so. 25Ebɔrɛ ta mo nna n sa basa nɛ e wu m mata be luwu nɛ k bee shin nɛ dimɛdi bee bɔla yirda so a nya alubi be ketampaŋ na. Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ nna nɛ e ŋini kananɛ e bee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so, ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋɛ na e daa nyi basa be alubi nna nsaa nyiti bumo. 26Ama naniere bre e maa kplaŋ dimɛdi be alubi so, a ŋini e ka bee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so. Loŋ malɛ e naa ŋini mo gbagba ka la asheŋ be keji nɛ amo be ekpa so be Ebɔrɛ, mo alɛ nseŋ naa ta esa nɛ e yirda Yesu a ki elelapo mbe anishito.
27To, nɛ manɛ so nɛ esa bee wu mbe kumu? E beeŋ tiŋ ŋkpal e ka bee bɛ mbra na so so a wu mbe kumu a? Ayai, ŋkpal manɛ so, mannɛ e ka bee bɛ mbra na so e shin nɛ e ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, ama ŋkpal e ka yirda so. 28Ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ an baa kɔ to e la fanɛ yirda e naa shin nɛ esa bee ji a lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, mannɛ kebaabɛ mbra na be asheŋ woraso so. 29Ŋko Ebɔrɛ la Juwebi nawule be Ebɔrɛ nna a? Mannɛ basa pɔtɛ gba be Ebɔrɛ e la mo a? Bumo alɛ gba be Ebɔrɛ nna walɛ. 30Ebɔrɛ koŋwule e wɔtɔ, mo alɛ Juwebi nɛ basa pɔtɛ kikɛ, ekpa koŋwule so nɛ e bee bɔla a shin nɛ baa ji a lar. Bumo kikɛ be yirda so nɛ e bee yili a wora loŋ. 31Ama an ta le be yirda ere n ti mbra na ekpa ŋko? Ayai, an baa kraa kɔ kumo to a ti kumo so eleŋ.

english_text:
The Example of Abraham
1Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham? 2If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God. 3 The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
4Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working. 5But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him. 6In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
7-8 “What a blessing
when God forgives our sins
and our evil deeds.
What a blessing
when the Lord erases our sins
from his book.”
9Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him. 10But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
11 Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised. 12This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised.
The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
13 God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable. 14 If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
15God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken. 16 Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all. 17 The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
18 God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations. 19 Abraham's faith never became weak, not even when he was nearly 100 years old. He knew he was almost dead and that his wife Sarah could not have children. 20But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
21Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised. 22So God accepted him, 23just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham. 24They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life. 25 God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_text:
Kananɛ Eebraham ŋini yirda be asheŋ
1To, nɛ an keni an nananyɛn Eebraham malɛ be kebaawɔtɔ to, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ? Manɛ nɛ e daŋ wu mbe kebaawɔtɔ to? 2Nɛ fanɛ ashuŋ ko nɛ e daŋ wora nseŋ ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, kumo ere e daa beeŋ tiŋ ŋkpal amo so m puchi, ama e maaŋ tiŋ m puchi Ebɔrɛ bre be anishito. 3Ŋkpal manɛ so, le nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ: “Eebraham daŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ nna so nɛ mo ere Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na.” 4Nɛ esa baŋ shuŋ kushuŋ, baa ka mo loŋ be kushuŋ na be kukɔ nna. Fo maaŋ tiŋ n tre loŋ be kakɔka na kakɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e shuŋ nna n nya kushuŋ na be kakɔka. 5Ama esa nɛ e lara mbe yirda ashi mbe ashuŋ shunso to n lɛ nseŋ ta yirda na n deŋi Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee shin nɛ alubiworapoana bee ji a lar mbe anishito na so, loŋ be yirda na beeŋ ki alelasheŋ Ebɔrɛ be anishito n sa mo. 6Loŋ gbagba nɛ Ewura Deevid daa de saŋɛ nɛ e daŋ malga nɛfa nɛ k wɔ esa kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee lar amodoŋwura be ashuŋ shunso be kaman a ta mo a ki elelapo na be asheŋ na. 7E yɛ:
“Nɛfa la bumo nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta bumo be alubi m paŋ bumo na peya nna, bumo nɛ e kpra bumo be alubi bumo so na.
8Nɛfa la esa nɛ Enyɛnpe na maa nyiŋi mbe alubi be asheŋ na peya nna.”
9To, nɛfa nɛ Ewura Deevid daŋ malga kumo be asheŋ ere la basa nɛ b ku atutu na nawule peya nna ŋko bumo nɛ b maŋ ku atutu gba peya nna? Bumo nɛ b maŋ ku atutu gba ti so. Kumo be asheŋ nɛ an teŋ nyiŋi anyi be amu ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na kaŋɛ le na: “Ŋkpal Eebraham ka daŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ so, Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo nna.” 10Saŋɛ mo nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ wora loŋ Eebraham daŋ ku kututu nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ ŋko e daŋ wora loŋ nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Eebraham ku? E daŋ wora loŋ nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Eebraham ku. 11Mbe yirda na be kaman nɛ e daŋ ku kututu a ŋini fanɛ ŋkpal mbe yirda na so nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo pɔɛŋ nɛ e ku. Amoso, abɔrɛsheŋ be kaplɛa so, mo e la bumo nɛ b maŋ ku nseŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ na kikɛ bumo tuto, saŋɛ na so Ebɔrɛ beeŋ nase kumo fanɛ b la belelapo. 12Mo ere Eebraham koŋwule na e la bumo nɛ b ku atutu na gba bumo tuto, ama mannɛ b ka baŋ ku na so, b ka wɔ yirda be kebaawɔtɔ koŋwule nɛ mo ere Eebraham daa wɔ to pɔɛŋ nseŋ ku kututu na gba so.
Kananɛ yirda la Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso be kumu be asheŋ
13Ebɔrɛ daŋ nase kɔnɔ nna n sa Eebraham nɛ mbe kaman to ebi fanɛ baaŋ nya durnya ere. Mannɛ Eebraham ka daa bɛ mbra na so so nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ na, e ka daŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na so nɛ e daŋ wora loŋ. 14Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso na la bumo nɛ baa bɛ mbra na so na peya nna, kumo ere esa be yirda maŋ kɔ kifi nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso na malɛ gba maŋ la shɛŋ. 15Ŋkpal manɛ so, mbra e naa shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ be agbo bee lar efuli. Kaplɛkama nɛ mbra maŋ wɔtɔ, kewora n da so malɛ gba maŋ wɔtɔ.
16Amoso, yirda e la kɔnɔ naseso be kumu, saŋɛ na so, loŋ be kɔnɔ naseso na beeŋ baa la Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ be tɔɔnɛ a sa Eebraham be kaman to ebi kikɛ, mannɛ bumo nɛ baa bɛ mbra na so nawule na, ama bumo nɛ b yirda Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kananɛ Eebraham daŋ yirda na gba ti so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, Eebraham e la anyi kikɛ be etuto ashi abɔrɛsheŋ be kaplɛa so. 17Loŋ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Eebraham le na. E yɛ: “N ta fo ŋ ki efuli damtaana so ebi bumo tuto.” Amoso, Ebɔrɛ be anishito Eebraham nɛ e daŋ yirda mo ere Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa basa wuso ŋkpa nsaa shin nɛ asɔ nɛ a maŋ wɔ durnya to bee fara kebaawɔtɔ na e la an tuto. 18Saŋɛ nɛ Eebraham daŋ yirda nseŋ tama na, e daa maŋ wu shɛŋ pɔɛŋ nna nseŋ tama. Amoso nɛ e ki efuli damta so ebi bumo tuto fanɛ kananɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na kaŋɛ mo le na: “Loŋ nɛ fo kaman to ebi beeŋ ba wora keshi a sa.” 19Mo ere Eebraham na daŋ fo fanɛ nfɛ kalfa, ama e ka daŋ keni mo gbagba be eyur ka daa maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ so, mbe yirda be eleŋ daa maŋ yɔɔ. Mo alɛ ka daŋ naŋ wu fanɛ mbe eche Sɛɛra be kakurge be saŋɛ baŋ so, mbe yirda na be eleŋ maŋ yɔɔ. 20Mbe yirda daa maŋ gbuŋgbuŋ to n shin nɛ e fara a lar Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso be kaman. E daŋ nya yirda be eleŋ nna n ti so nseŋ ta kemaŋkura n sa Ebɔrɛ. 21E daa nyi geeŋ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ n wora kusɔ nɛ e daŋ nase kɔnɔ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e beeŋ wora na. 22Amoso nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na.
23Kekaŋɛ fanɛ: “Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na,” maŋ de mo nawule nna ashi abɔrɛsibɛ na to. 24Anyi nɛ an yirda mo Ebɔrɛ nɛ e tiŋi Yesu an Nyɛnpe ashi luwu to ŋkaa beeŋ nase kumo fanɛ an la belelapo na gba ti so. 25Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ b daŋ ta mo nna n sa nɛ e wu ŋkpal anyi be alubi so nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ e tiŋi luwu na to nɛ an baa la belelapo Ebɔrɛ be anishito.

english_text:
What It Means To Be Acceptable to God
1By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God. 2Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God. 3But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure. 4And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope 5that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
6Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful. 7No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person. 8But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
9But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger. 10Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son. 11And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us.
Adam and Christ
12 Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die. 13Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law. 14Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did.
In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later. 15But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
16There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times. 17Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
18 Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life. 19Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
20The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful. 21Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_text:
Ebɔrɛ nɛ nyiŋgbasa be kenya kɔnɔkoŋwule be asheŋ
1Naniere Ebɔrɛ ka kpal anyi be yirda so n shin nɛ an ji n lar mbe anishito ere bre, an bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo so a kɔ kagbenewushi ashi Ebɔrɛ na be anishito. 2Yesu kpal anyi be yirda so n shin nɛ an nya le be kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ an wɔ ere to. Amoso, anyi be ŋgbene fuli anyi ŋkpal an ka kɔ tama fanɛ anyi alɛ gba beeŋ nya Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura nɛ e kɔ a jo anyi na so. 3Mannɛ aloŋ gba nawule so, ama an ka wɔ tɔrɔ to so nɛ anyi be ŋgbene kraa naŋ fuli anyi n ti so, ŋkpal manɛ so, an nyi tɔrɔ ka bee bar kenya kagbene a kɔ to be kebaawɔtɔ 4nɛ kumo alɛ bee sa esa da lela, nɛ da lela malɛ bee sa esa tama. 5Ebɔrɛ bɔla Kiyoyu Cheeŋ nɛ e la Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ nɛ e kɔ a sa anyi na so nna n ta mbe kasha m bɔlɔ anyi be ŋgbene to. 6Ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋɛ nɛ an daa maŋ kɔ eleŋ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ be jemanɛ fo nɛ Kristo wu n sa bumo nɛ b maŋ kɔ kabɔrɛŋana na. 7Pɔɛŋ nɛ esa e wu n sa elelapo, k du kpakpa. Shere esa ko beeŋ shuli n wu n sa esa nɛ e la esa bre. 8Ama kananɛ Ebɔrɛ ŋini anyi mbe kasha nde fanɛ saŋɛ nɛ an daa la alubiworapoana na nɛ Yesu wu n sa anyi. 9Ŋkpal manɛ so, naniere Kristo wu n shin nɛ an ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, amoso, mbe kumɔlga anyi kachako ashi Ebɔrɛ be agbo na bre to nɛ e maaŋ wora a? 10An daa la Ebɔrɛ mo doŋana nna, ama e bɔla mo Pibinyɛn Kristo be luwu na so n shin nɛ anyi nɛ mo naŋ nyalɛ. To, nɛ naniere anyi nɛ mo ka nyalɛ ere bre nɛ e maaŋ bɔla Kristo be ŋkpa na so m mɔlga anyi kachako a? 11Mannɛ aloŋ gba nawule so nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, an bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo nɛ e shin nɛ anyi nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ nyalɛ na so n nya kagbenefuli ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ so n ti so.
Adam nɛ Kristo be asheŋ
12To, naniere, men baa nyi fanɛ esa koŋwule so nɛ alubi bɔla m ba durnya to nɛ luwu malɛ ba ŋkpal alubi na so m ba sɔ durnya kikɛ to nyam, ŋkpal manɛ so, basa kikɛ wora alubi. 13Alubi malɛ daa wɔ durnya to nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa mbra. Ama kakpa nɛ mbra maŋ wɔtɔ, Ebɔrɛ maa karga alubi. 14Ama baŋ yili Adam be jemanɛ na m ba fo Mosis be jemanɛ to be basa kikɛ, luwu pɔɔ ekama so, hale bumo nɛ b maŋ wora n da Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ so geeŋ fanɛ kananɛ Adam daŋ wora na gba. Adam e daa la esa nɛ e daa ba na be kaduli.
15Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ ŋkpal esa koŋwule na be kulubi na so, basa damta wu. Ama le be basa anyɔ ere kɔr abar to, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ be kagbene koŋwuleso be kakɛ na nɛ Adam be kulubi na kɔr abar to. Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ na chɔ Adam be kulubi na ga. Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ mbe kagbene koŋwuleso be kakɛ nɛ e bee bɔla esa koŋwule Yesu Kristo be kuwɔr na so a sa basa damta na gba chɔ kumo. 16Kusɔ nɛ k lar kakɛ na malɛ gba be kaman naa chɔ kusɔ nɛ k lar esa koŋwule be kulubi na be kaman, ŋkpal manɛ so, Adam ka baŋ wora kulubi koŋwule na n loge nɛ kewora n da so be nfɛra ba. Ama alubi damta malɛ be kewora ka ba nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ shin nɛ kejinlar Ebɔrɛ be anishito malɛ ba. 17Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ esa koŋwule be kulubi so nɛ luwu ba kaa ji kuwura basa so, ama kusɔ nɛ esa koŋwule, Yesu Kristo wora na chɔ kumo ga. Ekama malɛ nɛ e sɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ damta na nɛ mbe alelasheŋ be kakɛ na, beeŋ bɔla Kristo so a wɔ ŋkpa to a ji kuwura.
18Amoso, kananɛ esa koŋwule be kulubi na baŋ shin nɛ basa kikɛ tɔr Ebɔrɛ be ntaŋ n nya kasogberge na, loŋ koŋwule na nɛ esa koŋwule be kelela koŋwule nɛ e wora na bee sɔ basa kikɛ a yige a sa bumo ŋkpa. 19Nɛ kananɛ esa koŋwule be kasomaanu shin nɛ basa kikɛ ki alubiworapoana na koŋwule na nɛ esa koŋwule mo na be kasonu beeŋ shin nɛ basa damta e ki belelapo Ebɔrɛ be anishito. 20Ebɔrɛ bar mbra na nna nɛ basa be alubi e wora keshi n ti so, ama kanaŋkamaso malɛ nɛ alubi bee wora keshi a ti so, saŋɛ na so nɛ Ebɔrɛ malɛ bee shin nɛ mbe kuwɔr be kakɛ bee wora keshi a ti so a chɔ loŋ. 21Amoso, kananɛ alubi baŋ bɔla luwu so ŋ ŋini amo be eleŋ na, loŋ koŋwule na nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ na bee bɔla alelasheŋ so a ŋini kumo be eleŋ m bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo so a kɔ anyi a yɔ ŋkpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar to.

english_text:
Dead to Sin but Alive because of Christ
1What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better? 2No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning? 3Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death? 4 When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
5If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him. 6We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin. 7We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
8As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him. 9We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die. 10When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God. 11In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
12Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires 13or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God. 14Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law.
Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
15What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not! 16Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him. 17You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received. 18Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
19I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
20When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God. 21But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death. 22Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life. 23Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
translation_text:
Kenya ŋkpa ŋkpal Yesu Kristo so be asheŋ
1To, naniere, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ? Fanɛ an baa wɔtɔ a wora alubi nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ na malɛ e baa wora keshi a ti so ŋko? 2Kaarɛ, loŋ maŋ daga, ŋkpal manɛ so, alubi be kewora be kaplɛa so, an wu nna, amoso, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ wora ŋ kraa wɔ amo be kewora be kebaawɔtɔ to? 3Ŋko men maŋ nyi fanɛ anyi kikɛ nɛ b bɛr kabɔrɛbɛr ŋkpal Yesu Kristo so ere, b bɛr anyi nna n wɔtɔ mbe luwu na to a? 4Anyi nɛ mo alɛ nɛ b puli saŋɛ nɛ b bɛr anyi kabɔrɛbɛr a ŋini fanɛ anyi nɛ mo koŋwule na e luri mbe luwu na to na, saŋɛ na so, kananɛ Etuto na baŋ ta mbe eleŋgboŋ n shin nɛ Kristo na tiŋi luwu to na, anyi alɛ gba beeŋ nya kebaawɔtɔ popɔr a wɔtɔ. 5Nɛ anyi nɛ mo e baŋ ki kukoŋwule ashi mbe luwu na to, kumo ere k baa dese geeŋ nna fanɛ anyi nɛ mo beeŋ naŋ bɔla mbe ketiŋi luwu to na so m ba abar so. 6Anyi alɛ nyi fanɛ anyi be kebaawɔtɔ dra na nɛ Yesu nɛ b daŋ mɔ kedibi largato na so na, saŋɛ na so alubi be eleŋ nɛ k bee ji da dra na so eleŋ na beeŋ mur nɛ an sa maŋ naa la alubi be anya. 7Ŋkpal manɛ so, esa baŋ wu, kumo ere e nya mbe kumu ashi alubi be eleŋ to. 8Nɛ anyi nɛ Kristo na e wu, kumo ere an yirda fanɛ anyi nɛ mo e naaŋ baa wɔ ŋkpa to. 9Ŋkpal manɛ so, an nyi fanɛ Kristo ka baŋ tiŋi luwu to ere bre, e maaŋ naŋ wu kikɛ. Luwu maŋ naa kɔ mbe eleŋ. 10Mbe luwu be kaplɛa so, kela koŋwule pati nɛ e wu m pɔɔ alubi be eleŋ so, mbe ŋkpa malɛ be kaplɛa so, e wɔ kumo to nna ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ so. 11Loŋ koŋwule na e daga fanɛ menyi alɛ gba e baa ta menyi be amu fanɛ men wu nna nɛ alubi maŋ naa ji menyi so eleŋ, ama men bɔla Kristo Yesu so nna a kɔ ŋkpa a wɔtɔ ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ so. 12Amoso, men sa maŋ naa shin nɛ alubi e baa pɔɔ menyi be eyurana nɛ a beeŋ wu ere so nɛ men baa nu a sa amo be ayɛlgasɔ lubiana. 13Menyi alɛ e sa maŋ naa shin nɛ menyi be eyurana be mba kama malɛ gba e naa wora kulubi nɛ men baa kɔ loŋ be kaba na a wora edalubisheŋ. Kusɔ nɛ k daga fanɛ men wora e la fanɛ men ta menyi be amu m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ fanɛ basa nɛ b shi luwu to m ba luri ŋkpa to. Men ta menyi be eyurana kikɛ m bɔɔ mo enɔ nɛ e ta n shuŋ ashuŋ lela. 14A maŋ daga alubi ka ji menyi so kuwura, ŋkpal manɛ so, men maŋ naa wɔ mbra na to. Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ na be kebaawɔtɔ to nɛ men wɔ.
Alelasheŋ be anya be asheŋ
15To, naniere, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ? Fanɛ ŋkpal an ka maŋ naa wɔ mbra na to nsaa wɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ be kebaawɔtɔ to so an baa wora alubi a? Kaarɛ, loŋ maŋ daga. 16Men maŋ nyi fanɛ men baŋ ta menyi be amu m bɔɔ esa enɔ fanɛ amodoŋwura be anya, men ki mbe anya kashenteŋto a? Menyeeŋ tiŋ a la alubi nɛ a beeŋ shin nɛ men wu na be anya, menyi alɛ beeŋ naŋ tiŋ a la kasonu nɛ kumo be lalaloge beeŋ shin nɛ men ki belelapo Ebɔrɛ be anishito na be anya. 17Ama anyee chɔrɔ Ebɔrɛ ga, ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋko men daa la alubi be anya nna, ama naniere, men ta menyi be ŋgbene kikɛ m bɛ kashenteŋ be keŋiniana nɛ men nya na kikɛ so. 18Ebɔrɛ shin nna nɛ men nya menyi be amu ashi alubi be eleŋ to nseŋ ba ki alelasheŋ be anya. 19Enyiŋgbasa be nfɛra be kaplɛa so nɛ mee ber kesheŋ ere a sa menyi nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, loŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ men pin amo to. Saŋko men daŋ ta menyi be amu kikɛ nna nyam ŋ ki kusɔjigaya nɛ dalubisheŋ be anya a wɔtɔ a wora asheŋ nɛ a maŋ daga. Naniere loŋ koŋwule na e daga fanɛ men naŋ ta menyi be amu kikɛ nyam ŋ ki alelasheŋ be anya a wɔtɔ a wora asheŋ nɛ a daga a du cheembi. 20Men ka daa la alubi be anya na, menyi nɛ alelasheŋ daa maŋ kɔ shɛŋ. 21Men ka daa wora asheŋ nɛ amo be asheŋ bee pɛ menyi anishinyɔr ere, manɛ be tɔnɔ nɛ men daŋ nya amo to? Loŋ be asheŋ na be tɔnɔ e la luwu. 22Ama naniere men ka nya menyi be amu ashi alubi to m ba ki Ebɔrɛ be anya ere bre, tɔnɔ mo nɛ menyee nya e la kebaawɔtɔ cheembi, kumo alɛ be lalaloge e la ŋkpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar na. 23Ŋkpal manɛ so, asheŋ lubi be kakɔka e la luwu, ama Ebɔrɛ be kagbene koŋwuleso be kakɛ e la ŋkpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar na ashi an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo to.

english_text:
An Example from Marriage
1My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive. 2For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free 3to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
4That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God. 5When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die. 6But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law.
The Battle with Sin
7 Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this. 8It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
9Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life, 10and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death. 11 Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died. 12Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
13Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is. 14We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin. 15 In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate. 16Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good. 17So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
18I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot. 19Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong. 20And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
21The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right. 22With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God. 23But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do. 24What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die? 25Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me.
So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
translation_text:
Kakil be mbra nɛ anyi nɛ Yesu be kebaawɔtɔ be asheŋ
1Ŋ kurgepoana, m baa nyi men ka beeŋ pin kusɔ nɛ mee sha kekaŋɛ menyi ere to, ŋkpal manɛ so, men la basa nɛ b nyi mbra na nna. Kumo e la fanɛ nɛ esa kraŋ baa wɔ ŋkpa to bre, mbra na e naa ji mo so kuwura ŋko? 2An ta fanɛ eche kilpo nɛ kakil be mbra na ŋ keni. Eche baŋ kil nɛ mo kul kraa wɔ ŋkpa to, mbra na bee kre mo nna a mata mo kul na loŋ hale n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ mo kul na beeŋ wu. Ama nɛ ekul na ba wu bre, kumo ere kakil be mbra maŋ naa kɔ mbe eleŋ. 3Amoso, nɛ mo kul na kraa wɔ ŋkpa to nɛ e ya kil enyɛn pɔtɛ, e ki bojua. Ama nɛ mo kul na baŋ wu bre, kumo ere mbra sa ekpa fanɛ e naŋ kil, e maŋ ki bojua. 4Ŋ kurgepoana, loŋ nɛ k du n sa menyi alɛ gba, ŋkpal manɛ so, mbra na be kaplɛa so, menyi alɛ gba wu nna ŋkpal men ka la Kristo be eyur na be kaba ko so. Naniere malɛ, men la mo koŋwule nɛ Ebɔrɛ tiŋi mo ashi luwu to nɛ an tiŋ a la basa nɛ b kɔ tɔnɔ ashi Ebɔrɛ be kushuŋ to na peya nna. 5Ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋɛ nɛ anyi be kebaawɔtɔ dra nɛ k daa wɔ anyi nɛ mbra na daa shin nɛ eyur to be ayɛlgasɔ daa kɔ anyi to a shuŋ na, luwu nɛ an daa kɔ tɔnɔ a sa. 6Ama naniere bre mbra na maŋ naa ji kuwura anyi so, ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ k daŋ nyaŋ anyi a wɔtɔ na be kaplɛa so, an wu nna naniere. Anyi maŋ naa shuŋ ekpa dra nɛ k la mbra nɛ b sibɛ n nase na, ekpa popɔr nɛ k la Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na peya na nɛ an naa shuŋ.
Mbra nɛ kulubi be asheŋ
7To, naniere, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ? An kaŋɛ fanɛ mbra na gbagba lubi nna ŋko? Kaarɛ, anyi maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ loŋ kuraa. Ŋkpal manɛ so, mbra na e shin nɛ m pin kusɔ nɛ k la kulubi. Nɛ mbra na daa maŋ kaŋɛ le nna: “Sa maŋ yɛlga fo barkasa be kusɔ,” n daa maaŋ pin loŋ be kayɛlga be asheŋ to. 8Ntaŋ malɛ so nɛ alubi nya ekpa n shin nɛ ayɛlgasɔ be yiri kikɛ nyam kaa, ŋkpal manɛ so, kakpa nɛ mbra maŋ wɔtɔ alubi malɛ gba wu nna a dese. 9Ŋ gbagba daa wɔ ŋkpa to nna a maŋ nyi mbra saŋko, ama ŋ ka ba pin ntaŋ na nɛ alubi malɛ nya ŋkpa ma to 10nɛ n wu, nɛ ntaŋ nɛ k daŋ daga fanɛ k bar ŋkpa na bar luwu m ba sa ma. 11Ŋkpal manɛ so, ntaŋ na so nɛ alubi nya ekpa n fule ma. Amoso, ntaŋ na so nɛ alubi bɔla m mɔ ma. 12Ade e naa ŋini fanɛ mbra na bre gbagba maŋ kɔ kulubi kumo to. Loŋ koŋwule na gba nɛ ntaŋ na gba la kusɔ lela a kɔ ekpa nsaa maŋ kɔ kulubi kumo to.
Kebagato nɛ k wɔ esa to be asheŋ
13To, kede bee ŋini fanɛ kusɔ lela e bar luwu ŋko? Cha, mannɛ aloŋ nna kuraa. Kulubi e bɔla kusɔ lela so m bar ma luwu nɛ kumo be da lubi gbagba e lar efuli. Amoso, ntaŋ na so nɛ esa bee wu kananɛ kulubi baŋ lubi kashenteŋto. 14An nyi mbra na ka la abɔrɛsheŋ, ama ma ere la nyiŋgbasa nna nɛ alubi kɔ ma fanɛ kenya. 15Amoso, ma ere gbagba maa pin ma asheŋ woraso to, ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ nɛ mee sha kewora, amo nɛ m maa wora nsaa wora asɔ nɛ ŋ kishi. 16Nɛ ma alɛ baa wɔtɔ a wora asɔ nɛ m maa sha kebaawora, kumo ere mee ŋini fanɛ mbra na kɔ kashenteŋ nna na. 17Amoso, mannɛ ma gbagba e naa wora kesheŋ na, kulubi nɛ k wɔ ma to na e naa wora kumo. 18M baa nyi kelela kikɛ ka maŋ wɔ ma to, ma kagbene lubi ere to nɛ n de na. Ŋkpal manɛ so, kelela be kewora be kasha wɔ ma to, ama ma alɛ maaŋ tiŋ n wora kumo. 19Kelela nɛ mee sha fanɛ m baa wora na, m maa wora. Ama kulubi nɛ m maa sha fanɛ n wora na nɛ mee wora. 20To, naniere k ka baa la fanɛ kusɔ nɛ m maa sha nɛ mee wora ere, kumo ere mannɛ ma e naa wora kumo na, kulubi nɛ k wɔ ma to na e naa wora kumo. 21Amoso, k du fanɛ le be kebaawɔtɔ e baa wɔtɔ fanɛ nɛ m baa sha kewora kelela nɛ kulubi teŋ ba sɔ kejuŋkpar. 22Ma kagbene bre gbagba bee sha Ebɔrɛ be mbra na. 23Ama ma alɛ bee wu mbra pɔtɛ ko ka wɔ ma eyur to a shuŋ. Mbra ko nna nɛ k bee kɔ mbra nɛ ma nfɛra bee sha na nsaa ta ma a ki alubi be mbra nɛ k wɔ ma eyur to a shuŋ na be kabutipo. 24Yee, nuso bre be asheŋ e nya ma le? Nɛ wanɛ malɛ e naaŋ mɔlga ma ashi le be eyur nɛ k kɔ ma a yɔ luwu to ere? 25Mee chɔrɔ Ebɔrɛ ga fanɛ mo e naaŋ bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo so m mɔlga ma.
Kusɔ nɛ k baa wɔtɔ kikɛ nde fanɛ ma ere gbagba be nfɛra to n la Ebɔrɛ be mbra na be kenya nna, ama ma kagbene lubi ere bre to n la kulubi be mbra be kenya nna.

english_text:
Living by the Power of God's Spirit
1If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished. 2The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death. 3The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin. 4He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
5People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things. 6If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace. 7Our desires fight against God, because they do not and cannot obey God's laws. 8If we follow our desires, we cannot please God.
9You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him. 10But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins. 11 Yet God raised Jesus to life! God's Spirit now lives in you, and he will raise you to life by his Spirit.
12My dear friends, we must not live to satisfy our desires. 13If you do, you will die. But you will live, if by the help of God's Spirit you say “No” to your desires. 14Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children. 15 God's Spirit doesn't make us slaves who are afraid of him. Instead, we become his children and call him our Father. 16God's Spirit makes us sure that we are his children. 17His Spirit lets us know that together with Christ we will be given what God has promised. We will also share in the glory of Christ, because we have suffered with him.
A Wonderful Future for God's People
18 I am sure what we are suffering now cannot compare with the glory that will be shown to us. 19In fact, all creation is eagerly waiting for God to show who his children are. 20 Meanwhile, creation is confused, but not because it wants to be confused. God made it this way in the hope 21that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children. 22We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
23 The Spirit makes us sure about what we will be in the future. But now we groan silently, while we wait for God to show that we are his children. This means that our bodies will also be set free. 24And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping. 25However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
26In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words. 27 All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people. 28We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose, 29and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children. 30God then accepted the people he had already decided to choose, and he has shared his glory with them.
God's Love
31What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us? 32God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else? 33If God says his chosen ones are acceptable to him, can anyone bring charges against them? 34Or can anyone condemn them? No indeed! Christ died and was raised to life, and now he is at God's right side, speaking to him for us. 35Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, suffering, and hard times, or hunger and nakedness, or danger and death? 36 It is exactly as the Scriptures say,
“For you we face death
all day long.
We are like sheep
on their way
to be butchered.”
37In everything we have won more than a victory because of Christ who loves us. 38I am sure that nothing can separate us from God's love—not life or death, not angels or spirits, not the present or the future, 39and not powers above or powers below. Nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love for us in Christ Jesus our Lord!
translation_text:
Kebaawɔtɔ nɛ k la Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na peya be asheŋ
1Bumo nɛ b wɔ Kristo Yesu to naniere bre, kejimbri be kasogberge maŋ naa wɔ bumo so. 2Ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋkpa be Kiyoyu na be mbra bɔla Yesu Kristo so n shin nɛ n nya ma kumu ashi kulubi nɛ luwu be mbra to. 3Ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ mbra na daa maaŋ tiŋ n wora ŋkpal dimɛdi be kapɔr lubi ere ka maŋ kɔ eleŋ na so, Ebɔrɛ bre wora kumo. E shuŋi mo Pibinyɛn gbagba nna n ji m bri kulubi nɛ k wɔ dimɛdi be eyur to na. Mo Pibinyɛn na ta eyur fanɛ dimɛdi be alubi be eyur ere nna m ba lara kulubi ashi to. 4Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ nna nɛ alelasheŋ nɛ mbra na bee sha na e nya n wora anyi to nɛnɛ ashi anyi nɛ an maŋ naa wɔ alubi be eyur be kebaawɔtɔ to nsaa wɔ Kiyoyu na be kebaawɔtɔ to na to. 5Bumo nɛ b wɔtɔ a bɛ bumo be kapɔr lubiana be keŋini so, asɔ nɛ bumo be eyurana na bee sha na e wɔ bumo be nfɛra na. Bumo nɛ bumo alɛ wɔtɔ a bɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na be keŋini na so, asɔ nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na bee sha na e wɔ bumo be nfɛra. 6Keshin nɛ kapɔr lubi ere e baa wɔ fo nfɛra bee yɛr fo luwu to nna nɛ keshin nɛ Kiyoyu na e baa wɔ fo nfɛra malɛ bee yɛr fo ŋkpa nɛ kagbenewushi to. 7Amoso, nyiŋgbasa baŋ shin nɛ kapɔr lubi ere wɔ mbe nfɛra, kumo ere e ki Ebɔrɛ mo doŋ nna na, ŋkpal manɛ so, e maa nu a sa Ebɔrɛ be mbra na. Kashenteŋto, e baŋ maaŋ tiŋ n nu n sa kumo nna gba kuraa. 8Bumo nɛ b wɔ bumo be kapɔr lubi na be keŋini to maaŋ tiŋ m par Ebɔrɛ kikɛ. 9Ama naniere bre, mannɛ asɔ nɛ menyi be kapɔr lubiana bee ŋini menyi na to nɛ men wɔ, asɔ nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na bee ŋini menyi na to nɛ men wɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu na baa wɔ menyi to nna na, ŋkpal manɛ so, esa kama nɛ e maŋ kɔ Kristo be Kiyoyu na maŋ la Kristo na peya. 10Amoso, nɛ Kristo baa wɔ menyi to, hale nɛ menyi be eyurana ere beeŋ wu ŋkpal alubi so gba, menyi be ayoyu bre kɔ ŋkpa nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ menyi la belelapo nna mbe anishito. 11Nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛ e tiŋi Yesu ashi luwu to na be Kiyoyu baa wɔ menyi to bre, kumo ere mo koŋwule nɛ e tiŋi Kristo ashi luwu to na gbagba beeŋ naŋ bɔla mbe Kiyoyu nɛ e wɔ menyi to na so n sa menyi be eyurana nɛ a beeŋ kaŋ wu kachako ere ŋkpa.
12Kusɔ ko malɛ nde: Ŋ kurgepoana, an ji kebaawɔtɔ ko be kukɔ nna, ama kumo alɛ maŋ la kapɔr lubi nɛ an wɔ to ere peya nna nɛ an baa wɔ kumo to a wora kumo be aparsheŋ. 13Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ men baa bɛ menyi be kapɔr lubiana ere be keŋini so, menyeeŋ wu, ama nɛ men baŋ bɔla Kiyoyu na so n jija kapɔr lubi ere be ashuŋ lubi na, menyeeŋ nya ŋkpa. 14Bekama nɛ Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu na bee juŋkpar bumo na kikɛ la Ebɔrɛ be mbia nna. 15Kiyoyu nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa menyi na malɛ maa ta menyi nna a ki anya n shin nɛ men naa lɔ kufu. Men nya Kiyoyu nɛ e bee ta menyi a ki mbia nna. Kiyoyu na malɛ so nɛ anyee tiŋ a tre Ebɔrɛ ‘Aba’, kumo e la fanɛ an Tuto. 16Kiyoyu na malɛ gbagba e naa chɛ anyi be ayoyu to a ŋini fanɛ an la Ebɔrɛ be mbia nna kashenteŋto. 17To, nɛ anyi alɛ baa la mbia bre, kumo ere anyeeŋ nya enɛfa nɛ e kɔ a jo mbe basa na. Kumo be kaman nɛ anyi nɛ Kristo e naaŋ nya kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a sa mo na, ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ an baa tu Yesu a ji mbe awurfoŋ na fanɛ kananɛ e daŋ ji na, anyi alɛ beeŋ naŋ tu mo n nya mbe kemaŋkura na.
Kachako so be kemaŋkura na be asheŋ
18M baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ tɔrɔ mo nɛ anyee nya naniere maaŋ tiŋ n fo kemaŋkura nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ bugi to n sa anyi na kikɛ so kuraa. 19Ebɔrɛ be kepɔrso kikɛ nyam malɛ baa jɔŋ kumo be aya so nna a jo saŋɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ lara mbe mbia efuli na. 20Ŋkpal manɛ so, b yili kumo nna fanɛ kepɔrso kikɛ e sa maa kɔ tɔnɔ kikɛ, mannɛ ŋkpal kepɔrso na gbagba be keparso, ama ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ nɛ e yili kumo loŋ na be katiŋ so. 21Ama le be tama ere e chɛr a wɔtɔ fanɛ kepɔrso kikɛ gbagba beeŋ nya kumo be kumu a maaŋ naŋ wu m bɛ kachako nɛ Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ k nya kumo be kemaŋkura nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a sa mbe mbia na. 22Ŋkpal manɛ so an baa nyi fanɛ yili kulubi be sososo na m ba fo mbre, kepɔrso kikɛ bee shu ebesa nɛ k du fanɛ kakurge to be ebesa na to nna. 23Mannɛ asɔtoso na gba nawule, anyi nɛ an nya Kiyoyu nɛ e la Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ juŋkparso na gba bee shu to nna nsaa jo saŋɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ta anyi ŋ ki mbe mbia n shin nɛ an nya anyi be amu kikɛ nyam na. 24Tama so nɛ Ebɔrɛ mɔlga anyi, ama nɛ esa tea wu kusɔ nɛ e bee tama bre, kumo ere mannɛ tama e naa la na, ŋkpal manɛ so, esa mo e naa wu kusɔ nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ e bee tama kumo be kenya a wora fanɛ e ka maŋ naŋ wu kumo na? 25Ama nɛ an baa tama kusɔ nɛ anyi maŋ naŋ wu bre, kumo ere, kanyiti nɛ an kɔ a jo kumo. 26Loŋ koŋwule na malɛ nɛ Kiyoyu na bee ba m ba kaa chɛ anyi mo nɛ an maŋ kɔ eleŋ ashi yirda na to na to. Anyi maŋ nyi kananɛ k daga fanɛ an kule Ebɔrɛ gba, ama Kiyoyu na gbagba e naa bugi kagbene a kule kabɔrɛkule nɛ k bee mɔ kɔnɔ a sa anyi. 27Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee wu basa be ŋgbene to na e nyi Kiyoyu na be nfɛra. Kiyoyu na malɛ e naa bɔla ekpa nɛ k bee par Ebɔrɛ so a kule mo a sa mbe basa. 28Anyi alɛ nyi fanɛ asɔ kikɛ to, Ebɔrɛ bee wora asheŋ nna nɛ a bee ba abar so m ba kaa ki asɔ lela a sa mbe beshapo nɛ e tre m ba mo kutɔ fanɛ b ba kaa wora mbe aparsheŋ na. 29Bumo nɛ e chɛr a nyi koŋwule na nɛ e lara n yili fanɛ b baa du fanɛ mo Pibinyɛn na, saŋɛ na so, Ebinyɛn na beeŋ baa la bekurgepo damtaana na to be ejuŋkparso. 30Amoso, Ebɔrɛ tre bumo nɛ e lara n yili na nna. Bumo nɛ e tre na malɛ kikɛ nɛ e shin nɛ b ji n lar. Bumo nɛ e shin nɛ b ji n lar malɛ kikɛ nɛ e shin nɛ mo nɛ bumo nya mbe kemaŋkura na.
Kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bɔla Kristo Yesu so ŋ ŋini mbe kasha be asheŋ
31To, asheŋ nɛ an nu ere kikɛ be kaman, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ? Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baa wɔ anyi be kaman, wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ anyi so? 32Esa nɛ e maŋ mɔn anyi mo gbagba Pibinyɛn nseŋ ta mo m bɔɔ basa enɔ ŋkpal anyi kikɛ so na, manɛ nna nɛ e maaŋ bugi kagbene n sa anyi kusɔ kikɛ n ti mo Pibi so? 33Nɛ wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ n wu Ebɔrɛ be basa kulubi, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ gbagba e kaŋɛ fanɛ b ji n lar. 34Esa ko malɛ naa wɔtɔ nna nɛ e tiŋ n ji m bri bumo a? Kristo Yesu e la emo nɛ e wu, mo alɛ nseŋ naa la emo nɛ Ebɔrɛ tiŋi ashi luwu to nɛ e ya kaa tase Ebɔrɛ be jisoso, ebunyampo be kakpa a kule Ebɔrɛ a sa anyi na. 35To, manɛ e naaŋ tiŋ n lara kasha nɛ Kristo kɔ a sa anyi ashi anyi so? Tɔrɔ ŋko awurfoŋ ŋko basa be kekɔrfɛ anyi ŋkpal anyi be yirda so ŋko akoŋ ŋko ketir ŋko kenishipere ŋko luwu bre e naaŋ tiŋ n lara mbe kasha ashi anyi so? 36Loŋ malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ:
“Ŋkpal fo so nɛ an wɔ kenishipere
nɛ k kɔ anyi a yɔ luwu to kachɛ kama na.
An ki fanɛ mbolpɔ nɛ b kɔ a yɔ nɛ b ya teŋ nna.”
37Kashenteŋto, shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n lara mbe kasha ashi anyi so. Kusɔ kama malɛ kikɛ to an bɔla emo nɛ e daŋ sha anyi na so nna a kɔ eleŋ kusɔ kikɛ so. 38Ŋkpal manɛ so, m baa nyi geeŋ nna fanɛ shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n lara kasha nɛ e kɔ a sa anyi na anyi so. Nɛ an wu ŋko an wɔ ŋkpa to gba, anyi maaŋ tiŋ n lar mbe kasha na to. Emalaika ŋko mbuibi lubiana ŋko asheŋ nɛ a bee wora naniere ŋko amo nɛ a beeŋ wora kachako gba ŋko eleŋana maaŋ tiŋ n lara kasha na anyi so. 39Shɛŋ maŋ wɔ durnya ere be esoso ŋko kumo be kaseto nɛ k tiŋ n lara mbe kasha na ashi anyi so. Shɛŋ shɛŋ maŋ wɔ durnya ere kikɛ to nɛ k tiŋ n lara anyi ashi Ebɔrɛ be kasha nɛ k bɔla an Nyɛnpe Kristo Yesu so a la anyeya na to.

english_text:
God's Choice of Israel
1I am a follower of Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness to my conscience. So I tell the truth and I am not lying when I say 2my heart is broken and I am in great sorrow. 3I would gladly be placed under God's curse and be separated from Christ for the good of my own people. 4 They are the descendants of Israel, and they are also God's chosen people. God showed them his glory. He made agreements with them and gave them his Law. The temple is theirs and so are the promises that God made to them. 5They have those famous ancestors, who were also the ancestors of the Christ. I pray that God, who rules over all, will be praised forever! Amen.
6It cannot be said that God broke his promise. After all, not all of the people of Israel are the true people of God. 7-8 In fact, when God made the promise to Abraham, he meant only Abraham's descendants by his son Isaac. God was talking only about Isaac when he promised 9 Sarah, “At this time next year I will return, and you will already have a son.”
10Don't forget what happened to the twin sons of Isaac and Rebekah. 11-12 Even before they were born or had done anything good or bad, the Lord told Rebekah that her older son would serve the younger one. The Lord said this to show he makes his own choices and it wasn't because of anything either of them had done. 13 That's why the Scriptures say that the Lord liked Jacob more than Esau.
14Are we saying God is unfair? Certainly not! 15 The Lord told Moses that he has pity and mercy on anyone he wants to. 16Everything then depends on God's mercy and not on what people want or do. 17 In the Scriptures the Lord says to the king of Egypt, “I let you become king, so that I could show you my power and be praised by all people on earth.” 18Everything depends on what God decides to do, and he can either have pity on people or make them stubborn.
God's Anger and Mercy
